# PREFACE

In the First Part, the first fifteen chapters of *Genesis* were explained, along with the things they contain in their *Internal Sense* <note>original: "Sensu Interno"; the deeper spiritual meaning the author believes lies beneath the literal text</note>. Attached to each chapter were accounts of those things which, by the Lord’s Divine Mercy, I was granted to see and hear in the *World of Spirits* and the *Heaven of Angels*. Now follows the Second Part, in which similar accounts will be added to each chapter. To this 16th chapter, I will add accounts concerning visions and dreams—including the prophetic ones found in the *Word* <note>original: "Verbo"; referring to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible</note>.

I know that few will believe it possible for anyone to see the things that exist in the other life, and thereby report anything concerning the *State of Souls* after death. This is because few believe in the *Resurrection*; indeed, fewer among the learned believe in it than among the simple-hearted. They say with their lips that they will rise again, because it is according to the *Doctrine of Faith*, yet in their hearts they deny it. 

Indeed, some even openly confess that they would only believe if someone were to rise from the dead and they could see, hear, and touch him. But if this were to happen, it would have to happen for every individual; and even then, anyone who denies it in their heart would not be persuaded. Instead, thousands of objections would flow in, which would only harden their mind in its negative stance. 

Some still say they believe they will rise again, but only on the day of the *Last Judgment*. They have adopted the opinion that at that time, everything visible in the world will perish. Because they have waited in vain for that day for so many centuries, they are also in doubt. However, what is meant by the "Last Judgment" mentioned in the Word, will be explained at the... <note>original: "finem"; the text cuts off, likely leading to "at the end of this chapter" on the next page.</note>

<summary>The author introduces the second part of his commentary on Genesis, defending his spiritual visions against widespread skepticism regarding the afterlife and the nature of the Resurrection.</summary>
<keywords>Genesis, Internal Sense, World of Spirits, Heaven of Angels, Resurrection, Last Judgment, Skepticism, Afterlife</keywords>

--- Page 8 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's discussion on the nature of the afterlife and the internal sense of the Word, specifically addressing skepticism regarding the resurrection.</meta>

At the end of the following Chapter 17, by the Lord’s Divine Mercy, more will be said shortly. From this, it can be established what kind of people exist today in the **Christian World**. The **Sadducees** <note>original: *Sadducæi*; a Jewish sect known in the New Testament for denying the resurrection</note>, of whom we read in Matthew 22:22 and following, openly denied the **Resurrection**. However, they acted more honestly than those today who claim they do not deny it—because, as mentioned, it is a doctrine of faith—yet in their hearts they deny it anyway. Thus, they speak against what they believe and believe against what they speak. 

But so that they might no longer confirm themselves in that false opinion, by the Lord’s Divine Mercy, it has been granted to me—while I am in the body in this world—to be in the other life in spirit. For man is a spirit clothed with a body. There, I have spoken with souls who rose again not long after their death; indeed, I have spoken with almost all those I knew during their bodily life who have since died. For several years now, I have spoken daily with **Spirits** and **Angels**, seeing amazing things there that have never entered into anyone’s imagination. 

This has happened without any deception. Many people say they would believe if someone from the other life came to them; it will now be seen whether they can be persuaded against the stubbornness of their hearts. I can assert this: those who come into the other life from the **Christian World** are the worst of all. They hate their neighbor, they hate faith, and they deny the Lord; for in the other life, hearts speak, not mouths. Furthermore, they are more prone to adultery than others. Because **Heaven** is thus beginning to be removed from those within the **Church** <note>original: *Ecclesiam*; here referring to the organized body of Christian believers</note>, it can be established—as has been granted to me to know for certain—that the final time is at hand.

***

Regarding the **Internal Sense of the Word** <note>original: *Sensu Interno Verbi*; the spiritual meaning hidden beneath the literal text of the Bible</note>, what it is and its quality, see what has been said and shown in Part One, numbers 1 to 5, 64, 65, 66, 167, 605, 920, 937, 1143, 1224, 1404, 1405, 1408, 1409, 1502 (end), 1540, 1659, 1756; especially 1767 to 1777, and 1869 to 1879, 1783, 1807; and in this Part, numbers 1886 to 1889 inclusive.

# PART TWO
## THE BOOK OF GENESIS
### CHAPTER SIXTEEN

1886. In this chapter, the story of Hagar and Ishmael is addressed. However, what is represented and signified by Hagar and Ishmael in the Internal Sense <note>original: "Sensu Interno"; the deeper spiritual meaning within the literal text</note> has remained unknown to anyone until now. Nor could it have been known, because until this point the world—even the learned world—has thought that the historical accounts of the Word <note>the Bible</note> are nothing more than history and involve nothing deeper. Even though people have said that every "jot and tittle" <note>original: "jotha"; the smallest letter or stroke of a pen</note> is divinely inspired, they have understood nothing more by this than that these things were revealed, and that some dogma applicable to the doctrine of faith could be deduced from them to be useful for teachers and students. They believed that because the text is divinely inspired, it has a Divine power over minds and works toward the good more than any other historical writing. 

But historical facts, viewed in themselves, do little for the improvement of a person, and contribute nothing to eternal life; for in the next life, historical details are forgotten. Indeed, what would it matter there if they knew about Hagar the servant—that she was given to Abram by Sarai—or about Ishmael, or even about Abram himself? Nothing is necessary for souls to enter into Heaven and enjoy joy—that is, eternal life—except those things which belong to the Lord and which come from the Lord. It is for the sake of these things that the Word exists, and these are the things contained within its interior meanings.

<summary>This page introduces the spiritual interpretation of the story of Hagar and Ishmael in Genesis 16, arguing that the Bible's historical accounts contain deep, divine meanings necessary for eternal life that go beyond literal history.</summary>
<keywords>Hagar, Ishmael, Internal Sense, Divine Inspiration, Word of God, Abram, Sarai, Eternal Life, Biblical Commentary</keywords>

# GENESIS

1887. Inspiration implies that in every detail of the Word—both in its historical accounts and in its other parts—there are celestial things which belong to love or "the good," and spiritual things which belong to faith or "the truth," and thus they are Divine. For whatever is inspired by the Lord descends from Him, passing through the Angelic Heaven and then through the World of Spirits until it reaches Man, with whom it is presented as it appears in the literal letter. However, it is entirely different in its first origin. In Heaven, there is never any worldly historical matter, but everything is a representation of Divine things, and nothing else is perceived there. This can also be known from the fact that the things there are inexpressible <note>original: "ineffabilia"</note>. Therefore, unless the historical accounts are representations of Divine things, and thus celestial, they could never be divinely inspired. What the Word is like in the Heavens is known only from the Internal Sense, for *the Internal Sense is the Lord’s Word in the Heavens.*

1888. That the literal sense of the Word represents Divine secrets <note>original: "arcanorum"</note>, and that it is a vessel and thus a storehouse for the Lord’s celestial and spiritual things, may be illustrated by two examples: first, that by "David" is not meant David but the Lord; and second, that Names signify nothing other than actual things; and consequently, so does everything else. Regarding David, it is said in Ezekiel: "*My servant David shall be King over them, and there shall be one Shepherd for them all; they shall dwell upon the land, they and their children, and their children's children forever; and David my servant shall be their Prince forever*" (Ezekiel 37:24, 25). And in Hosea: "*The children of Israel shall return and seek Jehovah their God, and David their King*" (Hosea 3:5). These were written by those Prophets long after David’s time, and yet it is clearly stated that he shall be their King and Prince. From this, it can be evident to anyone that by "David" in the internal sense, the Lord is meant. This is the case in other places as well, even in the historical books where David is named. 

That the names of Kingdoms, Regions, Cities, and Men signify actual things <note>original: "res"</note> can be clearly seen in the Prophets. For example, take this passage in Isaiah: "*Thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts <note>original: "Jehovih Zebaoth"</note>: O my people, inhabitant of Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria <note>original: "Aschure"</note>; he shall strike you with a rod, and lift up his staff against you in the way of Egypt. Jehovah of Hosts shall stir up a scourge against him, like the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb, and as His rod was over the sea, so shall He lift it up in the way of Egypt. He is come against Aiath; he has passed into Migron; at Michmash he has commanded his weapons; they have passed over the crossing; Geba is our lodging; Ramah <note>original: "Chormah"</note> trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled. Cry aloud with your voice, O daughter of Gallim; listen, O Laish; O poor Anathoth! Madmenah is a fugitive; the inhabitants of Gebim gather themselves together. As yet he shall remain at Nob that day; he shall shake...*"

<meta>his hand</meta>

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

"...he shall shake *his hand against the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem; he will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron; and Lebanon shall fall by a Mighty One*" <note>original: "manum suam mons filiæ Zionis; collis Hierosolymæ succidet implexa sylvæ ferro; & Libanus per Magnificum cadet"</note> (Isaiah 10:32, 34). In this passage, there are almost nothing but names, from which no clear meaning would emerge unless each name signified a specific thing. If a reader focused only on these names, they would never recognize this as the Word of the Lord. But who would believe that all these names, in their internal sense, contain the secrets <note>original: "arcana"</note> of Heaven? They describe the state of those who try to enter into the mysteries of faith through ratiocination <note>original: "ratiocinia"; the process of logical reasoning</note> based on <term>scientifics</term> <note>original: "scientificis"; in this context, "scientifics" refers to external facts or memory-knowledge gathered from the world</note>. Every single name describes something specific about that state. Furthermore, these reasonings are dispersed by the Lord through the celestial things of love and the spiritual things of faith. It is clearly evident that "Assyria" <note>original: "Aschurem"</note> signifies the act of reasoning discussed here, as shown in sections 119 and 1186; and that "Egypt" signifies scientific knowledge, as shown in sections 1164, 1165, and 1462. If these references are examined, one can see how this is the case; the same applies to all other names and every individual word.

1889. The same logic applies in this chapter to the names of Abram, Sarai, Hagar, and Ishmael. What these names involve can be seen from the summary of contents and the detailed explanation that follows. However, these concepts are not easily explained to the human understanding <note>original: "captum"</note>. This is because they deal with the Lord’s <term>Rational</term> <note>The "Rational" refers to the faculty of reason—the part of the mind that mediates between our higher spiritual nature and our lower natural instincts</note>—how it was conceived and born, and what its quality was before it was united to the Lord’s "Internal," which was Jehovah Himself. The reason this is difficult to understand is that today it is not known what the "Internal Man" is, or what the "Interior" and "Exterior" parts are. When someone mentions the "Rational" or the "Rational Man," we have some general idea of it; but when it is said that the Rational is a medium between the Internal and the External, few, if any, can grasp this. Nevertheless, because the internal sense here deals with the Rational Man within the Lord—how it was conceived and born from the influence <note>original: "influxu"</note> of the Internal Man into the External—these are the themes wrapped within the historical accounts of Abram, Hagar, and Ishmael. To ensure that the following explanations do not seem entirely foreign, it must be understood that within every human being there is an Internal Man, a Rational Man (which is in the middle), and an External Man; and these are very distinct from one another. Regarding this distinction, see what was previously stated in section 978.

### CHAPTER XVI

1. And Sarai, Abram’s wife, did not bear him any children; and she had an Egyptian servant-woman, and her name was Hagar.
2. And Sarai said to Abram, "See now, I beg you, <term>Jehovah</term> has prevented me from giving birth. Go in, I beg you, to my servant; perhaps I will be built up through her <note>original: "ædificabor ab ea"; a reference to the custom where a wife could claim her servant's children as her own to build up a family line</note>." And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
3. And Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, at the end of ten years from when Abram began living in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband, to be his wife.
4. And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was worthless <note>original: "vilis"; held in low esteem or despised</note> in her eyes.
5. And Sarai said to Abram, "The wrong done to me is upon you! I gave my servant into your bosom, and she saw that she conceived, and I am worthless in her eyes. May <term>Jehovah</term> judge between me and you."
6. And Abram said to Sarai, "Look, your servant is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes." And Sarai humbled <note>original: "humiliavit"; treated harshly or afflicted</note> her, and she fled from her presence.
7. And the Angel of <term>Jehovah</term> found her at a spring of water in the wilderness, at the spring on the way to Schur.
8. And he said, "Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?" And she said, "I am fleeing from the presence of Sarai, my mistress."
9. And the Angel of <term>Jehovah</term> said to her, "Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hands."
10. And the Angel of <term>Jehovah</term> said to her, "In multiplying I will multiply your offspring, and they shall not be numbered for their great multitude."
11. And the Angel of <term>Jehovah</term> said to her, "Look, you are pregnant, and you shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Ishmael <note>original: "Iischmael"; meaning "God hears"</note>, because <term>Jehovah</term> has heard your affliction."
12. And he will be a wild-ass man <note>original: "onager homo"; referring to someone who is free, wild, or lives outside of conventional society</note>; his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him, and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers.
13. And she called the name of <term>Jehovah</term> who spoke to her, "You are the God who sees me," for she said, "Have I even here seen after him who sees me?" <note>original: "num etiam hic vidi post videntem me"; expressing her amazement at seeing a divine manifestation and remaining alive</note>
14. Therefore the spring was called the Spring of the Living One who sees me; see, it is between Kadesh and Bared.

<header>CHAPTER SIXTEEN.</header>

15. And Hagar bore a son to Abram, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.

16. And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

### C O N T E N T S.

1890. This chapter deals with the first **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>original: "Rationali"; referring to the faculty of reason or the "rational man" that bridges the gap between the spiritual and the natural mind</note> in the Lord. This was conceived by the influence of the **Internal Man** into the affection for the **sciences** <note>original: "scientiarum"; in this context, it refers to worldly knowledge, facts, and sensory information</note> of the **External Man**. The Internal Man is Abram; the affection for the sciences of the External Man is the Egyptian servant Hagar; the Rational resulting from this is Ishmael. His nature is described here, and later in Chapter 21, it is shown how he was expelled from the house after the Lord's **Divine Rational**, represented by Isaac, was born.

1891. The Lord's first Rational was conceived in the proper order through the influx (or joining) of the Internal Man with the life of the affection for sciences, which belongs to the External Man (verses 1, 2, 3). But because it originated from the External man, its nature was such that it looked down upon intellectual truth (verse 4). Therefore, the Lord thought about bringing it under control (verses 5, 6, 7, 8, 9). When it was brought under control, it would become Spiritual and heavenly (verses 10, 11). What it would be like if it were *not* brought under control is described (verse 12). The Lord’s insight from His Interior Man into the cause is shown (verses 13, 14). Thus, the quality of the Rational is described, as well as the Lord's state when it arose (verses 15, 16).

---

### I N T E R N A L  S E N S E.

1892. **Verse 1.** *And Sarai, Abram’s wife, did not bear him children; and she had an Egyptian servant-woman, and her name was Hagar.* "Sarai, Abram’s wife, did not bear him children" signifies that there was not yet a rational man. Sarai is Truth joined to Good; Abram is the Lord’s Internal Man, who is <term>Jehovah</term>. "And she had an Egyptian servant-woman" signifies the affection for the sciences. "And her name was Hagar" signifies the life of the exterior or natural man.

1893. The fact that "Sarai, Abram’s wife, did not bear him children" signifies that there was not yet a rational man will become clear from what follows regarding Isaac. For, as has been said, within every person there is an **Internal man**, a **Rational man** (who is the middle), and an **External man** (who is properly called the **Natural man**). In the Lord, these were represented by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the Internal man by Abra-

<header>G E N E S I S.</header>

[...the Lord was represented by] Abraham, the **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>original: "Rationalis"; referring to the level of the mind that reasons and mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge</note> by Isaac, and the **Natural** <term>Natural</term> <note>original: "Naturalis"; the lower part of the mind focused on the physical world and external senses</note> by Jacob. The **Internal Man** within the Lord was Jehovah Himself, for He was conceived by Jehovah; this is why He so often called Him His Father, and why He is called in the Word the Only-begotten of God and the only Son of God. 

A rational man is not born as such; only the faculty to become rational is born with him. This is clear from the fact that newborn infants possess no reason at all, but they become rational over time through external and internal sensory means, just as they are steeped in various sciences and pieces of knowledge. In children, a certain "rationality" appears, but it is not yet truly rational; it is only a beginning or seed of it, which is known by the fact that true Reason only belongs to adults and the elderly. 

This chapter deals with the Rational man in the Lord. The **Divine Rational** <note>original: "Rationale Divinum"</note> itself is represented by Isaac. However, the *first* Rational—before it was made Divine—is represented by Ishmael. Therefore, the fact that Sarai, Abram's wife, had not yet borne him a child signifies that the Divine Rational did not yet exist at this point. 

The Lord, as previously stated, was born like any other man and was like any other man regarding what He inherited from His mother, Mary. Because the Rational mind is formed through **scientifics** <term>Scientifics</term> <note>original: "scientifica"; factual knowledge or data gathered from the world</note> and information that enters through the external senses (or the "external man"), His first Rational was born just like that of any other person. But because He would make everything human within Himself Divine by His own power, He did the same with His Rational. His first Rational is described here in this chapter, and also in Chapter 21 (verses 4 to 21), which discusses Hagar and Ishmael and how Ishmael was eventually sent away when Isaac—who represents the Divine Rational—had grown up.

**1894.** It was previously stated and shown in section number 1468 (and elsewhere) that Sarai represents truth joined to good. Similarly, Abram represents the Lord’s Internal Man, which is Jehovah. The reason why the Lord’s Internal Man (Jehovah) is called "Man" is that no one is truly a man except Jehovah alone. In its genuine sense, the word "Man" signifies that **Being** <note>original: "Esse"</note> from which "Man" originates. The very Being from which Man comes is Divine, and therefore Celestial and Spiritual. Without the Divine Celestial and Spiritual, there is nothing human in a person; they would be merely an animal, like the beasts. 

Every person's status as a "human" comes from the "Being" of Jehovah (the Lord); this is why he is called a man. The celestial quality that makes someone a man is the ability to love the Lord and love one's neighbor. In this way, a person is a man because they are an image of the Lord, and because they receive that quality from the Lord. Otherwise, a person is a wild beast. Regarding the fact that Jehovah (the Lord) is the only Man, and that humans are only called "men" because of Him—and that one person may be "more of a man" than another—see sections 49, 288, 477, and 565. 

Furthermore, this is evident from the fact that Jehovah (the Lord) appeared to the fathers of the **Most Ancient Church** <note>A symbolic name for the first state of humanity or the earliest "Golden Age" church</note> as a Man, and later to Abraham and the Prophets. This is also why the Lord deigned to take on human nature—by being born like any other man—after there was no longer any "man" left on earth (meaning there was no longer anything celestial or spiritual remaining in humanity). By making that human nature Divine, He became the "Only Man." Additionally, the entire Heaven reflects the image of a man before the Lord because it originates from Him; for this reason, Heaven is called the **Greatest Man** <note>original: "Maximus Homo"; also known as the "Grand Man," the idea that the collective heaven functions as a single human organism</note>, primarily because the Lord there is everything in all things.

**1895.** **And she had an Egyptian servant girl,** signifies the affection for the sciences <note>original: "affectionem scientiarum"</note>.

Truth joined to Good is **Intellectual Truth** <term>Intellectual Truth</term> <note>original: "Verum intellectuale"; in this context, the highest form of truth perceived directly by the soul's inner light</note> in its genuine sense. However, **Rational Truth** <term>Rational Truth</term> <note>original: "Verum rationale"; truth as it is processed by human reason</note> is below that, and thus inferior. This rational truth is born from sciences and pieces of knowledge, which are brought to life by an affection corresponding to them. This affection, because it belongs to the external man, must serve Intellectual Truth (which resides in the innermost part of the person) just as a handmaid serves a mistress or a female servant serves a lady. For this reason, that affection is what is represented and signified by the handmaid, Hagar.

How these things work cannot be easily explained to the common understanding. First, one must know what Intellectual Truth is in its genuine sense, and then how the "Rational" is born—namely, from the **Internal Man** as a father and from the **External** or **Natural** man as a mother. Without the union of both, nothing "Rational" can ever exist. The Rational is not born from sciences and pieces of knowledge themselves, as is commonly thought, but from the *affection* for those sciences and pieces of knowledge. This is clear from the fact that no one can ever become rational unless some delight or affection for knowledge inspires them. 

Affection is the very life of the "mother," and the celestial and spiritual element within that affection is the life of the "father." Therefore, a person becomes rational only to the extent and quality of their affection. In themselves, scientific facts and pieces of knowledge are merely dead things—or "instrumental causes"—which are brought to life through the life of affection. This is how the Rational man is conceived in every person. The reason she is called an "Egyptian handmaid" is that **Egypt** signifies sciences <note>original: "Ægyptus significat scientias"</note>, as was shown previously in sections 1164, 1165, 1186, and 1462.

1896. Her name was **Hagar**, which signifies the life of the external or natural man. Sojourners represented those who were to be instructed, and "sojourning" represented instruction and the way of life established by it, as shown previously in section 1463. When it is said in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures</note> that "her name is" something—as here, that her name is Hagar—it signifies that the name involves a specific quality that should be observed. To call something by a name is to know its quality, as shown previously in sections 144, 145, and 340. Not even a single small word exists in the Word without a cause and without signifying something in the internal sense.

Before these scientifics exist, there is indeed communication in the meantime, but only through affections. These affections rule the External man, producing only the most general movements, certain appetites, and blind inclinations, such as those seen in infants. 

However, this life becomes more distinct by degrees as the "vessels" of the memory are formed through pieces of knowledge, and the vessels of the *interior* memory are formed through rational concepts. As these vessels are formed and arranged in a series—organized so they relate to each other like family relatives or societies—the correspondence <note>A technical term for the harmonious "echoing" or matching between the spiritual and natural worlds.</note> of the External man with the Internal is perfected. This is improved even further through rational things, which act as intermediates. 

Still, this connection is not proper unless the pieces of knowledge used to form these vessels are **truths**. The celestial and spiritual elements of the Internal man only find a match within truths. These truths, stored in the organic forms of both memories, are the genuine vessels into which the celestial things of love and the spiritual things of faith can be fitted. When this happens, they are arranged by the Lord according to the idea and image of the **Societies of Heaven** <note>The organized communities of angels in the afterlife</note> or His Kingdom. In this way, the person becomes "Heaven" or "the Lord's Kingdom" in a small, individual form—which is why the minds of those who live in love and faith are called "the Kingdom" in the Word <note>The "Word" is the author's term for the Holy Scriptures.</note>. These things are explained for those who enjoy thinking more deeply.

We can conclude this because all animals, whatever they may be, are born with all the factual knowledge necessary and useful for their food, protection, housing, and procreation, because their nature follows this order. Why not humans, unless order had been destroyed in them? For humans alone are born with no innate knowledge. What causes this is hereditary evil from the father and mother; because of this, all of a person’s faculties are turned the wrong way regarding what is true and good. These faculties cannot be brought back into their proper forms by a direct influx of heavenly and spiritual things from the Lord. 

Therefore, a person's Rational mind must be formed in an entirely different way—namely, through facts and insights introduced through the senses. These flow in through an "external way," which is an inverted order. In this way, the Lord miraculously makes a person rational. This process is what is meant by "going in to the handmaid," which signifies the joining of the **Internal man** with the **External man**. The fact that *Abram listened to the voice of Sarai* signifies that this was the only way it could happen. He did this so that, through the struggles of temptation and His eventual victories, He might bring all things back into order. Therefore, His own Rational mind was conceived and born just like anyone else's, with one difference: the Divine (or Jehovah) was intimately present in every single part of Him. This was a life of love toward the entire human race, for whose salvation He fought in all His temptations.

# GENESIS

*To Abram her husband, to be his woman [or wife].* <note>original: "Abramo viro suo, illi in mulierem"</note> **Sarai, Abram's wife, took** signifies the affection for truth, which in its genuine sense is represented by Sarai the wife. **Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid** signifies the life of the external person and the affection for scientific knowledge <note>original: "affectionem scientiarum"; in this context, "science" refers to the broad category of factual or sensory knowledge</note>. **After Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan** signifies the remnants of good and the resulting truth which the Lord acquired for Himself, through which that rational part was conceived. **And gave her to Abram her husband to be his woman [or wife]** signifies a conjunction prompted by the affection for truth.

**1904.** **Sarai, Abram's wife, took**—that this signifies the affection for truth (which in its genuine sense is Sarai the wife) is clear from the meaning of **Sarai** as Truth joined to Good, and from the meaning of **wife** as "affection," as discussed previously in entries 915 and 1468. 

There are two distinct types of affection: the **affection for good** and the **affection for truth**. When a person is being regenerated <note>term: "regenerated"; the spiritual process of being reborn or made new by God</note>, the affection for truth comes first, for one is moved by truth for the sake of good. However, once a person is regenerated, the affection for good comes first, and from that good, one is moved by truth. 

The affection for good belongs to the **will**; the affection for truth belongs to the **understanding**. The most ancient people established a kind of marriage between these two affections: they called "Good" (or the love of good) the "man" or "husband," and "Truth" (or the love of truth) the "woman" or "wife." This comparison of good and truth to marriage originates from the **Heavenly Marriage**. 

Good and Truth, viewed in themselves, have no life of their own; they draw life from love or affection. They are merely the instruments of life. Therefore, the life of a person is determined by the quality of the love that influences their good and truth, for all life belongs to love or affection. This is why "Sarai the wife," in its genuine sense, signifies the affection for truth. In this specific verse, because the intellectual part desired a rational part (like a parent desiring a child), and because it is the desire or affection that is "speaking" through these actions, the text explicitly says: "Sarai, Abram’s wife... gave [her] to Abram her husband." It would not have been necessary to repeat these titles—which would otherwise be redundant—unless they involved such secrets in the internal sense.

Intellectual Truth is distinguished from Rational Truth, and Rational Truth from Scientific Truth <note>term: "Scientific Truth"; knowledge gained through the senses and study, rather than through direct spiritual perception</note>, much like the **Internal**, **Middle**, and **External**. 
*   **Intellectual Truth** is internal.
*   **Rational Truth** is middle.
*   **Scientific Truth** is external.

These are highly distinct from one another because one is more internal than the other. In any person, Intellectual Truth (which is internal or at their innermost core) does not belong to the person but is the Lord's presence with them. From there, the Lord flows into the **Rational** part, where truth first appears as if it belongs to the person; from there, it flows into the **Scientific** (external) knowledge. 

From this, it is clear that a person can never think from Intellectual Truth as if it were their own. Instead, they think from Rational and Scientific Truth, because these appear to be their own. Only the Lord, when He lived in the world, thought from Intellectual Truth, because that was His own Divinity joined to Good—or His Divine Spiritual joined to His Divine Celestial. In this, the Lord was distinct from every other person. Thinking from the Divine as if from Himself is never possible for a human, nor can it exist in a human; it was possible only in Him who was conceived by Jehovah. Because He thought from Intellectual Truth—that is, from the love or affection for Intellectual Truth—He also desired the Rational part from it. This is why it is said here that Sarai, Abram's wife (the affection for intellectual truth), took Hagar the Egyptian and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife. The remaining secrets contained here are beyond the grasp...

These states are stored away for the use of his life after death.

In the next life, all the states of a person's life return successively, and they are then tempered by the states of good and truth with which he was gifted by the Lord. Therefore, the more "Remains" he received during his physical life—that is, the more good and truth—the more pleasant and beautiful his other states appear when they return. Anyone can see that this is the case if they consider it: when a person is born, he has not a bit of good from himself, but is entirely defiled by hereditary evil. Yet all good flows in—such as the love he feels for parents, nurses, and his peers—and this comes from innocence. These are the things that flow from the Lord through the "Heaven of innocence and peace," which is the innermost heaven; thus, while a person is an infant, he is imbued with them.

Later, as he grows up, this infantile state of goodness, innocence, and peace gradually recedes. To the extent that he is introduced into the world, he enters into its pleasures and desires, and thus into evils. As this happens, the celestial or good states of his childhood begin to disappear. Nevertheless, they remain, and it is through them that the states the person later adopts and acquires for himself are tempered. Without these "Remains," a person could never be truly human; for the states of desire or evil, if not balanced by states of affection for good, would be more atrocious than those of any animal.

These states of good are what are called "Remains," gifted by the Lord and implanted in the person’s character, even when the person is unaware of it. In the following stage of life, he is also gifted with new states, but these are states not so much of good but of truth; for as he grows up, he is imbued with truths, and these are similarly stored away in his interior man. Through these "Remains" consisting of truth—which are born from the influx of spiritual things from the Lord—a person is able to think, to understand what is good and true in civil and moral life, and even to receive spiritual truth (or faith). But he can only do this through the "Remains of good" that he received in infancy. A person is entirely unaware that these "Remains" exist and that they are stored in his interior rational mind, because...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

Only love is what truly lives; all other objects are merely derivations from it, drawing their life from their purpose <note>original: "fine"; referring to the "end" or goal of an action</note>. Anyone can see what kind of life they have simply by exploring what kind of purpose they have. I do not mean the countless intermediate goals—for there are as many of these as there are intentions and almost as many as there are judgments and conclusions of thought—but rather the principal purpose, which the others are derived from or toward which they tend. Let a person explore the purpose they prefer above all others, and in comparison to which all others are as nothing. If they have themselves and the world as their purpose, they should know that their life is infernal <term>infernal: relating to or characteristic of hell; focused on self-interest</term>. If, however, they have the good of their neighbor, the common good, the Kingdom of the Lord, and above all the Lord Himself as their purpose, they should know that their life is heavenly.

**1910.** **And she conceived**, which signifies the first life of the **Rational** mind <term>Rational: the part of the human mind that mediates between the spiritual and the natural</term>. This is established from the meaning of "conception," which refers to the first stage of life. As for the Rational mind, it receives its life (as previously stated) from the life of the **Internal man** flowing into the affection for knowledge and science in the **Exterior** man. This affection for knowledge and science provides the Rational mind with a sort of body, or rather, it clothes the life of the Internal man just as the body clothes the soul. Knowledge and science function in no other way: a likeness of soul and body exists in every single thing within a person—in every single affection and every single thought. For there is nothing, however simple it appears, that is not a composite and does not exist from something prior to itself.

**1911.** **And she saw that she had conceived, and her mistress was despised in her eyes**, which signifies that this Rational mind, in its initial conception, would look down upon the very truth that is joined to goodness. This is established from the meaning of the "Mistress" (or **Sarai**), which represents truth joined to goodness. The Rational mind, when first conceived, cannot acknowledge intellectual or spiritual truth as being true. This is because it is still clinging to many fallacies derived from worldly sciences and nature, as well as appearances taken from the literal sense of the Word <note>original: "Verbi"; the Bible</note> which are not actually true.

For example:
*   It is an intellectual truth that all life comes from the Lord. The Rational mind, when first conceived, does not grasp this. It thinks that if it did not live from itself, it would have no life at all; indeed, it becomes indignant if told otherwise, as has often been observed among spirits who cling to the fallacies of the senses.
*   It is an intellectual truth that all goodness and truth come from the Lord. The newly conceived Rational mind does not grasp this either, because it feels as though they come from itself. It thinks that if they were not from itself, it could not think anything good or true, much less do anything; it fears that if they came from another, it would become passive and have to wait continually for an **influx** <term>influx: the spiritual flow of life, goodness, and truth from God into the human mind</term>.
*   It is an intellectual truth that nothing but good comes from the Lord, and not even a tiny bit of evil. The newly conceived Rational mind does not believe this either. It thinks that because the Lord rules over every single thing, evil must also come from Him; and because He is omnipotent and omnipresent and is Goodness itself, yet does not remove the punishments of the evil in hell, it thinks He must desire the "evil of punishment"—when in fact He does no evil to anyone, nor does He wish for anyone to be punished.
*   It is an intellectual truth that the heavenly person has a perception of goodness and truth from the Lord. The first Rational mind either denies this perception entirely or thinks that if it perceived from another and not from itself, it would be like an inanimate object with no life of its own.

Indeed, the more the Rational mind thinks based on scientific facts originating from the senses, and the more it relies on philosophy, the less it grasps these and other intellectual truths. This is because the fallacies arising from those sources are wrapped in even thicker shadows. This is why learned people often believe less than others do. When the Rational mind first...

# GENESIS

Once the rational mind is conceived in this way, it is evident that it holds its mistress in low regard—that is, it undervalues **Intellectual Truth** <term>Intellectual Truth: pure spiritual truth that exists above human reasoning</term>. Intellectual truth is not recognized until fallacies and appearances have been dispelled. These shadows are never dispelled as long as a person reasons about truths based only on sensory data and mere scientific facts. Instead, they are dispelled only when a person believes with a simple heart that something is true because the Lord has said it. Only then do the shadows of fallacies vanish, and nothing remains that the person cannot grasp. 

In the Lord, however, there were no fallacies. Yet, when His first **Rational** mind <term>Rational: the "middle" part of the mind that connects our higher spiritual self with our lower worldly knowledge</term> was first conceived, there were appearances of truth that were not truths in themselves (as was shown in section 1661). Consequently, His rational mind in its first conception undervalued intellectual truth. Gradually, however, as His **Divine Rational** was formed, the clouds of appearances were dispelled, and intellectual truths appeared to Him in their own light. This transition was represented and signified by the story of Ishmael being cast out of the house once Isaac had grown up. As will be clear from section 1914, it was not that the Lord Himself undervalued intellectual truth, but rather that He perceived and saw that His new rational mind was doing so.

**1912.** ***Verse 5. And Sarai said to Abram, "My wrong be upon you! I gave my maid into your arms <note>original: "sinum tuum"; literally "your bosom"</note>, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became small in her eyes. May Jehovah judge between me and you."*** 

*   **Sarai said to Abram** signifies that the affection for truth perceived it this way. 
*   **My wrong be upon you; I gave my maid into your arms** signifies that she did not want to take the blame upon herself. 
*   **And she saw that she had conceived** signifies the first life of the Rational mind. 
*   **And I am small in her eyes** signifies (as before) that this Rational mind, in its initial conception, undervalued truth when it was joined to goodness. 
*   **May Jehovah judge between me and you** signifies the Lord’s indignation.

**1913.** That **Sarai said to Abram** signifies that the affection for truth perceived it this way is established from the meaning of Sarai as the "affection for truth" (see section 1904). Furthermore, "to say" in the internal sense means "to perceive," as stated above in section 1898, where the same words appear.

**1914.** That **"My wrong be upon you; I gave my maid into your arms"** signifies that she did not want to take the blame upon herself is clear without further explanation. In the internal sense, these words imply that the Lord perceived that His first rational mind was of such a nature that it would undervalue intellectual truth, and for this reason, He rebuked it. The Lord thought from Intellectual Truth (as mentioned in section 1904); because this level of thought is above the rational, He was able to perceive and see the nature of that Rational mind—specifically, that it held Intellectual Truth in low regard. 

The fact that the Lord could perceive and see from within the nature of His own new rational mind is evident because the **Internal** <term>Internal: the highest part of the human spirit, closest to the Divine</term> can perceive what exists in the **External** (or, to put it another way, the higher can see what is in the lower, but not the reverse). Even people who possess a conscience are able to do this; when something contrary to the truth of their conscience flows into their thoughts or their intentions, they not only notice it but also condemn it—it even causes them pain to realize they have such thoughts. Those who have "perception" can do this even more clearly, for perception is a more internal faculty of the Rational mind. How much more, then, could the Lord do this, who possessed Divine celestial Perception and acted from the affection...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

The Lord’s thought came from **Intellectual Truth** <term>Intellectual Truth: pure spiritual truth that exists above human reasoning</term>, which is higher than the rational mind. Therefore, He could not help but feel indignation. He knew that no evil or falsity came from Himself, and that out of a profound love for Truth, He had worked tirelessly to ensure His rational mind was pure. It is clear from this that the Lord did not undervalue Intellectual Truth; rather, He perceived that the first stage of His **Rational** mind <term>Rational: the "middle" part of the mind that connects our higher spiritual self with our lower worldly knowledge</term> was undervaluing it.

What it means to "think from Intellectual Truth" is difficult to explain in a way that can be easily grasped. This is because no one has ever thought from that specific affection and truth except for the Lord. Anyone who thinks from this level is above the angelic heavens. Even the angels of the Third Heaven <note>The highest of the three heavens in Swedenborg's theology</note> do not think from Intellectual Truth itself, but from the interior part of the rational mind. 

However, as the Lord united His Human Essence with the Divine Essence, He began to think from **Divine Good** itself—that is, from **Jehovah**. The fathers of the Most Ancient Church <note>original: "Antiquissimae Ecclesiae"; the spiritual era before the Great Flood</note>, who possessed direct "perception," thought from the inner rational mind. The fathers of the Ancient Church <note>original: "Ecclesiae Antiquae"; the era after the Great Flood</note>, who did not have perception but had "conscience," thought from the outer or natural rational mind. 

However, all those who lack a conscience never think from the rational mind at all. They do not truly possess a rational mind, even though it may appear that they do; instead, they think from their sensory and physical nature. The reason for this is that a truly rational person is one who thinks in alignment with the good and truth of faith. No one who thinks in opposition to these can be called rational. Those who dwell on evil and falsity are actually mentally confused <note>original: "insaniunt cogitatione"; literally "are insane in thought"</note> in their reasoning, so the term "rational" can never be applied to them.

**1915.** *And she saw that she had conceived.* This signifies the first life of the rational mind. This is evident from the meaning of "conception" as the first spark of life, as discussed previously in section 1910.

**1916.** *I am despised in her eyes.* This signifies that this rational mind, in its initial conception, would undervalue truth itself when it is joined to good. This is clear from what was discussed just above in sections 1911 and 1914.

**1917.** *May Jehovah judge between me and you.* This signifies the Lord’s indignation. This follows from what was just said and requires no further explanation. How these states progress cannot be understood except by those who have been through the struggles of spiritual **temptations**. In these temptations, a person feels laid waste and desolate; they feel despair, which leads to grief and indignation, along with other painful internal emotions. These feelings alternate depending on the states of evil and falsity stirred up by evil spirits. 

Demonic spirits desire nothing more than to find some falsity in a person. In fact, it is common for them to project a falsity onto someone and then immediately accuse them of it. This explains the Lord's great indignation, for in His first rational mind there was no falsity, only "appearances of truth" that were not true in themselves (as discussed in section 1661 and at the end of section 1911).

**1918. Verse 6.** *And Abram said to Sarai, "Behold, your maid is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes." And Sarai humbled her, and she fled from her face.*

*Abram said to Sarai* signifies perception.
*Behold, your maid is in your hand* signifies that this newly conceived rational mind is under the power of truth joined to good.
*Do to her what is good in your eyes* signifies authority or control.
*And Sarai humbled her* signifies subjugation.
*And she fled from her face* signifies the indignation of this first-conceived rational mind.

# GENESIS

1919. **"Abram said to Sarai"** signifies perception. This is clear from what was stated above in section 1898: the Lord’s **perception** <term>Perception: a direct, intuitive spiritual realization of truth</term> was represented and signified here by what Abram said to Sarai. However, the **thought** that follows from perception is signified by what Sarai said to Abram. Thought comes from perception; those who possess perception do not think from any other source.

Nevertheless, perception is something different from thought. To illustrate this difference, consider **Conscience**. Conscience is a kind of general "dictate" from the Lord that flows in through the Heavens. It presents itself in a person’s inner rational mind like a cloud—a cloud made of appearances and illusions regarding the truths and goods of faith. **Thought**, however, is distinct from conscience, yet it flows from it. Those who have a conscience think and speak according to it. Their thought is essentially an explanation of what is in their conscience—the partitioning of those inner feelings into ideas and then into words. 

This is why people with a conscience are guided by the Lord to think well of their neighbor and are kept from thinking evil. Consequently, conscience can only exist in those who love their neighbor as themselves and think well of the truths of faith. From this, we can see the difference between conscience and thought, which helps us understand the difference between perception and thought.

The Lord's perception came directly from **Jehovah**, and thus from **Divine Good**. His thought, however, came from **Intellectual Truth** and its affection, as stated previously in sections 1904 and 1914. No idea—not even an angelic one—can grasp the Lord’s Divine perception, so it cannot truly be described. Even the perception of angels (discussed in sections 1384–1395) is almost nothing compared to the perception the Lord had. 

Because the Lord’s perception was Divine, it encompassed everything in the Heavens. And because it encompassed everything in the Heavens, it encompassed everything on earth. Such is the order, connection, and "influx" of the universe that whoever perceives the higher things also perceives the lower. 

But after the Lord’s **Human Essence** was united to His **Divine Essence** (becoming one with Jehovah), the Lord was then above even what is called perception. He was above the order that exists in the Heavens and on earth. He is Jehovah, the source of all order. Indeed, it can be said that Jehovah is **Order** itself. From Himself, He rules that order—not just "in general," as many people assume, but in the most specific details. 

The "Universal" is built from these most specific details. To speak of a "universal" while separating it from individual details would be like speaking of a whole that has no parts—something that exists but contains nothing. Therefore, it is entirely false—a mere **conceptual entity** <note>original: "ens rationis"; a philosophical term for something that exists only in the mind, not in reality</note>—to say that the Lord's **Providence** is "universal" but not "particular." To provide for and rule in general without providing for and ruling the smallest details is to provide for and rule absolutely nothing. This is philosophically true, yet it is surprising that even highly sophisticated philosophers understand and think about this incorrectly.

That **Rational mind** <term>original Latin: Rationale; the faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual insight and worldly knowledge</term> which was in the womb; however, once it was born and grew up, it is represented by Ishmael, who will be discussed in the following verses. That the Lord had power over the Rational mind within Him, and that He subjugated it by His own power, will become clear from what is about to be said.

1921. **"Do to her what is good in your eyes,"** which signifies command or dominion, is evident without further explanation. In the **internal sense** <term>the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Word hidden beneath the literal text</term>, these words represent and signify that the Lord, by His own power, defeated, subjugated, and expelled the evil which had insinuated itself into this first Rational mind from His inheritance. 

As previously stated, the Rational mind was conceived from the **Internal Man** (who was Jehovah) as the father, and born from the **External Man** as the mother. Whatever comes from the External Man brings with it an inheritance, including evil. This was what the Lord, by His own power, conquered, subdued, and removed, eventually making it Divine. That this was done by His own power is clear from every detail in this verse: 

*   **"Your maidservant is in your hand"** <note>original: "ancilla tua in manu tua"</note> signifies that the Rational mind was in His power. 
*   **"Do to her what is good in your eyes"** <note>original: "fac ei quod bonum in oculis tuis"</note> signifies His dominion over it. 
*   And finally, **"Sarai humbled her,"** which signifies subjugation. 

These words were spoken to Sarai, who represents **Intellectual Truth**. This truth belonged to the Lord Himself, and it was the source of His thought (as mentioned in sections 1904 and 1914) and His authority over both the Rational mind and the **Natural mind** (which belonged to the External Man). 

One who thinks from Intellectual Truth and perceives from **Divine Good** (which was also His because it belonged to the Father—for He had no other soul) cannot act in any way other than by His own power. Therefore, because He tamed and cast out inherited evil by His own power, He also united His **Human Nature** <note>original: Humana Essentia</note> to the **Divine Nature** by His own power; one is the necessary consequence of the other. 

He who is conceived by Jehovah has no other "Internal"—that is, no other soul—than Jehovah. Therefore, regarding His very life, He was Jehovah Himself. Jehovah, or the Divine Nature, cannot be divided like the soul of a human father. When a human child is conceived, the further that child departs from the likeness of the father, the more distant they become from him; this distance increases as they age, which is why a father’s love for his children often diminishes as they grow older. 

It was different for the Lord. As He grew, His Human Nature did not move away, but drew continually closer until there was a perfect union. From this, it is clear that He is one and the same with Jehovah the Father, as He Himself clearly teaches in John 14:6, 8, 9, 10, 11.

Here is described the indignation of the Rational mind against Intellectual Truth, because Intellectual Truth—or the Lord—wished to humble or subjugate it. When the Rational mind rises up against the Intellectual, an internal conflict arises, and indignation is felt by the part that is being subdued. 1925. That "the Angel of Jehovah found her" signifies the thought of the internal man—specifically within the Lord—can be established from the representation and meaning of the "Angel of Jehovah." The "Angel of Jehovah" is mentioned several times in **the Word** <note>the Word: A term used here to refer to the Holy Scriptures</note>, and whenever it is used in a positive sense, it represents and signifies something essential within the Lord and from the Lord. He fills them with the Divine and puts their own identity to sleep, so that they do not know at that time but that they are Jehovah themselves. In this way, the Divine of Jehovah, which is in the highest realms, flows down into the lowest part of nature where man exists in terms of sight and hearing. > "The Angel of *Jehovah* <note>original Latin: *Angelus Jehovae*</note> went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, 'I made you go up out of Egypt, and have brought you into the land which I swore to your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you'" (Judges 2:1).

That **the Word** <note>the Word: A term used here to refer to the Holy Scriptures</note> comes from the Lord is evident from many places, including Matthew: 

> "That it might be fulfilled which was *spoken by the Lord through the Prophet*, saying, 'Behold, a virgin shall be with child and shall bear a son'" (Matthew 1:22, 23).

In these instances, "Angel" signifies something essential within and from the Lord—as previously mentioned. In this specific context, it signifies the Lord’s **interior thought** <term>original: *interior cogitatio*; the deeper, more spiritual level of the Lord’s developing human mind</term>. This is why the Angel in this chapter is also called "Jehovah" and "God," as seen in verse 13: "And *Hagar* called the name of *Jehovah* who spoke to her, 'You are God who sees me.'"

Here, the "twelve Angels" signify the same thing as the "twelve tribes"—namely, all the components of faith, and thus the Lord, from whom faith and all its components originate. In the same book: "I saw an *Angel* flying in the midst of heaven, having the eternal Gospel" (Revelation 14:6). Here, the "Angel" signifies the Gospel, which belongs to the Lord alone. 

In Isaiah: "The *Angel of His presence* <note>original Latin: *Angelus facierum*; literally "the Angel of His faces"</note> saved us; in His love and in His pity He redeemed them, and He bore them and carried them all the days of old" (Isaiah 63:9). Here, the "Angel of His presence" refers to the Lord's mercy toward the entire human race in redeeming them. Similarly, when Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph: "The *Angel* who redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads" (Genesis 48:16). Here too, **Redemption**—which is the Lord's work—is signified by the "Angel." 

In Malachi: "The Lord whom you seek shall suddenly come to His temple, even the *Angel of the covenant* <note>original Latin: *Angelus foederis*</note> whom you desire" (Malachi 3:1). It is clearly evident here that the Lord is signified by the "Angel," as He is called the "Angel of the covenant" because of His coming. It is even more clearly shown that the "Angel" signifies the Lord in Exodus: 

> "Behold, I send an *Angel* before you, to keep you in the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared... he will not pardon your transgressions, for my name is in him" (Exodus 23:20, 21). 

From these examples, it is now certain that "Angel" in the Word refers to the Lord. However, exactly *what* aspect of the Lord is intended becomes clear from the sequence of the **internal sense** <term>original: *sensu interno*; the deeper spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories</term>.

**1927.** *At a fountain of waters in the wilderness:* that this signifies natural truth which has not yet attained life, is evident from the significance of a "fountain of waters" as truth, and from the significance of the "wilderness" as that which has little vitality as yet. What is meant by "truth not yet attaining life" will be clear from what is about to be said.

**1928.** *At the fountain on the way to Shur:* that this signifies that this truth originated from those things that proceed from scientific knowledge <term>original: *scientificis*; factual knowledge or external information gathered through the senses</term> is evident from the significance of a "fountain," a "way," and "Shur." A fountain, as stated, signifies truth; a "way" signifies that which leads to truth and proceeds from truth (as shown before in number 627); and "Shur" signifies a type of scientific knowledge that is still, as it were, in a wilderness—that is, knowledge that has not yet attained life. 

Truths derived from scientific knowledge are said to "attain life" when they join or associate themselves with truths into which the celestial quality of love flows; the very life of truth comes from that source. There are conjunctions of things (and thus of truths) just like the societies in Heaven, to which they also correspond; for a human being, in their inner self, is a miniature heaven. Things or truths that are not joined according to the form of heavenly societies have not yet attained life, because the celestial love from the Lord cannot flow into them properly until then. They first receive life when the form is similar on both sides—that is, when a person's "miniature heaven" is a corresponding image of the "Greatest Heaven" <note>the Greatest Heaven: The collective body of all angels, viewed as a single human form</note>. Before this happens, no one can be called a "heavenly person" <note>original: *coelestis homo*</note>. 

The Lord, who would govern the entire universe of heaven from Himself, brought the truths and goods in His External Man (or in His Human Essence) into such an order while He was in the world. But because He perceived that His Rationality, as it was first conceived, was not of that quality (as mentioned above regarding verses 4 and 5), He thought about the cause and perceived that natural truths arising from scientific knowledge had not yet attained life—that is, they had not yet been brought into that heavenly order. 

Furthermore, the truths of faith never have any life unless a person lives in **charity**. All the truths of faith flow from charity and are contained within charity; when they are in and from charity, they have life. Life is found in charity, and never in truths without charity. That "Shur" signifies scientific knowledge that has not yet attained life is evident from its meaning; for Shur was a wilderness not far from the Red Sea <note>original: *mari Suph*</note>, and thus...

**1929.** It can never be seen from the literal sense of the text—especially since it is written as a historical narrative—that these things are signified by the "Angel of Jehovah" finding Hagar at a fountain of waters in the wilderness, on the way to Shur. Angels have no concept of Hagar, nor of a fountain of water, a wilderness, a road, or Shur. These specific physical details do not reach them; they vanish at the very threshold of the spiritual world. Instead, the Angels understand what Hagar, the fountain, the wilderness, the road, and Shur signify. From that understanding, they form heavenly ideas and thus perceive the Word of the Lord; for the internal, spiritual sense is what the Word is to them.

**1931.** That "He said, Hagar, Sarai’s maid," signifies seeking information is clear from the flow of the text <note>original: *serie*</note>, as the Angel calls to Hagar as if to be informed. In the Word <note>the Word: The Holy Scriptures</note>, it is common for Jehovah to question a person and for the person to answer, even though Jehovah already knew everything beforehand—not only the actions but also the causes and the intended goals <note>original: *fines*</note>, including the most minute and innermost details. 

However, because humans do not know this and often believe that no one can ever know what they do in secret or what they think, the interaction is described according to the person’s own belief. Yet the truth is that general spirits perceive a person's thoughts better than the person does themselves. Angelic spirits perceive even more interior levels of thought, and Angels perceive even more deeply: the underlying causes and purposes of which the person knows very little. I have been allowed to know this from many years of continuous experience. Since spirits and Angels perceive these things, how much more does the Lord (or Jehovah), who is Infinite and provides the power of perception to everyone else?

**1933.** *And she said, "From the face of my mistress Sarai I flee."* That this signifies her response and indignation is clear from what has been said previously. **1934.** *Verse 9. "And humble yourself under her hands" signifies that He should compel Himself to remain under its power.

**1935.** "The Angel of Jehovah said." That this signifies the response of the Lord's Interior Man is established from the meaning of the "Angel of Jehovah," which is the Lord's interior thought (as discussed above in n. 1925). Because it is a thought, it is also a response. The Lord's interior thought came from the affection for intellectual truth, and this affection came from Divine Good itself. Such a thought, as previously mentioned, never occurs in any other human, nor can it. 

In a human being, there is also an interior thought that flows from the Lord through the internal man into the interior rational mind; this occurs in those who have a conscience. This is evident because such people can perceive the evil and falsity in their external self which fights against the good and truth in their interior self. However, this human thought is much lower and cannot be compared in any way with the Lord’s thought, which came from the affection of intellectual truth and was uniquely His own. Those who do not have a conscience cannot have interior thought, and therefore no such struggle exists within them. This is because their rational mind acts as one with their sensual and bodily desires. Even though good and truth continually flow into them from the Lord, they do not perceive it because they immediately extinguish and suffocate it; as a result, they do not believe any truth of faith.

**1936.** "Return to your mistress." That this signifies that He realized He should not trust in Himself, but in interior Truth and its affection, is clear from the meaning of "Mistress," which is the affection for interior truth. However, specifically what is signified by "Sarai," "Sarai the wife," and "Sarai the mistress" cannot be fully described because these concepts cannot be grasped by any human idea; as stated before, they are even above the understanding of angels. 

Here it is simply indicated how the Lord thought about the "appearances" <note>intellectual concepts that seem true but are not yet fully Divine</note> that first occupied His Rational mind—namely, that these appearances were not to be trusted, but only Divine Truths, however incredible they might appear to that Rational mind. This is the case with all Divine Truths: if the Rational mind is consulted about them, they can never be believed, for they surpass its entire capacity. 

For example: the fact that no human, spirit, or angel lives from themselves, but the Lord alone; and that the life of a human, spirit, or angel is only an appearance of life within them. This idea contradicts the Rational mind, which judges based on fallacies; yet it must be believed because it is the Truth. It is also a Divine Truth that there are infinite things <note>original: *indefinita*</note> in every single word of the Bible <note>original: *Verbi*; "the Word"</note>, which appears so simple and crude to humans. Indeed, there is more contained within it than in the whole of heaven, and the secrets <note>original: *arcana*</note> within it can be presented by the Lord before the Angels with perpetual variety forever. This is so incredible to the Rational mind...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

...rational mind, so that it never wishes to give any credit to it, but it is nonetheless True. Divine Truth is this: that no one is ever rewarded in the afterlife for good deeds if they have claimed merit <note>original: *meritum*; the belief that one deserves a reward from God for their own actions</note> for them, or if they have done them for the sake of personal gain, honor, or reputation. Furthermore, no one is ever punished for bad deeds if they acted from a truly good purpose; it is the "ends" <note>original: *fines*; the underlying goals or intentions</note> that are looked upon, and the deeds are judged from those intentions. These principles also cannot be believed by the Rational mind; but because they are true, the rational mind—which draws conclusions from external things rather than internal ones—should not be trusted. 

Divine Truth also dictates that whoever desires the least joy in the afterlife receives the greatest from the Lord, and whoever desires the most receives the least. Likewise, in heavenly joy, there is never any sense of being superior to another; for to the degree that one seeks superiority, they lack internal joy. Furthermore, in heavenly glory, there is not even a trace of worldly glory. These ideas are also repugnant to the Rational mind, yet they must still be believed because they are true. It is also Divine Truth that a person becomes wiser the more they believe that nothing of wisdom comes from themselves, and more insane the more they believe it comes from themselves (and thus the more they attribute prudence to themselves). The Rational mind denies this too, because it thinks that whatever does not come from itself is nothing. There are countless such examples. From these few instances, it can be established that the Rational mind is not to be trusted, for it dwells in fallacies and appearances. Therefore, it rejects truths when they are stripped of those fallacies and appearances—especially when the mind is immersed in self-love, its lusts, its reasonings, and its false principles concerning faith. See also what was cited above in number 1911.

**1937.** *That "humble yourself under her hands"* signifies that he should compel himself to be under her power is clear without further explanation. To "humble oneself" is expressed in the original language <note>Hebrew</note> by a word that signifies *to afflict*. That "to afflict oneself" in the internal sense means to "compel oneself" can be established from many places in the Word <note>The Bible</note>, as will be discussed regarding its meaning in what follows. 

The fact that a person must compel themselves to do good, to obey what the Lord has commanded, and to speak truths—which is to humble oneself under the Lord’s hands, or to submit oneself under the power of Divine good and truth—involves more secrets <note>original: *arcana*; hidden spiritual realities</note> than can be explained in a few words. There are certain spirits who, while they lived in the world, adopted the principle that because they heard all good is from the Lord and that man can do no good of himself, they should not compel themselves to do anything. Instead, they let themselves go, thinking every effort would be useless because the truth is as it is. Therefore, they waited for an immediate "influx" <note>a direct spiritual flow or inspiration</note> into their will’s endeavor and did not force themselves to do any good. Indeed, they went so far that when some evil crept in, because they felt no resistance from within, they abandoned themselves to it as well, thinking it was permitted. 

But such people are as if they have no "proprium" <note>original: *proprio*; a sense of selfhood or individual identity</note>, so that they have no power of determination. For this reason, they are among the more useless; they allow themselves to be led equally by the evil and the good, and they suffer much from the evil. But those who have compelled themselves against evil and falsity—even though they at first thought this was from themselves or from their own power—were afterwards enlightened to see that their effort was from the Lord (even the very smallest part of that effort). These people, in the afterlife, cannot be led by evil spirits, but are among the happy. From this, it is clear that a person ought to compel himself to do good and speak truth. The secret that lies hidden in this is that, by doing so, a person is gifted by the Lord with a heavenly "proprium."

<meta>This page continues the discussion on why the rational mind must be subordinated to divine truth and the spiritual practice of self-compulsion. It specifically explores how forcing oneself to do good leads to true spiritual freedom.</meta>

# GENESIS

...heavenly state from the Lord. A person’s heavenly *proprium* <note>original: *proprium*; a theological term for one’s sense of self or what belongs to the self</note> is formed within the effort of their thought. If a person does not seem to compel themselves, yet never actually performs this self-compulsion, they can never obtain this state. To make it clear how this works: in every instance of compelling oneself toward what is good, there is a certain hidden freedom. This freedom is not clearly perceived while the compulsion is happening, but it is nonetheless present. 

Consider someone who is willing to face the dangers of death for a specific goal, or someone who is willing to endure bodily pain for the sake of their health. There is a voluntary—and therefore a certain free—element in these actions, even though the dangers and pains take away the person's perception of being "free" while they are enduring them. 

It is the same for those who compel themselves toward what is good. Inwardly, there is a voluntary and free element from which and for the sake of which they compel themselves—namely, out of obedience to what the Lord has commanded, and for the salvation of their soul after death. Within these motives, there is something even more internal that the person does not yet recognize: a desire for the Lord’s Kingdom, and even for the Lord Himself. 

This happens most especially during temptations <note>original: *tentationibus*; spiritual trials or inner conflicts between good and evil</note>. When a person compels himself against the evil and falsity that are infused and suggested by evil spirits, there is more freedom then than in any state outside of temptation, though the person cannot realize it at the time. It is an internal freedom from which he wills to subjugate evil. This freedom is strong enough to match the force and strength of the evil attacking him; otherwise, he would never be able to fight. 

This freedom is from the Lord, who instills it into the person's conscience. Through it, the Lord enables the person to overcome evil as if by their own power. Through this freedom, the person receives a *proprium* in which the Lord can work what is good. Without a *proprium* acquired through freedom—that is, a *proprium* given as a gift by the Lord—no one can ever be reformed. This is because they cannot receive a new will, which is what conscience is. The freedom granted in this way is the very foundation <note>original: *planum*; literally a "plane" or level surface</note> into which the influx <note>original: *influxus*; the flowing in of spiritual life</note> of good and truth from the Lord can enter. This is why those who do not resist during temptations from that voluntary or free state eventually succumb to them.

A person's very life exists in all that is free, because freedom is rooted in their love. Whatever a person does from love appears "free" to them. In that specific freedom—when a person compels himself against evil and falsity in order to do good—there is a heavenly love which the Lord then instills, and through which He creates the person's new *proprium*. Therefore, the Lord wills that this should appear to the person as their own, even though it is not truly theirs. 

This *proprium*, which is received through what appears to be compulsion during physical life, the Lord fills with infinite delights and happiness in the afterlife. These individuals are also enlightened by degrees; indeed, they are eventually confirmed in the truth that they did not compel themselves in the slightest, but that even the smallest efforts of their will were from the Lord. It only appeared to be from themselves so that a new will <note>original: *voluntarium*; the voluntary faculty or the "will"</note> could be given to them by the Lord as if it were theirs, and thus the life of heavenly love could be made their own. 

For the Lord wishes to communicate what is His to everyone—that which is heavenly—so that it appears to be within them, even though it is not theirs. Angels possess such a *proprium*; and to the extent they stay in the truth that all good and truth come from the Lord, they remain in the joy and happiness of that *proprium*. 

However, those who despise and reject all good and truth, and who refuse to believe anything that contradicts their own desires and reasonings, cannot compel themselves. Consequently, they cannot receive this *proprium* of conscience or a new will. From what has been said, it is also clear that "compelling oneself" is not the same as "being compelled" by an outside force; for no good ever comes from being forced.
