1938. **Verse 10: *And the Angel of Jehovah said to her, "In multiplying, I will multiply your seed, and it shall not be numbered for its multitude."***
**"The Angel of Jehovah said"** signifies the thought of the internal man.
**"In multiplying, I will multiply your seed"** signifies the fruitfulness of the **rational man** <note>original: *Rationalis*; the part of the human mind that balances logic and spiritual insight</note> when it submits to the power of intellectual truth joined to good.
**"It shall not be numbered for its multitude"** signifies multiplication beyond measure.

1939. That **"The Angel of Jehovah said"** signifies the thought of the internal man is evident from the previous verse, where the same words were used.

1940. That **"In multiplying, I will multiply your seed"** signifies the fruitfulness of the rational man when it submits to the power of the internal man joined to good, is clear from the meaning of "seed." Seed represents love and faith (as seen previously in sections 1025, 1447, and 1610). In this specific context, "multiplying the seed" signifies the fruitfulness of heavenly love within the rational mind when that mind submits itself to interior or Divine truth.

Generally, "multiplication" refers to truths, while "fruitfulness" refers to goods (as shown in sections 43, 55, 913, and 983). However, since this passage concerns the Lord, "multiplication" signifies "fruitfulness" <note>original: *fructificatio*; the spiritual process of good producing more good, like a plant bearing fruit</note>. This is because every truth in His rational mind became good—and therefore Divine—which is what is being described here. It is different for a regular human: their rational mind is formed from truth or an affection for truth, and that affection is the "good" from which they act.

To understand how multiplication and fruitfulness work in a person's rational mind, one must understand **influx** <note>original: *Influxus*; the spiritual process of life and wisdom flowing from God into the human mind</note>. In general, every person has three levels:
1.  The **Internal Man**: This is the innermost part, the very thing that makes us human and distinguishes us from animals (who lack this innermost level). It acts as a gate or entrance for the Lord—specifically for His heavenly and spiritual gifts—to enter into a person. What happens at this level cannot be fully grasped by the person, because it is above the rational mind where our conscious thought takes place.
2.  The **Rational Man**: This is the middle level, which is subject to the internal man and feels like it belongs to the person themselves. Heavenly love and faith flow from the Lord into this level through the internal man.
3.  The **External Man**: From the rational level, these gifts flow into the "scientifics" <note>original: *scientifica*; the facts, data, and memories we acquire through the senses</note> belonging to the external man.

However, these incoming gifts are received according to each person’s state. Unless the rational mind submits to the Lord's goodness and truth, it either chokes, rejects, or perverts what flows in. This is especially true when those gifts reach the sensory facts of the memory. This is why the "seed" falls either on the path, on rocky ground, or among thorns, as the Lord teaches in Matthew 13:3–7, Mark 4:3–7, and Luke 8:5–7. But when the rational mind submits and trusts in the Lord—that is, in His Word—it becomes like good soil where the seed falls and bears much fruit.

# GENESIS

1941. **"And it shall not be numbered for its multitude"** <note>original: *Et non numerabitur præ multitudine*</note>—that this signifies multiplication into infinity is clear without further explanation. This phrase signifies Truth, which grows into a great multitude from "Good" <note>the spiritual impulse of love and kindness</note>. Because everything regarding the Lord—who is the subject of the internal sense here—is Divine and Infinite, it cannot be fully expressed in words. Therefore, to get some idea of how Truth multiplies from Good, we must speak of how it happens in a human being. 

In a person who is in "Good" (that is, someone living in love and charity), the seed from the Lord becomes so fruitful and multiplies so much that it cannot be numbered. This is not so visible while they live in the body, but in the afterlife, the growth is incredible. As long as a person lives in the body, the "seed" is in the "soil" of the physical self, surrounded by tangled and dense things like worldly facts <note>original: *scientitica*; scientific or external knowledge</note>, pleasures, and the cares and anxieties of life. But when these are stripped away—which happens when one passes into the next life—the seed is set free. It grows just as a tree seed grows when it rises out of the ground: it becomes a shrub, then a large tree, and eventually multiplies into a garden of trees. All knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom—along with their joys and happiness—multiply in this way and grow forever from a tiny seed. This is what the Lord teaches regarding the mustard seed in Matthew 13:31. This can be clearly seen from the intelligence and wisdom of the Angels, which was beyond description even when they were still human beings.

1942. **Verse 11: *And the Angel of Jehovah said to her, "Behold, you are pregnant, and shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Ishmael, because Jehovah has heard your affliction."***
**"The Angel of Jehovah said to her"** signifies the thought of the Interior Man.
**"Behold, you are pregnant"** signifies the life of the Rational Man.
**"You shall bear a son"** signifies his truth.
**"And you shall call his name Ishmael"** signifies the state of his life.
**"Because Jehovah has heard your affliction"** signifies the state when he would submit himself.

1943. That **"The Angel of Jehovah said"** signifies the thought of the Interior Man is evident from what was stated above regarding verses 7, 9, and 10.

1944. **"Behold, you are pregnant"** <note>original: *Ecce tu gravida*</note> signifies the life of the Rational Man. This is clear from what was said earlier about his conception and from what follows concerning Ishmael—specifically, that he represents the first stage of the "rational" mind in the Lord. 

Generally, regarding the Rational Man, one should know that the "Rational" is said to receive life, be in the womb, and be born when a person begins to think that the evil and falsity within themselves are contrary to—and work against—what is good and true. This is even more the case when the person desires to remove and subdue those evils. Unless a person can perceive and feel this conflict, they do not yet have a functioning Rational mind, no matter how much they think they do. 

The Rational is the bridge or mediator that unites the Internal man with the External man. In this way, it receives perception from the Lord about what is happening in the External man and brings the External man into obedience. Indeed, it lifts the person up from the physical and worldly things in which they are immersed, making a person truly human. It causes them to look toward heaven (where they are a native citizen) rather than merely toward the earth (where they are only a traveler), and certainly not toward hell. These are the duties of the Rational mind. Therefore, unless a person is capable of such thought, they cannot be said to possess a Rational mind. A person is known to be rational by the life of their actions and functions. Simply reasoning against good and truth—which a person might deny in their heart but knows only because they have heard of it—is not the same as being rational; many people are capable of this who...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

...they rush headlong without restraint into every kind of wickedness. The only difference is that those who believe they possess a **Rational** <note>original: *Rationale*; the faculty of reason</note> mind, but actually do not, speak with a certain outward decorum and act with a simulated honesty. They are held back only by external bonds—specifically, the fear of the law, the loss of profit, or damage to their honor, reputation, or life. If these external bonds were taken away, some would act more insanely than the clinically mad. 

Therefore, no one can be said to possess a truly Rational mind simply because they can reason. Indeed, those who lack a true rational faculty often speak about both sensory experiences and factual knowledge <note>original: *scientificis*; knowledge based on external facts rather than internal wisdom</note> much more skillfully than those who actually possess it. This is clearly seen from evil spirits in the afterlife. Although they were regarded as more rational than others while they lived in the body, once their external bonds are removed (the things that created their polite speech and simulated honesty, as happens to everyone in the afterlife), they are more insane than those who are openly mad in the world. They rush into every kind of wickedness without shame, fear, or horror. 

However, those who were truly Rational while they lived in the world are not like this. When their external bonds are removed, they remain even more sane, for they possessed internal bonds. These are the bonds of **conscience**, through which the Lord kept their thoughts bound to the laws of truth and goodness; these internal bonds were their true rationality.

1945. **"You shall bear a son"** <note>original: *Paries filium*</note>—that this signifies "Truth," specifically the truth belonging to the Rational mind represented by Ishmael, is clear from the meaning of a "Son," which refers to Truth (as discussed previously in sections 264, 489, 491, 533, and 1147). This Truth is described in the following verse.

1946. **"And you shall call his name Ishmael"** <note>original: *Et appellabis nomen ejus Jischmael*</note>—that this signifies the **state of life**. In ancient times, names were given to sons and daughters that signified the state in which the parents—especially the mothers—found themselves when they conceived, were pregnant, or gave birth, or the state the infants were in when born. Thus, names were meaningful. The reason Ishmael received his name is explained here: because "Jehovah heard her affliction," which was the mother's state. What Ishmael represents, however, is described in the next verse.

1947. **"Because Jehovah has heard your affliction"** <note>original: *Quia audivit Jehovah ad afflictionem tuam*</note>—that this signifies the moment one submits themselves is clear from what was said above in section 1937: that to humble and afflict oneself is to submit oneself to the power of the **Internal Man** <note>the spiritual part of the person that receives life from the Lord</note>. This submission was also discussed there, showing that it involves "forcing oneself." In this "forcing of oneself," there is freedom—that is, it is spontaneous and voluntary. This distinguishes "forcing oneself" from "being forced" by others. 

It was also shown that without freedom (or a spontaneous and voluntary will), a person can never be reformed or receive any "heavenly selfhood" <note>original: *proprium cœleste*; a sense of self that is aligned with heaven</note>. Furthermore, in times of **temptation**, there is actually more freedom than outside of temptation, even though it appears otherwise. At such times, freedom becomes stronger in response to the attacks of evils and falsehoods, and it is strengthened by the Lord so that a heavenly selfhood may be given to the person. For this reason, the Lord is most present during temptations. 

The Lord never forces anyone. A person who is forced to think what is true or do what is good is not reformed; instead, they often think even more falsely and desire even more evil. All coercion carries this result, as can be seen from life's experiences and teachings, which show two things: that consciences do not allow themselves to be forced, and that we naturally strive for what is forbidden. Everyone moves from a lack of freedom into **freedom**...

# GENESIS

He desires what is free, for this is the essence of their life. From this, it is clear that nothing is ever pleasing to the Lord unless it comes from freedom—that is, from what is spontaneous or voluntary. For when someone worships the Lord without freedom, they do not worship from anything of their own. Instead, it is something external that moves them; they are moved by compulsion, while their internal being is either absent, resisting, or even contradicting the action. 

When a person is being regenerated, out of the freedom granted by the Lord, they compel themselves. They humble—and indeed "afflict"—the **Rational** <note>original: *Rationale*; the faculty of reason</note> mind so that it may submit. From this, they receive a **heavenly selfhood** <note>original: *proprium cœleste*; a new sense of self granted by the Lord</note>, which is then perfected by the Lord in stages. It becomes more and more free, until it becomes an affection for what is good and, consequently, for what is true. In this state, they find a sense of delight, and within that delight, they find a happiness like that of the Angels. 

This is the **Freedom** <note>original: *Liberum*; the state of being free</note> of which the Lord Himself speaks in the Gospel of John: *"The truth shall make you free... If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed"* (John 8:32, 36). Those who have no **conscience** <note>original: *conscientia*; an internal moral compass</note> are completely ignorant of what this freedom is. They define freedom as whim and the license to think and speak what is false, and to will and do what is evil. They do not compel or humble these impulses, much less "afflict" them. Yet the truth is exactly the opposite, as the Lord also teaches in the same book: *"Everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin"* (John 8:34). 

This "slavish freedom" is received from the hellish spirits present with them, who instill it into them. When people live in the life of these spirits, they are also immersed in their loves and cravings, inspired by an impure and foul delight. Swept away by these impulses as if by a torrent, they imagine themselves to be in freedom. But it is a hellish freedom. The difference between this hellish freedom and heavenly freedom is that the former leads to death and drags them down to hell, while the latter—heavenly freedom—leads to life and raises them to heaven. 

That all true internal worship comes from freedom and not from compulsion (and that without freedom, there is no internal worship) is evident from the Word of God. This is shown by the **spontaneous sacrifices** <note>original: *Sacrificiis*; offerings</note>, the votive offerings, and the peace or thank-offerings—those gifts and oblations mentioned in Numbers 15:3, Deuteronomy 12:15, 16:10–11, 23:24, and elsewhere. As David says: *"With a free-will offering I will sacrifice to You; I will give thanks to Your name, O Jehovah, for it is good"* (Psalm 54:6). 

It is also shown by the **contribution** <note>original: *Thruma*; a Hebrew term for a heave-offering or contribution</note> or collection they were to make for the Tabernacle and the holy garments, of which Moses says: *"Speak to the children of Israel, that they take for Me a contribution; from every man whose heart prompts him willingly, you shall take My contribution"* (Exodus 25:2). And elsewhere: *"Everyone who is of a willing heart shall bring it, a contribution to Jehovah"* (Exodus 35:5). 

Furthermore, the humbling of the rational man—or his "affliction" from freedom, as was mentioned—was also represented by the **Affliction of souls** on feast days. Moses writes: *"It shall be a statute forever to you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls"* (Leviticus 16:29). And again: *"On the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement; it shall be a holy convocation to you, and you shall afflict your souls... for every soul that is not afflicted on that same day shall be cut off from his people"* (Leviticus 23:27, 29). For this reason, **unleavened bread** <note>original: *Atymum*; Greek for bread without yeast</note>, in which there is no leaven, is called the **Bread of Affliction** (Deuteronomy 16:3). 

Regarding this affliction, David says: *"Jehovah, who shall sojourn in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain? He who walks uprightly and works righteousness... who swears to afflict himself and does not change"* (Psalm 15:1, 2, 4). This "affliction" is the taming and subjugation of the evils and falsehoods rising up from the **External man** <note>original: *Externus homo*; the outward self or personality</note>...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

From what has been said, it can be seen that his **Rational** <note>original: *Rationalem*; the faculty of reason</note> mind is not formed by forcing oneself into poverty and misery, or by abandoning the pleasures of the body. Evil is not tamed or subdued by such methods; in fact, sometimes another evil is stirred up by them—specifically, a sense of self-merit for having given things up. Furthermore, this interferes with a person’s freedom, which is the only "soil" in which the good and truth of faith can truly be planted. Regarding "Affliction" also being a form of temptation, see section 1846.

1948. **Verse 12.** *And he will be a wild donkey of a man; his hand will be against everyone, and everyone's hand against him; and he will dwell in the presence of all his brothers.*

"He will be a wild donkey of a man" signifies the **Rational Truth** <note>original: *verum rationale*</note> that is being described. "His hand will be against everyone" signifies that it will fight against everything that is not true. "The hand of all against him" signifies that falsehoods will fight back against it. "He will dwell in the presence of all his brothers" signifies that there will be constant disputes regarding matters of faith, but that he will nonetheless be the victor.

1949. **He will be a wild donkey of a man:** That this signifies Rational Truth, which is being described here, is evident from the meaning of a **wild donkey** <note>original: *onager*</note> as "rational truth." In the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible</note>, horses, riders, mules, and donkeys are mentioned many times. Until now, no one has known that these signify things relating to the intellect, the reason, and factual knowledge. That they have these meanings will be confirmed in many places, by the Lord’s Divine Mercy.

The wild donkey is of the same class—it is a "mule of the wilderness" or a "wild donkey"—and it signifies a person’s **Rational** faculty. It does not mean the Rational faculty in its entirety, but specifically **Rational Truth**. The Rational mind consists of both "Good" and "Truth"—that is, from things belonging to charity and things belonging to faith. It is specifically "Rational Truth" that is signified by the wild donkey. This is what is represented by Ishmael and described in this verse. 

No one would believe that Rational Truth, when separated from **Rational Good** <note>original: *bono rationali*</note>, would be like this; I would not have known it myself if I had not been taught by living experience. Whether you call it "Rational Truth" or "a person whose Rational mind is of that nature," it is the same thing. 

A person whose Rational mind is such that they live only in Truth—even if it is the Truth of faith—without also living in the Good of charity, is exactly like this: they are a morose person, patient with nothing, against everyone, seeing everyone else as being in error, and immediately rebuking, scolding, and punishing. They have no mercy and do not try to adapt themselves or win others over to a better way of thinking. This is because they look at everything through the lens of Truth and nothing through the lens of Good. This is why Ishmael was cast out and later lived in the wilderness, and why his mother found him a wife from the land of Egypt (Genesis 21:9–21). All these details represent someone endowed with such a Rational mind.

Wild donkeys are mentioned in the prophetic books of the Word, such as in Isaiah: 

> "The palace will be deserted, the crowded city abandoned; the hill and the watchtower will become dens forever—the joy of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks" (Isaiah 32:14). 

This refers to the devastation of intellectual things. When these are stripped of Truths, they are called the "joy of wild donkeys," and when stripped of Goods, they are called a "pasture for flocks," indicating the loss of a functioning Rational mind. In Jeremiah: 

> "The wild donkeys stood on the hills; they gasped for wind like sea monsters <note>original: *ceti*; literally whales or sea monsters, implying a desperate struggle for breath</note>; their eyes failed because there was no grass" (Jeremiah 14:6). 

This refers to a state of spiritual "drought," or a lack of good and truth. It is said that wild donkeys "gasp for wind" when they chase after empty, vain things instead of real ones (which are truths). Their "eyes fail" means that the person can no longer perceive what is true.

Here, the text refers to Israel, or the spiritual Church. **Ephraim** represents its intellectual part; "going up to Assyria" represents reasoning about whether a truth is actually true; and the "wild donkey alone" represents the **rational faculty** <note>original: *rationale*</note> when it is deprived of genuine truths. In the same prophet: “Because he will be like a **wild donkey among brothers**, the east wind of **Jehovah** shall come from the desert, and his spring will fail, and his fountain will be dried up; he will plunder the treasure of all desirable vessels” (**Hosea 13:15**). 1950. **That "his hand will be against everyone" signifies that it will fight against things that are not true, and "the hand of everyone against him" signifies that falsehoods will fight back,** is evident because **Ishmael** signifies **Rational Truth** <note>original: *Verum rationale*</note> separated from **Good** <note>In this context, "Good" refers to the motive of love and charity, while "Truth" refers to intellectual concepts</note>. When it is said of this Truth that his hand is against all and everyone’s hand is against him, it is clear that this is what is meant.

It was indicated above that **Abram** represents the Lord’s **Internal Man** (His Divine celestial and spiritual nature); **Isaac** represents the Lord’s **Interior Man** (His Divine Rational nature); and **Jacob** represents the Lord’s **Exterior Man** (His Divine Natural nature).

This Rational faculty took its nature from the "life of the affection for sciences"—that is, from **Hagar the Egyptian**, the handmaid of **Sarai**. This life belonged to the "External Man" which the Lord inherited from His mother. This was something that had to be fought against and expelled. Therefore, the Rational faculty is described as it would be if it were without **Rational Good**. 

However, after the Lord—through the struggles of temptations and victories—humbled (or "afflicted") and subdued that inheritance, and brought His own Rational faculty to life with **Divine Good**, it then became **Isaac**. In other words, it is represented by Isaac once Ishmael was cast out of the house along with his mother, Hagar. 

Every genuine Rational faculty consists of both **Good** and **Truth** (the celestial and the spiritual). Good, or the celestial, is its very soul or life; Truth, or the spiritual, is what receives its life from that Good. A Rational faculty without life from celestial Good is exactly as described here: it fights against everyone, and everyone fights against it. 

**Rational Good** never fights, no matter how much it is attacked. It is mild and gentle, patient and yielding, for it is the nature of love and mercy. Even though it does not fight, it still conquers everyone. It never thinks about fighting, nor does it boast of victory. This is because it is Divine and safe in itself; no evil can attack Good. In fact, evil cannot even exist in the same sphere as Good. When Good merely approaches, evil retreats and falls back on its own, for evil is from hell and Good is from heaven. 

The same is true for "spiritual-celestial" truth—that is, Truth that comes from a celestial origin, or Truth that comes from Good. This kind of truth is formed by Good, so that it can be called the "form of Good." But **Truth separated from Good**, which is represented here by Ishmael...

1951. **That "he shall dwell against the face of all his brothers" signifies that there will be constant contentions in matters of faith, but that he will ultimately be victorious,** is clear from what has just been said. When spirits think about such Truth, a feeling of terror arises because its nature is to never yield or retreat. From this, we can see what it means to "dwell against the face of all his brothers." Anyone can see that a secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> lies hidden in this description, but its nature has been unknown until now.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of how the Lord (as Jesus) perceived the development of his own rational mind. # GENESIS

The speech which one hears <note>original: *loquelam, quam haurit*</note> is actually an internal hearing. The ear only discerns articulated sounds or voices; it is the internal hearing that captures them. Then, an internal sight or intuition perceives them, and through this hearing, the meaning of the speech is understood. The same is true for visual things: the first ideas received from objects of sight are "material" (as they are called), but there is a more internal sight that looks upon those ideas and thus thinks. 

It is the same with a person’s **Rational** <note>original: *Rationale*; the level of the mind capable of logical thought and reasoning</note>. The Rational can never look at itself, much less explore its own nature. There must be something more internal that does this. Therefore, when a person is able to perceive something false within their own Rational mind, or see some truth that shines through—and especially if they experience a struggle where truth overcomes error—they can know that this happens because of the **influx** <note>original: *influxu*; the spiritual flow of life and influence from God into the human soul</note> of the Lord through the **Internal Man** <note>original: *Internum hominem*; the highest part of the soul, directly connected to the Divine</note>. The Lord’s own **Interior Man** (mentioned above in section 1926) was that which was conjoined to the Internal, which is **Jehovah**. Thus, existing far above that Rational level, the Lord saw and perceived in heavenly light what His Rational would become if it were based on Truth alone, without the influence of **Good** <note>original: *Bono*; spiritual love and kindness</note>.

1954. **"You are the God who sees me"** signifies **influx**. This is evident from what has just been said. Looking from a higher level into a lower—or, what is the same, from an interior into an exterior—is called Influx, for it happens by a "flowing in." For example, unless a person's internal sight continually flowed into their external sight (the eye), the eye could never capture and discern any object. It is the internal sight that captures, through the eye, what the eye sees; the eye itself never sees on its own, even though it appears that way. 

From this, one can see how much a person is caught in the **fallacies of the senses** when they believe the eye is what sees. In reality, it is the sight of their spirit—the internal sight—which sees through the eye. The spirits who have been with me saw things in the world through my eyes just as clearly as I did (as mentioned in section 1880). However, some of those spirits, who were still caught in the fallacies of the senses, thought they were seeing with their own eyes. It was shown to them that this was not true; for when my eyes were closed, they could see nothing in this atmospheric world. 

The same is true for every person: it is the spirit that sees, not the eye, though it sees through the eye. This is also proven by dreams, in which a person sometimes sees as clearly as if it were day. Yet even this internal sight (the spirit) does not see by its own power; it sees from an even more internal level—the Rational mind. Indeed, not even the Rational sees from itself; there is something even more internal belonging to the Internal Man (section 1940). Ultimately, it is the Lord, acting through the Internal Man, who alone sees, because He alone truly lives; He grants the human being the ability to see and makes it appear as if the person sees from themselves. This is how Influx works.

1955. **"Because she said, 'Have I also here seen after Him who sees me?'"** <note>Genesis 16:13</note> signifies an influx into the life of the **Exterior Man** without the mediation of the Rational. This is clear from the meaning of "seeing after Him who sees." In the internal sense, "seeing after one who sees" means to see from what is interior or higher. What is "within" or "above" is expressed as "after" in the literal sense of the text when it appears in something that is "outside" or "below." 

It is **Hagar** who speaks here. As shown previously, Hagar signifies the life of the **sciences** <note>original: *scientiarum*; here meaning factual, sensory knowledge or "the life of learning"</note>, which belongs to the Exterior Man. Because the first Rational mind originated from that life, the Lord saw the cause of why this happened—viewing it from His Interior Man within the Exterior Man—and this occurred without the Rational mind acting as a mediator. That these things involve deep secrets <note>original: *arcana*</note>...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

Everyone can see this from the fact alone that no one can know what it means to *see after seeing me* <note>original: *videre post videntem me*</note>, except from internal sensation. In this sensation, there are things that cannot be explained to our understanding except through angelic ideas. Such ideas do not fit into words, but only into the deeper meaning of words; and even then, they are abstracted from the material ideas that usually form the basis of our language. Regarding these things which appear so obscure to man, the Angels have such clear and distinct ideas, enriched by so many visual representations, that a whole volume could be written even if only a tiny part of them were described.

1956. **"Therefore she called the fountain..."** This signifies the state of truth from that source. This is established by what has been said, and from the meaning of a "fountain" <note>original: *fontis*</note> as truth (see above, n. 1927). Because this truth was seen not in the **Rational** <note>the level of the mind capable of logical reasoning</note> but below the Rational, the word for "fountain" used in the original language <note>Hebrew</note> is a different term than the common one used previously.

1957. **"The Well of the Living One who sees me"** <note>original: *Fons Vivo videnti me*</note> signifies that Truth is so clear. This follows from what has been said: namely, that the Lord clearly saw the condition of the truth belonging to this Rational mind—that it was not "good." The Lord's **Interior Man**, from which He saw, is called **Living and seeing**, because it was conjoined to the **Internal**, which is **Jehovah**, Who alone lives and alone sees (as shown just above, n. 1954).

1958. **"Behold, between Kadesh and Bered"** signifies its quality; namely, that He saw what this Truth was like, and thus what the Rational was like. This is evident from the meaning of Kadesh and Bered. That **Kadesh** signifies Truth and contentions about truths was shown before (n. 1676). **Bered**, however, signifies what is below, and thus **scientific truth** <note>original: *Verum scientificum*; factual knowledge acquired through the senses and memory</note>, from which the Rational mind also originates. (Regarding how Names in the Word signify actual things, see n. 1876, 1888, 1889, as well as n. 1224, 1264.)

1959. **Verse 15. And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.**
"Hagar bore Abram a son" signifies the Rational man born from that conjunction and conception. "And Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael" signifies its quality <note>its specific character or nature</note>.

1960. **"Hagar bore Abram a son."** This signifies that the **Rational man** was born from that conception and conjunction. This is clear from the representation and meaning of Hagar, Abram, and a "son." It was said above (n. 1895, 1896) that **Hagar** signifies the life of the affection for sciences <note>the love of acquiring factual knowledge</note> in the **External Man**. **Abram** signifies the Lord's **Internal Man** (n. 1893, 1950). A **son** signifies Truth (n. 264, 489, 491, 533, 1147); specifically the truth that belonged to this Rational. Therefore, "Hagar bore to Abram" signifies the Rational man born from that conception and conjunction. The literal sense of the text is transformed into this spiritual meaning when it reaches the Angels.

1961. **"And Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael."** This signifies its quality. This is clear from the meaning of a "name"—which is to know what something is like (n. 144, 145, 1754)—and from the representation of **Ishmael**, which is **Rational Truth**. This is described in verses 11 and 12 with these words: "You shall call his name Ishmael, because Jehovah has heard your affliction. And he will be a wild-ass man; his hand will be against everyone, and the hand of everyone [against him]."

"...every man’s hand against him, and he against every man; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers" <note>original: *omnium in eum; & contra facies omnium fratrum suorum habitabit*</note>; about which more is said in the explanation of those verses, describing his nature as it is depicted there.

1962. Verse 16: ***"And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram."*** <note>original: *Et Abram filius octoginta annorum & sex annorum, in pariendo Hagar Jischmaelem*</note> "Abram was eighty-six years old" signifies the Lord’s state regarding the heavenly goods He acquired through the struggles of temptation. "When Hagar bore Ishmael" signifies when the life of the affection for scientific knowledge gave birth to the **Rational** <note>the part of the mind capable of logical reasoning and judgment</note>.

1963. "Abram was eighty-six years old" signifies the Lord’s state regarding the heavenly goods He acquired through the struggles of temptation. This is evident from the meaning of eighty, a number which carries a similar meaning to forty, which signifies temptations (as shown previously in sections 730 and 862). It is also evident from the meaning of six, which signifies struggle or combat (see sections 720, 737, and 900), and from the meaning of ten, which signifies **Remains** <note>original: *Reliquiæ*; these are spiritual states of goodness and truth stored within a person by the Lord from childhood</note> (see section 576). For the Lord, these "Remains" were the acquisitions of heavenly goods by which He united His Human Essence to His Divine Essence (see section 1906 at the end).

The number eighty-six is composed of these three numbers and carries these meanings; thus, it signifies the Lord’s state regarding heavenly goods acquired through the struggles of temptation. Indeed, all numbers in the Word <note>the Bible</note> signify spiritual realities, as shown previously (sections 482, 487, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813). Because these are numbers of years, and are mentioned historically regarding Abram, it might appear as if they were not symbolic. However, nothing is written in the Word that does not transition into a spiritual and heavenly meaning when it reaches the Angels. Angels possess only spiritual and heavenly ideas. While a person reads the Word, the Angels do not know or perceive what "eighty-six" is, nor do they care how old Abram was when Hagar bore him Ishmael. Instead, upon reading such a number, the spiritual realities involved in that number immediately occur to them, along with the rest of the internal sense as explained here.

1964. "When Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram" signifies when the life of the affection for scientific knowledge gave birth to the Rational. This is evident from the meaning of Hagar, which is the life of the affection for sciences, and from the meaning of Ishmael, which is the Rational as it is first conceived (discussed above).

In this chapter, because the subject is the human Rational and the description of what it is like when it is formed by truths alone, versus what it is like when it is formed by goods and truths from those goods, it should be understood that the Rational can never be conceived, born, or formed without scientific knowledge and information <note>original: *scientificis & cognitionibus*</note>. However, scientific knowledge and information must have **use** as their goal. When they have use as their goal, they have **life** as their goal, for all life consists of uses because it consists of goals. Unless things are learned for the sake of a life of use, they are of no consequence because they serve no purpose. From scientific knowledge alone, without a life of use, the Rational becomes just as it was described: like a **wild donkey** <note>original: *onagri*</note>—stubborn, combative, and having a parched and dry life, stemming from a certain love of truth that is defiled by self-love. 

But when people have use as their goal, they receive life from those uses—specifically, the kind of life that the use itself possesses. Those who learn information so that they may be perfected in the faith of love—for truths and faith itself are love for the Lord and toward one's neighbor—are engaged in the highest of all uses. They receive spiritual and heavenly life from the Lord, and when they are in that life, they have the ability to perceive everything belonging to the Lord's Kingdom.

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

...in this life are all the Angels; and because they are in that life, they are in intelligence and wisdom itself.

1965. This is now the internal sense of the events in this chapter concerning Abram, Hagar, and Ishmael. However, how abundant that sense is—or rather, how it contains infinite things—can be seen from the fact that everything in the Word, in its internal sense, regards the Lord and speaks of the Lord. Since the life of the Word comes from the Lord Himself, the internal sense also speaks simultaneously of the Lord’s Kingdom in the Heavens and His Kingdom on earth (which is the Church). Similarly, it speaks of every individual in whom the Lord’s Kingdom exists, and generally of everything heavenly and spiritual, for all these things come from the Lord. This is why the Celestial Church, the celestial person, and even "the celestial" <note>original: *ipsum cœleste*; the abstract principle of heavenly love</note> itself are represented by Abram. However, to extend the explanation that far would be far too long.

### ->Concerning Visions and Dreams, including Prophetic ones, which are found in the Word.<-

1966. **F**ew people know the true nature of visions or which ones are genuine. Because I have been in the afterlife almost continually for several years and have seen astounding things there (as is evident from the first part of this work), I have been informed about visions and dreams through actual experience. I am permitted to relate the following details.

1967. The visions of certain people who claimed to have seen many things are often promoted; and they did indeed see them, but only in **Phantasy** <note>original: *phantasia*; here meaning a state of hallucination or vivid mental imagery that is not grounded in spiritual reality</note>. I have been instructed about these and shown how they occur. There are spirits who induce such appearances through phantasies so that they seem real. For example, when people see something in the shadows, in the moonlight, or even in the daytime if an object is in the dark, these spirits hold the person's mind fixedly and continually on the thought of something—whether an animal, a monster, a forest, or some other thing. As long as the mind is held there, the phantasy increases and grows to such an extent that the person is persuaded and sees the object exactly as if it were really there, when in fact it is nothing but an illusion. These visions happen to those who indulge much in phantasies, possess a weakness of mind, and have thus become gullible. These people are called **Visionaries** <note>original: *Visionarii*</note>.

1968. **Enthusiastic Spirits** <note>original: *Spiritus Enthusiastici*; in the 18th century, "enthusiasm" referred to religious delusion or the mistaken belief that one was receiving direct, private revelations from God</note> are similar, but they have visions regarding matters of belief. They are so strongly persuaded of these visions—and so strongly persuade others—that they could swear that what is false is true and that a fallacy is a reality. Much more could be said about the nature of these spirits from experience, but by the Lord’s Divine Mercy, I will discuss them specifically later. They contracted this nature from the persuasions and false principles they held while they lived in the world.

# GENESIS

1969. Evil spirits in the other life are hardly anything more than **Lusts and Fantasies** <note>original: *Cupiditates & Phantasiæ*</note>. They have acquired no other life for themselves. Their fantasies are so powerful that they perceive them as being absolutely real. Human fantasies cannot be compared with theirs, for spirits are in a more intense state, even regarding such things. These fantasies are constant among those in Hell <note>original: *Infernales*</note>, where spirits use these delusions to miserably torture one another.

1970. By **genuine visions** <note>original: *Visiones genuinas*</note> are meant visions—or "sights"—of things that truly exist in the other life. These are simply things that can be seen by the eyes of the spirit rather than the eyes of the body. They appear to a person when their interior sight is opened by the Lord. This is the same sight that a person’s spirit possesses, and which they enter into when they pass into the other life after being separated from the body; for a human being is essentially a spirit clothed with a body. The visions of the Prophets were of this kind. When this sight is opened, those things that actually exist among spirits are seen in a light clearer than the midday sun of our world. In this state, one sees not only **Representatives** <term>symbolic objects or scenes that represent spiritual truths</term> but also the spirits themselves. This includes a perception of who they are, their character, their location, where they come from, where they are going, and what their motivations, persuasions, and even their faith are (see nos. 1388, 1394). This is all confirmed by living speech that sounds exactly like human speech, and it is entirely free from deception.

1971. The visions that appear before good spirits are "representatives" of things that exist in Heaven. When something that exists in Heaven before the Angels flows down into the <term>World of Spirits</term> (the intermediate realm), it is transformed into representatives. By looking at these and through them, one can perceive what they signify. Such scenes are constant among good spirits and possess a beauty and pleasantness that can hardly be described.

1972. Regarding visions—or rather "sights" <note>original: *visa*</note>—that appear to the eyes of the spirit rather than the body, they become increasingly more interior. The things I saw in the World of Spirits were seen in clear light. However, those in the heaven of <term>Angelic Spirits</term> were seen more obscurely, and those in the heaven of Angels even more obscurely still. Up to this point, the sight of my spirit has rarely been opened to that higher level; instead, I was given to know what they were saying through a certain "perception" (the nature of which cannot be described), often through intermediate spirits. Sometimes things from those higher levels appeared in the "shadow of the light of heaven." This shadow is not like the shadow of physical light; it is a light that grows thin and fades because it is incomprehensible to both the intellect and the sight.

1973. It would be far too long to list every type of vision, for there are many. To illustrate the point, I will only relate two visions that show what they are like. These will also show how spirits are affected by what they see, and how evil spirits are tortured when the ability to see what others see and hear is taken away from them. They cannot bear to have such a thing taken from them, for spirits do not have a sense of taste...

# CHAPTER 16

*...but a desire—like an appetite for knowing and learning—takes its place. This is like their food, which nourishes them (no. 1480); how much they suffer, therefore, when this food is taken away from them, can be seen from the following example.*

1974. After a restless sleep, around the first watch <note>original: *primam vigiliam*; the first of the four periods into which the night was divided</note>, a most pleasant vision was presented to me. There were wreaths like laurel <note>original: *serta sicut laurea*</note>, green and arranged in a beautiful order. They were moving as if they were alive, and they were of such form and elegance that they cannot be described for their beauty and harmony, nor for the feeling of happiness that flowed from them. They were joined together in a double row, a short distance apart, extending quite a long way, and constantly changing their state of beauty. This was clearly visible to the spirits, even the evil ones.

Afterward, another even more beautiful vision followed, in which a happy, heavenly state was only dimly visible. There were infants in heavenly games, which affected the mind in an inexpressible way. Later, I spoke about these visions with the spirits, who admitted that they saw the first one just as I did, but they did not see the second, except so dimly that they could not say what it was. This caused indignation among them, which gradually turned into envy because it was said that angels and infants saw it. I was allowed to perceive their envy so clearly that nothing escaped me for my instruction. The envy was so intense that it caused them not only the greatest annoyance, but also anguish and internal pain, simply because they had not seen the second vision as well. 

They were led through various stages of envy until their hearts literally ached. While they were in that state, I spoke with them about envy, saying they could have been content with what they saw first, and that they could have seen the second as well if they were good. This indignation only sharpened their envy, which grew to such a degree that they could not later endure even the slightest memory of it without being affected by pain. The state and process of envy—with its stages, increases, and various mixed sicknesses of the mind and heart—cannot be described. This showed how much the wicked are tortured by envy alone when they see the happiness of the good from a distance, or even when they only think about it.

1975. Regarding **Dreams** <note>original: *Somnia*</note>, it is known that the Lord revealed the secrets of heaven to the Prophets not only through visions but also through dreams. These dreams were just as representative and meaningful as visions, and they were essentially of the same kind. Furthermore, future events were revealed through dreams to people other than the Prophets—such as the dreams Joseph had, those of the people in prison with Joseph, and those of Pharaoh, Nebuchadnezzar, and others. From these examples, it is clear that dreams of that kind, just like visions, flow in from Heaven. The difference is that dreams occur while the body is asleep, whereas visions occur when it is not. I have been shown vividly how prophetic dreams and those found in **The Word** <term>The Word: A common term in these texts for the Bible</term> flow in—or rather, descend—from heaven; I can report the following from my own experience.

# GENESIS

1976. There are three types of dreams. The first type comes from the Lord, mediated through Heaven; these were the Prophetic Dreams described in the Word <note>original: *in Verbo*; referring to the Bible</note>. The second type comes through angelic spirits, especially those who are located in front and above to the right, where paradisiacal things are. It was from this source that the people of the Most Ancient Church <note>original: *Antiquissimæ Ecclesiæ*; a term Swedenborg uses for the first, most celestial era of humanity</note> had their dreams, which were instructive (see no. 1122). The third type comes through spirits who are near a person when they sleep; these are also meaningful <note>original: *significativa*</note>. However, illusory <note>original: *phantastica*</note> dreams come from a different source entirely.

1977. So that I might understand exactly how dreams flow into a person, I was put into a sleep and dreamed that a ship was arriving, filled with all kinds of delicious and savory things to eat. These were not visible on the ship but were stored away. On the ship stood two armed guards, besides a third who was the captain. The ship passed into a kind of vaulted dock. When I woke up, I thought about the dream. Then angelic spirits, who are positioned above, in front, and to the right, spoke to me and said that they had introduced this dream. 

To ensure I knew for certain it came from them, I was put into a state that was like both sleeping and being awake at the same time. They introduced various pleasant and delightful things, such as a small, unknown creature that dissolved into something like blackish and shining rays, which flew into my left eye with amazing speed. They also presented people, as well as infants decorated in various ways, along with other things of inexpressible beauty, which I also discussed with them. This happened not just once, but several times, and each time I was instructed by them with a living voice. 

These are the angelic spirits who are at the threshold of the paradisiacal regions, and they are the ones who instill such dreams. They are also assigned the task of guarding certain people while they sleep so that they are not infested by evil spirits. They perform this duty with the greatest pleasure, even competing to see who might be present; they love to affect the person with the joys and delights they see within that person's character and affections. These spirits are those who became angelic because, during their physical lives, they delighted in and loved making the lives of others pleasant in every way. When one's spiritual hearing is opened to that level, a sweet, rhythmic sound like singing is heard from a distance. 

They said they do not know where such beautiful and pleasant representations <note>original: *Repræsentativa*; symbolic spiritual images</note> come from so suddenly, but it was stated that they come from heaven. These spirits belong to the province of the cerebellum <note>original: *Cerebelli*</note>, because the cerebellum, as I was taught, remains awake while the cerebrum <note>original: *Cerebrum*</note> sleeps. It was from this source that the people of the Most Ancient Church had their dreams, along with a perception of what they signified. From these dreams, a large part of the symbols and signs <note>original: *Significativa*</note> used by the ancient world were derived, under which deeply hidden truths were presented.

1978. Furthermore, there are other spirits who belong to the province of the left chest <note>original: *Thoracis sinistri*</note>, who frequently interrupt these dreams, as well as others whom the angelic spirits do not mind.

1979. Quite often, after such dreams, I was allowed to speak with spirits and angels...

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

...to the angels who introduced them, they telling what they introduced, and I what I saw; to bring forward the experience of all these things would be too long.

1980. It is worth mentioning that after I woke up and recounted what I had seen in my dream at great length, certain angelic spirits (not those mentioned above) said that my dream coincided exactly with the things they had been discussing among themselves. They said the dream was identical to their conversation, yet with this difference: the things I saw were not the actual topics they spoke about, but were **representations** <note>original: *repræsentativa*; symbols or images that stand for spiritual truths</note> of those topics. 

The ideas held by angels are turned into these representations when they flow down into the world of spirits <note>original: *Mundo spirituum*; a transitional realm between heaven and hell</note>. Therefore, every single thing they spoke about was represented this way in my dream. They further explained that the very same conversation could have been turned into different representations—even into similar or completely different ones—with unlimited variety. The reason they appeared as they did was due to the state of the spirits around me, and consequently, my own state at the time. In short, many different dreams can flow down and be presented from a single source or conversation. This is because a person's memory and affections are "recipient vessels" <note>original: *vasa recipientia*; the mental structures that catch and shape spiritual influence</note> in which representative ideas are varied according to the changes in their form and state.

1981. I can share another similar example: I had a dream, but an ordinary one. When I woke up, I recounted everything from beginning to end. The angels said that it coincided exactly with what they had been saying to each other. It was not that the things in the dream were the same as their talk, but that the thoughts of their conversation were turned into those specific dream images. This happened in such a way that the dream was representative and corresponding <note>original: *correspondentia*; the specific relationship between a spiritual cause and its natural effect</note> in every detail, with nothing missing. 

I then spoke with them about **Influx** <note>original: *Influxu*; the process by which the spiritual world flows into the natural world</note> and how such things flow in and are varied. In the dream, there was a person of whom I had the idea that he was in "Natural Truth" <note>original: *Vero naturali*; truth as it is understood on a basic, literal, or worldly level</note>, an idea I gained from his life's actions. Among the angels, there was a conversation about natural truth, which is why that person was represented to me. What he said to me and did in the dream followed in order, representing and corresponding to their mutual conversation; and yet, there was nothing in the dream that was exactly the same as their speech.

1982. Certain souls recently arrived from the world <note>original: *Animæ recentes e mundo*; people who have recently died and entered the afterlife</note> who desire to see the glory of the Lord are not yet in a state where they can be admitted directly. Instead, they are lulled into a sweet sleep that affects their outer senses and lower faculties. Then, their interior senses and faculties are awakened into a state of heightened wakefulness, and in this way, they are brought into the **Glory of Heaven** <note>original: *Cæli gloriam*</note>. Once wakefulness is restored to their outer senses and faculties, they return to their previous state.

1983. Evil spirits greatly desire and burn with a wish to infest and attack a person while they sleep, but it is then especially that the Lord guards the person; for **Love does not sleep**. The spirits who attempt such infestations are miserably punished.

# GENESIS

I have heard more often than can be told the punishments of those who are deceptions <note>original: *disceptiones*; those who cause disputes or engage in deceptive reasoning</note>, about which see numbers 829, 957, and 959. These punishments occur under the heel of the left foot and sometimes last for hours. **Sirens** <note>original: *Sirenes*; a specific class of deceptive spirits who use psychological manipulation</note>, who are interior deceivers, are those who lie in wait especially at night. They attempt to pour themselves into a person’s inner thoughts and affections at that time, but they are frequently driven away by angels from the Lord and are eventually deterred by very severe punishments. 

They have also spoken with others during the night, sounding exactly like me—using my own speech so perfectly that the difference could not be told—suggesting filthy things and persuading others of falsehoods. Once, I was in a most sweet sleep in which I had nothing but peaceful rest. When I woke up, certain good spirits began to rebuke me for having infested them so atrociously (as they put it) that they thought they had been in hell. They laid the blame on me, to which I responded that I knew nothing at all about the matter, but that I had slept most quietly and could not possibly have troubled them. Stunned by this, they finally realized it had been done through the deceits of **Sirens**. 

A similar thing was shown to me later, so that I might know what the crowd of Sirens is like. They are primarily from the female sex, who during their physical life sought to allure companions to themselves through interior cunning. They insinuated themselves through outward appearances, capturing people's minds in any way they could, entering into anyone's affections and pleasures—but with an evil end in mind, especially the desire to rule. 

Because of this, they have such a nature in the other life that they seem able to do anything by themselves. They soak up and invent various arts which they seize upon as easily as sponges soak up water, whether it is dirty or clear. Thus, they absorb both profane and holy things, which they swallow up and put into action for the sake of—as mentioned—ruling over others. 

I was permitted to perceive their interiors and see how foul they are, defiled by adulteries and hatreds. I was also permitted to perceive how powerful their "sphere" <note>original: *sphæra*; the spiritual aura or influence radiating from a being</note> is. They bring their inner selves into a state of persuasion so that their inner thoughts conspire with their outward appearance toward whatever they intend. In this way, they constrain and violently lead other spirits to think exactly as they do. No reasoning is apparent in them; instead, there is a simultaneous burst of arguments inspired by evil affections. This works by applying themselves to a person’s natural disposition and flowing into the minds of others, whom they then lead and—through persuasion—either overwhelm or captivate. 

They strive for nothing more than to destroy **Conscience**. When Conscience is destroyed, they take possession of—and indeed besiege—the interior parts of a person, even though the person is unaware of it. In the present day, external obsessions <note>original: *obsessiones externæ*; traditional demonic possession of the physical body</note> like those of old do not occur; instead, there are internal obsessions caused by such spirits. Those who have no conscience are obsessed in this way; their inner thoughts are similarly insane, but they are hidden and veiled by an outward decorum and a pretense of honesty for the sake of their own honor, gain, or reputation. This can be known to them if they only pay attention to their own thoughts.

->**THE END.**<-

# PART TWO

## THE BOOK OF GENESIS

### CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

<margin>1984.</margin> Few can believe that there is an internal sense within the Word <note>original: *Verbo*; referring to the Bible</note> that does not appear at all in the literal text. This is because it is so remote from the sense of the letter that it is almost as far apart as Heaven is from earth. However, that the literal sense contains such things within itself—and that it represents and signifies mysteries <note>original: *arcanorum*; refers to hidden spiritual truths</note> which no one sees except the Lord and the angels from the Lord—is evident from what has been said throughout the First Part. The literal sense is related to the internal sense just as the human body is related to its soul. While a person is in the body and thinks from bodily things, they know almost nothing about the soul, for the body's functions are different from the soul's; indeed, if the soul's functions were revealed, they would not be recognized as such. It is the same with the internal aspects of the Word. In its internal parts is its soul—that is, its life. These internal parts look toward nothing else but the Lord, His Kingdom, the Church, and those things belonging to His Kingdom and Church within a person. When these are the focus, it is truly the Lord's Word, for then life itself is within it. That this is the case was confirmed by many examples in the First Part and has been granted to be known for certain. For no ideas of bodily or worldly things can ever pass to the angels; instead, they are stripped off and utterly removed at the very threshold when they depart from a person, as can be seen from actual experience in the First Part, numbers 1769 to 1772 inclusive, and how they are changed, numbers 1872 to 1876. # G E N E S I S.

<page-num>4</page-num>

...can be clearly established from the many things in the Word <note>original: *Verbo*; referring to the Bible</note> which are nowhere intelligible in the sense of the letter. Unless such a soul or life were within them, they would not be recognized as the Lord’s Word; nor would they appear Divine to anyone who has not been taught from infancy to believe that the Word is inspired and thus holy. 

Who could know from the sense of the letter what those things signify which Jacob spoke to his sons before his death in Genesis Chapter 49? For example: "*That Dan is a serpent on the path, an asp on the road, biting the horse's heels, so that its rider falls backward*" (verse 17); "*That a troop will plunder Gad, and he will plunder the heel*" (verse 19); "*That Naphtali is a doe set free, giving elegant speech*" (verse 21); or "*That Judah will tie his donkey’s colt to the vine, and his donkey’s son to the choice vine: he will wash his clothes in wine, and his cloak in the blood of grapes: his eyes red from wine, and his teeth white from milk*" (verses 11, 12). 

It is the same in very many places in the Prophets. But what these things signify is nowhere apparent except in the internal sense, in which each and every detail fits together in a most beautiful order. 

It is the same with what the Lord said about the final times in Matthew: "*In the end of the age, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken; and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear; and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn*" (Chapter 24:29–30). These words do not literally signify the darkening of the sun and moon, nor the falling of stars from Heaven, nor the mourning of tribes. Instead, they signify Love <note>original: *Charitatem*; spiritual love or charity</note> and Faith, which in the internal sense are the Sun and Moon, and which will be obscured. They also signify the knowledge of what is good and true, which are the stars and are here called the "powers of the heavens," which will fall away and vanish; and they signify all things of faith, which are the "tribes of the earth." This has also been shown in Part One (numbers 31, 32, 1053, 1529, 1530, 1531, 1808). 

From these few examples, it can now be established what the internal sense of the Word is, as well as how remote—and in some places extremely remote—it is from the sense of the letter. Nevertheless, the sense of the letter represents truths and presents the appearances of truth, in which a person can remain while they are not yet in the light of truth.

### THE INTERNAL SENSE
<note>original: SENSUS INTERNUS</note>

<margin>1987.</margin> VERSE 1. *And Abram was ninety-nine years old, and Jehovah appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Shaddai <note>original: Deus Schaddai</note>; walk before Me and be perfect <note>original: integer</note>."* "Abram was ninety-nine years old" signifies the time before the Lord fully joined the Internal Man with the Rational [Man]; "Abram" signifies the Lord in that state and at that age; "and Jehovah appeared to Abram" signifies manifestation; "I am God Shaddai" signifies the name of Abram's God in the literal sense, through which the Lord was first represented to them; "walk before Me" signifies the truth of faith; "and be perfect" signifies good.

<margin>1988.</margin> "Abram was ninety-nine years old": That this signifies the time before the Lord fully joined the Internal Man with the Rational is evident from the meaning of the number nine when it precedes ten—or what is the same, ninety-nine before a hundred. For Abram was a hundred years old when Isaac was born to him. What the internal sense of the Word <note>original: Verbi; referring here to the Bible</note> is can be seen especially from numbers, just as it can from names. Whatever numbers appear in the Word signify actual things, just as names do; for there is nothing anywhere in the Word that does not contain the Divine, or that does not have an internal sense. This is especially clear in how remote that sense can be from the literal meaning; for names and numbers are never noticed in Heaven. Instead, the things signified by those names and numbers are what the angels perceive. For example, whenever the number Seven occurs, the idea of "holy" <note>original: sanctum</note> immediately occurs to the angels, because the celestial man becomes the "seventh day" or the Sabbath, which is the Lord’s rest (see numbers 84 to 87, 395, 433, 716, 881). It is the same with other numbers, such as Twelve. Whenever Twelve occurs, the angels perceive the idea of all things belonging to faith, because the twelve Tribes of Israel signified those things (see number 577). That numbers signify things in the Word may be seen in the demonstrations in Part One (numbers 482, 487, 488, 493, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, 893). The same applies to the number Ninety-nine. That it signifies the time before the Lord fully joined the Internal Man with the Rational is clear from the significance of the "one hundred years" that Abram reached when Isaac was born to him, by...

...by which the Lord's Rational Man is represented and signified, which is joined to His Internal [Man]—that is, to the Divine. In the Word, the number one hundred signifies the same thing as ten, because that number is composed of ten multiplied by ten. Ten signifies "remains" <note>original: Reliquiæ; in this context, "remains" refers to the stores of goodness and truth preserved by God in a person's inner being from infancy</note>, as shown in Part One (number 576). Regarding what remains are in a person, see numbers 468, 530, 561, 660, and 1050; and regarding what remains are in the Lord, see number 1906. These secrets <note>original: arcana</note> cannot be explained further here, but anyone can draw a conclusion once they first understand what remains are; today, their nature is unknown. It should only be known that remains in the Lord signify the Divine goods that He acquired for Himself by His own power, through which He united the Human Essence to the Divine Essence. 

From this, it can be established what is signified by "ninety-nine." Because it precedes one hundred, it signifies the time before the Lord fully joined the Internal Man with the Rational. Through Ishmael <note>original: Jischmaelem</note> was represented the first Rational in the Lord, the nature of which was shown more than enough in the previous chapter (sixteen). But through Isaac <note>original: Isacum</note> is represented the Lord's Divine Rational, as will be clear in what follows. Anyone can see that a secret <note>original: arcanum</note> is involved in the fact that Abram lived so long in the land of Canaan—now twenty-four years, including ten years before Ishmael was born and thirteen years afterward—and yet had no son by his wife Sarai until this first promise of a son was made when he was ninety-nine years old. The secret was that through these things, he represented the union of the Lord’s Divine Essence with His Human Essence, specifically the union of His Internal Man (who is Jehovah) with His Rational.

<margin>1989.</margin> That **Abram** signifies the Lord in that state and at that age is evident from what was previously said about Abram. In the internal sense, Abram represents the Lord; for when "Abram" is named in the Word, no other Abram is understood in Heaven. Those born within the Church who have heard about him from the Word know who Abram is when they enter the next life. However, because he is like anyone else and cannot offer them any help, they no longer care about him. They are informed that by "Abram" in the Word, no one else is meant but the Lord. Indeed, the angels—who have celestial ideas and do not fix them upon any particular person—are completely unaware of Abram. Therefore, when a person reads the Word and Abram is named, the angels perceive no one but the Lord. Regarding these words, they perceive the Lord in that state and at that age, for here Jehovah is speaking with Abram—that is, with the Lord.

<margin>1990.</margin> **Jehovah appeared to Abram** signifies manifestation; this is clear without explanation, for as stated, the Lord is represented by Abram. No human being in the entire world has seen Jehovah, the Father of the Lord, except the Lord alone, as He Himself said in John:
> "No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made Him known" (1:18). <note>original: Deum nemo vidit unquam, Unigenitus filius, qui in sinu Patris, ille exposuit</note>

In the same author:
> "You have never heard His voice, nor seen His form" (5:37). <note>original: Neque vocem Ipsius audivistis unquam, neque speciem Ipsius vidistis</note>

And again in the same author:
> "Not that anyone has seen the Father, except him who is from God; he has seen the Father" (6:46). <note>original: Non quod Patrem viderit quis, nisi qui apud Patrem, hic vidit Patrem</note>

The Infinite itself, which is above all heavens and above the innermost parts of man, cannot be manifested except through the **Divine Human**, which belongs to the Lord alone.

### CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

<page-num>9</page-num>

Communication of the Infinite with the finite is not possible from any other source. This is the reason why, when Jehovah appeared to the people of the Most Ancient Church, and later to the Ancient Church (which existed after the flood), and then to Abraham and the Prophets, He was manifested to them as a man. The Lord Himself clearly teaches that this "man" was actually Himself; in the Gospel of John, He says: "Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it and was glad. Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am" (John <term>VIII</term>: 56, 58). This is also seen in the Prophets, such as in Daniel, where He appeared as the "son of man" (Daniel <term>VII</term>: 13). 

From this, it can be established that the Infinite Being, who is Jehovah, could never be manifested to man except through the Human Essence—that is, through the Lord. Thus, He was manifested to no one but the Lord alone. This was also necessary so that He could be present with and joined to humanity. After people had completely removed themselves from the Divine and immersed themselves in foul lusts—and thus in purely physical and worldly things—the Lord actually took on the Human Essence through birth. He did this so that He could join the Infinite Divine to a humanity that was so far removed. Otherwise, they would have perished in the death of the damned forever. Other secrets <note>original: arcana</note> regarding the manifestation of Jehovah in the Lord’s Human [nature]—when He was in a state of humiliation before He fully united the Human Essence to the Divine and glorified it—will be explained in the following sections, as far as they can be understood, by the Lord's Divine Mercy.

> "...choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve: whether the gods whom your fathers served that were **across the river**, or the gods of the Amorites," <note>The original citation says xxxiv (34), but this quote is from Joshua 24:2, 14, 15.</note> 2, 14, 15. 

It is also clear that Nahor, Abraham's brother, and the nation descended from him, served other gods. One may see what was written regarding these in Part First, number 1356. 

That they worshipped **Shaddai** instead of **Jehovah**, calling him their god, is plainly stated in the writings of Moses: 

> "I, ***Jehovah***, *appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Shaddai; but by my name Jehovah I was not known to them*" (Exodus 6:3). 

From these passages, it can be established what kind of person Abraham was in his youth: namely, that like other Gentiles, he was an idolater. Even while he was in the land of Canaan, he had not yet in his heart rejected "God Shaddai"—the name by which the god of Abraham is identified in the literal sense. It was by this name that the Lord was first represented to them—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—as is clear from the cited passage in Exodus 6:3. 

The reason the Lord willed to be represented to them first by the name **Shaddai** is that the Lord never wants to destroy—suddenly or in a single moment—the form of worship implanted in someone since their infancy. To do so would be to tear up the root and thus destroy the "holy sense of adoration" <note>original: sanctum adorationis</note> and worship that is deeply implanted. The Lord never breaks this; instead, He bends it. 

The holiness of worship rooted from infancy has this quality: it does not tolerate violence, but only a slow and gentle bending. A similar process occurs with the Gentiles who worshipped idols during their physical lives, yet lived in mutual charity <note>original: charitate mutua; here meaning love for one's neighbor</note>. Because their "holy sense of worship" was rooted from infancy, it is not removed in a moment in the next life, but gradually. For those who have lived in mutual love, the "goods" and "truths" of faith can easily be implanted, and they receive them afterward with joy; for love is the very soil where they grow. 

Thus it was with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the Lord permitted them to retain the name "God Shaddai," even to the point of saying that He Himself was God Shaddai. This was done because of the name's significance. Interpreters translate *Shaddai* as "the Almighty," while others translate it as "the Thunderer." However, it properly signifies "the Tester" <term>original: Tentatorem</term>, and after temptations <term>spiritual trials</term>, "the Benefactor." This is evident in the book of Job, who mentions him so often because he was in the midst of trials, as seen in these passages from that book:

> "Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects; therefore, do not reject the discipline of **Shaddai**" (5:17). 
> "The arrows of ***Shaddai*** are with me; the terrors of God set their battle lines against me" (6:4). 
> "He will leave behind the fear of ***Shaddai***" (6:14). 
> "I will speak to ***Shaddai***, and I desire to reason with ***God***" (13:3). 
> "He stretches out his hand against ***God***, and strengthens himself against ***Shaddai***" (15:25). 
> "His own eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the fury of ***Shaddai***" (21:20). 
> "***Shaddai***—you cannot find him; he is great in power, and in judgment, and in the greatness of justice; *he will not afflict*" (37:23).

The same is found in Joel: 

> "Alas for the day! For the day of Jehovah is near, and it shall come as a devastation from **Shaddai**" (1:15). 

This can also be seen from the word *Shaddai* itself, which signifies "devastation" <note>The Hebrew root shadad (שדד) means to overpower or devastate.</note> and thus "temptation," for temptation is a species of devastation. But because the name originated among the Gentiles in Syria, he is not called *Elohim Shaddai*, but *El Shaddai*; and in Job, he is sometimes called just *Shaddai*, while *El* (God) is named separately.
