They attributed to Shaddai <note>original: Schaddai</note> the good that comes from trials, as seen in Job 22:17, 23, 25, 26; as well as the understanding of truth, which also comes from there (Job 32:8; 33:4). Because he was regarded as the god of Truth—since vastation <term>a process of spiritual emptying or purification</term>, temptation, punishment, and rebuke never come from "the Good," but from "the Truth"—and because the Lord was represented by this name to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the name was retained even by the Prophets. However, in the Prophets, Shaddai signifies Truth.

For example, in Ezekiel:
> "I heard the sound of the wings of the Cherubim, like the sound of many waters, like the ***voice of Shaddai*** <note>original: vocem Schaddai</note>, as they went; the sound of their wings was like the noise of a camp" (Ezekiel 1:24).

And again in the same book:
> "The court was filled with the brightness of the glory of Jehovah, and the sound of the wings of the Cherubim was heard even to the outer court, like the ***voice of God Shaddai when He speaks***" <note>original: vox dei Schaddai cum loquitur</note> (Ezekiel 10:4–5).

In this passage, "Jehovah" stands for the Divine Good, while "Shaddai" stands for the Divine Truth. Similarly, in the internal sense of the Word, "wings" signify things belonging to truth.

Isaac and Jacob also use the name "God Shaddai" in a similar sense—referring to the one who tests and then delivers from temptation, and afterwards bestows blessings. Isaac said to his son Jacob, when he was fleeing from Esau:
> "May ***God Shaddai*** bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you" (Genesis 28:3).

Jacob said to his sons when they were departing for Egypt to buy grain, at a time when they greatly feared Joseph:
> "May ***God Shaddai*** give you mercies before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin" (Genesis 43:14).

Jacob (referred to there as Israel), when blessing Joseph—who had faced evil temptations more than his brothers and was delivered from them—said:
> "By the God of your father, who will help you, and with ***Shaddai***, who will bless you" (Genesis 49:25).

This is why the Lord first willed to be represented as "God Shaddai," whom Abram worshipped, saying, "***I am God Shaddai***." He later said the same to Jacob: "***I am God Shaddai: be fruitful and multiply***" (Genesis 35:11). Another reason for this is that the preceding sections, in their internal sense, dealt with temptations.

The worship of Shaddai among them originated from the fact that—just as with a certain nation to be discussed in the following pages by the Lord’s Divine Mercy—those who belonged to the Ancient Church <term>the spiritual era following the Flood</term> often heard spirits who would rebuke them and then later console them. The rebuking spirits were perceived at the left side, under the arm; at such times, angels were present at the head to govern the spirits and moderate the rebuke. 

Because those people thought everything said to them by spirits was Divine, they called that rebuking spirit "Shaddai"; and because he also gave comfort afterward, they called him "God Shaddai." At that time, like the Jews later, they were of the religious belief—because they did not understand the internal sense of the Word—that all evil (and thus all temptation) came from God, just as all good (and thus all comfort) did. However, for a different perspective on this, see the entries in Part First, numbers 245, 592, 696, 1093, 1874, and 1875.

1994. **"And be blameless"** <note>original: integer; often translated as perfect or whole</note> signifies the good of charity. 1995. **Verse 2.** *And I will establish my covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you very, very much.*
"I will establish my covenant between Me and you" signifies the union of the **Internal Man** <term>the highest part of the soul, which is Divine</term>, who is Jehovah, with the **Interior Man** <term>the rational or middle part of the soul</term>.
"And I will multiply you very, very much" signifies the infinite fruitfulness of the affection for truth.

1996. **"I will establish my covenant between Me and you"** signifies the union of the Internal Man, who is Jehovah, with the Interior Man. This is evident from the meaning of a "covenant," which signifies a conjunction <note>original: conjunctio; a joining together</note>. Whenever a covenant between Jehovah and man is mentioned in the Word, in the internal sense it signifies nothing other than the joining of the Lord with man. The covenants so often made between Jehovah and the descendants of Jacob represented nothing else. Since this was confirmed in Part One (sections 665, 666, 1023, 1038, and 1864), it would be unnecessary to prove it again here. The Lord's Internal Man was Jehovah because He was conceived from Him; the Interior Man, however, is represented here by Abram. Therefore, "a covenant between Me and you" signifies the union of the Internal Man (or Jehovah) with the Interior Man, and thus with the Lord’s **Human Essence**.

1997. **"I will multiply you very, very much"** signifies the infinite fruitfulness of the affection for truth. This can be seen from the meaning of "being multiplied," which is a term applied to truth (as noted in sections 43, 55, 913, and 983). Because this refers to the Lord, it signifies the infinite fruitfulness of Truth from Good (as mentioned previously in section 1940).

There are two types of **Affections**: namely, the affection for good and the affection for truth.
*   **Affection for good** is doing good out of a love for what is good.
*   **Affection for truth** is doing good out of a love for what is true.

These two affections appear at first glance to be the same, but they are distinct in themselves, both in their essence and their origin. The affection for good (doing good from a love of good) belongs properly to the **will**; however, the affection for truth (doing good from a love of truth) belongs properly to the **understanding**. Thus, these two affections are as distinct from one another as the will is from the understanding. 

The affection for good comes from **celestial love** <term>love directed toward the Lord</term>, while the affection for truth comes from **spiritual love** <term>love directed toward the neighbor</term>. The affection for good can only be attributed to the "celestial man," while the affection for truth is attributed to the "spiritual man." What "celestial" and a "celestial man" are, and what "spiritual" or a "spiritual man" are, was sufficiently shown in Part One. 

The **Most Ancient Church**, which existed before the flood, lived in the affection for good; but the **Ancient Church**, which existed after the flood, lived in the affection for truth. The former was a Celestial Church, while the latter was a Spiritual Church. All angels in the heavens are divided into celestial and spiritual: the celestial are those in the affection for good, and the spiritual are those in the affection for truth. To the former, the Lord appears as a Sun; to the latter, He appears as a Moon (see sections 1529, 1530, 1531, and 1838). This affection for truth is what the Lord united to the affection for good (which is doing good from a love of good) when He united His Human Essence to the Divine.

1998. **Verse 3. *And Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, saying.***

1999. **"Abram fell on his face,"** which signifies adoration, is clear without further explanation. Falling on the face was a rite of worship in the Most Ancient Church <term>the earliest spiritual state of humanity, characterized by direct love and perception</term>, and consequently among the Ancient peoples. This was because the face signified the interior parts of a person, and the state of their humiliation was represented by falling on the face. For this reason, it became a solemn practice in the Jewish Representative Church. 

True adoration, or humiliation of the heart, carries with it a physical prostration to the ground on one’s face before the Lord as a naturally flowing gesture. In the humiliation of the heart, there is an acknowledgment of oneself—that one is nothing but filth—and a simultaneous acknowledgment of the Lord's infinite Mercy toward such a person. When the mind is held in these acknowledgments, the mind itself humbles itself toward hell, and the body prostrates itself; nor does the person lift themselves up until they are raised by the Lord. This occurs in all true humiliation, accompanied by a perception of being lifted up by the Lord's Mercy. Such was the humiliation of the people of the Most Ancient Church. However, the case is different with worship that does not come from the humiliation of the heart (see section 1153). 

That the Lord adored and prayed to Jehovah His Father is known from the Word in the Gospels, and He did this as if to someone other than Himself, even though Jehovah was actually within Him. But the state in which the Lord was then was His state of humiliation, the nature of which was described in Part One—namely, that He was then in the infirm human nature <note>original: *infirmo humano*</note> inherited from the mother. But as much as He cast this off and put on the Divine, He was in a different state, which is called His state of Glorification. In the former state, He worshiped Jehovah as someone other than Himself, even though He was within Him (for, as stated, His Internal was Jehovah); but in the latter state—the state of glorification—He spoke with Jehovah as with Himself, for He was Jehovah Himself. 

How these things are related cannot be understood unless one knows what the "Internal" is, and how the Internal acts upon the "External"; and further, how the Internal and External are distinct from each other and yet joined together. Nevertheless, this can be illustrated by something similar: the Internal in man and its influence and operation on his External. That man has an Internal, which is the Interior or Rational part, and an External, may be seen in sections 1889 and 1940. It is from the Internal that a human is truly human, and by it, he is distinguished from brute animals. Through this Internal, man lives after death and into eternity; and through it, he can be raised by the Lord among the Angels. It is the very first form from which a person is created and exists as a human. Through this Internal, the Lord is united to man. Heaven itself is closest to the Lord through these human internals; yet they are still above the highest Angelic Heaven, and therefore they belong to the Lord Himself. Thus, the entire human race is most present under the eyes of the Lord. The distance that appears in this sublunary world <note>the physical earth</note> does not exist in heaven, and even less so above heaven (see the experiences in sections 1275 and 1277). But as much as He put off this maternal human, the Lord was not distinct from Jehovah, but was one with Him. The former state was, as previously mentioned, the Lord’s state of humiliation, while the latter was His state of Glorification.

**2002.** Verse 4. ***"As for me, behold, my covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations."***

"As for me, behold, my covenant is with you" signifies the union of the Divine Essence <note>original: *Divinae Essentiae*; the core, infinite nature of God</note> with the Human Essence. "And you shall be a father of a multitude of nations" signifies the union of the Human Essence with the Divine. **Father** signifies what originates from Him; **multitude** signifies truth; **nations** signifies the "good" <note>in this context, "good" refers to love, kindness, and moral excellence</note> that results from that truth.

**2003.** Regarding the phrase ***"As for me, behold, my covenant is with you"***: That this signifies the union of the Divine Essence with the Human is established by the meaning of **covenant**, which is "conjunction" <note>original: *conjunctio*; a joining together</note>, as discussed in numbers 665, 666, 1023, and 1038. That it here specifically refers to the union of the Divine Essence with the Human is evident from the internal sense of the preceding verses and the words themselves: "my covenant with you."

**2004.** Regarding the phrase ***"And you shall be a father of a multitude of nations"***: That this signifies the union of the Human Essence with the Divine cannot be so easily seen by explaining individual words in their internal sense, unless they are viewed through a certain general idea. 

The internal sense is sometimes of this nature: it can be described as "more universal" because it is "more remote" from the literal words. From the explanation of individual words, the most immediate sense is that all truth and all good come from the Lord. For, as will be stated below, **Father** signifies "from Him" (that is, from the Lord), **multitude** signifies truth, and **nations** signifies the "good" that comes from it. 

However, because truths and goods are the means by which the Lord united His Human Essence to the Divine, that "more universal and remote" sense arises from them. Angels perceive these words in this way, seeing them as representing a **reciprocal union** <note>original: *unitio reciproca*; a two-way connection</note>—namely, the union of the Lord’s Divine Essence with the Human, and the Human with the Divine. For as was said, "my covenant with you" signifies the union of the Divine with the Human, and the phrase following it signifies the union of the Human with the Divine. 

That this union was made reciprocally is a secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> that has not yet been revealed. It is of such a nature that it can hardly be explained to the human understanding; for as long as the nature of **influx** <note>original: *influxus*; the flow of life or influence from a higher spiritual level to a lower one</note> is unknown, it is impossible to form any idea of what a reciprocal union is. 

However, this can be illustrated to some extent by the way influx works in humans. In a person, there is also a reciprocal conjunction. From the Lord, life continually flows into a person's **Rational** <note>original: *Rationale*; the faculty of reason</note> through their **Internal** (mentioned just above in number 1999). It flows through the Rational into the **External**, specifically into its facts <note>original: *scientifica*; scientific knowledge or stored information</note> and cognitions <note>original: *cognitiones*; things known or learned</note>. The Lord not only adapts these to receive life but also arranges them into order, thereby enabling a person to think and eventually to be rational. 

This conjunction is the Lord's work with the human being; without it, a person could never think, let alone be rational. This is evident to everyone because in a person's thought there are countless hidden depths of science and analytical logic—so many that they could never be fully explored. These never flow in through the senses or the "External man," but through the "Internal." On their part, the human being "goes to meet" <note>original: *obviam it*; meets or responds to</note> this life from the Lord through their facts and knowledge, and thus joins themselves to the Lord reciprocally. 

But as for the union of the Lord's Divine Essence with His Human, and the Human with the Divine, this infinitely transcends our experience. For the Lord’s "Internal" was Jehovah Himself—life itself. The "internal" of a human being, however, is not the Lord, and thus is not...

->**GENESIS**<-

...life, but receiving life. The Lord’s relationship with Jehovah was a **union**, but a human being’s relationship with the Lord is not a union, but a **conjunction** <note>original: *conjunctio*; in this context, a "union" means becoming one essence, while a "conjunction" means being joined together while remaining distinct individuals</note>. The Lord, by His own power, united Himself to Jehovah, which is why He also became **Justice**; a human being, however, is never joined to God by their own power but only by the Lord’s power, so that the Lord joins the human to Himself.

This is a reciprocal union <note>original: *unio*; a two-way becoming-one</note>, which is what the Lord means when He attributes His own things to the Father, and the Father’s things to Himself. As it says in the Gospel of John: *"Jesus said, he who believes in Me, does not believe in Me, but in Him who sent me. I have come as a light into the world, so that everyone who believes in Me should not remain in darkness"* (<term>John 12:44-46</term>). Within these words lie the most hidden secrets <note>original: *arcanissima*; the deepest spiritual mysteries</note> concerning the union of **Good** with **Truth**, and **Truth** with **Good**—or what is the same thing, the union of the **Divine Essence** with the **Human Essence**, and the **Human** with the **Divine**. This is why He says, "he who believes in Me does not believe in Me, but in Him who sent me," and then immediately adds, "he who believes in Me"—speaking of that union—and then, "he who sees Me, sees Him who sent Me."

In the same book: *"The words that I speak to you, I do not speak from Myself; the Father who remains in Me, He does the works. Believe Me, that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me; truly I say to you, he who believes in Me, the works that I do..."* (<term>John 14:10-12</term>). These words contain the same secrets: namely, the union of **Good** with **Truth** and **Truth** with **Good**, or the union of the Lord’s **Divine Essence** with the **Human** and the **Human** with the **Divine**. This is why He says, "the words that I speak to you I do not speak from Myself, the Father who is in Me does the works," and then, "the works that I do," referring here to the union in the same way: "he who sees Me, sees Him who sent Me." This is the **mystical union** <note>original: *unio mystica*</note> that many people speak about.

From this it is clear that the Father was not someone different from the Lord, even though He spoke of the Father as if He were someone else. This was because of the reciprocal union that was being achieved, and which was eventually completed. For He says openly and often that He is one with the Father, as in the places already cited: *"He who sees Me, sees Him who sent Me"* (<term>John 12:45</term>); and, *"The Father who remains in Me; believe Me, that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me"* (<term>John 14:10-11</term>). Also: *"If you knew Me, you would also know My Father"* (<term>John 8:19</term>). And again: *"If you have known Me, you have also known My Father; and from now on you know Him, and have seen Him."* Philip said to Him, "Show us the Father." Jesus said to him, *"Have I been with you for so long, and yet you do not know Me, Philip? He who has seen Me has seen the Father; so how can you say, 'Show us the Father'? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me?"* (<term>John 14:7-10</term>). And finally: *"I and the Father are one"* (<term>John 10:30</term>). This is why in Heaven they know no other Father than the Lord, because the Father is in Him and He is one with the Father; when they see Him, they see the Father, as He Himself said (see number 15).

**2005.** That **Father** signifies what originates from Him is clear from the meaning of "Father" discussed just above: namely, that whatever comes from the Father was from Himself, because they are one. The **Internal** <note>the inner spirit or soul</note> of every human being is from the father, and the **External** <note>the outer body and natural self</note> is from the mother. Or to put it another way, the **soul** itself is from the father, and the **body** which clothes the soul is from the mother. Yet the soul and body make a single unit, for the soul belongs to the body and the body to the soul; therefore they are inseparable. The Lord’s **Internal** was from the Father, and thus He was the Father Himself. This is why the Lord says that the Father is in Him.

In the Word of the Old Testament, the Lord is also called "Father," as in Isaiah: *"For a child is born to us, a son is given to us, and the government shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Hero, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace"* (<term>Isaiah 9:6</term>). To "create" here means to regenerate <note>original: *regenerare*; in this context, spiritual rebirth or being made anew by God</note>, as was shown in Part One (nos. 16, 88, 472). Furthermore, wherever "Jehovah" is mentioned in the Word of the Old Testament, it refers to the Lord, because all the rituals of the Church represented Him, and everything in the Word, in its internal sense, looks toward Him.

**2006.** That a **multitude** signifies truth is evident from the meaning of "multitude" as truth (discussed previously in no. 1941), and from the meaning of "to be multiplied," which is a term applied to truth (see nos. 43, 55, 913, 983).

**2007.** That **nations** signify the "good" that comes from truth is evident from the meaning of "nations" as goodness (discussed in Part One, nos. 1159, 1258, 1259, 1360, 1416, 1849).

**2008. Verse 5.** *And your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, for I have made you a father of a multitude of nations.* "Your name shall no longer be called Abram" signifies that He will put off the human <note>original: *exuet humanum*; refers to the Lord shedding the limited, physical nature inherited from a human mother</note>. "And your name shall be Abraham" signifies that He will put on the Divine <note>original: *induet Divinum*; refers to the Lord taking on a fully Divine nature</note>. "For I have made you a father of a multitude of nations" signifies here, as before, that every truth and the resulting good comes from Him.

**2009.** That "your name shall no longer be called Abram" signifies putting off the human, and "your name shall be Abraham" signifies putting on the Divine, is evident from the meaning of a "Name," and from the specific meanings of the names "Abram" and "Abraham." In the Word, when it is said "your name shall be," it signifies what a person's quality or nature will be (as shown in Part One, nos. 144, 145, 1754). 

Because a "Name" signifies quality, it encompasses everything about a person in a single summary. In heaven, no attention is paid to a person's literal name. Instead, when someone is named or when a Name is spoken, an idea of their quality—or everything belonging to them and within them—comes to mind. Therefore, "Name" in the Word signifies "quality." To make this easier to understand, we can bring forward more confirming evidence from the Word, such as the Blessing in the books of Moses: *"Jehovah bless you and keep you; Jehovah make his face shine upon you and be merciful to you; Jehovah lift up his face toward you and give you peace. So shall they put my Name upon the children of Israel"* (<term>Numbers 6:24-27</term>). From this, it is clear what a "Name" is: to "put the Name of Jehovah upon the children of Israel" means that Jehovah blesses, protects, enlightens, and has mercy <note>original catchword: *mifereatur* (may he have mercy)</note>.

In this context, "taking the Name of God in vain" does not merely refer to the word "God," but to every single thing that comes from Him—meaning everything related to His worship. These things are not to be despised, much less blasphemed or contaminated with filth. 

In the Lord's Prayer, it says: *"Hallowed be Your Name; Your kingdom come; Your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth"* (Luke 11:2). Here too, "name" does not mean a literal name, but all things belonging to love and faith. These belong to God (or the Lord) and come from Him. Because these things are holy, when they are held as sacred, the Kingdom of the Lord comes and His will is done on earth as it is in heaven.

That "Name" signifies such things is evident from every passage in the Word of the Old and New Testaments where "Name" is mentioned. For example, in Isaiah: *"In that day you will say: give thanks to Jehovah, call upon His Name, make His deeds known among the peoples; remind them that His Name is exalted"* (Isaiah 12:4). To "call upon the Name of Jehovah" and "remind them that it is exalted" never means placing worship in a literal name or believing that Jehovah is invoked simply by a word. Rather, it means knowing His quality—that is, every single thing that proceeds from Him.

In the same book: *"Therefore, honor Jehovah in the fires <note>original: *in Urim*; Urim literally means "lights" or "fires," often associated with the brilliance of divine truth or the east</note>; in the islands of the sea, honor the Name of Jehovah, the God of Israel"* (Isaiah 24:15). To "honor Jehovah in the fires" refers to the holy things of love; to honor "the Name of Jehovah, the God of Israel" in the islands of the sea refers to the holy things of faith. Again, in Isaiah: *"Jehovah our God, only in You will we remember Your Name"* (Isaiah 26:13). And: *"I will stir up one from the north, and he shall come; from the rising of the sun he shall call upon My Name"* (Isaiah 41:25). To remember and call upon the Name of Jehovah is to worship from the "goods" of love and the "truths" of faith. 

Those "from the north" are those outside the Church who are in ignorance of the Name of Jehovah; yet they still "invoke His Name" when they live in mutual charity and worship the Divine Creator of the universe. This is because the invocation of Jehovah consists in the quality of worship, not in a literal name. (That the Lord is present even among the Gentiles, see numbers 932, 1032, 1059). 

In Isaiah again: *"The nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of Jehovah shall name"* (Isaiah 62:2). Here, being "called by a new name" means becoming someone else—namely, being newly created or regenerated—and thus having a new quality. 

In Micah: *"For all people walk each in the name of his god, but we will walk in the Name of Jehovah our God for ever and ever"* (Micah 4:5). "Walking in the name of his god" clearly refers to profane worship, while "walking in the Name of Jehovah" refers to true worship.

In Malachi: *"From the rising of the sun even to its setting, My Name is great among the nations; and in every place incense is offered to My Name, and a pure offering <term>mincha: a grain offering or gift</term>; for My Name is great among the nations"* (Malachi 1:11). Here, "name" does not signify a literal word, but worship, which is the "quality" of Jehovah (or the Lord) by which He desires to be adored.

In Moses: *"The place which Jehovah your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put His Name there, and to make His Name dwell there, to that place you shall bring everything that I command you..."*

Deuteronomy 12:5, 11, 14; Chapter 16:2, 6, 11: Where it says "to put His Name" and "to cause His Name to dwell there," it does not signify a literal name, but worship. A name alone—without an idea of His nature, a knowledge of His nature, or faith in His nature—is merely a sound. Thus, it is clear that "Name" represents a person's nature <note>original: *quale*; the specific character or quality of a person</note>, and "knowing a name" means knowing what that person is like.

In the books of Moses: "At that time, Jehovah set apart the tribe of Levi to minister to Him and to bless in His Name" (Deuteronomy 10:8). To "bless in the Name of Jehovah" is not done through the literal name, but through the things belonging to His Name, as discussed above. 

In Jeremiah: "This is His Name by which they will call Him: Jehovah Our Righteousness" (Jeremiah 23:6). Here, "Name" stands for "Righteousness," which is the nature of the Lord, who is the subject of this passage. 

In Isaiah: "Jehovah called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother He mentioned my Name" (Isaiah 49:1). This also refers to the Lord; "mentioning His Name" means to instruct concerning His nature.

It is clearly evident here that "name" is not a literal name, but refers to the person's nature or quality. A "name in the Book of Life" means nothing else; the same applies to "confessing his name before the Father" and "writing the Name of God and the city and the new name" upon him. Similarly, in other places, the "names" said to be written in the Book of Life and in heaven (Revelation 13:8; 17:18; Luke 10:20) refer to spiritual qualities. In heaven, nothing exists except one's nature, by which one person is known from another; in the literal sense of scripture, this is expressed as a "name." 

Anyone can see this from the fact that every person named on earth is represented in another person's mind as a certain character, by which they are known and distinguished. In the next life, these mental ideas remain, but the literal names vanish—and this is even more true among the angels. This is why "Name" in the internal sense signifies the nature of a person or knowing what they are like. 

In the same book: "On the head of him who sat on the white horse were many crowns, and he had a Name written that no one knows except himself; he was clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his Name is called The Word of God" (Revelation 19:12, 13). Here it is explicitly stated that the "Name" is the Word of God, and thus the nature of Him who sat on the white horse.

That the "Name of Jehovah" means knowing His nature—namely, that He is all the good of love and all the truth of faith—is clearly established from these words of the Lord: "Righteous Father, I have known You, and these have known that You sent Me, for I have made known to them Your Name, and I will make it known, so that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and..." <note>The text continues on the next page: "...I in them." Thus, the meaning of these words in the internal sense is that the Lord strips away the Human and puts on the Divine. This follows logically from what came before and leads into what follows, for the promise is now made concerning his son Isaac, who represents the Lord's "Divine Rational" <note>the Lord's perfect, divine capacity for reason and understanding</note>.

2011. The statement, **"Because I have made you a father of a multitude of nations,"** signifies here (as before) that all truth—and the resulting good—comes from Him. This is evident from the meaning of **"Father"** as being from Him; from the meaning of **"multitude"** as Truth; and from **"nations"** as the good that comes from it (as discussed above in sections 2005, 2006, and 2007). In a more universal or abstract sense, these same words signify the union of the Human Essence with the Divine <note>original: *Humanæ Essentiæ unionem, cum Divina*</note> (see section 2004). The union of the Lord’s Human Essence with the Divine is like the union of Truth with Good, and the union of His Divine Essence with the Human is like the union of Good with Truth, which is a reciprocal union. Indeed, in the Lord, it was Truth itself that united itself to Good, and Good that united itself to Truth; for the Divine Infinite can only be described as Good itself and Truth itself. Therefore, the human mind falls into no error when it thinks of the Lord as Good itself and Truth itself.

2012. ***Verse 6. And I will make you exceedingly fruitful; and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come out of you.*** "I will make you exceedingly fruitful" <note>original: *fructificabo temet in valde valde*</note> signifies the infinite multiplication of good. "And I will make nations of you" signifies that all good is from Him. "And kings shall come out of you" signifies that all truth is from Him.

2013. **"I will make you exceedingly fruitful"** signifies the infinite multiplication of good. This is clear from the meaning of "being fruitful," which is a term used in relation to good (as seen previously in sections 43, 55, 913, and 983). Because the text says "exceedingly" <note>original: *valde valde*, literally "greatly greatly"</note> and refers to the Lord, it signifies multiplication to an infinite degree.

2014. That **"I will make nations of you"** signifies that all good is from Him is clear from the meaning of "Nations" <term>gentes</term> in its genuine and primary sense, which is "good" (as discussed in Part One, sections 1259, 1260, 1416, and 1849).

2015. That **"kings shall come out of you"** signifies that all truth is from Him is clear from the meaning of a "King" <term>rex</term> in the Word—both in the historical and prophetic books—as "truth" (as mentioned in section 1672, though not yet fully demonstrated). From the meaning of "Nations" as goods and "Kings" as truths, one can see the nature of the *internal sense* of the Word, and how far removed it is from the *literal sense*. 

When someone reads the Word, especially the historical parts, they never believe otherwise than that "nations" mean literal nations and "kings" mean literal kings, and that the Word is specifically about the peoples and rulers named there. However, the idea of nations and kings completely vanishes when the text is received by the Angels; in their place, Good and Truth emerge. This cannot help but seem strange—even like a paradox <note>original: *paradoxon*</note>—but that is how it works. 

Anyone can see that if "nations" only meant nations and "kings" only meant kings in the Word, then the Lord’s Word would involve little more than any other historical book or piece of writing, and would thus be merely worldly. Yet in the Word, everything is Divine, and therefore celestial and spiritual. Take this verse alone: if it only meant that Abraham would be fruitful, and become nations, and that kings would descend from him, what would this be but a purely worldly matter with nothing celestial about it? Such things involve only worldly glory, which is absolutely nothing in heaven. But if it is the Lord’s Word, it must be about the glory of heaven and not the glory of the world. Therefore, the literal sense is completely wiped away and disappears as it passes into heaven, being purified so that nothing worldly remains mixed in. For "Abraham" does not mean Abraham, but the Lord; and "being fruitful"...

<header>GENESIS</header>

...it is not his physical descendants who will multiply "exceedingly," but rather the Good of the Lord’s Human Essence into infinity. By "nations," the text does not mean literal nations but "goods"; and by "kings," it does not mean literal kings but "truths." While the historical account remains true in its literal sense—for it was a fact that these things were promised to Abraham, that he was made fruitful, and that literal nations and kings descended from him—there is a deeper meaning.

That **"Kings"** signify "truths" <note>original: *vera*</note> can be established from several passages. In Isaiah: 

> "Foreigners will build up your walls, and **their kings** will serve you; you will suck the milk of nations, and the breast of **kings** you will suck" <term>LX</term>: 10, 16. 

What it means to "suck the milk of nations and the breast of kings" is never clear from the literal words, but it is clear from the internal sense, which refers to being gifted with "goods" and instructed in "truths." 

In Jeremiah: 

> "**Kings** and princes will enter through the gates of this city, sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses" <term>XVII</term>: 25; Chapter <term>XXII</term>: 4. 

"Riding in chariots and on horses" is a prophetic expression; it signifies an abundance of intellectual things, as can be seen in many places in the Prophets. Thus, when it says "kings will enter through the gates of the city," it signifies in the internal sense that people would be imbued with the truths of faith. This is the celestial sense of the Word, into which the worldly literal sense transitions. 

In the same author: 

> "Jehovah has despised the **king** and the priest in the indignation of his anger; the gates of Zion have sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars; the **king** and the princes are among the nations, there is no law" (Lamentations <term>II</term>: 6, 9). 

Here, "king" stands for the truth of faith, and "priest" for the good of charity. "Zion" stands for the Church, which is destroyed and whose "bars" (defenses) are broken. Therefore, "the king and princes among the nations" means that Truth and those things belonging to Truth will be exiled, to the point that there is no "law"—meaning no doctrine of faith. 

In Isaiah: 

> "Before the child knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that you dread will be forsaken by both its **kings**" <term>VII</term>: 16. 

This refers to the coming of the Lord. The "land that will be forsaken" represents faith, which would then be non-existent; its "truths" are the "kings" that would be dreaded. 

In the same author: 

> "I will lift up my hand to the nations, and set up my standard to the peoples; and they will bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders. **Kings** will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers" <term>XLIX</term>: 22, 23. 

"Nations" and "daughters" represent "goods," while "peoples" and "sons" represent "truths," as shown in Part One (nations as goods: sections 1259, 1260, 1416, 1849; daughters similarly: 489, 490, 491; peoples as truths: 1259, 1260; sons similarly: 489, 491, 533, 1147). Therefore, "kings" stand for "truths" in general, which provide spiritual nourishment, and "queens" <note>original: *dominae*</note> for "goods," which provide nursing. Whether you say "goods and truths" or "those who are in goods and truths," the meaning is the same. 

In the same author: 

> "He will sprinkle many nations; **kings** will shut their mouths because of him; for what had not been told them they will see, and what they had not heard they will understand" <term>LII</term>: 15. 

This refers to the coming of the Lord; "nations" stands for those affected by "goods," and "kings" for those affected by "truths." 

In David: 

> "Now therefore, O **kings**, be wise; be instructed, you judges of the earth; serve Jehovah with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry and you perish in the way" (Psalm <term>II</term>: 10, 11, 12). 

"Kings" stands for those who are in truths; they are also frequently called "king's sons" because of those truths. "The Son" here stands for the Lord, who is called "the Son" because he is Truth itself, and all truth comes from him. 

In John: 

> "They sang a new song: You are worthy to take the book, and..."

> "...you may open its seals; you have made us **kings** and **priests** to our God, so that we may reign upon the earth" <note>original: "aperias sigilla ejus; fecisti nos Deo nostro Reges & Sacerdotes, ut regnemus super terra," Revelation 5:9, 10</note>. In this passage, those who are in possession of "truths" are called **kings**. The Lord also calls them "sons of the kingdom" in Matthew: "He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man; the field is the world; the seed are the **sons of the kingdom**, and the weeds are the sons of the evil one" <term>XIII</term>: 37, 38. 

In the book of John, it is written: 

> "The sixth angel poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the **kings** from the rising of the sun" <note>original: "Sextus Angelus effudit phialam suam super fluvium magnum Euphratem, cujus exsiccata est aqua, ut pararetur via Regum, qui ab oriente solis," Revelation 16:12</note>. 

It is clear that "Euphrates" does not mean the literal river, nor do "kings from the rising of the sun" mean literal kings from that region. Regarding the meaning of the Euphrates, see notes 120, 1585, and 1866. From this, it is evident that the "way of the kings from the rising of the sun" refers to the truths of faith that come from the "goods of love" <note>The "rising of the sun" or the East symbolizes the Lord and His love.</note>. 

In the same book: 

> "The nations who are saved shall walk in its light, and the **kings of the earth** shall bring their glory and honor into it" <note>original: "Gentes, quæ salvantur, in luce ejus ambulabunt, & Regis terræ adferent gloriam & honorem suum in eam," Revelation 21:24</note>. 

Here, "nations" <term>original: gentes</term> stands for those who are in "goods," and "kings of the earth" for those who are in "truths." This is further proven by the fact that these are prophetic writings, not historical ones. Again: 

> "With the great prostitute sitting upon many waters, the **kings of the earth** have committed fornication, and were made drunk with the wine of her fornication" <note>original: "Cum meretrice magna sedente super aquis multis, scortati sunt Reges terræ, & inebriati sunt vino scortationis ejus," Revelation 17:2</note>. 

And elsewhere: 

> "Babylon has made all nations drink the wine of her fornication, and the **kings of the earth** have committed fornication with her" <note>original: "Babylon ex vino scortationis suæ potavit omnes gentes, & Reges terræ cum ea scortati sunt," Revelation 18:3, 9</note>. 

In these verses, it is likewise clear that "kings of the earth" do not mean literal kings. Instead, the passage describes the falsification and corruption <term>original: scortatio; literally "fornication"</term> of the doctrine of faith—that is, the corruption of truth. "Kings of the earth" represent those truths which have been falsified and corrupted. 

In the same book: 

> "The ten horns you saw are **ten kings**, who have not yet received a kingdom. They receive power as if for one hour with the beast; these will have one mind, and will hand over their power and authority to the beast" <note>original: "Decem cornua, quæ vidisti, decem Reges sunt, qui nondum regnum acceperunt. potestatem tanquam unam horam accipiunt cum bestia; hi unam mentem habebunt, & potentiam & potestatem suam tradent bestiæ," Revelation 17:12, 13</note>. 

It is obvious to anyone that "kings" here are not literal kings; otherwise, it would be entirely unintelligible why ten kings would receive power for only "one hour." Similarly: 

> "I saw the beast and the **kings of the earth**, and their armies gathered to make war with him who sat upon the horse, and with his army" <note>original: "Vidi bestiam & Reges terræ, & exercitus eorum congregatos ad faciendum bellum cum sedente super equo, & cum exercitu ejus," Revelation 19:19</note>. 

It is openly stated in verse 13 that the "one sitting on the horse" is the **Word of God**. The "kings of the earth" are said to be gathered against him. Here, the "beast" represents "goods of love" that have been profaned, and "kings" represent "truths of faith" that have been corrupted. They are called "kings of the earth" because they are within the Church (as "the earth" signifies the Church; see notes 662, 1066, 1067, 1262). The "white horse" represents the understanding of truth, and the "one sitting upon the horse" represents the Word. 

This is even more manifest in Daniel, Chapter 11, which discusses the war between the **King of the South** and the **King of the North**. These terms signify truths and falsehoods that struggle against one another; their spiritual conflicts are described there historically as wars. 

Because a "king" signifies Truth, we can understand the internal sense of why the Lord is called both **King** and **Priest**, and what "kings" and "priests" represented in the Lord’s time. Kings represented His **Divine Truth**, and priests represented His **Divine Good**. All the laws of order by which the Lord governs the universe as King are "Truths"; however, all the laws by which He governs the universe as Priest—and by which He rules those very truths—are "Goods." For a government based on Truth alone would condemn everyone to hell, but a government based on Goodness/Mercy lifts them out of there and raises them into heaven (see note 1728). Because...

These two qualities are joined in the Lord and were represented in ancient times by the union of Kingship and the Priesthood. This is seen in the case of Melchizedek, who was both the **King of Salem** and, at the same time, a **Priest to God Most High** <note>original: "Rex Schalem & simul Sacerdos Deo Altissimo," Genesis 14:18</note>. Later, among the Jews, the **Representative Church**—in its own institutional form—was established through Judges and Priests, and then through Kings. However, because kings were meant to represent **Truths** (which ought not to rule on their own because, as previously stated, Truth alone condemns), the establishment of earthly kings was so displeasing that the people were rebuked. The nature of Truth when viewed in isolation was described through the "rights of kings" in 1 Samuel 8:11–18. Earlier, through Moses, it was commanded in Deuteronomy 17:14–18 that the people should choose genuine Truth (that which comes from Good) rather than spurious truth, and that they should not corrupt it with mere reasoning or scientific facts. This is the underlying meaning of the laws concerning kings in the passage from Moses. No one can see this from the literal sense of the words alone, yet it is evident in every detail of the **internal sense** <term>internal sense</term> <note>the deeper spiritual meaning of the Bible hidden beneath the literal text</note>. From this, it is clear that "King" and "Kingship" represent and signify nothing other than **Truth**.

2016. Regarding the fact that all **Good** and, consequently, all **Truth** comes from the Lord, this is a constant truth. Angels possess such perception that they can feel how much of what is good and true comes from the Lord, and how much of what is evil and false comes from themselves. They even confess this to newly arrived souls and to spirits who doubt. They go even further, stating that they are held back from the evil and falsity of their own selfhood <term>proprium</term> <note>the "ego" or "own-self" of a person, which is naturally inclined toward selfish desires</note> and are kept in good and truth by the Lord. This holding-back and the actual **influence** <term>influx</term> <note>the spiritual flow of life and thought from God into the human mind</note> is perceivable to them (see note 1614). 

However, for a human to think that they do good or think truth from themselves is an appearance. This happens because humans are in a state where they lack perception and are in the deepest obscurity regarding this spiritual influence. Therefore, they conclude based on appearance and fallacy—a belief they will not let go of as long as they trust only their senses and reason from them. Yet, even though this is the reality, a person must still do good and think truth **as if from themselves**. Otherwise, they cannot be reformed or regenerated. For the reason why this is so, see notes 1937 and 1947. 

This verse deals with the **Human Essence** of the Lord being united to the **Divine Essence**. The fact that all good and truth comes to humanity from the Divine Essence through His Human Essence is a Divine secret <term>arcanum</term> that few believe because they do not understand it. Many think Divine Good can reach a person without the Lord’s Human being united to the Divine. However, it was previously shown in notes 1676 and 1990 that this is impossible. Specifically, humanity has removed itself so far from the Supreme Divine through the lusts they have immersed themselves in and the falsities that have blinded them, that there could never have been any influence of the Divine into the rational mind except through the Human, which the Lord united to the Divine within Himself. Communication was established through His Human; for in this way, the Supreme Divine could reach humanity. The Lord states this openly in several places, saying that He is **the way**, and that there is no access to the Father except through Him. This is what is meant here: that from Him—specifically the Human united to the Divine—comes all good and all truth.

### CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

*And to your seed after you.* "I will establish my covenant between Me and you," signifies **union**. "And between your seed after you," signifies **conjunction** <term>conjunction</term><note>A spiritual connection or joining together, distinct from a total union of essence.</note> with those who have faith in Him. "Throughout their generations," signifies those things which belong to faith. "For an everlasting covenant," signifies conjunction with these people. "To be a God to you," signifies the Divine of the Lord within Himself. "And to your seed after you," signifies the resulting Divine among those who have faith in Him.

2018. **I will establish my covenant between me and you**, which signifies **union**, is evident from the meaning of a "covenant" <note>original: "fœdus"</note> as a union (as discussed previously in numbers 665, 666, 1023, and 1038). This union is the primary subject of this chapter and has been discussed throughout this work. It has been shown that Jehovah, who is speaking here, was within the Lord because they were one from the very first conception and birth. Since the Lord was conceived from Jehovah, His "Internal" was Jehovah. 

This can be illustrated by the human experience (as noted in number 1999): a person’s soul is one with their body, or their internal is one with their external, even though they are distinct from each other. Sometimes they are so distinct that one struggles against the other, as happens during spiritual temptations. In those moments, the Internal rebukes the External and seeks to reject the evil within it. Yet they remain joined, or are "one," because both the soul and the body belong to the same person. 

For example: consider someone who thinks one thing but shows another on their face, speaks differently with their mouth, or acts differently with their gestures. In that case, the Interior disagrees with the External, yet they are still one, for the thought belongs to the person just as much as the facial expression, speech, or gesture does. However, **union** occurs when these things—the face, the speech, and the gestures—agree with the thought. This is provided for illustration.

2019. **And between your seed after you**, which signifies **conjunction** with those who have faith in Him, is evident from the meaning of "Seed," which is faith (see numbers 1025, 1447, and 1610). It is also evident from the meaning of "After you," which means to follow. It is a common formula in the Word <term>the Word</term><note>The Bible or Holy Scripture.</note> to "walk after" someone (as in Jeremiah 7:6, 8:2; Ezekiel 20:16; and also Mark 8:34, Luke 9:23, and 14:27). Therefore, "seed after you" here signifies those who are in faith and follow the Lord. In the internal sense, it signifies those who are "born" from Him.

2020. **Throughout their generations**, which signifies those things belonging to faith, is evident from the meaning of "Generations." These are the things generated and born from **charity** <note>original: "charitate"</note>—that is, all things of faith. Or, what is the same, "generations" refers to all those who are regenerated by the Lord, in whom the faith of charity exists. (By the Lord’s Divine Mercy, this will be discussed in the following pages.) It was shown in the first part of this work (numbers 613, 1041, 1145, and 1330) that "Generations," as well as "Births," signify these spiritual things in the internal sense.

2021. **For an everlasting covenant**, which signifies **conjunction** with these people, is evident from the meaning of a "covenant" as a conjunction (as noted before in numbers 665, 666, 1023, and 1038). That it refers to those called "seed" is clear because it follows immediately after, and because "covenant" is mentioned twice in this verse. The first mention refers to the **union** of Jehovah with the Human Essence, and the second refers to the **conjunction** with those who are the "seed." 

To have a clearer idea regarding the Union of the Lord’s Divine Essence with His Human Essence, and the Lord’s Conjunction with the human race through the faith of charity, it is helpful here and in the following sections to call the first "Union" and the second "Conjunction."

This **conjunction** <note>original: "Conjunctionem"</note> was also the union of the Lord’s Divine Essence with His Human Essence. However, the connection between the Lord and the human race through the faith of charity is called "conjunction." This is clear because Jehovah, or the Lord, is Life itself. His Human Essence also became Life, as shown above. The meeting of Life with Life is a **union**. 

But a human being is not Life itself; they are only a recipient of life, as was also shown before. When Life flows into a recipient of life, it is called a **conjunction**. The recipient is adapted to life like a passive subject to an active force, or like something living in itself acting upon something dead in itself, which then receives life. While the "principal" and the "instrumental" <note>scholarly terms used to describe a primary cause and the tool it uses to act</note> appear to be joined as if they were one, they are nonetheless not one; each exists distinctly. Humans do not live from themselves, but the Lord, out of His mercy, joins them to Himself and thus makes them live forever. Because the Lord and humanity are so distinct, this relationship is called **conjunction**.

2022. **To be a God to you**, which signifies the Divine of the Lord within Himself, is evident from what was said above regarding the Lord’s Divine Essence being within Him.

2023. **And to your seed after you**, which signifies the resulting Divine among those who have faith in Him, is clear from the meaning of **Seed** as the "faith of charity" (see numbers 1025, 1447, 1610). It also follows from the meaning of the phrase **After you**, which refers to following Him (as mentioned just above in number 2019). 

The "Divine" among those who have faith in Him is Love and Charity. By **Love**, we mean love for the Lord; by **Charity**, we mean love toward the neighbor. Love for the Lord can never be separated from love for the neighbor. This is because the Lord’s love is toward the entire human race; He wants to save everyone for eternity and join them closely to Himself so that none of them perish. Therefore, whoever has love for the Lord shares in the Lord’s love, and thus cannot help but love their neighbor. 

However, not everyone who has love for their neighbor is necessarily in a state of love for the Lord in the same way. This is the case for righteous Gentiles <note>non-Christians or those outside the formal church</note> who are in ignorance regarding the Lord, yet the Lord is still present with them in their charity (as shown in Part One, numbers 1032 and 1059). This also applies to others within the Church. Love for the Lord is of a higher degree. Those who have love for the Lord are called "celestial" people, while those who have love for the neighbor (charity) are called "spiritual" people. The **Most Ancient Church**, which existed before the Flood and was celestial, focused on love for the Lord. The **Ancient Church**, which existed after the Flood and was spiritual, focused on love for the neighbor, or charity. This distinction between love and charity will be maintained whenever they are named in the following text.

2024. Verse 8. *And I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.* 

**I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land of your sojournings**, signifies that the Lord acquired all things for Himself by His own power—these things are meant by the "land of sojournings." **I will give to you** signifies that everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to Him. **And to your seed after you** signifies that He will give these things to those who have faith in Him. **All the land of Canaan** signifies the heavenly Kingdom. **For an everlasting possession** signifies forever. **And I will be their God** signifies that He is the one God.

2025. **"Which I will give to you and to your seed after you, the land of your sojourning,"** <note>original: "terram peregrinationum tuarum"</note> signifies that the Lord acquired all things for Himself by His own power. These things are represented by the "land of sojourning." This is evident from the meaning of **sojourning** (or traveling), which signifies being instructed (as seen in number 1463). Because a person acquires life for themselves primarily through instruction in <term>scientific facts</term> <note>original: "scientificis," referring here to external data or learned knowledge</note>, doctrines, and the knowledges of faith, "sojourning" represents the life acquired in this way. 

When applied to the Lord, this refers to the life which He prepared for Himself through knowledges, the struggles of temptations, and His victories in those temptations. Because He prepared this life for Himself by His own power, it is signified here by the **land of sojourning**. That the Lord prepared all things for Himself by His own power—and by His own power united the Human Essence to the Divine and the Divine to the Human—becoming Justice through His own merit, is clearly stated in the Prophets. For example, in Isaiah: 

> "Who is this, coming from Edom, marching in the greatness of His strength? I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples there was no one with me. I looked around, and there was no one helping; and I was stunned, and there was no one supporting; therefore my own arm brought salvation to me." <term>63</term>: 1, 2, 5. 

**Edom** represents the Lord’s Human Essence; **strength** and **arm** represent power. It is clearly stated to be from His own power because it says, "there was no one helping" and "no one supporting," and that His "own arm" brought Him salvation. Similarly, in the same Prophet: 

> "He saw that there was no one, and was stunned that there was no mediator; therefore His own arm brought salvation to Him, and His own Justice supported Him. He put on Justice like a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on His head." <term>59</term>: 16, 17. 

This likewise shows He acted by His own power and thus became **Justice**. That the Lord is Justice is stated in Daniel: 

> "Seventy weeks are determined to atone for iniquity, and to bring in the Justice of the ages, to seal up the vision and the prophet, and to anoint the Holy of Holies." <term>9</term>: 24. 

And in Jeremiah: 

> "I will raise up for David a righteous branch, and He shall reign as King, and shall act wisely, and shall execute judgment and Justice on the earth. In His days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell in confidence; and this is His Name by which they shall call Him: *Jehovah our Justice*." <term>23</term>: 5, 6; Chapter <term>33</term>: 15, 16. 

For this reason, He is also called the **Dwelling Place of Justice** in Jeremiah <term>31</term>: 23 and Chapter <term>50</term>: 7; and in Isaiah, He is called **Wonderful** and **Hero**. <term>9</term>: 6.

The reason the Lord so often attributes to the "Father" what is actually His own was explained above (numbers 1999, 2004). This is because Jehovah was within Him, and consequently, in every single part of Him. This can be illustrated by a human example, though it is not a perfect comparison: a person's soul is within them, and because it is within them, it is in the most specific parts of their thoughts and actions. Whatever does not have the soul within it is not truly theirs. 

The Lord’s soul was Life itself, or Being <note>original: "Esse"</note> itself, which is Jehovah, for He was conceived of Jehovah. Thus, Jehovah was in every single part of Him. And because Life itself, or Being itself (which is Jehovah), was His—just as a soul belongs to a person—all that belonged to Jehovah was His. This is what the Lord means when He says He is "in the bosom of the Father" (John <term>1</term>: 18) and that "all things that the Father has are mine" (John <term>16</term>: 15; Chapter <term>17</term>: 10, 11). 

From **Good**, which belongs to Jehovah, He united the Divine Essence to the Human; and from **Truth**, He united the Human Essence to the Divine. Thus, He did all things from Himself. Indeed, His Human was left to itself so that it might fight by itself against all the hells...

...and that He might overcome them; and because He had life in Himself, as was said, which was His own, He conquered them by His own power and strength, as is also clearly stated in the Prophets in the cited passages. From this now, because He acquired all things for Himself by His own strength, having become **Justice**, He rescued the world of spirits from infernal geniuses and spirits, and thus liberated the human race from destruction—for the human race is governed by spirits—and so redeemed it. Therefore, in the Word of the Old Testament, He is so often called **Deliverer**, **Redeemer**, and **Savior**, which is His name: **Jesus**.

2026. **"Which I will give to you"** signifies that all things in the heavens and on the earth are His. This follows from what has just been said. In the literal sense, "to give to you" means that God or Jehovah would give to Him—just as it says in the Gospels that the Father gave Him all things in heaven and on earth. However, in the **internal sense** <note>original: "sensus internus," the deeper spiritual meaning within the literal words of scripture</note>, where the truth itself is presented in its purity, it means that the Lord acquired these things for Himself, because Jehovah was in Him and in every part of Him, as was stated. 

This can be illustrated by a comparison: it is like when a person’s inner or <term>rational mind</term> <note>original: "Rationale," the part of the human mind that reasons and connects spiritual truths to worldly experience</note>, or their thought, says that their physical body should have rest or peace if it stopped doing this or that. In this case, the one speaking is the same person as the one being spoken to, for both the rational and the physical belong to the same person. Furthermore, that all things in the heavens and on the earth belong to the Lord is clear from many passages of the Word—not only from the Old Testament but also from the Gospels (Matthew 11:27; Luke 10:22; John 3:34, 35; 17:2; 28:18) and from what was shown in the first part (numbers 458, 551, 552, 1607). 

Because the Lord rules the entire Heaven, He also rules all things on the earth. These are so connected that whoever rules one rules all. For the heaven of **angelic spirits** <note>original: "spirituum angelicorum," spirits in the process of becoming angels or residing in the lower heavens</note> depends on the Heaven of angels; from that depends the **world of spirits**; and from that, in turn, the human race. Similarly, all things in the world and in nature depend on the Heavens; for without **influx** <note>original: "influxus," the flow of life or influence from the spiritual world into the natural world</note> from the Lord through the heavens, nothing that exists in nature and its threefold kingdom could ever exist or persist (see number 1632).

Those who place **merit** in their own life’s actions do not possess the faith of charity, and thus they are not the "seed" meant here. They wish to be saved not by the Lord’s Justice, but by their own. The fact that they have no faith of charity—that is, no charity—is evident because they prefer themselves to others. They look only at themselves, or at others only as much as those others serve them; those who are unwilling to serve them, they either despise or hate. Thus, through **self-love**, they drive people apart and never unite them. By doing so, they destroy what is heavenly, namely **mutual love**, which is the very foundation of heaven; for heaven itself, and all its community and harmony, exists and consists in that love. Whatever destroys harmony in the next life is contrary to the order of heaven itself, and thus conspires toward the destruction of the whole. Such are those who place merit in their own life’s actions and claim justice for themselves. There are many such people in the next life; at times they...

### CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

...world is a mystery <note>original: "arcanum"</note> that many people wonder about. Because they do not understand it, they do not believe it; and because they do not believe it simply because they cannot grasp it, it becomes a "stumbling block" <note>original: "scandalum"</note> to them. It has been shown through much experience that this is the case for those who enter the afterlife. Many of them—even the most clever in the world—find that as soon as they think about how the Lord became a man, lived like any other man in His external form, and suffered, yet still rules the universe, they immediately fill their spiritual atmosphere <note>original: "sphæram"; the "sphere" or aura of a person's inner thoughts and feelings</note> with objections. This is because this was a stumbling block to them during their earthly life, even if they never spoke of it publicly and even if they worshipped Him with outward holiness. In the afterlife, one’s inner thoughts are open and revealed through the "sphere" they radiate (as discussed in Part One, numbers 1048, 1053, 1316, 1504). In this way, it is clearly perceived what kind of faith they truly had and what they thought of the Lord.

Since this is the case, it is worth explaining briefly how the matter stands. After everything celestial in man had died out—that is, all love for God, so that there was no longer any will for what is good—the human race was separated from the Divine. Nothing joins us to God except love. When love ceased, a "disjunction" <note>original: "disjunctio"; a total separation or disconnection</note> occurred, and with that separation comes destruction and total loss. Therefore, a promise was made about the Lord’s coming into the world, who would unite the **Human** to the **Divine** and, through this union, join the human race to Himself through the faith of love and charity <note>original: "charitatis"; selfless love for others</note>. From the time of the first promise (found in Genesis 3:15), faith in the coming Lord served as this connection. 

However, when there was no longer any faith of love left on the earth, the Lord came and united His **Human Essence** to the **Divine Essence** so that they were entirely one, just as He clearly stated. At the same time, He taught the way of truth: that everyone who believes in Him—meaning everyone who loves Him and the things that belong to Him, and lives in His love (which is love toward the whole human race and thus toward one's neighbor)—would be connected to Him and saved. 

When the **Human** became **Divine** and the **Divine** became **Human** in the Lord, an "influx" <note>original: "influxus"; a spiritual flowing-in of energy or life</note> from the Infinite or Highest Divine became possible for humanity. This could never have happened otherwise. Through this union, the "dreadful false beliefs" <note>original: "diræ persuasiones falsi"</note> and the "dreadful cravings for evil" <note>original: "diræ cupiditates mali"</note> that filled the <term>world of spirits</term> were cleared away. This world of spirits was being continually flooded by souls coming from the physical world; those who lived in such evils were cast into the hells and thus separated from the rest. Had this not been done, the human race would have perished, for humanity is governed by the Lord through spirits. These evils could not have been cleared away in any other way, because the Divine power could not operate through the human "rational" mind into the "internal sensory" levels of man while those levels were so far removed from the Highest Divine. 

Beyond this, there are even deeper mysteries that are far beyond any person's ability to understand (see numbers 1676, 1990, 2016). It should also be noted that the Lord appears as a **Sun** in the heaven of "celestial" angels and as a **Moon** in the heaven of "spiritual" angels. The Sun represents His celestial love, and the Moon represents His spiritual love (see numbers 1053, 1521, 1529, 1530, 1531). All things, down to the smallest detail, are under His sight (see numbers 1274 and 1277).

2035. **In their generations.** That this signifies the things that belong to faith is evident from the meaning of "generations" and "births," which refer to the components of faith (as seen in numbers 613, 1145, 1255, 1330). The things that belong to love and faith are related to each other like the family ties and lineages of generations (see numbers 685, 917).

2036. **Verse 10.** *“This is my covenant, which you shall keep between Me and you, and your seed after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.”* <note>original: "Hoc foedus meum, quod custodietis inter Me & inter vos..."</note> **“This is my covenant, which you shall keep between Me and you”** signifies a sign of the conjunction <note>original: "conjunctionis"; a spiritual joining or union</note> of everyone with the Lord. **“And your seed after you”** signifies those who have faith in Him. **“Every male among you shall be circumcised”** signifies purity.

2037. **“This is my covenant, which you shall keep between Me and you,”** which signifies a sign of the conjunction of everyone with the Lord, is evident from the meaning of a **covenant** as a "conjunction" (as discussed previously). That it is a "sign" or "indication" of conjunction here is clear from the following verse, where it is explicitly called the **Sign of the covenant**: *“You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.”* All the **External Rituals** of the Church were signs of the covenant; they were to be held as holy because they symbolized **Internal Realities**.

Circumcision, which is the subject here, was nothing more than a representative <note>original: "Ritus repraesentativus"; a physical act that mirrors or represents a spiritual truth</note> and symbolic rite, as will be discussed in what follows. Yet, such rites are frequently called a "covenant" in the Word because external things represented—and thus symbolized—internal things. The internal things are what actually constitute the covenant because they are what truly join us to God. External things do not join us to God except through internal ones; the externals were only "signs of the covenant" or indicators of conjunction, by which people might be reminded of internal truths and thus be joined to God through them. (Regarding signs of the covenant, see number 1308). All internal things belonging to the covenant, or which create a union, relate to **love and charity** and proceed from them. For upon these two—namely, loving the Lord above oneself and one's neighbor as oneself—hang all the law and all the prophets, which is to say, the entire doctrine of faith (Matthew 22:34–39; Mark 12:28–35).

2038. **“And your seed after you,”** which signifies those who have faith in Him, is evident from the meaning of **“seed,”** which refers to faith derived from charity <note>original: "fides ex charitate"; faith that is lived out through love for others, not just intellectual belief</note>, as discussed previously.

2039. **“Every male shall be circumcised,”** which signifies purity, is evident from the "representation" and the resulting meaning of "to circumcise" in the internal sense. Circumcision, or the cutting away of the foreskin, signified nothing other than the removal and wiping away of those things that hindered and polluted **heavenly love** <note>original: "amor coelestis"</note>. These are the "evils of lusts," especially the lusts of self-love and the false ideas that come from them.

The reason for this symbolism is that the reproductive organs of both sexes represent heavenly love. There are three kinds of love that constitute the heavenly aspects of the Lord’s Kingdom:
1.  **Conjugial love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis"; the deep, spiritual love between spouses</note>, which is the primary love of all, for its end is the greatest use: the propagation of the human race and, consequently, the Lord's Kingdom, for which the human race is the nursery.
2.  **Love for children**, which follows closely and stems from the first.
3.  **Mutual love**, or the love of society.

Whatever covers, hinders, or defiles these loves is signified by the **foreskin**. Therefore, its removal (circumcision) was made into a representative act. To the extent that the evils of lusts and their false ideas are removed, a person is purified, and to that same extent, heavenly love can become visible. How contrary and filthy self-love is compared to heavenly love has been stated and shown in numbers 760, 1307, 1308, 1321, 1594, 2045, and 2057. From these points, it is clear...

2041. **"You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin":** That this signifies the removal of the love of self and the world is clear from the representation and meaning of Circumcision, which is purification from foul loves (as mentioned just above in number 2039). It is also clear from the meaning of "Flesh," which refers to a person's <term>proprium: The Latin term for a person's "own" nature, ego, or the sense of self that feels independent from God.</term> (as seen in number 999). A person's *proprium* is nothing but the love of self and the world, along with every selfish desire that comes from them. The foulness of this *proprium* was shown in the First Part (numbers 141, 150, 154, 210, 215, 694, 731, 874, 875, 876, 987, 1047). Because it is this *proprium* that must be removed, it is here called the "flesh of the foreskin."

There are two loves, so named, and their associated desires, which block the flow of heavenly love from the Lord. When these rule over a person’s inner and outer self and occupy them, they either reject or stifle the incoming heavenly love; they even pervert and contaminate it, for they are completely opposite to heavenly love. That they are completely opposite will be demonstrated, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, in the following pages. 

However, as much as these selfish loves are removed, heavenly love flowing from the Lord begins to appear—indeed, to shine—in the person's inner self. Then the person begins to see that they are in evil and falsity, and eventually they see these things as "unclean and foul" <note>original: "immundo & spurco"</note>, finally realizing that this was their own *proprium*. This happens to those who are being "regenerated" (spiritually reborn). This can even be perceived by those who are not being regenerated: when the desires of those loves are quiet—which happens sometimes during holy meditation, or when they are "put to sleep" during misfortunes, sickness, or disease, and especially at the moment of death—then, because bodily and worldly things are dormant and as if dead, they perceive...

2042. **And it shall be for a sign of the covenant between Me and you.** That this signifies a representation and a symbol of purity is evident from what was shown just above (number 2039)—namely, that circumcision was nothing other than a representation of purification from foul loves <note>original: "amoribus spurcis"</note>. Thus, a "week" is called a period, whether it lasts a thousand years, a hundred, or ten; it also applies to days, hours, minutes, and so forth, as can be seen from the passages cited in Part One (number 728). Because the eighth day is the first day of the following week, it signifies any beginning. From this it is also clear that just as circumcision itself was a representation of purification, so too was the timing—the eighth day. This does not mean that they then entered into a purer state and were therefore purified, but that just as circumcision signified purification, the eighth day signified that it must be done at all times, and thus always as if from a new beginning.
