# GENESIS

...they truly are. For there is a certain pleasure and delight that soothes, favors, and flatters, making people love that kind of life and prefer it over any other. Because of this, they believe there is no evil in it; for whatever supports a person’s love, and thus their life, is believed to be good. Consequently, the rational mind agrees and suggests false reasons to confirm this, which blind the person to such an extent that they cannot see what heavenly love is. Even if they did see it, they would say in their hearts that it is something miserable, or nothing at all, or a mere fantasy that grips the mind like a sickness. 

Yet, any person can see—if they are willing to think from the rational faculty they have been given—that a life driven by self-love and love of the world, with its pleasures and delights, is foul and unclean. Self-love <note>original: "amor sui"</note> is the source of all the evils that destroy civil society. From it, as if from a filthy well, flow all forms of hatred, all acts of revenge, all cruelties, and indeed all adulteries. For someone who loves themselves either despises, criticizes, or hates everyone else who does not serve them, honor them, or favor them. When they feel hatred, they breathe nothing but revenge and cruelty—and they do this to the same degree that they love themselves. 

Thus, that love is destructive to society and the human race. For further proof of its nature, see what was said in the First Part regarding this (numbers 693, 694, 760, 1307, 1308, 1321, 1506, 1594, 1691, and 1862). In the afterlife, self-love is most foul and is the direct opposite of mutual love, which is what makes up Heaven; this will be discussed in the following pages by the Lord’s Divine Mercy. Because hatred, revenge, cruelty, and adultery spring from self-love, it is the source of everything called sin, crime, abomination, and profanation. 

Therefore, when self-love resides in a person’s rational mind and in the cravings and fantasies of their external self, the flow of heavenly love from the Lord is continually blocked, distorted, and contaminated. It is like a foul waste that ruins every sweet smell—indeed, it defiles it. It is like an object that turns the continually flowing rays of light into hideous and black colors. It is like a tiger or a serpent that rejects kindness and kills those who offer it food with its bite and venom. Or it is like a criminal who turns the best intentions and even the favors of others into insults and malice. From this, it is clear that these loves—namely self-love and love of the world—are what are represented and signified by the foreskins which must be cut away.

**2046.** The fact that **every male** signifies those who are in the truth of faith is evident from the symbolic meaning of a "male" as truth (as discussed in numbers 672 and 749). The reason the text specifies the male (signifying the truth of faith) is that no one can be purified from those foul loves unless they possess the truth. It is through truth that a person learns what is pure and impure, and what is holy and profane. Until a person knows this, there are no means through which heavenly love (which flows continually from the Lord) can work; for heavenly love can only be received within truths. 

Therefore, a person is reformed and regenerated <note>original: "reformatur & regeneratur"; "regeneration" refers to the spiritual process of being "born again" or made new by God</note> through the knowledge of truth, and this does not happen until they have been thoroughly imbued with those truths. Conscience itself is formed through the truths of faith; for conscience is the sense of what is true and right, which is given to those who are being regenerated (on this, see numbers 977, 986, 1033, 1076, and 1077). This is also the reason why stone knives—or "swords of flint," as they are called—were used for circumcision; as shown above (at the end of number 2039), these signify truths.

# CHAPTER SEVENTEEN

2047. **Throughout your generations**, <note>original: "In generationes vestras"</note> which signifies the things that belong to faith. This is evident from the meaning of "Generations" and "Births," which refer to matters of faith (as discussed in numbers 613, 1145, 1255, 2020, and 2035).

2048. That **one born in the house** <note>original: "natus domus"</note> signifies **celestial people**, and that **one bought with silver** <note>original: "emptio argenti"</note> signifies **spiritual people**—that is, those within the Church—is evident from the meaning of being "born in the house." In the Word, a "house" signifies what is **celestial** <note>term: celestial; Swedenborg’s term for the highest level of heaven or the mind, characterized by direct love for the Lord</note> because this is the most internal level. For this reason, in a universal sense, the "House of God" signifies the Lord’s Kingdom; in a less universal sense, it signifies the Church; and in a particular sense, it signifies the person themselves in whom the Kingdom or Church of the Lord exists. When a person is called a "house," it signifies the celestial aspect of faith in them; when they are called a "temple," it signifies the truth of faith in them. Thus, here, those "born in the house" signify celestial people.

Furthermore, that being "bought with silver" signifies spiritual people is clear from the meaning of **silver**, which is truth, and thus the spiritual aspect of faith (as discussed in Part One, number 1551). **Celestial people** are those who are in love for the Lord. Because the Most Ancient Church (which existed before the flood) was in that love, it was a "Celestial Church." **Spiritual people** <note>term: spiritual; in this context, those whose faith is rooted in neighborly love and doctrinal truth rather than direct celestial perception</note> are those who are in love toward the neighbor and thus in the truth of faith. Such was the Ancient Church (which existed after the flood). The distinction between the Celestial and the Spiritual has been discussed many times in Part One. Anyone can see that there are heavenly secrets <note>original: "arcana coelestia"</note> here: specifically, that those "born in the house" and those "bought with silver" were to be circumcised, as well as the sons of foreigners. These groups are mentioned several times (as in verses 13, 23, and 27), and these mysteries are only revealed through the **internal sense**. This sense shows that those "born in the house" and "bought with silver" signify the celestial and spiritual—those within the Church—while the **son of a foreigner** <note>original: "filius alienigena"</note> who is not of your seed signifies those who are outside the Church.

2049. **From every son of a foreigner, who is not of your seed**, which signifies those who are outside the Church. This is evident from the meaning of "son of a foreigner" as those not born within the Church, and thus not in the goods and truths of faith because they lack knowledge of them. "Sons of foreigners" can also signify those who are in external worship (as discussed in number 1097), but that refers to people within the Church. Here, however, because the passage concerns the Lord's Church in a universal sense, "sons of foreigners" are those not born within the Church, such as the **Gentiles** <note>term: Gentiles; historically, non-Jewish nations, but used here to mean people outside the revealed Church who lack the Word</note>.

Gentiles who are outside the Church can be in truths, but not the **truths of faith**. Their truths are like the commands of the **Decalogue** <note>term: Decalogue; the Ten Commandments</note>: that parents are to be honored, that one must not kill, steal, commit adultery, or covet the belongings of others, and that the Divine must be worshiped. But the "truths of faith" are all the doctrinal teachings about eternal life, the Lord's Kingdom, and the Lord Himself. These cannot be known to them because they do not have the Word. These are the people signified by the "sons of foreigners" who are not of the seed, yet are to be circumcised—that is, purified. From this, it is clear that they can be purified just as easily as those within the Church, which was represented by circumcision. They are purified when they reject foul loves <note>original: "spurcos amores"</note> and live among themselves in **charity**. When they do this, they are living in truths, for all truths belong to charity (though these are the general moral truths mentioned before). Those who live in these truths easily absorb the truths of faith—if not during their physical life, then certainly in the afterlife—because the truths of faith are the internal truths of charity. # GENESIS CHAPTER XVII

...the more interior truths of charity are admitted. The internal aspects of charity are what the Lord’s Kingdom consists of; regarding these, see numbers 932, 1032, 1059, 1327, 1328, and 1366. In the other life, the mere science of the knowledge of faith <note>original: "scientia cognitionum fidei"</note> counts for nothing. For the worst people—even those in hell—can possess such knowledge, sometimes even more than others. Rather, what matters is a life lived according to that knowledge, for all knowledge has life as its end. Unless things are learned for the sake of living well, they are of no use, except perhaps for talking about them and being considered learned in the world, being raised to honors, or gaining reputation and wealth.

From this, it is clear that a life of faith's knowledge is nothing other than a life of charity. For the "Law and the Prophets"—that is, the entire doctrine of faith with all its knowledge—consists in Love for the Lord and love toward the neighbor. This is clear to everyone from the Lord’s own words in Matthew 22:34–39 and Mark 12:28–35. Nevertheless, the doctrines or concepts of faith <note>original: "doctrinalia seu cognitiones fidei"</note> are extremely necessary for forming a life of charity, which cannot be formed without them. It is this life that saves after death, and never any "life of faith" without it; for without charity, a life of faith is impossible. Those who live a life of love and charity are in the Lord's life, and no one can be joined to Him through any other.

From this it is also clear that the truths of faith can never be acknowledged as true—that is, the "Acknowledgment" people speak of cannot exist—except externally and with the mouth, unless they are implanted in charity. Internally or in the heart, they are denied; for as was said, everything has charity as its end. If charity is not within, those truths are internally rejected. When external things are taken away, as happens in the other life, their internal nature is revealed; they are shown to be utterly contrary to all the truths of faith. It is never possible to receive the life of charity or mutual love in the other life if one had none in the life of the body; for a person's life in the world remains with them after death. Such people recoil from and hate mutual love. When they merely approach a community where the life of mutual love exists, they tremble, feel horror, and are seized with agony. 

Such people, even if they were born within the Church, are called "foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh," <note>original: "filii alienigenæ præputiati corde & præputiati carne"</note> who are not to be admitted into the Sanctuary—that is, into the Kingdom of the Lord. These are also meant in Ezekiel: "No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter My sanctuary" (Ezekiel 44:7, 9). And again in the same prophet: "To whom are you thus like in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lower world; you shall lie in the midst of the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword" (Ezekiel 31:18). This refers to Pharaoh, by whom "sciences" <note>term: sciences; here meaning general knowledge or academic learning</note> in general are signified (see numbers 1164, 1165, 1186, 1462). By the "trees of Eden," with which they would descend into the lower world, "sciences" are also meant, but specifically the sciences of the knowledge of faith. From this it is now clear what "uncircumcised" means in the internal sense: namely, one who is in filthy loves and lives according to them.

...the Lord's union with man in his impurity, and also its significance: "for an everlasting covenant" signifies a permanent union.

2051. The phrase **"circumcising, he shall be circumcised"** <note>original: "circumcidendo circumcidetur"</note> signifies that they must completely remove from themselves the loves of self and the world. Specifically, this refers to those within the Church, who are signified by those "born in the house" and "bought with silver." This is evident from the symbolic meaning of circumcision, which represents purification from the loves of self and the world, as discussed above in section 2039. It is repeated here—that "circumcising, he shall be circumcised"—to express the absolute necessity of this purification. Because it refers to those within the Church, "foreigners" are not mentioned here; as shown in section 2048, foreigners signify those outside the Church. 

From the repetition of what was said in the previous verse regarding those "born in the house" and "bought with silver," anyone can see that there is a Divine secret <note>original: "arcanum"</note> here that is not obvious from the literal sense. The secret is that purification from these foul loves is most necessary for those within the Church. This is because those within the Church can make holy things themselves impure—something those outside the Church (the Gentiles) cannot do. Therefore, the danger of damnation is greater for them. Furthermore, those within the Church can form and become steeped in false principles against the very truths of faith; those outside the Church cannot do this because they are ignorant of those truths. Thus, the former can profane holy truths, while the latter cannot. For more on this, see Part One, sections 1059, 1327, and 1328.

2052. It was shown above in section 2047 that "he who is born in your house" and "the purchase of your silver" signify those within the Church of both types: the "celestial," who are "born in the house," and the "spiritual," who are the "purchase of silver."

2053. **"My covenant shall be in your flesh"** signifies the Lord's union <note>original: "conjunctionem"</note> with man even in his impurity. This is clear from the meaning of "covenant" as a union, and from the meaning of "flesh" as man's <term>proprium</term> <note>original: "proprium" — a Latin term used to describe man's "own nature" or "self-hood," which is inherently inclined toward the ego rather than the Divine.</note>. The impurity of this self-hood was discussed in section 2041 and shown in Part One (sections 141, 150, 154, 210, 215, 694, 731, 874, 875, 876, 987, and 1047). 

The fact that "My covenant in your flesh" represents the Lord's union with man in his impurity works like this: no pure intellectual truth—that is, Divine Truth—actually exists within a person. Rather, the truths of faith held by a person are "appearances of truth" <note>original: "apparentiæ veri"</note>. These are joined to the fallacies of the senses, and these in turn are joined to the falsehoods stemming from the desires of the love of self and the world. Such are the "truths" found in man. How impure these are is evident from what they are attached to. Nevertheless, the Lord joins Himself with man in these very impurities, because He animates and gives them life through innocence and charity, and in this way forms the **conscience**. The truths of conscience vary according to each person's religion. The Lord does not wish to violate these, because the person has been steeped in them and regards them as holy, provided they are not contrary to the "goods of faith" <note>the practical benefits/deeds of faith</note>. The Lord breaks no one but gently bends them <note>original: "Dominus neminem frangit sed flectit"</note>. This is clear from the fact that within every religious doctrine in the Church, there are people who are gifted with a conscience. This conscience is better the more its truths approach the genuine truths of faith; for it is out of the truths of faith that such a conscience is formed.

It is established that this [faith] is formed in the intellectual part of man, for it is the intellectual part that receives such things. 2054. **For an everlasting covenant** <note>original: "In fœdus æternum"</note>: That this signifies a union <note>original: "conjunctionem"</note> is clear from the meaning of a "covenant," which is a union, as stated previously. Those outside are like the organs that live by means of the heart and lungs. Celestial people <note>those motivated by love</note> are like the Heart, while Spiritual people <note>those motivated by truth</note> are like the Lungs. Because of this shared necessity, the text here deals specifically with those within the Church, and the word "covenant" is repeated twice.

Those within the Church who profane the goods and truths of faith are those of whom it is said that "that soul shall be cut off from his people." For they are capable of profaning <note>original: "prophanare," meaning to treat something sacred with irreverence or to corrupt a spiritual truth one has already acknowledged</note> these things, while those outside the Church are not, as was shown in Part One, numbers 593, 1008, 1010, and 1059.

2057. **He who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin**: That this signifies one who is in self-love is established from what was said above regarding the meaning of being circumcised and of the "foreskin" (numbers 2039, 2049), as well as the meaning of "flesh" (number 2041). Here, the "flesh of the foreskin" signifies self-love. Those within the Church who are in falsehood and simultaneously in self-love are the ones who primarily profane holy things. This is not the case for those in any other kind of love, for self-love is the filthiest of all. This is because it is destructive to society and thus destructive to the human race, as shown above in number 2045. 

Furthermore, self-love is diametrically opposed to mutual love <note>original: "amori mutuo," the heavenly love of others</note>, which is the very foundation of Heaven; thus, it is destructive to heavenly order itself. This can be seen from the evil spirits and "genii" <note>original: "geniis," referring to a specific class of internal, more malicious evil spirits</note> in the other life <note>original: "altera vita," the spiritual world or afterlife</note>, as well as from the hells, where nothing reigns but self-love. Because self-love rules there, all kinds of hatred, revenge, and cruelty also reign, for these spring from it. 

Mutual love in Heaven consists in people loving their neighbor more than themselves. Because of this, the whole of Heaven represents, as it were, a single person, for everyone is joined together by the Lord through mutual love. From this, the happiness of all is shared with each individual, and the happiness of each individual is shared with all. The heavenly form is such that everyone is, as it were, a center—a center of communication and therefore of happiness from everyone else. This occurs according to all the differences of that love, which are innumerable. 

Because those who are in that love perceive the highest happiness from the fact that they can share what flows into them with others—and do so from the heart—the communication becomes perpetual and eternal. As the Lord’s Kingdom grows, so does the happiness of each individual. Though the angels are organized into distinct societies and dwellings, they do not think about this structure; rather, the Lord disposes all things and every detail. Such is the Lord’s Kingdom in the Heavens. 

However, nothing attempts to destroy this form and this order more than self-love. Therefore, all those in the other life who are in self-love are more deeply "infernal" <note>original: "infernales," belonging to hell</note> than others. Self-love shares nothing with others but instead extinguishes and suffocates the joys and happiness of others. Whatever joy flows into them from others, they take for themselves, concentrate it within themselves, turn it into the filth of self, and prevent it from being passed on any further. Thus, they destroy everything that is unanimous and social. From this comes disunity and, consequently, destruction. 

Because every one of them wants to be served, honored, and adored by others, and loves no one but himself, dissociation follows. This results in wretched states where they perceive nothing as more joyful than torturing others in dreadful ways and through fantasies, driven by hatred, revenge, and cruelty. When such spirits come toward a society where there is mutual love, they are like impure and dead weights in a pure and living atmosphere; because all the inflowing joy stops with them, they are cast down by their own nature. Because they exhale a filthy idea of self, their "joy" there is turned into a cadaverous stench <note>original: "fœtorem cadaverosum," a smell of rotting corpses</note>, which they experience as their own hell, besides being seized by agonizing distress. From this, it can be seen what the nature of self-love is: namely, that it is not only destructive to the human race, as noted in number 2045...

The Truth represented by Sarai was not yet Divine because it was not yet so united to Good that it flowed *from* Good as its source. But when it was so united to Good that it proceeded entirely from Good, it then became Divine. At that point, the Truth itself also became Good because it was the "truth of good" <note>original: *boni verum*</note>.

There is a difference between truth that strives toward Good in order to be united with it, and truth that is already united with Good so that it proceeds entirely from Good. Truth that strives toward Good still retains something from the human side. However, truth that is completely united with Good sheds everything human and puts on the Divine.

This can be illustrated by a similar process in a person. When a person is being regenerated—that is, when they are to be conjoined to the Lord—they proceed toward that conjunction through Truth, meaning the truths of faith. No one can be regenerated except through the knowledge of faith, which are the truths through which one moves toward conjunction. The Lord meets these truths with Good—that is, through charity—and fits that charity into the knowledge of faith (its truths). All truths are "receiving vessels" <note>original: *vasa recipientia*</note> for Good. Therefore, the more genuine the truths are and the more they are multiplied, the more space Good has to receive them as vessels, to bring them into order, and finally to manifest itself. This continues until the truths no longer appear except as the light of Good shining through them; thus, truth becomes "celestial spiritual" <note>original: *coeleste spirituale*</note>. Because the Lord is present only in Good (which belongs to charity alone), a person is thus conjoined to the Lord. Through Good—that is, charity—the person is gifted with a conscience, from which they then think what is true and do what is right. However, this is done according to the specific truths and right principles into which Good or charity has been fitted.

# GENESIS.

What is being discussed here is represented and symbolized by Isaac, who was to be born of Sarah. That which was represented by Ishmael was the **Rational** <term>original: *Rationale*; refers to the human faculty of reason or the reasoning mind</term> that was later driven from the house. However, this Rational, represented by Isaac, is the one that stayed in the house because it is Divine. We will speak more about this Rational in the next chapter concerning Isaac, through the Lord's Divine Mercy.

2067. **"And I will bless her,"** which signifies its multiplication—specifically, the multiplication of the Rational meant by the son—is clear from the meaning of "to be blessed," which is to be enriched with every good and truth, as mentioned just above.

2068. **"And she will become nations,"** which signifies the resulting "goods" <note>In this theological context, "goods" refers to the positive qualities of love and charity</note>, is clear from the meaning of "Nations." 2069. **"Kings of peoples will come from her,"** which signifies truths derived from the union of truths and goods (which are the "kings of peoples"). This is because "Kings" are spoken of in relation to "peoples," but not usually in relation to "nations," unless "nations" signify evils (as noted in numbers 1259 and 1260).

In the prophetic **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures</note>, "Kings" and "Peoples" are mentioned many times, but these terms never refer to literal kings or peoples. This is because the Word, in its internal sense, is not concerned with earthly kings and nations, but with the celestial and spiritual things that belong to the Lord's Kingdom—namely, goods and truths. The literal sense of the text merely provides the objects (like human words) through which we can understand the deeper meaning.

Since we are discussing Sarah here—and the text says that "Kings of peoples" will come from her—and since Sarah represents the Divine Truth belonging to the Lord, it is clear that "Kings of peoples" signify truths derived from the union of truths and goods. These are all the Internal Truths of the Church, or the inner aspects of faith. Because these truths come from the Lord, they are called "Kings" throughout the Word, as well as "sons of the King" (as shown above in number 2015).

Anyone can see that some hidden Divine internal meaning <note>original: *arcanum*</note> lies within these words: "Kings of peoples will come from her." Similarly, it was said of Abraham above in verse 6 that "Kings will come from him," but not "Kings of peoples" as it says of Sarah. The secret hidden here is too deep to be fully explained in just a few words. 

However, it is somewhat clear from the representation of Abraham (who symbolizes Divine Good) and Sarah (who symbolizes Divine Truth) that every **celestial truth** comes from the Lord's Divine Good (represented by Abraham), and every **spiritual truth** comes from the Lord's Divine Truth (represented by Sarah). 

Celestial truth is what exists among the **Celestial Angels**, and spiritual truth is what exists among the **Spiritual Angels**. Put another way, celestial truth existed among the people of the **Most Ancient Church** (the celestial church before the flood), while spiritual truth existed among the people of the **Ancient Church** (the spiritual church after the flood). Indeed, angels—just like the people of the Church—are distinguished into "Celestial" and "Spiritual." The Celestial are distinguished from the Spiritual by their love for the Lord, while the Spiritual are distinguished from the Celestial by their love... <note>The text breaks off here; the catchword "rem" completes the word "amorem," or "love."</note>

## 2088

It would be too long to describe here exactly who the **Celestial** and **Spiritual** people are, as they have been described before (see numbers 81, 597, 607, 765, 2069, 2078, and elsewhere). The Celestial are those who are in the affection for good for its own sake; the Spiritual are those who are in the affection for good because of truth. From the beginning, all people were Celestial because they were in love with the Lord. From that love, they received **Perception** <term>an intuitive understanding of truth and goodness</term>, through which they perceived what was good not by studying rules, but from an inner feeling for goodness. However, later, when love for the Lord faded, the "Spiritual" era followed. People were called "Spiritual" when they lived in love toward their neighbor, or charity. However, this charity was implanted through truth, and so they received a **Conscience**. According to this conscience, they acted not out of a natural feeling for good, but out of a feeling for what they knew to be true. Charity appears to them to be an affection for good, but it is actually an affection for truth; because of this appearance, charity is still called "good," but it is specifically the "good of their faith." These are the ones understood by the Lord in the Gospel of John:

> "I am the door; if anyone enters through Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture. I am the good Shepherd, and I know My own, and am known by My own; and I have other sheep which are not of this fold; those also I must lead, and they will hear My voice, and there shall be one flock and one Shepherd." (John 10:9, 14, 16).

...become rational, that is, spiritual; concerning which also see above in numbers 2078, 2087, and 2088.

### 2109
**A son of thirteen years** <note>original: *Filius tredecim annorum*</note> signifies "holy remains." This is evident from the meaning of the number **Ten**, which signifies "remains" <term>Remains: In this context, "remains" refers to the spiritual goods and truths stored up by the Lord in a person’s inner mind from childhood</term> (as seen in numbers 576 and 1988), and from the meaning of **Three**, which signifies what is "holy" (as seen in numbers 720 and 901). Therefore, the number **Thirteen**, being composed of ten and three, signifies holy remains. That numbers in the Word <note>original: *Verbum*; the Bible</note> signify actual things and states, see numbers 482, 487, 488, 493, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, and 893. Regarding what "remains" are in a person, see numbers 468, 530, 561, 660, 1050, and 1906.

### 2110
**In circumcising the flesh of his foreskin** <note>original: *In circumcidendo illi carnem præputii ejus*</note> signifies purification. This is clear from the meaning of being **circumcised**, which is to be purified from the loves of self and the world (see number 2039), and from the meaning of the **flesh of the foreskin**, which refers to the removal of those specific loves (see numbers 2041, 2053, and 2057).

### 2111
**On that same day** <note>original: *In eodem die*</note> signifies "at that time." This is clear from the meaning of "day," which represents a time and a state (as discussed previously in numbers 23, 487, 488, 493, and 893).

### 2112
**That Abraham was circumcised, and Ishmael his son** <note>original: *Quod circumcisus est Abraham, & Jischmael filius ejus*</note> signifies that when the Lord joined His **Human Essence** to His **Divine Essence**, He also joined to Himself all others who become rational through truth, and He saved them. This is evident from the representation of **Abraham** in this chapter, who represents the Lord in that state and at that age (see number 1989), and from the representation of **Ishmael** here, who represents those who become rational through truth (see numbers 2078, 2087, and 2088). 

Furthermore, the meaning of being **circumcised** is to be purified (see number 2039), and when applied to the Lord, it means to be **Glorified**—that is, to put off the human nature and put on the Divine nature. That being "glorified" means to put on the Divine nature can be seen above in number 2033; and that He then also joined to Himself those who become rational (that is, spiritual) through truth can be seen in numbers 2034, 2078, and 2088.

### 2113
**Verse 27: And all the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.** 

**All the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with silver** signifies all those who are within the Church at that time. **From a foreigner** signifies all those who are rational outside the Church. **Were circumcised with him** signifies that they were justified by the Lord.

### 2114
That **all the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with silver** signifies all those within the Church is evident from the meaning of those **born in the house**, who are the "celestial," and from the meaning of those **bought with silver**, who are the "spiritual" (see numbers 2048, 2051, and 2052). <term>Celestial and Spiritual: The "celestial" are those who act from love for the Lord; the "spiritual" are those who act from a love for truth or neighborly charity.</term> 

It was stated there that these are the people within the Church, for everyone who is within the Church—that is, everyone who constitutes the Church—is either celestial or spiritual. For who specifically is celestial and who is spiritual, see number 2088. In this final verse of the chapter, there is a summary of everything said above: namely, that those who are purified from the loves of self and the world, whether they are within the Church or outside the Church, are justified.

# GENESIS

...by the Lord: these and those are called **men of the house**, for **house**, in the internal sense, signifies the **Lord's Kingdom** <note>original: *Regnum Domini*</note> (see number 2048).

### 2115
**From a son of a stranger** <note>original: *A filio alienigena*</note> signifies all those who are rational but outside the Church. This is established from the meaning of a "son of a stranger" as those who are outside the Church (as mentioned above in number 2049). This refers to the **Gentiles** <term>Gentiles: In this context, people who do not have the Word (the Bible) and therefore do not know anything of the Lord</term>. 

It has been shown in Part One (numbers 593, 932, 1032, 1059, 1327, and 1328) that these people are saved just as much [as those within the Church] when they are rational—that is, when they live in charity or mutual love among themselves and have acted according to the conscience they received from their own religious upbringing.

### 2116
**That they were circumcised by him** signifies that they were **justified by the Lord**. This can be seen from the representation—and thus the meaning—of being **circumcised** as being purified (as discussed in number 2039). The fact that they were "circumcised by him"—that is, by Abraham—was also representative, meaning they were purified and thus justified by the Lord.

As for **Justification**, it does not happen according to the common opinion: namely, that all evils and sins are wiped away and completely deleted when people believe (as they imagine), even if this belief occurs only in their final hour of death after they have lived a life of wickedness and crimes. 

I have been fully informed that not even the smallest evil that a person has thought and actually done during their physical life is wiped away and completely deleted. Instead, every single thing remains, down to the smallest detail. The reality is this:
*   Those who have thought about and practiced hatred, revenge, cruelty, and adultery—and thus lived without charity—retain that life after death. Indeed, every single part of that life returns in succession, which is the source of their torment in **hell** <note>original: *inferno*</note>. 
*   However, for those who lived in love for the Lord and in charity toward their neighbor, the evils of their life also remain, but they are tempered by the "goods" <term>Goods: Spiritual qualities of kindness, love, and truth</term> which they received from the Lord through their life of charity while in the world. 

Thus, they are raised into **heaven** <note>original: *cœlum*</note>. In fact, they are held back by the Lord from the evils they carry with them so that those evils do not appear. Those in the afterlife who doubt they still have evils within them (because the evils are not visible) are allowed to experience them until they realize the truth, and then they are raised back into heaven. This is what it truly means to be **Justified**; in this state, they acknowledge not their own justice, but the **Justice of the Lord**. 

When people say that those who have **faith** <note>original: *fides*</note> are saved, this is true. But in the Word, nothing else is meant by "faith" than **love for the Lord** and **charity toward the neighbor**, and the life that comes from them. The formal doctrines and dogmas of faith are not "faith," but rather they belong to faith; every single one of them exists for the sake of an "end" or purpose: that a person might become the kind of person the doctrines teach. 

This is clearly established from the Lord’s own words: that the **Law and all the prophets**—that is, the entire doctrine of faith—consists in **love for God** and **love for the neighbor** (Matthew 22:34–39; Mark 12:28–35). It has been shown in Part One (numbers 30–38, 379, 389, 724, 809, 896, 904, 916, 989, 1017, 1076, 1077, 1121, 1158, 1162, 1176, 1258, 1285, 1316, 1608, 1798, 1799, 1834, 1843, and 1844) that no other faith exists that is truly faith, and that Heaven itself consists in love for the Lord and mutual love (numbers 537, 547, 553, 1112, and 2057).

### On the LAST JUDGMENT
<note>original: *De ULTIMO JUDICIO*</note>

**2117.** Few people today know what the **Last Judgment** <note>original: *Ultimum Judicium*</note> really is. They think it will happen at the destruction of the world. This leads to conjectures that the earth will perish by fire, along with everything in the visible world, and that only then will the dead first rise and be brought before the Judgment—the evil to be cast into hell, and the good to ascend into Heaven. These conjectures arise from the **Prophetic books of the Word** <term>the Word: The Bible, viewed as having a deep, coded spiritual meaning</term>, where a "New Heaven and a New Earth" are mentioned, as well as a "New Jerusalem." People do not realize that the prophetic parts of the Word mean something entirely different in their **internal sense** <note>original: *sensu interno*</note> than what appears in the **literal sense** <note>original: *sensu literæ*</note>. In these prophecies, "Heaven" does not mean the sky, nor does "Earth" mean the physical ground; rather, they signify the Lord's Church—both in general and within every individual person.

**2118.** By the "Last Judgment" is meant the final period of a Church, as well as the final period of every person's life. Regarding the final periods of the Church:
*   There was a Last Judgment of the **Most Ancient Church** <note>original: *Ecclesia Antiquissima*</note>, which existed before the Flood. When its descendants perished, their destruction was described by the story of the Flood. 
*   The Last Judgment of the **Ancient Church** <note>original: *Ecclesia Antiqua*</note>, which existed after the Flood, occurred when almost everyone belonging to that Church became idolaters and were scattered. 
*   The Last Judgment of the **Representative Church** <note>original: *Ecclesia Repræsentativa*</note>, which followed among the descendants of Jacob, happened when the Ten Tribes were led away into captivity and dispersed among the nations; later, the Jews were expelled from the land of Canaan after the Lord's coming and were scattered throughout the entire world. 
*   The Last Judgment of *this* Church—which is called the **Christian Church** <note>original: *Ecclesia Christiana*</note>—is what is meant in John's **Revelation** <note>original: *Apocalypsi*</note> by the "New Heaven and the New Earth."

**2119.** Some people are aware that the end of an individual's life when they die is their own "Last Judgment," yet few truly believe it. Nevertheless, it is a constant truth that every person rises into the next life immediately after death and is presented for Judgment. This Judgment works like this: as soon as the physical body grows cold (which happens after a few days), the person is **resurrected** <note>original: *resuscitatur*</note> by the Lord through **Celestial Angels**, who are the first to be with them. However, if the person’s character is such that they cannot remain with those angels, they are then received by **Spiritual Angels**, and successively afterward by **Good Spirits**. Everyone who enters the other life is welcomed as a guest and accepted; but because a person's own desires follow them, someone who has lived an evil life cannot stay long with the Angels and good spirits. Instead, they gradually [separates]... <margin>separates</margin>

It describes the process of resurrection where a person is guided by different levels of angels based on their inner character.</summary>

The sound of the clashing and confused murmurs was three-fold:

2. Another flowed toward the left temple, and I was told this was the conflict of **reasonings** <note>original: "ratiocinationum"</note> regarding certain truths which they were unwilling to believe.
3. The third flowed from above toward the right; this was a grating sound, not so confused, which moved back and forth. I was told this happened because **Truths** were clashing as they were tossed to and fro by those reasonings. 

While these conflicts continued, there were still Spirits who spoke with me, explaining what each thing signified; their speech penetrated distinctly through those various noises.

Furthermore, it was shown that the Apostles cannot judge even a single human being, but that all Judgment belongs to the Lord alone. Regarding the second point, it is not to be understood that only those who have suffered persecutions and miseries will come into Heaven; rather, the rich and the poor, and those in high authority as well as those in humble conditions, are admitted alike. The Lord has mercy on all, especially those who have been in spiritual miseries and temptations—which are "persecutions" by the wicked—and those who acknowledge that they are miserable of themselves, believing that their salvation comes from the Lord's Mercy alone.

**2130.** Regarding the other matter—namely, the idea of the **Last Judgment** <note>original: "Ultimum Judicium"</note> as it appears to the good when they are introduced into Heaven—I may relate how it happened. It is said in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible.</note> that the door was shut so that no more could be let in, and that the oil had failed and they arrived too late and were therefore not admitted—by which the state of the Last Judgment is signified. I was shown how these things occur and how they are to be understood. 

I heard societies of spirits, one after another, saying in a clear voice that the "Wolf" <note>original: "Lupus"; a metaphor for evil spirits or the devil attempting to seize souls.</note> had wanted to carry them away, but that the Lord had rescued them, and thus they were restored to the Lord. They rejoiced from the depths of their hearts, for they had been in despair and in fear that the door was shut and they had come too late to be let in. Such thoughts had been infused into them by those who are called "wolves." But this fear vanished when they were "let in"—that is, when they were received by Angelic Societies. Introduction into heaven is nothing other than this reception. 

I saw this introduction as if it were a continuous process through various societies, up to twelve in number. The twelfth society was admitted—or received—with more difficulty than the previous eleven. Afterwards, about eight societies consisting of the female sex were also admitted. When these were seen, it was explained that this process of admission (or reception) into celestial societies appears this way continuously, moving in order from one place to another. Furthermore, Heaven is never [closed]...

<header>CHAPTER SEVENTEEN</header>

<meta>catchword: 2133. Twice</meta>

...forever filled up, much less that the door would be closed. Instead, the more people who arrive there, the more blessed and happy it is for those already in Heaven, because the unanimity of the group becomes even stronger. After those people were admitted, it then appeared as if Heaven were being closed; for there were many others who also wanted to be let in—that is, to be received. However, they received the answer that they could not be admitted yet. This is signified in the Bible by those who arrive late, the door being shut, and the knockers who lacked oil in their lamps. <note>This refers to the Parable of the Ten Virgins in Matthew 25.</note> The reason they were not admitted was that they were not yet prepared to participate in the **Angelic Societies**, where **mutual love** <note>original: "amor mutuus"</note> reigns. For, as was said above in section 2119, those who lived in **charity** <note>In this context, "charity" means active love and goodwill toward others.</note> toward their neighbor while in the world are raised into Heaven by the Lord in gradual stages. There were also other spirits who did not understand what Heaven was—that it is essentially mutual love. They also wanted to be let in at that time, thinking that admission was a simple matter of entry; but they received the answer that it was not yet time for them, but would be at another time when they were prepared. The fact that twelve societies appeared was because "Twelve" signifies all things belonging to faith, as mentioned above in section 2129.

2131. Those who are admitted are received by the **Angelic Societies** with the most profound charity and joy. All love and friendship are shown to them. However, if they do not wish to remain in the first societies they encounter, they are then received by other societies. This happens successively until they reach the specific society that harmonizes with their own life of mutual love. They remain there until they become even more perfected, at which point they are elevated and exalted into even greater happiness. This occurs by the **Mercy of the Lord**, according to the life of love and charity they received while living in the world. But this transfer from one society to another never happens by being "rejected" by the society where they currently are; rather, it happens through a voluntary movement within the spirits themselves, according to a desire inspired in them by the Lord. Because it happens according to their own desires, everything is done in total freedom.

2132. Regarding the passage in the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> stating that a man entered who was not dressed in a **wedding garment** (Matthew 22:11–13) and was cast out: the reality of how this happens was also shown. There are some people who, during their life in the body, become so practiced in deceit that they can pretend to be "angels of light." When they are in that hypocritical state in the other life, they can sometimes sneak into the nearby heavenly societies. However, they do not stay there for long. As soon as they perceive the "sphere" <note>In spiritual terms, a "sphere" is the outward vibration or atmosphere of a person's inner character.</note> of mutual love there, they are seized with fear and horror and throw themselves out. In the **world of spirits**, it then appears as if they have been cast out—some toward a lake, some toward Gehenna <note>original: "gehennam" - a term for hell or a place of spiritual trial</note>, and others into some other kind of hell.

<header>GENESIS</header>

2133. Two or three times, by the Divine Mercy of the Lord, Heaven was opened to me so far that I heard a general glorification of the Lord <note>original: "Glorificationem Domini communem"</note>. This glorification is such that many societies <note>In this context, "societies" refers to organized groups of angels in Heaven.</note> act together and in unison, yet each society glorifies the Lord on its own, with its own distinct affections <note>In 18th-century theological writing, "affections" refers to the deep-seated feelings or loves of the heart.</note> and the ideas that flow from them. The heavenly voice was heard far and wide, across such an immense distance that hearing failed to find its end—much like the way sight fails when looking at the universe. This occurred with the deepest joy and the most profound happiness. I also sometimes perceived this glorification of the Lord as a kind of flowing radiance that affected the innermost parts of the mind. This glorification happens when the angels are in a state of tranquility and peace; for it is then that it flows out from their innermost joys and from their very happiness.

# PREFACE <note>original Latin: "PRÆFATIO"</note>

At the end of the previous chapter, we discussed the **Last Judgment** <term>Last Judgment: In Swedenborg's theology, this refers not to the physical destruction of the world, but to a spiritual transition at the end of a "Church" or religious era</term> and showed what is signified by it. Specifically, it does not mean the destruction of the world, but the final stage of the **Church**. When this time is near, the Lord says that He will come in the **clouds of heaven** with power and glory (*Matthew* 24:30; *Mark* 13:26; *Luke* 21:27). 

Until now, no one has known what is meant by the "clouds of heaven," but it has been revealed to me that nothing else is meant than the **literal sense of the Word** <note>the "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures</note>. By "power" and "glory" is meant the **internal sense of the Word**; for in the internal sense of the Word there is glory, because everything there concerns the Lord and His Kingdom. (See Part One, sections 1769 to 1772). 

It is the same with the **cloud** that surrounded Peter, James, and John when the Lord appeared to them in glory. Regarding this, it is written in Luke: 

> *"A voice came out of the cloud, saying, 'This is my beloved Son; listen to Him.' When the voice had ceased, Jesus was found alone"* (Luke 9:35, 36). <note>original Latin: "Vox facta est e Nube, dicens, hic est Filius meus dilectus, Hunc audite: cum autem facta esset vox, inventus est Jesus Solus"</note>

By **Moses and Elijah**, who spoke with the Lord there, was represented the Word of the Old Testament (which is also called "Moses and the Prophets"). By "Moses" are meant his books, including the historical books; by "Elijah the prophet" are meant all the Prophets. By Peter, James, and...

<summary>Swedenborg explains that the "clouds of heaven" mentioned in the Bible represent the literal meaning of the Scriptures, while "glory" represents their deeper spiritual meaning. He uses the Transfiguration of Jesus to illustrate how different biblical figures represent different parts of the Word.</summary>

<keywords>Last Judgment, Second Coming, clouds of heaven, literal sense, internal sense, Transfiguration, Moses, Elijah, Word of God</keywords>

and **John** <note>original Latin: *Johannem*</note>, were represented. Just as they are elsewhere, wherever they are named in the books of the Evangelists, they represent **Faith**, **Charity**, and the **Good of Charity** <term>Good of Charity: In Swedenborg's theology, this refers to the actual practice or living expression of love and kindness, not just the feeling of it</term>. 

The fact that only these three disciples were present signifies that no one can see the glory of the Lord—which resides in His **Word** <note>the "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures</note>—except those who are grounded in faith, in charity, and in the good of that charity. Others may indeed be able to see the text, but they do not truly "see" its depth because they do not believe. This is the **internal sense** <term>internal sense: The hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words</term> regarding those two aspects. 

Throughout the books of the Prophets as well, **Cloud** everywhere signifies the Word in its literal sense, and **Glory** signifies the Word in its living essence. What this internal sense of the Word is, and its specific nature, has been discussed in many places and demonstrated in the detailed explanation of individual words. 

The **experts in the law** <note>original Latin: *Legisperiti*; this refers to the scribes and theologians who studied religious law</note> in the Lord's time were those who, least of all, believed that anything had been written in the Word concerning the Lord. The experts in the law today certainly know that the Word speaks of Him, but perhaps they are the least likely of all to believe that there is any other Glory within the Word than that which appears in its literal letter. That literal sense, however, is merely the "cloud" in which the glory resides.

# PART TWO

## THE BOOK OF GENESIS

### CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

2135. From this chapter, it can be established above all else what the **internal sense** <term>internal sense: The hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words</term> of the **Word** <note>the "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures</note> is like, and how the **Angels** perceive it when it is read by a person. 

From the historical sense of the literal text, nothing else is understood than that **Jehovah** appeared to **Abraham** in the form of three men, and that **Sarah**, Abraham, and his servant prepared food for them—specifically cakes made of fine flour, a calf, and also butter and milk. Although these are true historical events that actually happened, they are nevertheless not perceived that way by the Angels. Instead, the Angels perceive them entirely abstractly from the literal text, according to what they represent and signify as described in the summary of contents. 

Specifically, in place of those historical details, they perceive the state of the Lord’s perception while in His **Human** <note>original Latin: *Humano*; referring to Jesus Christ's human nature while on Earth</note>, and the communication He then had with the **Divine** <note>original Latin: *Divino*; referring to the infinite Divine nature or "the Father"</note>. This occurred before the perfect union of His **Divine Essence** with the **Human**, and the **Human** with the **Divine**. This is also the state concerning which the Lord says, *"No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known"* <note>original Latin: *Deum nemo vidit unquam, Unigenitus Filius, qui in sinu Patris est, ille exposuit*; John 1:18</note>. 

Furthermore, the foods mentioned there signify nothing but celestial and spiritual "goods" <term>goods: In this context, "goods" refers to the various forms of love, kindness, and divine grace</term>, which will be discussed in the detailed explanation. Finally, what is said regarding the son whom Sarah would bear at the set time of the following year signifies nothing other... <note>original Latin: *aliud*</note>

# GENESIS

[Angels] perceive nothing else than that the Lord’s human rational <term>human rational: The part of the human mind capable of reasoning and logic, which the Lord transformed into something Divine</term> was becoming Divine. Furthermore, through the things Abraham spoke with **Jehovah** about the destruction of **Sodom** and **Gomorrah**, they perceive nothing else than the Lord’s intercession for the human race. Specifically, through the fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten <note>These numbers refer to Abraham's bargaining with God in Genesis 18:24–32 to spare the city for the sake of the righteous</note>, they perceive intercession for those whose truths are joined to goodness, and those who receive goodness through temptations and struggles, or through other states. This is how it works with everything else in the **Word** <note>the Word: The Sacred Scriptures or Bible</note>, as can be better established from the explanation of individual words, where it is shown that similar spiritual meanings are involved in every single word, whether the text is historical or prophetic.

That such an **internal sense** <term>internal sense: The hidden, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words</term> exists everywhere in the Word—which deals only with the Lord, His Kingdom in the heavens, His Church on earth, and specifically within every individual (thus concerning the "goods" of love and the "truths" of faith)—can be established by anyone from the passages of the Old Testament quoted by the **Evangelists** <note>the authors of the Gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John</note>. For example, in Matthew: 

"*The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool*" <note>original: *Dixit Dominus Domino meo, sede a dextris meis, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum*</note>, <term>Matthew 22:44</term> <term>Psalm 110:1</term>. 

That these words refer to the Lord cannot be seen from the literal sense in the passage cited from David (Psalms), yet the Lord Himself teaches there that no one else is meant but Him. Similarly: 

"*You, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means the least among the leaders of Judah; for out of you shall come a Leader who will shepherd my people Israel*" <note>original: *Tu Bethlehema, terra Jehuda, nequaquam minima es in ducibus Jehudæ, ex te enim exibit Dux, qui pascet populum meum Israelem*</note>, <term>Matthew 2:6</term> <term>Micah 5:2</term>. 

Those who remain in the literal sense, such as the Jews, do know from this that the Lord was to be born there. However, because they expect a leader and king who will lead them back to the land of **Canaan**, they explain the words according to the letter—namely, that "the land of Judah" means the physical land of Canaan, and "Israel" means the literal people of Israel (even though they do not know where they are), and "the Leader" is still their expected **Messiah**. Yet, other things are meant by **Judah** and **Israel**: by "Judah" is meant the Celestial, and by "Israel" the Spiritual <note>In this system, "Celestial" refers to the highest heaven or love, while "Spiritual" refers to the second heaven or truth</note>, both in heaven and on earth; and by "the Leader" is meant the Lord. Again: 

"*A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping, and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more*" <note>original: *Vox in Ramah audita est, lamentatio, clamor, & ejulatus multus, Rachel deplorans liberos suos, & non volebat consolationem admittere, quia non sunt*</note>, <term>Matthew 2:18</term> <term>Jeremiah 31:15</term>. 

Those who remain in the literal sense never grasp from those words the internal sense that is within them; yet that there is such a sense is clear from the Evangelist. Again: 

"*Out of Egypt I called my son*" <note>original: *Ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum*</note>, <term>Matthew 2:15</term> <term>Hosea 11:1</term>. 

In the prophet it is said: "*When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son; they called them, so they went from their faces; and I made Ephraim go*" <note>original: *Cum puer Israel, & amavi illum, & ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum: vocarunt illos, sic iverunt a faciebus eorum; & Ego feci ire, Ephraimum*</note>. Those who are unaware that an internal sense exists cannot know otherwise than that **Jacob**... <meta>catchword: Jacobus</meta>

### CHAPTER XVIII.

1. **A**nd **JEHOVAH** appeared to him in the oak groves of **Mamre** <note>Mamre: An ancient site near Hebron, often associated with sacred trees where Abraham resided</note>, as he was sitting at the door of the tent in the heat of the day.

2. And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing over him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the door of the tent and bowed himself toward the ground.

3. And he said, "My Lord, if I have now found favor in your eyes, please do not pass by your servant."

4. "Please let a little water be taken, and wash your feet, and rest under the tree."

5. "And I will bring a piece of bread to sustain your heart <note>original Latin: "fulcite cor vestrum" — literally "support your heart," meaning to provide strength or refreshment</note>; afterward you may pass on, since you have come to your servant." And they said, "Do so, just as you have spoken."

6. And **Abraham** hurried into the tent to **Sarah** and said, "Hurry, take three measures <note>original Latin: "fata" — a reference to the Hebrew 'seah,' a unit of dry measure for grain</note> of fine flour, knead it, and make cakes."

7. And Abraham ran to the herd and took a tender and good calf and gave it to a servant, and he hurried to prepare it.

8. And he took butter and milk, and the calf which he had prepared, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree while they ate.

9. And they said to him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" And he said, "Behold, in the tent."

10. And he said, "I will certainly return to you when this season of life comes around <note>original Latin: "juxta tempus hoc vitæ" — a phrase indicating the time of birth or the following year</note>, and behold, Sarah your wife shall have a son." And Sarah was listening at the door of the tent, which was behind him.

11. Now Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in years; it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.

12. And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?"

# GENESIS.

13. And **Jehovah** <term>Jehovah: A Latinized transliteration of the Hebrew name for God, typically rendered as "the LORD" in English Bibles</term> said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Shall I truly give birth, even though I have grown old?’" <note>original Latin: "num etiam vere pariam, & ego consenui"</note>

14. "Is anything too wonderful for **Jehovah**? At the set time I will return to you, according to this time of life, and Sarah shall have a son."

15. And Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh," because she was afraid; and He said, "No, but you did laugh."

16. Then the men rose up from there and looked toward the face of **Sodom** <note>original Latin: "Sodomae"</note>; and Abraham went with them to see them off.

17. And **Jehovah** said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing?"

18. "Since Abraham shall surely become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him."

19. "For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of **Jehovah** to do righteousness and justice <note>original Latin: "justitiam & judicium"</note>, so that **Jehovah** may bring upon Abraham what He has spoken concerning him."

20. And **Jehovah** said, "Because the outcry against **Sodom** and **Gomorrah** <note>original Latin: "Amorae"</note> has become great, and because their sin has become very heavy,"

21. "I will go down now and see whether they have acted altogether according to the cry that has come to Me; and if not, I will know."

22. And the men turned away from there and went toward **Sodom**; but Abraham was still standing before **Jehovah**.

23. And Abraham drew near and said, "Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?"

24. "Perhaps there are fifty righteous within the city; will You also destroy it and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in its midst?"

2136. **F**IRST, this section deals with the Lord's **State of Perception** <term>Perception: In this theological context, an internal "sensing" or direct spiritual understanding from the Divine</term> while in His human form, and His communication with the Divine at that time. 2137. The Lord's state of perception in His human form at that time is symbolized by the **oak groves of Mamre** (Verse 1). He rejoiced in this (Verse 3) and desired for the Divine to draw closer to His human side by taking on something natural (Verse 4), while His human side drew closer to the Divine by taking on what is heavenly (Verse 5). The heavenly and resulting spiritual qualities He took on are symbolized by the **three measures of fine flour** <note>original Latin: "triasata farinæ similaginis"</note> from which cakes were made (Verse 6). The fact that He also took on a corresponding natural quality is symbolized by the **calf** <note>original Latin: "filium bovis," literally 'son of an ox'</note> (Verse 7). From this came the adaptation and communication of the Divine with the Human, and the Human with the Divine (Verse 8).

2139. That the Rational would become Divine is symbolized by the **son** whom Sarah was to bear (Verse 9). 2140. **Thirdly**, this section discusses the Lord’s grief and anxiety over the human race, because it was so deeply filled with self-love and the resulting desire to rule over others based on evil and falsehood. In that state, He interceded for humanity and obtained salvation for those who possessed "goods and truths" <note>original: bona & vera; spiritual virtues and correct understandings</note>. The specific groups of people who can be saved are listed in order.

2141. The Lord’s perception of the human race was that it was steeped in evil and falsehood. **Sodom** signifies self-love and the resulting desire to rule based on evil; **Gomorrah** <note>original: Amora</note> signifies the same based on falsehood (Verses 16, 20). This could not be hidden from the Lord in that state, because all salvation comes through Him and from Him (Verses 17, 18, 19). Specifically, a "visitation" <note>original: visitandi; a spiritual reckoning or judgment</note> occurs when their wickedness reaches its peak (Verses 20, 21). 

While in that state of perception (Verse 22), the Lord interceded for them:
* First, for those who possess truths full of good, who are signified by the number **fifty** (Verses 23, 24, 25, 26).
* Then, for those who possess less good, but who are still connected to truths, signified by **forty-five** (Verses 27, 28).
* Next, for those who have undergone temptations, signified by **forty** (Verse 29).
* Also, for those who have been in some degree of struggle against evils, signified by **thirty** (Verse 30).
* Furthermore, for those who possess a state of affection for good from elsewhere, signified by **twenty** (Verse 31).
* Finally, for those who possess a state of affection for truth, signified by **ten** (Verse 32).

The constant response was that these individuals would be saved (Verses 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32). Once these matters were concluded, the Lord returned to His former state of perception (Verse 33). These are the secrets <note>original: arcana</note> contained in the internal sense of this chapter, which are not apparent from the literal text.

2142. **Verse 1.** *And Jehovah appeared to him in the oak groves of Mamre, as he sat at the door of the tent in the heat of the day.*

...concerning the internal sense of the Lord and His perception, which was represented by Jehovah appearing to Abraham. Every appearance, every word, and every deed in the historical accounts of the Word are of such a nature <note>i.e., they represent deeper spiritual realities</note>. What they truly represent, however, is not apparent unless the historical facts are viewed as nothing more than objects—much like things seen by the eye that provide an opportunity or a means for thinking about higher things. For example, when we see gardens, we may think of fruit, the uses of those fruits, the joy of life derived from them, and even more sublimely, the happiness of Paradise or heaven. When these higher things are thought of, the individual objects of the garden are indeed seen, but so lightly that they are hardly noticed. The same is true for the historical accounts of the Word: when the celestial and spiritual things within the internal sense are being considered, the history and the words themselves are barely noticed.

**2144.** **In the oak groves of Mamre**: That this signifies the quality of perception is clear from the representation and meaning of **oak groves**, as well as the representation and meaning of **Mamre**. What "oak groves" in general represent and signify was shown in Part One (numbers 1442, 1443); and what the "oak groves of Mamre" specifically signify (number 1616) is **perceptions**, but specifically those that are human, derived from <term>scientifics</term> <note>original: scientificis; factual knowledge or learned data</note> and from the first rational concepts that stem from them.

What **Perception** is is almost entirely unknown today, because no one today is in the state of perception that the Ancients—and especially the Most Ancients—possessed. The Most Ancient people knew from perception whether something was good, and consequently whether it was true. There was an influx into their <term>rational mind</term> from the Lord through heaven; because of this, the moment they thought about something holy, they perceived whether it was so or not. 

This type of perception later vanished in man when he was no longer centered in celestial ideas but began to focus only on worldly and bodily things. In its place succeeded **conscience**, which is also a type of perception. To act against conscience or according to conscience is nothing other than perceiving from that source whether a thing is right or wrong, or should be done. However, the perception of conscience does not come from the "Good" that flows in directly, but from "Truth." This truth is implanted in the rational mind from infancy according to one’s holy worship, and is later confirmed; this is what people then believe to be the only good. Thus, conscience is a species of perception, but it arises from such truth; when charity and innocence are breathed into this truth by the Lord, the "good" of that conscience is produced. 

From these few points, one can understand what Perception is; but there is a great difference between Perception and Conscience. (See what was said about Perception in Part One, numbers 104, 125, 371, 483, 495, 503, 521, 536, 597, 607, 784, 865, 895, 1121, 1616; and regarding the Perception of Spirits and Angels, numbers 202, 203, 1008, 1383, 1384, 1390, 1391, 1392, 1394, 1397, 1504; and that the learned do not know what Perception is, number 1387.)

As for the Lord, while He lived in the world, His entire thought came from **Divine Perception**, because He alone was the Divine and Celestial Man. He alone was the one in whom Jehovah Himself dwelt, and from Jehovah came His perception (as also discussed in Part One, numbers 1616, 1791). His perceptions became increasingly more interior the closer He came to union with Jehovah. What His perception was like can be understood from what was said about the oak groves of Mamre (number 1616); and what it became when He perceived the things contained in this chapter will be described in the following sections.

**2145.** **Sitting at the door of the tent**: That this signifies a holy state—specifically the holy state of love which belonged to the Lord at that time and is signified by the **heat of the day**—is clear from the meaning of a **Tent**. In the internal sense, a tent represents what is holy <note>original: "sanctum"</note> (as seen in numbers 414, 1102, and 1566). The reason tents signify holy things can be found in those sections. At this time, the Lord was in the state of **Perception** signified by the **oak groves of Mamre**. This represents a lower level of the rational mind, yet it is more "interior" (deeper or more spiritual) than the state signified by the "oak grove of Moreh" (see numbers 1442 and 1443). 

The Lord's state is represented here by his "sitting at the door of the tent," which means being at the very entrance to a holy state. We can illustrate how these perceptions vary in depth by looking at the "Most Ancient people" <note>The "Antiquissimi," referring to the earliest spiritual era of humanity</note>. I have learned from them that the more they focused on <term>scientifics</term> <note>original: "scientificis"; factual knowledge derived from the senses</note>—things they heard or saw—the more "exterior" or lower their perceptions became. However, the more they were raised up from those facts toward the heavenly qualities of charity and love, the more "interior" their perceptions became, because they were then closer to the Lord.

**2146.** **As the day grew hot**: That this signifies a state of love is clear from the meaning of **heat**. In the internal sense, heat is love. Because heat is a quality of both the day and the year, love is represented by the heat of the day or the heat of the season, depending on the historical context. That heat signifies love is evident from the fact that love is often called "spiritual heat" <note>original: "calor spiritualis"</note>, and even in common speech, we say a person's "affections are warming up." 

Furthermore, love and its affections manifest themselves as a type of physical heat in a person's inner and outer self, and even in the body itself. This heat has no other source than the internal life flowing outward. However, the quality of the heat depends on the quality of the love. Heavenly love and spiritual love produce genuine heat. Every other kind of heat—such as that which comes from self-love, love of the world, or other "unclean" loves—is itself unclean. In the afterlife, this selfish heat fades away into something foul and <term>excrementitious</term> <note>original: "excrementitium"; waste-like or dung-like</note> (see number 1773). Additionally, it should be known that nothing is ever called "holy" unless it comes from love and charity. Faith is not called holy except to the extent that love or charity is present within the truths of that faith. The truths of faith are not holy unless they come from that source (see number 2049).

**2147.** **Verse 2.** *And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three Men stood over him; and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the door of the tent, and bowed himself toward the earth.*

*   **He lifted up his eyes** signifies that he saw within himself.
*   **And behold, three Men stood over him** signifies the Divine Itself, the Divine Human, and the Holy Proceeding <note>The three "Men" here represent the Trinity: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit</note>.
*   **And he saw** signifies when he perceived this.
*   **And he ran to meet them** signifies that he approached more closely in thought to those things being perceived.
*   **From the door of the tent** signifies from the holy state that the Lord was in at that time.
*   **And he bowed himself toward the earth** signifies the effect of humiliation resulting from the joy of that perception.

**2148.** That **he lifted up his eyes** signifies that he saw within himself is clear from the meaning of "lifting the eyes." In the Word, the **eyes** signify internal sight or the understanding (as shown in the passages cited in number 212). Therefore, "lifting the eyes" means to see and perceive things that are "above" oneself. In the Word, things that are interior (more spiritual) are expressed as being "superior" (higher), such as "looking upward," "lifting the eyes to heaven," or "thinking high thoughts."

# GENESIS

->[The Son] of man signified **Truth** itself, and by the "Son of God" was signified **Good** itself, which belonged to His Human Essence when it was made Divine. The former state was the Lord's **Humiliation** <note>original: "Humiliatio"</note>, but this current state is His **Glorification** <note>original: "Glorificatio"</note>, as discussed previously in section 1999. In the former state—namely, Humiliation—when He still had with Him the **infirm human nature** <note>original: "Humanum infirmum"; the mortal, limited part of His humanity</note>, He worshiped Jehovah as someone other than Himself, and indeed as a **Servant** <note>original: "Servus"</note>; for the Human is nothing else in comparison. Therefore, in the Word, that human nature is described as a servant.<-

As written in **Isaiah**:
> "**I will protect this city to save it for my own sake, and for the sake of my servant David,**" (37:35).
 
This refers to the Assyrians, in whose camp one hundred and eighty-five thousand were struck down by an angel. Here, **David** stands for the Lord; because He was to come, He is called a "servant" regarding His Human nature. (For evidence that David in the Word represents the Lord, see section 1888).

In the same Prophet:
> "**Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth judgment to the nations,**" (42:1).

This is clearly about the Lord, who is called "servant" and "chosen" when He was in His human nature. In the same Prophet:
> "**Who is blind, but my servant? Or deaf, like the messenger I will send? Who is blind as the perfect one, and blind as the servant of Jehovah?**" (42:19).

This also refers to the Lord, who is similarly called "servant" and "messenger" <note>original: "angelus"; often translated as messenger in this context</note> when He was in His human nature. In the same Prophet:
> "**You are my witnesses, says Jehovah, and my servant whom I have chosen; so that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am He,**" (43:10).

Again, in the same Prophet:
> "**Jehovah, who formed me from the womb to be a servant to Him, said that I should bring Jacob back to Him, and that Israel might be gathered to Him. And He said, 'It is a light thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob; I have given you as a light to the nations, to be my salvation to the end of the earth,'**" (49:5-6).

This is also clearly about the Lord and His Human nature before it became the "Light of the nations" and "Salvation to the end of the earth." In the same Prophet:
> "**Who among you fears Jehovah and hears the voice of His servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of Jehovah and rely on his God,**" (50:10).

"Servant" also stands for the Human nature in the Lord; when He was in that nature and taught the way of truth, the phrase "voice of the servant of Jehovah" is used. In the same Prophet:
> "**Jehovah goes before you, and the God of Israel gathers you. Behold, my servant shall act wisely; he shall be extolled, and exalted, and lifted up very high,**" (52:12-13).

It is clear that the Lord is called "servant" when He was in His Human nature, for it says of Him that He will be extolled, exalted, and lifted up. In the same Prophet:
> "**He has no form or honor; we saw him, but he had no beauty. He was despised, a man of sorrows, acquainted with sickness. Jehovah willed to crush him; He made him weak. If he makes his soul a guilt offering, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the will of Jehovah shall prosper by his hand. From the labor of his soul he shall see and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many; and he himself bore their iniquities,**" (53:2-3, 10-11).

Here, as in this entire chapter, the subject is openly the Lord's state of humiliation. It is said that He was then in a weak human nature—specifically that He was a "man of sorrows," "acquainted with sickness," "weak," and in the "labor of His soul," among many other descriptions—and in this state, He is called a "servant."
