2160. **Verse 4.** *“Let a little water be brought, please, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.”*
**“Let a little water be brought, please”** signifies that they should approach and lower themselves from Divine levels closer to his intellectual things. **“And wash your feet”** signifies that they should put on something natural so that, in the state he was then in, he might perceive better. **“And rest yourselves under the tree”** signifies a drawing near to the perception of his own state; for a **tree** <note>original: "arbor"</note> signifies perception.

2161. The fact that **“let a little water be brought, please”** signifies that they should approach and lower themselves from Divine levels closer to his intellectual things cannot be proven from these words alone. Rather, it is clear from the series of events in this verse and their connection with what comes before and after. From the literal words of this verse, no one would ever know that **“let a little water be brought, please, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree”** signified that the Divine would lower itself closer to the state of perception in which the Lord then was, and would put on something natural to better perceive. Not a trace of this mystery <note>original: "arcani"</note> is visible in the words when understood historically. 

However, I know for certain that these things do signify such matters in the **internal sense** <note>original: "sensu interno"</note>, and that this is how the angels perceive them. From this, it is clear how many and how deep are the secrets hidden in **the Word** <note>original: "Verbo"</note>. Furthermore, this can be seen from the significance of the words in the internal sense: specifically, from the meaning of **water** as intellectual things, the meaning of **feet** as natural things, and the meaning of a **tree** as perception. Once these meanings are understood, what they signify in the internal sense becomes clear from the sequence and connection of the narrative. It has already been shown in Part One (sections 38 and 680) that **waters** signify scientific, rational, and therefore intellectual things; this is also evident from many other places in the Word, which would be too numerous to list here.

2162. That **“wash your feet”** signifies that He should put on something natural—so that He might better perceive in His current state—is clear from the meaning of **feet** as "natural things" <note>original: "naturalia"</note>, as well as from the context of the story. That hidden mysteries lie here is somewhat evident from the fact that Abraham begged the three men to take a little water and wash their feet and rest under the tree, even though he knew that the Lord, or **Jehovah**, was present. Otherwise, such details would not have been recorded. 

The fact that **feet** signify "natural things" is clear from the **Representations** <note>original: "Representativis"; spiritual symbols or correspondences</note> in the other life, which were also used by the most ancient people and thus appear in the Word. Celestial and spiritual things are represented by the **head** and the parts belonging to the head. Rational things and their components are represented by the **breast** and the parts belonging to the breast. Natural things are represented by the **feet** and the parts belonging to the feet. 

This is why the **sole** and the **heel** of the foot signify the lowest natural things (see section 259), and why a **shoe** signifies the lowest things of all, which are "filthy" <note>original: "sordent"; referring to worldly or external concerns</note> (see section 1748). Similar things are signified by the visions and dreams of the Prophets, such as the **statue seen by Nebuchadnezzar**, whose:
* **Head** was of fine gold, 
* **Breast and arms** were of silver, 
* **Belly and thighs** were of brass, 
* **Legs** were of iron, 
* **Feet** were partly iron and partly clay (Daniel 2:32, 33).

In this vision, the **head** signifies celestial things, which are innermost and are represented by **gold** (as shown in sections 113, 1551, 1552). The **breast and arms** signify spiritual or rational things...

The **feet**, however, are the lower things which are **natural** <note>In this context, "natural" refers to the outermost level of human experience and the physical world, as opposed to the "spiritual" or "celestial" levels.</note>. The truths of these natural things are signified by **iron**, and the goods by **clay** or mud. These levels succeed one another in the Lord’s Kingdom in the heavens, in the Church (which is the Lord’s Kingdom on earth), and also in every individual who is a kingdom of the Lord. 

The same applies to the vision given to **Daniel**, of which it is written: 
> “I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a certain man clothed in linen, whose waist was girded with the gold of Uphas; his body was like Tarshish <note>original: "Tharschisch"; likely referring to a yellow jasper or beryl</note>, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like lamps of fire, and his arms and **feet** like the shine of polished bronze.” (Daniel 10:5–6)

The arms and feet are its exterior things, which are the **literal sense**, because natural things are there—for the literal sense is taken from natural things. Furthermore, what each part signifies—namely the waist, body, face, eyes, and other parts of a man—can be established from the "representatives" in the next life. It also signifies the **literal sense of the Word**, in which externals are represented by natural things (as was said). These are the "feet," under which there was something like a work of sapphire and the substance of heaven. That it was the Lord who appeared to them, but only in those lower or natural things, is clear; for He is called the "God of Israel," whom all things of the Church represented and all things of the Word signified in the **internal sense**. 

The Lord presents Himself to be seen according to the things being signified at the time. The living creatures seen by **Ezekiel**, which were Cherubim, are described regarding celestial and spiritual things by their faces and wings; but regarding natural things, it is said:

By this angel, the Word is similarly signified as it is in the internal sense (by the rainbow over the head and the face like the sun). But the external sense, or the literal sense, is signified by the **feet**. The "sea" represents natural truths, and the "earth" represents natural goods. From this, it is clear what is signified by the fact that he placed his **right foot**...

The term **Footstool** <note>original: "Scabellum pedum"; literally "a stool for the feet"</note> is mentioned frequently throughout the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible</note>, but its meaning in the internal sense is generally unknown. As seen in Isaiah: 

> "Thus says Jehovah: 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my **footstool**. Where is the house that you will build for me? And where is the place of my rest?'" (<term>Isaiah 66:1</term>)

**Heavens** signify celestial and spiritual things—the innermost levels of both the Lord's kingdom in the heavens and the Lord's kingdom on earth (that is, in the Church). This also applies to every individual who is a "kingdom of the Lord" or a "church." Thus, the heavens represent celestial and spiritual things in themselves, which belong to love, charity, and the resulting faith. They encompass everything belonging to internal worship and the internal sense of the Word. These are called the **Lord's Throne**.

**The Earth**, however, signifies all the lower things that correspond to the heavens, such as the lower rational and natural things. Because of this correspondence, celestial and spiritual qualities are also attributed to them. These include the things in the lower heavens, the Church, and external worship, as well as the literal sense of the Word. In short, all things that proceed from internal sources and are presented in external forms—because they are **Natural**—are called the "Earth" and the **Lord's Footstool**.

They did not know that the House of God and the Temple signified external representative worship. They were entirely ignorant of the internal things of the Church, which were signified by "heaven" or the "Throne of God."

When these things are perverted and defiled, they are called enemies. But because they relate to internal worship when viewed in their proper state, they become the "footstool" once that worship is restored—both the elements of external worship and the literal sense of the Word.

This passage concerns the Lord's Kingdom and the Church. For example, Aaron and his sons were commanded to wash their **hands and feet** before they entered the Tabernacle (<term>Exodus 30:19, 20; 40:31, 32</term>). 

Anyone can see that these rituals represented hidden spiritual secrets. After all, what is the washing of hands and feet but an external act? It accomplishes nothing unless the internal self is clean and pure; yet the internal cannot be cleaned or purified by such a washing. However, because all the rites of that Church signified internal things—which are celestial and spiritual—this rite did as well. Specifically, it signified the purity of **External worship**. External worship is considered "clean" only when the "internal" (the spiritual intent) is present within it. This is why their washing basins were made of bronze <note>original: "æs"; often translated as brass in older texts, but referring here to the natural level of "good"</note>. This was also why the great basin in Solomon's Temple was called the "Brazen Sea," surrounded by ten smaller bronze basins (<term>1 Kings 7:23, 38</term>). Bronze represented the "good" found in external worship, which is the same as "natural good" (for the meaning of bronze, see numbers 425 and 1551).

Similarly, it was a symbolic law that any man from the lineage of Aaron who had a **broken foot** or a broken hand could not approach to offer the fire-offerings to Jehovah (<term>Leviticus 21:19, 21</term>). Those with broken feet and hands represented people whose external worship is distorted or "perverse."

That **Feet** signify "natural things" is also clear throughout the writings of the Prophets. Consider the prophecy of Moses: 

> "Blessed above sons is Asher; let him be acceptable to his brothers, and let him dip his **foot** in oil. Your **shoe** shall be iron and bronze." (<term>Deuteronomy 33:24, 25</term>)

These words cannot be understood unless one knows what "Oil," "Foot," "Iron," "Bronze," and "Shoe" signify in the internal sense. The **Foot** signifies the natural level of the person; the **Shoe** signifies an even lower natural level, such as the "corporeal sensual" <note>The most basic level of the mind tied directly to the physical senses</note> (see number 1748). **Oil** signifies the celestial (number 886), **Iron** signifies natural truth (numbers 425, 426), and **Bronze** signifies natural good (numbers 425, 1551). From this, the hidden meaning of the verse becomes clear.

In Nahum: 
> "Jehovah’s way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the **dust of His feet**." (<term>Nahum 1:3</term>)

Here, the "dust of the feet" signifies the natural and corporeal things in man, which give rise to "clouds" (obscurity or lack of spiritual sight). The same is signified in David: 
> "Jehovah bowed the heavens and came down, and darkness was **under His feet**." (<term>Psalm 18:10</term>)

When the "goods" and "truths" of faith are distorted by what people call "natural light" (reasoning based only on the physical world), it is described in the Word as the **feet and hooves** of a beast that disturb the waters and trample food. As seen in Ezekiel: 
> "You broke forth into the rivers and troubled the waters with your **feet**, and trampled their rivers... I will destroy every beast from beside the great waters; neither shall the **foot of man** trouble them anymore, nor the **hooves of beasts** trouble them." (<term>Ezekiel 32:2, 13</term>)

As previously shown (numbers 1164, 1165, 1462), **Egypt** signifies "scientifics" <note>original: "scientifica"; factual knowledge or data gathered through the senses</note>. People use these to argue about the secrets of faith, refusing to believe until they can grasp those secrets through natural data. This is essentially never believing at all; for the more such people reason this way, the less they believe (see numbers 128, 129, 130, 215, 232, 233, 1072, 1385).

From all these examples, it is now clear that in the Word, **Feet** signify "natural things." Exactly what else they signify is made clear by the context of the specific subject being discussed.

In the inner meaning, all these things are called "Heavenly Foods." This can be even better understood from the burnt offerings <note>original: "Holocaustis"</note> and sacrifices made from lambs, oxen, she-goats, kids, rams, and young bulls. These were collectively called the **Bread of the Fire of Jehovah**, as is clearly evident from those passages in the writings of Moses concerning the various sacrifices. It is said that "the priest shall burn them on the altar as the **Bread of the Fire of Jehovah**, as a soothing aroma" (Leviticus 3:11, 16). All those sacrifices and burnt offerings were called by this name.

In the same book, it says: "The sons of Aaron shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they offer the **Fire-offerings of Jehovah, the Bread of their God**. You shall sanctify him, because he offers the **Bread of your God**. In these verses, the sacrifices and burnt offerings are called "Bread," as they also are in Leviticus 22:25. 

Elsewhere it is written: "Command the children of Israel and say to them, 'My offering, My **Bread**, for My fire-offerings of a soothing aroma, you shall be careful to offer to Me at its appointed time'" (Numbers 28:2). Here, "Bread" stands for all the sacrifices listed there. In Malachi, it says: "Offering polluted **Bread** upon My altar" (1:7), which also refers to sacrifices. Even the sanctified parts of the sacrifices that the people ate were called Bread, as is clear from Moses: "Whoever has touched an unclean thing shall not eat of the holy things, but shall wash his flesh in water; and when the sun goes down, he shall be clean, and afterward he shall eat of the holy things, because **this is his Bread**" (Leviticus 22:6–7).

The burnt offerings and sacrifices in the Jewish Church represented nothing other than heavenly things <note>original: "Coelestia"</note> belonging to the Lord's kingdom in the heavens and the Lord's kingdom on earth (which is the Church). They also represented the things of the Lord’s kingdom or the Church within each individual—specifically, everything related to love and charity, for these are heavenly things. Each specific kind of sacrifice represented something particular. At that time, all these things were called <term>Bread</term>. 

Therefore, when sacrifices were abolished and other things were commanded to take their place for outward worship, Bread and Wine were used. It is now clear what "Bread" signifies: it represents everything that the sacrifices once represented—specifically, the Lord himself. Because it signifies the Lord himself, it signifies love itself toward the entire human race and everything that belongs to love. It also signifies a person’s reciprocal love back to the Lord and toward their neighbor. Thus, Bread signifies all heavenly things, just as Wine signifies all spiritual things. 

The Lord teaches this in clear words in the Gospel of John: "They said, 'Our fathers ate manna in the desert, as it is written: **He gave them bread from heaven to eat**.' Jesus said to them, 'Truly, truly, I say to you, Moses did not give you the **Bread from heaven**, but My Father gives you the **true Bread from heaven. For the Bread of God** is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.' They said to Him, 'Lord, always give us **this Bread**.' Jesus said to them, '**I am the Bread of life; he who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst**'" (John 6:31–35). 

And in the same chapter: "Truly I say to you, he who believes in Me has eternal life. **I am the Bread of life**. Your fathers ate manna in the desert and are dead. **This is the Bread which comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die. I am the living Bread which came down from heaven**" (John 6:47–51).

"If anyone eats of this Bread, he will live forever" <note>original: "si quis comederit ex hoc Pane, vivet in æternum"</note> (John 6:47–51). Because of this, Bread is also every celestial thing—that is, all love and charity within a person—for these come from the Lord. Therefore, those who are not in love and charity do not have the Lord with them, and thus they are not granted the good and happy states signified by "Bread" in the internal sense. 

This external symbolic command was given because the majority of the human race focuses on external worship. Without some external sign, there would hardly be any sense of the holy among them. However, when people live in love for the Lord and in charity toward their neighbor, they still possess the internal sense within themselves, even if they do not know that this is the very core of worship. Thus, through their external worship, they are confirmed in the good things signified by "Bread."

2166. **Refresh your heart**, <note>original: "Fulcite cor vestrum"</note> signifies "as much as is appropriate." This was done by taking on something natural, with something celestial joined to it, "as much as was appropriate," which is what "refresh the heart" means. In the most literal sense, to refresh the heart with bread is to be restored and thus to enjoy a small measure of celestial good, as much as is appropriate.

2168. **For this is why you have come to your servant**, signifies that they came for this purpose; this is clear even without explanation.

However, those who do not know what Perception is cannot understand how it functions, nor can they know that there are increasingly interior levels of perception—namely, natural perception, then rational perception, and finally internal perception. This internal perception was Divine and belonged to the Lord alone. Those who are in Perception, such as the Angels, know perfectly well which level they are in, whether they are in natural, rational, or a still more interior perception that is Divine to them. How much more so the Lord, who had perception from the Supreme and Infinite Divine itself (concerning which, see numbers 1616 to 1791 <note>original: "n: 1616, ad f: 1791"</note>), which no angels ever have? This is because they exist in this way: there is a Divine Marriage between celestial and spiritual things—or, what is the same, between the things of love and the things of faith. Or, to put it yet another way, between the things of the will and the intellect. The former belong to "Good," and the latter belong to "Truth." 

Such a Marriage exists in the Lord's Kingdom in the Heavens, and likewise in the Lord's Kingdom on earth (the Church), and in every single person, in all their parts, and even in the most minute details of everything. Anything that is not in such a Marriage does not live. Indeed, such a Marriage exists throughout all of nature and in its individual parts, though under a different form and appearance; otherwise, nothing would ever survive there. 

Because this marriage exists in every detail, the Prophets express every single thing in two ways—especially Isaiah—where one expression refers to the celestial or "good," and the other refers to the spiritual or "truth" (concerning which, see numbers 683, 793, 801). That it is like a marriage in every detail may be seen in numbers 718, 747, 917, and 1432. This is why the Lord's good is represented by Abraham, and His truth by Sarah.

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

It is clear that specific rules were established for Burnt Offerings <note>original: *Holocaustis*</note> as well as for various other types of sacrifices. These included daily, Sabbath, and festival offerings, as well as voluntary, thanksgiving <note>original: *eucharisticis*</note>, and votive offerings. There were also offerings for guilt and sin, for purification and cleansing, and for inaugurations. In every case, the specific animals to be offered were expressly named, as well as the exact number of them required for each type of sacrifice. This would never have been done unless every single detail signified something unique. This is clearly shown in the biblical passages where sacrifices are discussed, such as Exodus 29; Leviticus 1, 3, 4, 9, 16, and 23; and Numbers 7, 8, 15, and 29. While it is not the place here to explain what each specific detail signifies, the same principle holds true when these animals are named by the Prophets.

From these sources, it can be established that **bullocks** <note>original: *juvenci*</note> signify "celestial-natural" things <note>referring to a high level of goodness expressed in the outer, everyday life</note>. That they signify nothing other than heavenly things is also clear from the **Cherubim** seen by Ezekiel and the living creatures seen by John before the throne. Regarding the Cherubim, the Prophet says: "As for the likeness of their faces, each of the four had the face of a **Man**, and the face of a **Lion** on the right side, and the face of an **Ox** <note>original: *Bovis*</note> on the left side, and the face of an **Eagle**" (Ezekiel 1:10). Regarding the four living creatures before the Throne, John writes: "Around the throne were four living creatures; the first creature was like a **Lion**, the second creature was like a **Bullock** <note>original: *Juvenco*</note>, the third creature had a face like a **Man**, and the fourth creature was like a **flying Eagle**. They said: 'Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and is, and is to come'" (Revelation 4:7-8). Anyone can see that these Cherubim and living creatures represented holy things; therefore, the oxen and bullocks mentioned there do so as well.

The same applies to the prophecy of Moses concerning Joseph: "Let it come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of him who was separate from his brothers. His glory is like the firstborn of his **bull** <note>original: *Bovis*</note>, and his horns are like the horns of a **unicorn** <note>original: *monocerotis*; likely referring to a wild ox or powerful horned animal</note>; with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth" (Deuteronomy 33:16-17). These words would be impossible to understand unless one knows what a Bull, a Unicorn, horns, and the other terms signify in the **internal sense** <note>the deeper spiritual meaning hidden within the literal words of the Bible</note>.

Regarding sacrifices in general: they were indeed commanded to the Israelite people through Moses. However, the **Most Ancient Church** <note>the era before the Great Flood</note> knew nothing of sacrifices; it never even entered their minds that they should worship the Lord by slaughtering animals. The **Ancient Church** <note>the era immediately following the Flood</note> was also initially unaware of them. Although that church used **representatives** <note>physical objects and rituals meant to symbolize spiritual realities</note>, they did not use sacrifices. Instead, sacrifices were first instituted in a later church called the **Hebrew Church**, and from there the practice spread to the surrounding nations. It eventually reached Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and thus their descendants.

That the surrounding nations practiced sacrificial worship was shown in number 1343. That Jacob’s descendants also did so—even before they left Egypt and before sacrifices were formally commanded by Moses on Mount Sinai—is clear from Exodus 5:3, 10:25, 27, 18:12, and 24:4-5. This is especially evident from their idolatrous worship of the **Golden Calf**, of which Moses writes: "Aaron built an altar before the calf; and Aaron made a proclamation and said, 'Tomorrow is a feast to Jehovah.' And they rose up early the next day, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play" (Exodus 32:5-6). This occurred while Moses was still on Mount Sinai, and therefore *before* the commandment regarding...

The sanctified things came from sacrifices that were not burned on the altar. They were eaten either by the priests or by the people who offered them, as can be seen from several places where sacrifices are discussed:

The law regarding the **Nazirite** <note>original: *Naziræus* — a person consecrated by a specific vow of separation</note> stated that he should not eat anything from the grape—from which wine comes—from the seeds even to the skin, during the days of his Naziriteship (Numbers 6:4). The celestial man is of such a character that he does not even wish to name spiritual things (as can be seen in Part One, numbers 202, 337, 880 to the end, 1647). Since wine, grapes, and everything derived from grapes signify the **spiritual**, the Nazirite was forbidden from eating them—that is, from having communication with them, joining himself to them, or appropriating them to himself.

The Tree of Life is the celestial itself, and in the highest sense, the Lord Himself, because every celestial thing—that is, all love and charity—comes from Him. Thus, to eat from the tree of life is the same as to "eat" the Lord. To eat the Lord is to be gifted with love and charity, and thus with the things of celestial life. 2189. The phrase **"They said to him, 'Where is Sarah your wife?'"** signifies Rational Truth, which did not appear then because it was in Rational Good. This is evident from the representation of Sarah here as Rational Truth (as discussed above in number 2173). 

How this works—as well as the following sections regarding the state of the Rational in the Lord, represented by Sarah—cannot be easily understood unless one knows the general nature of the Rational mind in terms of **Good** <note>Good: Spiritual love or charity</note> and **Truth** <note>Truth: Spiritual wisdom or faith</note>. This applies both to humans and to the Lord regarding the Divine and the Human states He was in at that time. 

The primary element of the Rational in a human is Truth (as stated before in number 2072); consequently, it is an affection for truth. The reason for this is so that a person can be reformed and thus **regenerated** <term>Regeneration: The process of spiritual rebirth or transformation</term>. This process occurs through knowledge and scientific facts—which are matters of Truth—that are continually implanted in "Good" (that is, in charity), so that the person may receive the life of charity. This is why the affection for truth dominates a person's Rational mind. 

The life of charity, which is heavenly life itself, works like this: in those who are being reformed and regenerated, that life is continually born, grows to maturity, and increases—and it does so through Truths. Therefore, the more truth is introduced, the more the life of charity is perfected. *Consequently, the state of charity in a person depends on the quality and quantity of Truth.*

From this, it can be somewhat clear how the Rational mind of a human works. However, life is not actually *in* Truth, but in Good. Truth is merely the recipient of life (that is, of Good). Truth is like the clothing or garment of Good. For this reason, Truths are called "clothing" or "garments" in the Word. When Good constitutes the Rational, Truth disappears and becomes as if it were Good itself; Good then shines through the truth. This is similar to what happens with Angels: when they appear clothed, their clothing is actually a brightness that takes on the appearance of a garment, which is how Angels appeared before the Prophets. 

These points explain what is meant by "Rational Truth not appearing" because it was within Rational Good (signified by the question, "Where is Sarah your wife?"). However, because the Lord's Rational Good at that time was Divine—a state that no Angel can attain—it cannot be fully described.

2190. The phrase **"Behold, she is in the tent"** signifies that she was in what is holy. This is expressed here by saying the door where Sarah stood was "behind him." 

Regarding the fact that the merely human rational truth then present with the Lord was separated from Him when He joined Himself with the Divine, the situation is as follows: human rational truth does not grasp Divine things because these are above its sphere of understanding. This type of truth communicates with "scientifics" <term>scientifics: facts or knowledge acquired through the senses and worldly study</term> which reside in the natural man. To the extent that it looks at things above itself from these worldly facts, it fails to recognize them. This is because this truth exists in **appearances** <term>appearances: the way spiritual truths seem to our limited human perception before we are fully enlightened</term> which it cannot easily strip away. These appearances are born from sensory perceptions, which lead a person to believe that even Divine things are like sensory ones; however, Divine things are actually exempt from all such appearances. When these Divine truths are explained, the human rational can never believe them because it cannot grasp them. 

For example:
*   **Life:** Rationality thinks, based on appearances, that a person has no life unless it is their own. Yet, in reality, a person first truly lives only when they perceive that their life comes from the Lord. 
*   **Goodness:** Rationality thinks, based on appearances, that the good a person does comes from themselves. In truth, no good comes from oneself, but only from the Lord. 
*   **Merit:** Rationality thinks, based on appearances, that a person deserves salvation when they do good. In truth, a person can merit nothing from themselves; all merit belongs to the Lord. 
*   **Holiness:** A person thinks, based on appearances, that when they are kept from evil and held in good by the Lord, there is nothing but good, justice, and even holiness within them. In truth, there is nothing in a person but evil, injustice, and profanity. 
*   **Charity:** A person thinks, based on appearances, that when they do good out of charity, they do it from their own "will." In truth, it is not from their own will, but from the intellectual part of the mind where charity has been implanted. 
*   **Glory:** A person thinks, based on appearances, that there can be no glory without the glory of this world. In truth, the glory of heaven does not contain even a tiny bit of worldly glory. 
*   **Love:** A person thinks, based on appearances, that no one can love their neighbor more than themselves, but that all love begins with self. In truth, there is no self-love in heavenly love. 
*   **Light:** A person thinks, based on appearances, that no light can exist except that which comes from the world's sun. In truth, there is not a bit of the world's light in the heavens, yet the light there is so great that it exceeds the world's midday light a thousand times over.

...that the Lord cannot shine before the whole of heaven like a sun—even though all the light of heaven comes from Him. From outward appearances, a person also cannot grasp how spirits and angels can be seen (since they are invisible to our physical eyes), or that they can speak with human beings. Because human rationality is limited in this way, the text says it was "separated" while the Lord was united to the Divine in His **Divine Perception**. This is signified by the statement that Sarah (who represents this human rational truth) "stood at the door of the tent" and was "behind Him."

## 2197. Verse 11. 
*And Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in years; and it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.* 

**"Abraham and Sarah were old"** signifies the human nature in the Lord that was to be cast off <note>original: "exueretur"</note>. **"Well advanced in years"** <note>original: "intrantes in dies," literally "entering into days"</note> signifies that the time for this had arrived. **"It had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women"** signifies the state of rational truth, showing that it could no longer remain as it was.

## 2198. 
The reason **"Abraham and Sarah were old"** signifies the human nature in the Lord that was to be cast off is clear from the symbolic roles <note>original: "repræsentatione"</note> of Abraham and Sarah, as well as the meaning of "old age." 

In this chapter, **Abraham** represents the Lord regarding **Rational Good**, and **Sarah** represents the Lord regarding **Rational Truth**. Therefore, both represent the "human" element in the Lord. This is because Jehovah was now present and speaking with Abraham; Jehovah was the Lord’s own Divine essence, not something separate from Him. Even though the historical narrative presents them as separate individuals, the internal meaning reveals they are one, as historical stories cannot represent Divine unity in any other way.

When it says they were "old," it implies that this human state was being laid aside. In the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture.</note>, "old age" simply refers to the final stage of a time or state. Although the Bible often mentions people growing old and dying, in the internal or spiritual sense, there is no such thing as "old age" or physical death. Those in the afterlife do not even know what those concepts are. Instead, "old age" here signifies that the Lord was finishing His transition and casting off His merely human qualities.

## 2199. 
It follows, then, that **"well advanced in years"** (literally, "entering into days") signifies that the time had come. In the Word, "days," "years," and "time" in general signify a "state" (as shown in numbers 23, 487, 488, 493, and 893). Thus, "entering into days" signifies, in the internal sense, entering into that specific state where the human nature would be laid aside—meaning the time was at hand.

2214. **Verse 15. *And Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh," for she was afraid; and He said, "No, but you did laugh."*** "And Sarah denied it, saying, 'I did not laugh,' for she was afraid," signifies that **human rational truth** <term>Human rational truth: The logical part of the human mind that relies on worldly appearances rather than spiritual reality.</term> wanted to excuse itself because it perceived that it was not as it ought to be. "And He said, 'No, but you did laugh,'" signifies that it was nevertheless in that state.

2215. That Sarah’s denial and her excuse—"I did not laugh," for she was afraid—signifies that human rational truth wanted to excuse itself because it realized it was not what it should be, is evident without further explanation.

2216. That the reply, "No, but you did laugh," signifies that it was nevertheless in that state, is also clear without explanation. How these things relate can be seen from what was said above in section 2072 concerning the meaning of "laughing" or "laughter." Specifically, laughter is an affection of the **Rational** <term>The Rational: The faculty of the mind that connects the spiritual to the natural.</term>, and specifically an affection for truth or falsity within the rational mind; this is where all laughter comes from. As long as such an affection is in the Rational and expresses itself in laughter, there is something of the body or the world present—it is purely human. **Celestial good** and **spiritual good** <note>original: *bonum coeleste & bonum spirituale*</note> do not "laugh" in this way; instead, they express their delight and cheerfulness through the face, speech, and gestures in a different manner. In laughter, there are many things involved, usually including a hidden element of contempt, which, though it might not appear on the surface, lies beneath it. It is easily distinguished from true joy of the spirit, which also produces something similar to a laugh. The state of the Lord’s human Rational is described here by the fact that Sarah laughed. This signifies the specific affection with which the **Truth of the Rational** (then separated from Good) viewed the promise that it would strip off the human and put on the **Divine**. It does not mean that the Lord literally laughed, but that from His Divine nature He perceived the quality of His human state at that time—how much of the "human" was still present and needed to be expelled. This is what is signified by Sarah's laughter in the **internal sense** <term>Internal sense: The deeper spiritual meaning within the literal words of the Bible.</term>.

2217. **Verse 16. *And the men rose up from there and looked toward the face of Sodom; and Abraham went with them to send them on their way.*** "The men rose up from there" signifies that this particular **perception** <term>Perception: An immediate, intuitive spiritual understanding or realization.</term> was ending. "And they looked toward the face of Sodom" signifies the state of the human race; "Sodom" represents every kind of evil stemming from **self-love** <note>original: *amore sui*</note>. "And Abraham went with them" signifies that the Lord still remained in that perception with them, but now regarding the human race. "To send them on their way" signifies that He wished to depart from that state.

2218. That "the men rising up" signifies that this perception was ending can be seen from the meaning of "rising," which is to go away, and from the meaning of "the men" discussed above. By the arrival of the **Three Men** (or Jehovah) to Abraham, the Lord’s **Divine Perception** was represented. As shown before, the Lord’s perception from the Divine was first concerning the **Divine Trinity** <note>original: *Trino Divino*</note>—which is the Divine itself, the **Divine Human**, and the **Proceeding** <note>original: *Divinum ipsum, Humanum Divinum & Procedens*; often understood as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit</note>. Afterward, it concerned His own Human nature, which was to put on the Divine. Now follows the perception from the Divine regarding the quality of the human race. These are the three topics treated in this chapter, and they follow in order: first, that the Divine would take on the Human; second, that He would make this Human Divine; and third, that He would do this to save the human race. Regarding the first two, it is said that the perception ended (signified in the internal sense by the "men rising up"). But the perception regarding the state of the human race is signified by their "looking toward the face of Sodom" and "Abraham going with them." In that perception, He did not wish...

2219. **They looked toward the faces of Sodom**, which signifies the state of the human race. This is evident from the meaning of "looking toward the faces," and here, "toward the faces of Sodom." By "faces" are signified all of a person’s internal qualities, whether evil or good, because these shine out from the face (as shown in Part One, section 358). Therefore, in this context, "faces"—since they are said of Sodom—signify internal evils, specifically those of **self-love** <note>original: *amor sui*</note>. These are the evils signified by "Sodom" in general, as will be clear from what follows immediately. 

The reason why the worst of all evils originate from self-love is that self-love is destructive to human society (as shown above in section 2045) and destructive to **heavenly society** <note>original: *Societas coelestis*</note> (section 2057). Because the perversity of the human race is known from this, the "faces of Sodom" here signify the state of the human race. 

Furthermore, it has been shown in various places in Part One what the nature of self-love is: namely, that it is completely contrary to the **order** <term>Order: The divine structure and laws of the universe, particularly the spiritual laws that govern human behavior and happiness.</term> in which humanity was created. Humans were given a rational mind above the animals for the purpose that everyone should wish well and do well to others, both individually and collectively. This is the order in which humanity was created; consequently, it is love for God and love toward the neighbor. This would be the true life of a human, by which they would be distinguished from brute animals. 

This is also the **order of heaven** <note>original: *ordo coeli*</note>, in which a person would exist while living in the world, and thus in the Lord's kingdom. They would transition into this same order when they shed the body that served them on earth, and there they would rise into a state of continually increasing heavenly perfection.

But self-love is the primary—indeed, the only—thing that destroys these things. The love of the world does not do this in the same way; for although the love of the world is opposed to the spiritual things of faith, self-love is diametrically opposed to the **celestial** <term>Celestial: Pertaining to the highest level of heaven, characterized by deep love for the Lord and mutual love, rather than just intellectual faith.</term> things of love. For whoever loves themselves does not love others; instead, they attempt to destroy anyone who does not worship them. They do not wish well or do well to anyone unless that person is "in" with them, or can be won over to be "in" with them, like something grafted into their own desires and fantasies. 

From this, it is clear that from self-love spring all hatreds, all vengeances and cruelties, as well as all infamous pretenses and deceptions—indeed, all unspeakable acts against the order of human society and against the order of heavenly society. 

In fact, self-love is so unspeakable that when its restraints are loosened—that is, when it is given the opportunity to run wild—it rushes forward so far that it wants to rule not only over neighbors and nearby people, but over the whole universe, and even over the **Supreme Divine** <note>original: *Supremum Divinum*</note> itself. A person is unaware of this because they are held in check by bonds they don't fully notice; but as much as these bonds are loosened (as mentioned), that person rushes forward. This has been given to me to know through much experience in the other life. 

Because these things lie hidden within self-love, those who are in self-love and are not gifted with the bonds of **conscience** <note>original: *conscientia*</note> hate the Lord above all others, and thus they hate all the truths of faith. For these truths are the very laws of order in the Lord's kingdom; such people reject them to the point of loathing, which is also clearly manifested in the other life. This love is also the **head of the serpent** <note>original: *caput serpentis*</note> which the **Seed of the woman** <note>original: *Semen mulieris*</note>—that is, the Lord—tramples underfoot (concerning which, see Part One, section 257). 

However, self-love is not always that which appears in external form as arrogance or pride; for sometimes people in these states can have charity...

**Verse 18.** *And Abraham, in becoming, shall become a great and numerous nation; and in him shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.* <note>original: "Et Abraham essendo erit in gentem magnam & numerosam; & benedicentur in illo omnes gentes terræ."</note>

2227. That "Abraham, in becoming, shall become a great and numerous nation" signifies that all good and every truth from it will come from the Lord, is established by the representation of Abraham. It is also established by the symbolic meaning of a "nation" as representing "good" (as seen in sections 1159, 1258, 1259, 1260, 1416, and 1849). "Great" is a term used to describe **good**, while "numerous" is used to describe **truth**, as can be seen in other places in the Word—though we will skip citing those for now.

Truth derived from good—or "truth from good"—is, in its genuine sense, **spiritual good**. There are two distinct types of "good": **celestial good** and **spiritual good**. Celestial good is the love of the Lord; spiritual good is love toward one's neighbor. Spiritual good comes from celestial good, for no one can love the Lord unless they also love their neighbor. Love for the neighbor is contained within love for the Lord. Because love for the Lord comes from the Lord Himself, it also comes from Love itself toward the entire human race. To be in love with the Lord is the same as being in the Lord; and someone who is in the Lord cannot help but be in His love, which is directed toward the human race—and thus toward the neighbor. 

In this way, such a person is in both types of good: celestial and spiritual. The first (celestial) is "good" in its most essential form, while the second (spiritual) is its "truth," or the truth that comes from it. This truth is what we call spiritual good. "Greatness" signifies the first (celestial good), and "numerousness" signifies the second (spiritual good).

2228. That "all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him" signifies that everyone who is in charity will be saved by Him is clear from the meaning of being **blessed**. Those who are gifted with goods of heavenly origin—that is, celestial and spiritual goods, as mentioned just above—are also gifted with eternal salvation; in other words, they are saved.

By "all the nations of the earth," the internal sense <term>Internal Sense: The deeper spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</term> refers to those who are in the "goods" of love and charity. This is clear from the symbolic meaning of "nation" as "good" (sections 1159, 1258, 1259, 1260, 1416, and 1849). It should be obvious to anyone that "all the nations of the earth" does not literally mean every single person in the world, because there are many among them who are not saved; rather, it refers only to those who are in charity—that is, those who have attained a life of charity.

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

The greater part of people do not know what faith is. Some think it is mere thought; some that it is the acknowledgment of something to be believed; others that it is the entire doctrine of faith which must be believed; and others think differently. Thus, they err in the very knowledge of what faith is, and consequently, in what it is that saves a person. But faith is not mere thought, nor is it the acknowledgment of a creed, nor the knowledge of all things belonging to the doctrine of faith. No one can be saved by these things, for they cannot take root any deeper than in the thought. Thought does not save anyone; rather, it is the life which a person has acquired for themselves in the world through the knowledge of faith. This life remains, but all thought that does not agree with one’s life perishes, even to the point of becoming nothing. 

Heavenly societies <note>original: *Consociationes cœlestes*</note> are organized according to lives, and never according to thoughts that are not part of one's life. Thoughts that are not part of one's life are hypocritical and are utterly rejected. In general, there are two types of life: one is infernal, the other is heavenly. Infernal life is contracted from all those ends, thoughts, and works that flow from self-love, and consequently from hatred against one's neighbor. Heavenly life is contracted from all those ends, thoughts, and works that are of love toward the neighbor. This is the life to which all things called "faith" look, and it is acquired through all the things of faith. From this, it can be established what faith is: namely, that it is **charity** <term>Charity: Active love and goodwill toward others as a spiritual principle.</term>. For everything called the doctrine of faith leads to charity; everything is contained within charity, and everything is derived from charity. After the life of the body, the soul is exactly as its love is.

**Verse 19.** *For I know him, because he will command his children and his household after him, and they will keep the way of Jehovah to do justice and judgment, so that Jehovah may bring upon Abraham that which he has spoken concerning him.* <note>original: "Quia novi illum, propterea quod præcipiet filiis suis, & domui suæ post se, & custodient viam Jehovæ ad faciendum Justitiam & Judicium, propterea ut adducat Jehovah super Abrahamum, illud quod loquutus est super illum."</note>

"Children" are those who are in truths; "household" are those who are in goods; "way" is doctrine; "justice" <term>Justice: In this context, the pursuit of what is morally good.</term> pertains to good; "judgment" pertains to truth. "So that Jehovah may bring upon Abraham that which he has spoken concerning him" signifies that for this reason, the Human Essence will be joined to the Divine Essence.

**2230.** "For I know him": That this signifies being true can be established from the meaning of "to know." To know someone is properly to know that they are of such a character; similarly, when applied to a thing or any other matter, it is to know that it is of such a nature. Therefore, "to know" refers to that which is predicated and signifies that which is understood according to the series of things—that it is so, or that it is true.

**2231.** "Because he will command his children and his household after him, and they will keep the way of Jehovah, to do justice and judgment": That this signifies that all doctrine of charity and faith is from Him can be established from the signification of children, household, way, justice, and judgment. This doctrine regarding "good" is signified by "justice," and regarding "truth" by "judgment." The doctrine of good is the doctrine of charity, and the doctrine of truth is the doctrine of faith. # GENESIS

... of charity; for as was stated in number 2228, everything belonging to faith looks toward **charity** <term>Charity: In this context, it refers to the spiritual principle of active love and goodwill toward others.</term>. There is no other difference between charity and faith than that which exists between willing good and thinking good. Whoever wills good also thinks good; it is the same as the relationship between the **will** <note>original: *voluntas*</note> and the **intellect** <note>original: *intellectus*</note>. Those who reflect on it know that the will is one thing and the intellect is another. In the learned world <note>original: *in orbe erudito*</note>, this distinction is well known, and it appears clearly in those who intend evil and yet, out of their thought, speak well. From this, it is obvious to anyone that the will is one thing and the intellect is another, and thus that the **human mind** is divided into two distinct parts which do not always act as one.

However, a person was created in such a way that those two parts should constitute one mind. There should be no other distinction than what might be called a comparative one—like that between a flame and the light it produces. Love for the Lord and charity toward the neighbor would be like the flame, and every perception and thought would be like the light coming from it. In this state, love and charity would be the essence of all perception and thought—that is, present in every single part of it. Perception or thought concerning the quality of love and charity is what is called **faith**. 

But because the human race began to will evil, to hate their neighbor, and to practice revenge and cruelty, that part of the mind called the "will" became utterly ruined. People then began to distinguish between charity and faith. They began to refer all **doctrinal matters** <note>original: *doctrinalia*</note> of their religion to "faith" and to call those things by the single name of "faith." Eventually, they went so far as to say that they could be saved by **faith alone** <note>original: *sola fides*</note>. By this, they meant their doctrines, provided they believed them, regardless of how they lived. 

Thus, charity was separated from faith. In such a state, faith is nothing more (to use a comparison) than a certain light without a flame—like the light of the sun in wintertime, which is so cold and frozen that the plants of the earth grow numb and die. Yet, faith derived from charity is like the light in spring and summer, through which all things sprout and bloom. This can also be known from the fact that love and charity are a heavenly flame, and faith is the spiritual light derived from it. These things present themselves similarly to be perceived and seen in the **other life** <note>original: *altera vita*; referring to the spiritual world or afterlife</note>. For there, the Lord’s "Celestial" quality manifests before the angels as a flaming radiance like the sun, and the Lord’s "Spiritual" quality manifests through the light from it. Angels and spirits are affected by these according to the life of love and charity they have within them. From this come the joys and happiness, with all their variations, in the other life. From these points, it can be established how the matter stands with the claim that "faith alone saves."

### 2232. 
That **sons** signify those who are in truths is evident from the signification of a "son" in the Word, which is truth (as discussed in numbers 489, 491, 533, and 1147). In an abstract sense, "sons" signify truths; but when applied to a person, "sons" refers to all those who are in truths.

### 2233. 
That a **house** signifies those who are in goods is evident from the signification of a "house" as being "good" (as discussed in numbers 710, 1708, and 2048). By "house," or those "born of the house," goods are likewise signified in an abstract sense; but when applied to a person, it refers to all who are in goods.

2235. That **justice** <note>original: *Justitia*</note> relates to what is good, and **judgment** <note>original: *Judicium*</note> relates to what is true, can be seen from the meaning of "Justice" and the meaning of "Judgment." In the **Word** <term>The Word: A term for the Bible, specifically its deeper spiritual meaning.</term>, "Justice" and "Judgment" are frequently named together, but what they signify in the **internal sense** <note>original: *sensu interno*; the hidden, spiritual meaning of scripture</note> has not been known until now. In the most literal sense, "Justice" is spoken of regarding what is just, and "Judgment" regarding what is right. We call it "just" when someone is judged based on what is good, according to their conscience; we call it "right" when they are judged according to the law—the "justness of the law"—and thus also according to conscience, because the law serves as the standard.

In the internal sense, however, **Justice** is what comes from good, and **Judgment** is what comes from truth. "Good" includes everything belonging to love and charity; "truth" includes everything belonging to the faith derived from that love. Truth draws its very essence from good and is called "truth from good," just as faith comes from love; in the same way, judgment comes from justice. That Justice and Judgment signify these things is clear from these passages in the Word:

In Jeremiah: "Thus says Jehovah: Do **judgment and justice**, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the oppressor. Woe to him who builds his house by **unrighteousness** <note>original: *non-Justitia*</note>, and his upper rooms by **injustice** <note>original: *non-Judicio*</note>. Did not your father eat and drink and do **judgment and justice**? Then it was well with him" (<term>chapter 22</term>: 3, 13, 15). Here, "judgment" stands for the things of truth, and "justice" for the things of good.

In Ezekiel: "If the wicked man turns from his sin and does **judgment and justice**... all his sins that he has committed shall not be remembered against him; he has done **judgment and justice**, he shall surely live. When the wicked man turns away from his wickedness and does **judgment and justice**, he shall live because of them" (<term>chapter 33</term>: 14, 16, 19). Similarly, judgment stands for the truth of faith, and justice for the good of charity.

In Amos: "Let **judgment** flow like waters, and **justice** like a mighty stream" (<term>chapter 5</term>: 24).

In Isaiah: "Thus says Jehovah: Keep **judgment** and do **justice**, for My salvation is near to coming, and My **justice** to be revealed" (<term>chapter 56</term>: 1).

In the same author: "Of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom, to establish it and to uphold it in **judgment and justice**, from now and forever" (<term>chapter 9</term>: 7). This refers to being established in the truths of faith and the goods of charity.

In the same author: "Jehovah is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with **judgment and justice**" (<term>chapter 33</term>: 5). "Judgment" stands for faith, and "Justice" for love; "Zion" stands for the Church. Judgment is mentioned first because love is reached through faith; however, when Justice is mentioned first, it signifies that faith is coming from love.

As in Hosea: "I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you to Me in **justice and judgment**, and in mercy and in compassion; and I will betroth you to Me in **faith**, and you shall know Jehovah" (<term>chapter 2</term>: 19, 20). Here, "Justice" is mentioned first, as is "Mercy," which belong to love; "Judgment" follows, as do "Compassions," which belong to the faith that comes from love—both together are called **Faith** or **Faithfulness**.

In David: "Jehovah, Your mercy is in the heavens, Your truth reaches to the clouds; Your **justice** is like the mountains of God, Your **judgments** are a great deep" (Psalm <term>36</term>: 5, 6). There, both "Mercy" and "Justice" similarly refer to love, while "Truth" and "Judgments" refer to faith.

In the same author: "Truth shall spring out of the earth, and **justice** shall look down from heaven; even Jehovah..."

"...Jehovah will give what is good, and our land shall yield its increase," <note>original Latin: *Jehovah dabit bonum, et terra nostra dabit proventum suum*</note> Psalm 85:12–13. In that passage, "Truth" refers to faith, standing in for **judgment**, and "Justice" refers to love or mercy. In Zechariah: "I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God, in **truth** and in **justice**," (8:8). From this, it is also clear that judgment is truth and justice is good, because "truth" is used here in the place of "judgment." Similarly, in David: "He who walks uprightly, and works **justice**, and speaks **truth**," Psalm 15:2. 

Because faith belongs to charity (or truth belongs to good), the "truths of good" are frequently called the "judgments of justice" throughout the Word. In this sense, "judgments" mean nearly the same thing as "commandments," as seen in Isaiah: "They seek Me daily, and desire to know My ways, as a nation that does **justice** and does not forsake the **judgment** of its God; they ask of Me the **judgments of justice**, they desire to draw near to God," (58:2). Regarding commandments, in David: "Seven times a day I praise You because of Your **judgments of justice**; all Your **commandments** are **justice**," Psalm 119:164, 172. 

It is said of the Lord especially that He performs judgment and justice when He creates a person anew <term>creates a person anew: Refers to the process of spiritual rebirth or regeneration</term>, as in Jeremiah: "Let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows Me, that I am Jehovah, who exercises mercy, **judgment**, and **justice** in the earth," (9:24). There, "mercy," which belongs to love, is described through "judgment" and "justice." In the same prophet: "I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and act wisely, and shall perform **judgment** and **justice** in the earth," (23:5; 33:15). 

Hence it is said in John: "If I go away, I will send the Comforter <term>Comforter: Translated from the Greek 'Paracletos,' referring to the Holy Spirit</term> to you; and when he comes, he will convict the world of sin, of **justice**, and of **judgment**: of sin, because they do not believe in Me; of **justice**, because I go to my Father and you see Me no more; of **judgment**, because the prince of this world is judged," (16:7–11). In this context, "sin" stands for all unbelief. The phrase "convicting of justice" refers to everything that is against what is good—even though the Lord united the **Human** to the **Divine** to save the world (which is meant by "I go to the Father and you see Me no more"). The "convicting of judgment" refers to everything against what is true—even though evils have been cast down into their hells so they can no longer cause harm (which is meant by "the prince of the world is judged"). 

In general, the phrase "convicting of sin, justice, and judgment" means convicting the world of all unbelief against what is good and true, showing that there is no charity or faith. In ancient times, "justice and judgment" were understood to mean all mercy and grace regarding the Lord, and all charity and faith regarding humanity.

These are the things signified in the internal sense <note>original: *sensu interno*</note> by the statement that He would "bring upon Abraham what He had spoken concerning him."

2237. **Verse 20. And Jehovah said, "Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has become great, and because their sin has become very grievous."** <note>original Latin: *Et dixit Jehovah, clamor Sodomæ & Amoræ, quod magnus factus sit, & peccatum eorum quod grave factum valde.*</note> **"Jehovah said"** signifies perception. **"The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has become great, and because their sin has become very grievous"** signifies that the falsity and evil of self-love have increased even to the point of consummation <term>consummation: The final stage of a spiritual state or "church" where no good or truth remains.</term>. 2238. That **"Jehovah said"** signifies perception is established by the meaning of "to say" in the historical sense of the Word, which—as noted several times before—means to perceive. When the phrase "Jehovah said" occurs in the historical narratives of the Bible, it signifies a perception that is not entirely continuous with what came before, but is something following it, and sometimes something entirely new (see also section 2061).

2239. That **"the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has become great, and their sin has become very grievous"** signifies that the falsity and evil of self-love have grown until they reached their end (consummation) is clear from the following:
*   The meaning of **Sodom**, which represents evil stemming from self-love.
*   The meaning of **Gomorrah** <note>original: *Amoræ*</note>, which represents the falsity arising from that same self-love (as shown above in section 2220).
*   The meaning of **"cry,"** which is falsity, and **"sin,"** which is evil (as will be explained shortly).

From these points, it is evident that a "great cry" and a "grievous sin" signify that falsity and evil have reached their peak or limit. This is even clearer in the following verses, where it is said that if ten righteous people were found there, the city would be spared (Verse 32). This signifies that if any "remains" <term>remains: Small traces of good and truth preserved by God in a person's inner being.</term> were still present—that is, if there were any good or truth left—the city would remain. When there is no longer any good or truth within a person, then vastation and desolation <term>vastation and desolation: The total loss or stripping away of spiritual life and understanding.</term> occur, followed by consummation. This will be discussed in the next verse.

2240. That a **"cry"** signifies falsity and **"sin"** signifies evil can be seen from how "cry" is used in the Word. No one can see that "cry" signifies falsity unless they know the internal, spiritual sense of the Word. This term occurs several times in the Prophets; when the text deals with vastation and desolation, it says that people "howl" and "cry." This signifies that goods and truths have been wasted. In the internal sense, "cry" is a specific term used to describe falsity, as seen in Jeremiah: "A voice of the **cry** of the shepherds, and a howling of the powerful of the flock, because Jehovah is wasting their pasture" (25:36). Here, the "cry of the shepherds" means they are in falsity, which leads to their spiritual waste.

This passage describes the desolation of faith caused by falsities. The "overflowing flood" represents falsity (as shown in Part One, sections 705 and 790). 

In Zephaniah: "The voice of a **cry** from the fish gate, and a howling from the second quarter, and a great crashing from the hills... their wealth shall become a plunder, and their houses a desolation" (1:10, 13). Here also, a "cry" is predicted concerning the falsities that cause waste. 

In Isaiah: "On the way to Horonaim they shall raise a **cry** of destruction... for the waters of Nimrim shall be desolations, for the grass has withered, the herb is consumed, there is no green thing" (15:5–6; see also Jeremiah 48:3). Here, the desolation of faith and its final end are described by "cries"...

Nevertheless, it is phrased this way because it appears to man as if it happens that way. For man...

These are all *falsities from evil*.

<header>GENESIS.</header>

...What produces evil is when a person adopts a principle from their religious belief and believes it to be good or holy, when in fact it is inherently evil. For example, someone who believes because of their religion that a human being can save them, and therefore worships and adores that person, creates evil from that falsehood. The same applies to any other religious belief that is false in itself. Because falsehood stems from evil, and falsehood in turn produces evil, this state is called a "cry." <note>original: *clamor*. In Swedenborg’s terminology, a "cry" signifies a state of falsehood or the outcry of evil against truth.</note>

This "cry" signifies in a general sense everything that such a state involves—namely, evil. This is evident from the phrase: "to see whether they have done according to its cry" (using the singular "its" or *ejus*) "which has come to Me," and "they have made a consummation" (using the plural *fecerint*). <note>The author is pointing out a grammatical shift in the Latin Bible from singular to plural to show that while the "cry" is a single general state of falsehood, its "consummation" or fulfillment involves many specific evils.</note>

The meaning of **Consummation** was shown in Part One, number 1857. Furthermore, what Consummation is can be understood through the history of the various Churches:

1.  **The Most Ancient Church**, called "Man," was the most celestial of all. <note>original: *Antiquissima Ecclesia*. Swedenborg refers to the symbolic era of Adam/Eden as a "Church" of direct perception of God.</note> Over time, it drifted so far from the good of love that finally nothing celestial remained. This was its **Consummation**, described by the state of the people before the Great Flood.
2.  **The Ancient Church**, which followed the flood and was called "Noah," was less celestial. Over time, it also failed in the good of charity until nothing of charity remained. It turned partly into magic, partly into idolatry, and partly into a set of dogmas separated from charity. This was its **Consummation**.
3.  **The Hebrew Church** followed, and was even less celestial and spiritual, placing its holy worship in external rituals. Over time, this Church was deformed in various ways, and its external worship turned into idolatry. This was its **Consummation**.
4.  **A Fourth Church** was then established among the descendants of Jacob. It possessed nothing celestial or spiritual but only a *representation* of it. Therefore, this Church was a **Representative Church** of celestial and spiritual things. <note>original: *Ecclesia repræsentativa*. A church where the rituals symbolize spiritual truths even if the practitioners do not understand them.</note> They did not know what the rituals represented or signified, but the Church was established so that there might still be some connection between mankind and heaven—similar to the connection between a symbol of good and the good itself. Eventually, this Church fell into such falsehoods and evils that every ritual became idolatrous. This was its **Consummation**.

Because the connection between the human race and heaven had been completely broken in this last stage—and humanity would have perished because there was no Church to act as a link (see numbers 468, 637, 931, 2054)—the **Lord** then came into the world. By uniting His Divine Essence with His Human Essence within Himself, He joined heaven with earth. At the same time, He established a new Church, called the **Christian Church**. Initially, this Church was centered on the "good of faith," and its members lived together as brothers in charity. However, over time, this Church has diverged in various ways. Today, it has become such that people do not even know that the fundamental principle of faith is love for the Lord and charity toward one’s neighbor. Even though their doctrines state that the Lord is the Savior of the human race, that people will rise after death, and that there is a heaven and a hell, few actually believe it. Because the Church has become like this, its **Consummation** is not far off.

From all this, it is clear what **Consummation** is: namely, it is when evil reaches its peak. The same process happens "in particular"—that is, within every individual person. However, how consummation occurs individually for each person is determined by Divine...

The Lord’s Mercy will be discussed in the following pages. Throughout the Word, the topic of "Consummation" is addressed, describing the state that precedes it through "wastation" and "desolation," which is then followed by "Visitation." <note>original: *consumatio*, *vastatio*, *desolatio*, *visitatio*. These are technical terms in Swedenborg’s theology: "wastation" is the stripping away of false beliefs, "desolation" is the lack of truth, and "visitation" is the final judgment or turning point.</note>

2244. **Verse 22. And the men looked forth from there and went toward Sodom; and Abraham was still standing there before Jehovah.** 
"The men looked forth from there" signifies the Lord's thought from the Divine. "And they went toward Sodom" signifies the state of the human race, which is in such great evil. "And Abraham was still standing there before Jehovah" signifies the Lord's thought from the Human that was joined to the Divine, in the manner described above.

2245. **The men looked forth from there** signifies the Lord’s thought from the Divine. This is evident from the meaning of "looking forth," which is to think. To "see" in the internal sense (as in common speech) is to understand, for understanding is the sight of the internal man. Thus, to "look forth" is to think, which is the sight of the internal or the intellect. 

This is also evident from the meaning of the "Men," which represents the Divine. Throughout this chapter, the term "Men" is used interchangeably with "Jehovah." When "Men" is used, it signifies the **Trine** <note>original: *Trinum*. A term used to describe the Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit as the Divine Itself, the Divine Human, and the Divine Proceeding.</note>—namely, the Divine Itself, the Divine Human, and the Proceeding. The Lord's thought from this Divine is signified by the "men looking forth from there." This thought came from the Human conjoined with the Divine, a conjunction discussed at the beginning of this chapter. However, the **Perception** <note>original: *Perceptio*. In this context, an intuitive spiritual understanding that comes directly from the Divine.</note> from which the thought originated was from the Divine; therefore, it is said immediately afterward in the same verse, "Jehovah," and that "he stood before Jehovah." Since the Human was conjoined to the Divine, it was also one with the Proceeding.

2246. **And they went toward Sodom** signifies the human race that is in such great evil. This is clear from the meaning of "Sodom," which represents evil stemming from **self-love** <note>original: *amor sui*. This is considered the root of all spiritual opposition to God.</note> (as discussed above in number 2220). "To look toward the face of Sodom" means looking at the state of the human race (number 2219). 

The reason Sodom signifies the state of the human race in such evil is that "Sodom" here does not refer to the literal city of Sodom, but to everyone in the whole world who is in self-love. The description of Sodom represents the state of all who are in that evil, as will be clear from what follows. That self-love is the source of all evils—and is evil itself—is evident from what was previously said and shown in numbers 2045, 2057, and 2219. This is why the text says they were "in such great evil."

2247. **And Abraham was still standing there before Jehovah** signifies the Lord's thought from the Human that was adjoined in the manner just mentioned. This is evident from the representation of Abraham in this chapter as the Lord in His Human state. It follows without further explanation that "standing before Jehovah" means the thought came from the Human that was adjoined to the Divine, as described at the start of this chapter and in number 2045.

2248. **Verse 23. And Abraham drew near and said, "Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?"** 
"Abraham drew near and said" signifies the Lord’s thought from the Human, which joined itself more closely to the Divine. "Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?" signifies the Lord’s grief stemming from His love for the human race, and His intercession that good might still be joined to them, even though there is evil.

# GENESIS

2249. **Abraham drew near and said.** This signifies the Lord's thought from the **Human** <term>Human: In this context, Swedenborg refers to the "Human Essence" or the human nature the Lord assumed on earth</term> which joined itself more closely to the **Divine** <term>Divine: The "Divine Essence" or the infinite Godhead</term>. This follows from the preceding sections, which dealt with the Lord’s thought concerning the human race; therefore, it is stated here without further explanation. 

In this chapter, the internal sense describes the state of the Lord's thought and perception, and at the beginning, the state of the union of the Lord’s Human with His Divine. To a person, this might perhaps appear as if it were not of great importance; however, it is actually of the highest significance. For in the presence of **Angels** (to whom the internal sense of the **Word** <term>the Word: The Holy Scriptures, viewed here as having a hidden, spiritual meaning</term> is the primary focus), these things are presented vividly with their **representatives** <term>representatives: Spiritual appearances or symbols that perfectly mirror internal truths</term> in a most beautiful form. 

Beyond this, there are countless related things regarding the Lord’s conjunction with heaven and the reception of His Divine into the human nature of the angels. Angelic ideas are such that they find these topics more delightful than any other and perceive them as most pleasant. Through this, they are also enlightened and confirmed more and more regarding the union of the Lord’s Human Essence with the Divine. 

Angels were once people; and while they were people, they could not help but think of the Lord as a man, and of the Lord as God, as well as of the **Divine Trinity** <note>original: *Trino Divino*</note>, forming various ideas for themselves, even if they did not then know what kind they were. For **heavenly mysteries** <note>original: *arcana coelestia*</note> have this quality: even though they surpass all human understanding, everyone still forms some idea of them. Nothing can be held in the memory, much less enter into thought, except through some idea formed in one way or another. 

Because these ideas could only be formed from things in the world, or from analogies of things in the world, fallacies inevitably crept in based on a lack of understanding. In the next life, these fallacies alienate a person’s inner thoughts from the truth and good of faith. To dispel such misconceptions, this chapter (in its internal sense) deals with the union of the Lord’s Human with the Divine, and His Perception and Thought. When the Word is read, these truths are presented to the perception of angels in such a way that their earlier ideas—formed from foreign concepts and the doubts arising from them—are gradually dissipated, and new ideas, which conform to the light of truth in which the angels live, are introduced. This happens more with **spiritual angels** than with **celestial angels** <note>spiritual and celestial: Swedenborg distinguishes between two types of angels—spiritual angels, who are motivated by truth/intellect, and celestial angels, who are motivated by love/will</note>; for according to the purification of their ideas, they are perfected for the reception of heavenly things. It is well known that "heaven is not pure before the Lord," and it is a truth that angels are continually being perfected.

2250. **Will You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?** <note>original: *Num etiam delebis justum cum impio*</note>. This can be seen from the zeal of love that shines through here, and even more in the following verse (25), where it is said: "Far be it from You to do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked; far be it from You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" 

Furthermore, this is clear from the meaning of "the Righteous," which is **good** <note>original: *justum*; see paragraphs 612 and 2235</note>, and from the meaning of "the Wicked," which is the opposite of the righteous—that is, the opposite of good, or **evil**. It is also evident from these words and those following in this chapter that this is an Intercession. The Lord’s intercession for the human race took place while He was in the world, specifically when He was in a state of **humiliation** <term>humiliation: The state in which the Lord acted from His human nature, feeling separate from the Divine</term>; for then, as was previously stated...

2250. ...as previously mentioned, he spoke with **Jehovah** as if with another person; but in the state of **Glorification** <term>Glorification: The process by which the Lord's human nature was made one with His Divine nature</term>, when the **Human Essence** was made one with the **Divine**, and it too became Jehovah, then he does not "intercede" in the sense of one person pleading with another.
