2251. **Verse 24. *Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city; will you also destroy and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are within it?*** <note>original: "Forte sint quinquaginta justi in medio urbis..."</note>

**"Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city"** signifies that truths can be full of "goods" <term>goods: In this context, "goods" (Latin: *bona*) refers to acts and intentions of love, charity, and kindness</term>.

**"Will you also destroy and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are within it"** signifies intercession based on love, meaning that they would not then perish.

2252. The fact that **"fifty righteous within the city"** signifies that truths can be full of goods is established from the following:
* The meaning of **Fifty**, which signifies what is "full."
* The meaning of **Righteous**, which signifies "good" (as discussed in numbers 612 and 2235).
* The meaning of **Middle**, which signifies "within" (as discussed in number 1074).
* The meaning of **City**, which signifies "truth" (as discussed in number 402).

Thus, in the internal sense <term>internal sense: The hidden, spiritual meaning within the literal stories of the Bible</term>, "fifty righteous in the middle of a city" means that truths can be inwardly full of goodness. No one can see this spiritual meaning from the literal words alone, for the historical narrative of the literal sense carries the mind elsewhere. Yet, I know for certain that these words are perceived in this way by those who are in the internal sense.

The numbers themselves—such as **fifty** here, and later **forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty,** and **ten**—are never perceived as simple counts by those in the internal sense. Instead, they represent a specific "thing" or "state." This has been shown previously (in numbers 482, 587, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, 1963, 1988, and 2075). The Ancients also designated the states of their Church through numbers. The nature of their calculations can be seen from the meanings of numbers in the places cited. 

They derived the meanings of numbers from **representatives** <term>representatives: Symbolic spiritual appearances that perfectly mirror internal truths</term> that exist in the world of spirits. When something appears there as if it were numbered, it does not signify a specific amount, but rather a quality or state. This is evident from what was mentioned regarding the number **Twelve** (in numbers 2129, 2130, and 2089), which signifies "all the things of faith." The same applies to the numbers that follow. From this, it is clear what the Word is like in its internal sense.

The reason **Fifty** signifies **"full"** is that it is the number that follows seven times seven (forty-nine); thus, it is the fulfillment of them. For this reason, in the **Representative Church** <term>Representative Church: A historical period where religious rituals acted as symbols of spiritual realities</term>, the "Feast of Seven Sabbaths" was held on the fiftieth day <note>This is the festival of Pentecost</note>, and the **Jubilee** occurred in the fiftieth year. 

Regarding the **Feast of Seven Sabbaths**, **Moses** wrote:
> "You shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering; **seven full Sabbaths shall there be**, until the day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count **fifty days**, and you shall offer a new grain offering to Jehovah." (Leviticus 23:15) <note>original: "Numerabitis vobis a crastino sabbathi... usque ad a crastino Sabbathi Septimi, numerabitis Quinquaginta dies..."</note>

Regarding the **Jubilee**, he wrote:
> "You shall count seven Sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, and the days of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be forty-nine years to you... and you shall sanctify the **fiftieth year**, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants; it shall be a **Jubilee** for you." (Leviticus 25:8, 10) <note>original: "Numerabis tibi septem Sabbatha annorum... sanctificabitis Annum Quinquagesimum... Jubilæus ille erit vobis"</note>

From this, it is clear that the fiftieth is the "fullness" of the sabbaths. Furthermore, wherever **Fifty** is named in the Word, it signifies "Fullness," such as when the **Levites** were numbered from thirty years old and upward, even until the **fiftieth** year. <note>original: "Levitæ a filio triginta annorum & supra, usque ad filium Quinquaginta"</note>

2255. **"Far be it from You to do such a thing"** <note>original: *Absit Tibi a faciendo secundum rem hanc*</note> signifies the Lord’s horror at the thought, which is evident without further explanation.

2256. The phrase **"to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous is treated like the wicked"** signifies that what is good cannot "die" (perish), because evil can be separated from it. This is clear from the meaning of "righteous" <note>original: *justi*</note> as "good," and "wicked" <note>original: *impii*</note> as "evil" (as mentioned above in section 2250). Therefore, "putting the righteous to death with the wicked" refers to mixing good with evil. Because these things should not happen—and because even thinking of them causes horror—they are excluded in the internal sense. Instead, the meaning presented is that good cannot perish because evil can be separated from it.

Few people know how these things work. It should be understood that every good thing a person has thought and done—from infancy to the very end of their life—remains. Similarly, every evil remains, so that not even the smallest bit of it completely vanishes. These things are written in the "book of life" <note>original: *libro vitæ*</note>—that is, in both of a person's memories <note>term: Swedenborg refers to the "exterior memory" of worldly things and the "interior memory" of a person's character and spirit</note> and in their very nature, meaning their character and disposition. From these things, a person has formed their own life and, so to speak, the soul that remains after death. 

However, good is never mixed with evil (and evil with good) in such a way that they cannot be separated. If they were permanently fused together, a person would perish for eternity. The Lord provides against this. When a person enters the next life, if they have lived in the goods of love and charity <note>original: *charitatis*</note>, the Lord separates the evil from them and, through the good they possess, elevates them into heaven. If, however, they have lived in evil—that is, in things contrary to love and charity—then the Lord separates the good from them, and the evil carries them into hell. Such is the fate of everyone after death; yet this is a *separation*, never a complete removal <note>original: *ablatio*</note>. 

Furthermore, because the human will <note>original: *voluntas*</note> (which is the other half of a person's life) is completely corrupted <note>original: *deperdita*</note>, the Lord separates that corrupted part from the intellectual part. In those who are being "born again" (regenerated), He implants the good of charity within the intellect, thereby creating a new will. These are the people who possess a conscience. In this way, the Lord generally separates evil from good. These are the hidden truths <note>original: *arcana*</note> understood in the internal sense by the phrase "good cannot die, because evil can be separated from it."

...to do this according to truth separated from good <note>original: *secundum verum separatum a bono hoc facere*</note>. To understand how this should be interpreted, one must know that there are two things that constitute the order of the entire universe of Heaven, and consequently the entire universe: namely, Good and Truth. Good is the essential element of order, and everything belonging to it is of Mercy. Truth is the secondary element of order, and everything belonging to it is of verities. Divine Good judges everyone to heaven; however, Divine Truth <note>original: *Divinum Verum*</note> condemns everyone to hell <note>original: *infernum*</note>. Therefore, unless the Lord’s Mercy were eternal (which belongs to Good), every single person, no matter how many there are, would be condemned. For the Lord never casts anyone into hell; rather, the person casts themselves in, as has been said several times before. Furthermore, in this process, Divine Good is joined to Divine Truth because if the evil were not separated from the good, the evil would inflict harm upon the good and would continually attempt to destroy order. Thus, it is an act of Mercy that the good are not harmed. This is similar to the kingdoms of the earth: unless evils were punished, the entire kingdom would be infected with wickedness and would perish. Therefore, among kings and judges, it is a greater act of mercy to punish crimes and expel the wicked from society than to show them untimely or misplaced clemency.

### CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

<note>original: *...vat*</note> [continues from previous page] ...It should be known that among those who live in ways contrary to charity, true acknowledgment <note>original: *agnitio*</note> can never exist. Instead, there is only a certain persuasion joined to the love of self or the world; thus, in that acknowledgment, there is no "life of faith," which is the life of charity. 

The worst of people—driven by self-love or worldly love, or seeking to excel others in what is called "intelligence and wisdom" to hunt for honors, fame, and wealth—can seize upon the truths of faith and confirm them with many arguments. Yet, for these people, those truths are dead. The life of truth (and thus of faith) comes solely from the Lord, who is Life itself. The Lord's life is Mercy, which belongs to His love for the entire human race. Those who profess the truths of faith but despise others in comparison to themselves can never receive the Lord’s life; when their self-love or worldly love is challenged, they feel hatred for their neighbor and find pleasure in the loss of their neighbor's wealth, honor, fame, and life. 

However, the nature of the truths of faith is such that a person is regenerated through them, for they are the very vessels <note>original: *ipsissima vasa*</note> that receive what is good. Therefore, a person's state of bliss and happiness after death is determined by the quality of their truths, the quality of the "good" within those truths, and the resulting connection and capacity for those truths to be perfected in the next life.

2262. **That I will spare the whole place for their sake** signifies that they will be saved. This follows from the sequence of the narrative as a conclusion, and thus requires no further explanation. "Place" signifies "state," as shown in sections 1273 and 1378. Thus, "place" is used here for the city to signify that those who are in such a state will be saved.

2263. **Verse 27. *And Abraham answered and said, "Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak to my Lord, though I am but dust and ashes."***
"Abraham answered and said" signifies the Lord’s thought from the human nature <note>original: *ex humano*</note>. "Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak to my Lord, though I am but dust and ashes" signifies the humiliation of the human nature regarding what it was by comparison.

2264. **Abraham answered and said:** That this signifies the Lord's thought from the human nature is clear from the representation of Abraham in this chapter. Here, he represents the Lord in His human nature, as has been mentioned several times above.

2265. **Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak to my Lord, though I am but dust and ashes:** That this signifies the humiliation of the human nature regarding what it was by comparison [to the Divine]. The Lord’s state in the human (His state of humiliation) and His state in the Divine (His state of glorification) have been discussed several times before. In the state of humiliation, He spoke with Jehovah as if with another person; in the state of glorification, He spoke with Himself (see section 1999). 

Because Abraham represents the Lord in His human nature, it is said in that state that the human—relative to the Divine—is **dust and ashes.** This is why that state is called the "state of Humiliation." Humiliation arises from the acknowledgment of one's self, seeing that one is such by comparison. By "the human" here is not meant the **Divine Human** <note>original: *Humanum Divinum*</note>, but the human nature He inherited from His mother, which He completely expelled, putting on the Divine Human in its place. It is that maternal human nature which is described here as "dust and ashes" (see what was said above in section 2159).

2266. **Verse 28. *Perhaps there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: will you destroy all the city for the lack of five? And he said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there."***
"Perhaps there shall lack five of the fifty righteous" signifies "if there should be somewhat less." "Will you destroy all the city for the lack of five?" signifies "would it be destroyed for the small amount that is lacking?"

...is lacking, man will perish; and He said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there," signifies that he would not perish if they could be joined together. <note>original: *deest, peribit homo: & dixit, non perdam, si invenero ibi quadraginta quinque, significat quod non periret, si conjungi possint.*</note>

2267. **Suppose five should be lacking from the fifty righteous** <note>original: *Forte defuerint quinquaginta justis quinque*</note> signifies that if something were slightly less, it would still be accounted for. This is evident from the meaning of "five," which represents "a little" or "less" (concerning the meaning of that number, see Part One, n. 649). The meaning of "fifty righteous" was shown above in n. 2252.

2268. **Will you destroy the whole city for the sake of five?** <note>original: *Num disperdes in quinque totam urbem*</note> signifies asking if a person will perish because of the little that is lacking. This is clear from the meaning of "five," which is "a little" (as mentioned just above), and from the meaning of a "city," which represents "truth" (also discussed previously). In the Word <note>The Bible/Sacred Scripture</note>, the human mind—in terms of the truths it holds—is compared to a city and is even called a "city." The "good" qualities <note>Spiritual "good" refers to love and charity</note> that reside within those truths are compared to the city's inhabitants, and they are indeed called "inhabitants." 

The relationship is similar: if the truths held in a person's memory and thoughts exist without "good," they are like a city without residents—empty and hollow. In fact, it can even be said of angels that they dwell, as it were, in a person's truths. They introduce affections for what is "good" from the Lord when a person lives in love for the Lord and in charity toward their neighbor. This is because angels delight to dwell—that is, to live—with such people. It is quite different for those who possess certain truths but have no "good" of charity.

2269. **And He said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there,"** <note>original: *Et dixit non perdam, si invenero ibi quadraginta quinque*</note> signifies that the person would not perish if truths and goods could be joined together. This is clear from the meaning of the number "forty-five," which represents "conjunction" <term>conjunction: the spiritual joining together of truth in the mind with "good" from the heart</term>. 

It was shown earlier that simple numbers retain their meaning even when they are multiplied; thus, larger numbers carry the same meaning as the smaller ones they are made of. So it is with forty-five, a number composed by multiplying five by nine. Because it is five times nine, it signifies the same as both "five" and "nine." It has been shown that "five" signifies "a little" (n. 649) and "nine" signifies "conjunction" or "what is joined" (n. 2075). Therefore, in this context, it refers to a state where some "good" is joined to truths. 

That numbers in the Word signify actual things or spiritual states is clear from what was said regarding "fifty" (n. 2252) and from other numbers previously discussed (n. 482, 487, 575, 647, 648, 755, 813, 1963, 1988). Because "five" signifies "a little" and "forty-five" signifies "conjunction," the explanation of these numbers in this verse is as follows: 

The text says, *"suppose five should be lacking from the fifty righteous,"* signifying if something were slightly less. Then it says, *"will you destroy the whole city for five?"* signifying whether they will perish for the little that is lacking. Because "five" signifies "a little," the text does not repeat the number "five" afterward. Instead, it says, *"I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there,"* signifying they would not perish if they could be joined together. 

The reason "forty-five" is used here—rather than saying "if five are lacking from fifty"—is because "five" signifies not only "a little" (as shown in n. 649) but also "disjunction" <term>disjunction: the separation of truth from good</term> (as also shown in Part One, n. 1686). Therefore, to ensure that the meaning points to "conjunction" rather than "disjunction," this specific number—forty-five—is named. For forty-five represents a state of joining together, as stated above. In this way, every detail follows beautifully in its proper sequence within the internal sense <note>original: *sensus internus*; the deeper, spiritual meaning of the text</note>. <meta>catchword: yet</meta>

Regarding the conjunction of good with truth, this is a spiritual secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> that cannot be described in a way that common understanding can easily grasp. Only a few things can be said: the more genuine and pure the Truth is, the better the Good that comes from the Lord can be fitted to it, as if to a receiving vessel. However, the less genuine and pure the truth is, the less the Good from the Lord can be fitted to it. This is because they must correspond to one another; the conjunction happens according to this correspondence <note>In this context, "correspondence" refers to the spiritual law where natural things reflect or respond to spiritual realities.</note>. 

Good qualities can never be introduced into false ideas, nor can evil qualities be introduced into truths as receiving vessels, for they are of opposite characters and natures. One rejects the other as its enemy. Indeed, if they tried to join together, one would spit out the other—Good would reject Evil like a poison, and Evil would reject Good like an emetic <note>original: *vomitale*; something that induces vomiting.</note>. This enmity between evil and good is provided for by the Lord so that they might never be mixed; for if they were mixed, the person would perish. In deceitful people and hypocrites, they come very close to being joined, but the Lord constantly prevents them from truly uniting. This is why deceitful people and hypocrites suffer more dreadfully than all others in the next life.

2270. **Verse 29: And he spoke to Him yet again, and said, "Suppose forty are found there." And He said, "I will not do it for forty's sake."**
*And he spoke to Him yet again* signifies thought. 
*And he said, "Suppose forty are found there"* signifies those who have undergone temptations <note>original: *tentationibus*</note>.
*And He said, "I will not do it for forty's sake"* signifies that they will be saved.

2271. **And he spoke to Him yet again:** That this signifies thought is evident from the meaning of "speaking" in the internal sense. Speaking or speech is nothing other than that which flows from thought. Because internal things are represented by external ones—just as "understanding" is represented by "seeing," "the intellect" by "the eye," and "obedience" by "the ear," and so on—so "thinking" is represented by "speaking."

2272. **And he said, "Suppose forty are found there":** That this signifies those who have been in temptations is evident from the meaning of the number forty <note>original: *Quadraginta*</note> as representing temptations (as discussed in Part One, n. 730). How these things follow in sequence can be seen from the nature of temptations. Temptations exist for a purpose: not only to confirm a person in truths, but also so that truths may be more closely joined to good qualities. During a temptation, a person fights for truths against what is false. Because they are then in internal pain and torment, the pleasures of life's cravings and the resulting delights cease. At that time, Good from the Lord flows in, and simultaneously, evils are seen as abominable. This leads to new thoughts, opposite to the previous ones, which the person can later turn toward. In this way, they move from evils toward goods, and these goods are then joined to truths. Because the conjunction of good with truth happens through temptations—and because it was said in the previous verse that those in whom good can be joined to truth would be saved—this logically follows: they can be joined through temptations. This connection of ideas is clear to those who perceive the internal sense.

2273. **He said, "I will not do it for forty's sake":** That this signifies that they will be saved is evident without further explanation. Regarding those signified by "forty-five" in the previous verse, it was said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five," signifying they would not perish if good could be joined to truth. Now follows the mention of "forty," and it is said, "I will not do it for..."

# GENESIS

...forty, which does not mean that people are saved because of temptations <note>original: *tentationes*; refers to spiritual trials or internal conflicts</note>. For some undergo temptations but succumb to them, and thus good qualities are not joined together within them. Indeed, a person is not saved because of temptations if they believe they have earned merit <note>original: *meritum*</note> through them. If someone places merit in their temptations, it stems from self-love—boasting and believing they deserve heaven more than others. At the same time, they think of their own superiority while looking down on others; all of these attitudes are contrary to mutual love and the resulting heavenly happiness <note>original: *beatitudo cœlestis*</note>. 

Temptations in which a person is victorious result in the person believing everyone else to be more worthy than themselves, and that they are of an infernal rather than a heavenly nature. Such realizations come to a person during temptations. Therefore, if someone returns to thoughts contrary to these after their trials, it is a sign they did not win. The thoughts one has during temptation are the ones toward which the mind should be inclined afterward. If the mind cannot be so inclined, the person has either succumbed in the temptation or will fall back into similar and sometimes more severe ones, until they are restored to that state of spiritual health where they believe they have merited nothing. From this, it is clear that "forty" here signifies those in whom good has been joined to truths through temptations.

2274. **Verse 30: *And he said, "Oh, let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: Suppose thirty are found there." And He said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."***
*And he said, "Oh, let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak"* signifies anxiety concerning the human race. *Suppose thirty are found there* signifies a certain amount of combat <note>spiritual struggle</note>. *And He said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there"* signifies that they will be saved.

2275. *And he said, "Oh, let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak"*: That this signifies anxiety concerning the state of the human race is evident not so much from the words themselves, but from the affection <note>the underlying emotional or spiritual quality</note> within them. There are two aspects to the internal sense <note>original: *sensus internus*; the deeper spiritual meaning hidden behind the literal text</note> of the Word: the spiritual and the celestial. 

The spiritual aspect involves understanding things abstractly from the literal letter, where the literal sense serves as a starting point, much like things seen by the eye serve as objects for thinking about higher concepts. The celestial aspect involves perceiving only the affection of the things contained in the internal sense. Spiritual angels <note>original: *angeli spirituales*</note> operate in the former, while celestial angels <note>original: *Angeli cœlestes*</note> operate in the latter. Those in the celestial state—or in "affection"—immediately perceive what the letter involves when it is read by a human, solely from the affection. From that, they form celestial ideas for themselves with countless variety and in an inexpressible way, following the sequence of heavenly loves within that affection. 

From this, one can see what the Word of the Lord contains in its depths. Thus, when these words are read—*let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak*—celestial angels immediately perceive a certain anxiety, specifically an anxiety of love toward the human race. At that moment, countless and inexpressible details regarding the anxiety of love, which the Lord felt when thinking about the state of humanity, are communicated to them.

2276. *Suppose thirty are found*: That this signifies a certain amount of combat is clear from the meaning of the number thirty. That thirty signifies some combat—specifically a small amount of combat—is because that number is composed by multiplying *five* (which signifies "a little") by *six* (which signifies "labor" or "combat"), as explained in Part One, numbers 649, 737, 720.

### CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

2276. As was shown in paragraph 1709, the number thirty, wherever it is read in the Word, signifies something of relatively small value. This is seen in Zechariah: "I said to them, 'If it is good in your eyes, give me my price; and if not, forbear.' So they weighed out for my price *thirty pieces of silver*. And Jehovah said to me, 'Throw it to the potter—the magnificent price at which I was valued by them.' And I took the *thirty pieces of silver* and threw them into the house of Jehovah, to the potter" (Zechariah 11:12–13). This represents how little they valued the Lord's merit, as well as the redemption and salvation coming from Him. The "potter" represents reformation and regeneration. 

The same thirty pieces of silver are mentioned in Matthew: "They took the *thirty pieces of silver*, the price of Him who was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value, and gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord commanded me" (Matthew 27:9–10). From these passages, it is clearly evident that "thirty" here stands for a price estimated as small. 

Even the valuation of a servant, who was held in low esteem, was thirty shekels, as established in the laws of Moses: "If the ox pushes a male or female servant, he shall give to their master *thirty shekels of silver*, and the ox shall be stoned" (Exodus 21:32). How lowly a servant was considered is clear in verses 20 and 21 of that same chapter. In the internal sense, a "servant" signifies labor. 

The Levites were chosen to perform the ministry (described as "entering the service to do the work in the tabernacle") from the age of *thirty years* old up to fifty (Numbers 4:3, 23, 30, 35, 39, 43). This was because "thirty" signified those who were being initiated, and thus those who could as yet perform only a little "service" in the spiritual sense. 

This number appears elsewhere in the Word as well. For example, they were to offer a grain offering <note>original: *mincham*; a Hebrew sacrificial offering usually consisting of flour and oil</note> of *three-tenths* for a bull (Numbers 15:9). This was because a sacrifice of a bull represented natural good (as shown above in paragraph 2180), and natural good is small compared to spiritual good. Spiritual good was represented by the sacrifice of a ram, and it is even smaller compared to celestial good, which was represented by the sacrifice of a lamb. Because of this, the proportions of the grain offerings differed, as seen in Numbers 15:4–6, and also in Numbers 28:12–13, 20–21, 28–29, and Chapter 29:3–4, 9–10, 14–15. These ratios or proportions of "tenths" would never have been commanded unless they involved heavenly secrets <note>original: *arcana cœlestia*</note>. 

"Thirty" also stands for a small amount in Mark: "The seed that fell into good ground brought forth fruit that sprouted and increased; and it yielded one *thirty*, another sixty, and another a hundred" (Mark 4:8). Here, thirty represents a small harvest and a person who has labored little. These specific numbers would not have been designated unless they carried a symbolic meaning.

2277. **He said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."**
This signifies that they will be saved. This is evident from the sequence of events in the internal sense, even without further explanation.

2278. **Verse 31: *And he said, "See now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to my Lord: Suppose twenty are found there." And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty."***
*And he said, "See now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to my Lord,"* signifies here, as before, the humiliation of the Human before the Divine. *Suppose twenty are found there,* signifies a state where there is no conflict <note>original: *pugnæ*; referring to spiritual trials or temptations</note>, but there is still good. *And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty,"* signifies that they will be saved.

# GENESIS

2279. **He said, "Behold now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to my Lord."** <note>original: *Dixit, ecce quæso suscepi ad loquendum ad Dominum meum*</note> That this signifies the humiliation of the human nature before the Divine nature is evident from what was said above in paragraph 2265, where the same words appear.

2280. **"Perhaps twenty will be found there."** <note>original: *Forte inventi fuerint ibi viginti*</note> That this signifies a state not of spiritual conflict, but still one of "good," is evident from the signification of **twenty**. Just as all numbers named in the Word signify things and states (as mentioned and shown previously in many places, see paragraph 2252), so too does the number twenty. What it signifies can be seen from its derivation—namely, from "twice ten." In the Word, "ten" (as well as "tithes") signifies **Remains** <term>original: *Reliquias*; "Remains" refers to the spiritual reserves of good and truth stored up by the Lord in a person's inner being throughout their life.</term>. By these remains is signified every good and truth that the Lord instills in a person from infancy until the very end of their life. We will discuss this in the following verse. "Twice ten," or two-tenths—that is, twenty—signifies something similar, but in a higher degree: specifically, **good**. 

Three types of "good" are signified by "Remains": namely, the **Goods of infancy**, the **Goods of ignorance**, and the **Goods of intelligence**. 
*   **Goods of infancy** <note>original: *Bona infantiæ*</note> are those instilled in a person from their first birth until the age when they begin to be instructed and to know something. 
*   **Goods of ignorance** <note>original: *Bona ignorantiæ*</note> are those present when the person is being instructed and begins to know something. 
*   **Goods of intelligence** <note>original: *Bona intelligentiæ*</note> are those present when the person is able to reflect on what is good and what is true. 

The "good of infancy" lasts from a person's infancy until their tenth year of age. The "good of ignorance" lasts from that age until their twentieth year. From this year onward, a person begins to become rational and gains the faculty to reflect upon good and truth, thereby acquiring for themselves the "good of intelligence." 

The "good of ignorance" is what is signified by **twenty**, because those who are in the "good of ignorance" do not enter into any **temptation** <term>original: *tentatio*; a spiritual trial or inner struggle</term>. No one is tempted until they can reflect and perceive, in their own way, what is good and true. The two preceding verses dealt with those who received "goods" through temptations; this verse now deals with those who are not in temptations and yet still possess "good." 

Because "twenty" signifies those who have this good (called the "good of ignorance"), all those who left Egypt were counted from twenty years old and upward—described as everyone "going out to the army" (Numbers 1:20, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 38, 40, 42, 45; and Chapter 26:4). These were understood to be people who were no longer in the "good of ignorance." It is also for this reason that all those who were over twenty years old died in the wilderness (Numbers 32:10–11) <note>The original text mistakenly cites Leviticus 32; the correct reference is Numbers 32:10–11.</note>, because evil could be attributed to them, and they represented those who succumb in temptations. 

Furthermore, a valuation was made of a male from five years old to twenty years old at twenty shekels (Leviticus 27:5); and another valuation from twenty years old to sixty years old was fifty shekels (Leviticus 27:3). 

Regarding these "goods"—namely, those of infancy, ignorance, and intelligence—the situation is this: the "good of intelligence" is the best, for it belongs to wisdom. The "good" that precedes it—namely, that of ignorance—is indeed good, but because there is little intelligence in it, it cannot be called the "good of wisdom." The "good of infancy" is indeed good in itself, but it is nonetheless a lesser good than the previous ones, for as of yet, no truth of intelligence has been joined to it... <meta>catchword: intelligence</meta>

It explains that spiritual temptation only begins when a person reaches the age of rational reflection (twenty), and contrasts the different stages of "good" instilled by the Lord from infancy to adulthood.</summary>

...intelligence. Just as no good act is a product of intelligence itself, but intelligence simply makes it possible for good to happen, the knowledge of good and truth makes it so that a human being is wise. Even infancy itself—which signifies innocence—does not truly belong to childhood, but to wisdom. This will be more clearly established from the discussion concerning infants in the afterlife at the end of this chapter.

In this verse, the number **twenty** signifies the "good of ignorance" <note>original: *bonum ignorantiæ*</note>. This "good" is not only attributed to those who are under twenty years of age, but also to all who live in the good of charity while remaining in ignorance of the truth. This includes many within the Church who think holily of God and act well toward their neighbor, even if they do not know the specific truths of faith for various reasons. It also includes all those outside the Church, known as Gentiles, who live in a similar state of charity. Even though these people do not possess the specific truths of faith, because they live in "good," they have the capacity to receive those truths in the afterlife just as infants do. Their intellectual part has not yet been infected by false principles, and their will has not been hardened by a life of evil, because they were ignorant of what is false and evil. A life of charity naturally allows the falsehoods and evils of ignorance to be easily turned toward what is true and good. This is not the case for those who have confirmed themselves in principles contrary to the truth and have lived lives contrary to what is good.

Furthermore, **two-tenths** <note>original: *binæ decimæ*</note> in the Word signify both heavenly and spiritual good. Heavenly good (and the spiritual good derived from it) is represented by the "two-tenths" of flour used to make each loaf of the showbread <note>original: *panis dispositionis*; also known as the Bread of the Presence</note>, as seen in Leviticus 24:5. Spiritual good is also signified by the "two-tenths" of a grain offering <note>original: *minchæ*</note> accompanying the sacrifice of a ram, as seen in Numbers 15:6, 28:12, 20, 28, and 29:3, 9, 14. We will discuss these elsewhere, by the Divine Mercy of the Lord.

2281. **"He said, 'I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.'"** <note>original: *Quod dixit, non perdam propter viginti*</note> That this signifies that they will be saved is evident from the series of things in the internal sense, and thus requires no further explanation.

2282. **Verse 32: "And he said, 'Oh, let not my Lord be angry, and I will speak only this once: Suppose ten are found there.' And He said, 'I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.'"**
**"Let not my Lord be angry, and I will speak only this once"** signifies a continued anxiety concerning the state of the human race. **"Suppose ten are found"** signifies if there were still "remains" <term>original: *reliquiæ*; the spiritual reserves of truth and good stored by the Lord in the inner person</term> present. **"And He said, 'I will not destroy it for the sake of ten'"** signifies that they will be saved.

2283. **"Let not my Lord be angry, and I will speak only this once."** That this signifies a continued anxiety concerning the state of the human race is evident from the emotion behind these words, as discussed above in paragraph 2275, where the same words appear.

2284. **"Suppose ten are found there."** That this signifies if there were still **remains** is evident from the signification of the number **ten**. As shown in the First Part (paragraphs 576 and 1738), ten signifies "remains." The nature of these "remains" has been discussed and shown in various places before (such as paragraphs 488, 530, 560, 561, 660, 661, 1050, 1738, and 1906). To summarize, "remains" are every good and every truth in a person that lies hidden in their memories and in their life. It is well known that nothing good and nothing true comes from anywhere but the Lord. Furthermore, good and truth continually flow from the Lord into a person, but they are received differently...

<summary>This page defines the "good of ignorance" as a state that allows for salvation even without specific religious knowledge, and identifies the biblical number ten as signifying "remains"—the spiritual reserves of good and truth provided by the Lord.</summary>
<keywords>good of ignorance, remains, reliquiae, charity, salvation, twenty, ten, Abraham, internal sense</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the spiritual interpretation of Abraham's intercession for Sodom in Genesis 18, focusing on the concept of "remains" and the conditions under which a person can be saved regardless of their religious background.</meta>

# GENESIS

...in various ways. Indeed, this happens according to a person's life of evil and the principles of falsity in which they have confirmed themselves. These are the things that continually extinguish, suffocate, or pervert the "goods" and "truths" flowing in from the Lord. Therefore, to prevent "goods" from being mixed with "evils" and "truths" with "falsities"—for if they were mixed, a person would perish forever—the Lord separates them. He stores the goods and truths that a person has received in their interior man. From there, the Lord never permits them to emerge as long as the person is in a state of evil and falsity, but only when they are in a holy state, or in some state of anxiety, illness, and the like.

These things which the Lord has thus stored up in a person are what are called <term>remains</term> <note>original: *reliquiae*</note>. Frequent mention of these is made in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible</note>, but until now, no one has known what they signify. Depending on the quality and quantity of these "remains"—that is, the good and truth within them—a person enjoys blessedness and happiness in the afterlife. As was mentioned, these are stored in the interior man and become visible only when the person has left behind bodily and worldly things. 

The Lord alone knows the quality and quantity of a person's remains; a human being can never know this. Today, people are such that they can fake being good, even though inside there is nothing but evil. On the other hand, a person can appear to be evil, even though they have good within them. For this reason, it is never permitted for one person to judge the spiritual life of another; only the Lord, as was said, knows this. However, everyone is permitted to judge another regarding their moral and civil life, as this is necessary for society. 

It is very common for those who have formed a fixed opinion about some "truth of faith" to judge others, claiming they cannot be saved unless they believe exactly as they do. However, the Lord prohibited this in Matthew 7:1–2: <note>"Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged."</note>. From much experience, it has become known to me that people from every religion are saved, provided that through a life of charity they have received the remains of good and "apparent truth." This is what is meant by the phrase, **if ten were found, they would not be destroyed for the sake of ten.** This signifies that if there were "remains," they would be saved. 

A life of charity consists in thinking well of others, wishing them well, and feeling joy within oneself that others are also saved. But those who do not want anyone else to be saved except those who believe as they do—and even more so, those who are indignant that it might be otherwise—do not have a life of charity. This can be seen from the fact that more people are saved from among the Gentiles <note>non-Christians</note> than from among Christians. Those among the Gentiles who have thought well of their neighbor and wished them well receive the truths of faith in the afterlife more easily than those who call themselves Christians, and they acknowledge the Lord more than Christians do. Indeed, nothing is more pleasant or joyful for the Angels than to instruct those who come into the afterlife from the earth.

2285. **I will not destroy it for the sake of ten** signifies that they will be saved. This is clear from the sequence of subjects in the internal sense, and thus requires no further explanation.

2286. **Verse 33.** *And Jehovah went his way as soon as he had finished speaking to Abraham; and Abraham returned to his place.* 

**Jehovah went his way as soon as he had finished speaking to Abraham** signifies that this state of perception, in which the Lord was then, ceased to be such. **And Abraham returned to his place** signifies that the Lord returned to the state he was in before he perceived these things.

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

2287. **That "Jehovah went His way as soon as He had finished speaking to Abraham"** <note>original: *Quod ivit Jehovah, quando absolvit loqui ad Abrahamum*</note> signifies that this state of perception in which the Lord then was, had finished being such. This is clear from the meaning of "speaking" and the representation of "Abraham." In the internal sense, "speaking" signifies thinking (as shown above in paragraph 2671), but here it signifies perceiving, because it is said of Jehovah that He "finished speaking to Abraham." For thought comes from perception, as previously stated, and perception comes from the Lord’s internal, which was Jehovah. 

Abraham, in this chapter, represents the Lord in His human state. Therefore, it is clear that "Jehovah went His way when He had finished speaking to Abraham" signifies nothing else in the internal sense than that the state of perception the Lord was in at that time had come to an end. The reason why this chapter deals so much with the Lord’s perception and thought in the internal sense can be seen above in paragraph 2249.

2288. **That "Abraham returned to his place"** signifies that the Lord returned to the state He was in before He perceived these things. This is clear from the representation of Abraham in this chapter as the Lord in His human state, and from the meaning of "place," which signifies a "state" <note>original: *status*</note> (as discussed in Part One, paragraphs 1273 and 1378). Thus, "returning to his place" in the internal sense means returning to the state in which He was before. 

It has been previously stated and shown that the Lord experienced two states while He lived in the world: a **state of Humiliation** and a **state of Glorification**. His state of Humiliation occurred when He was in the human nature that He inherited from His mother; His state of Glorification occurred when He was in the Divine nature, which He had from Jehovah His Father. The Lord completely shed that former state—the human nature from the mother—and put on the <term>Divine Human</term> <note>original: *Humanum Divinum*</note> when He passed from the world and returned to the Divine itself in which He had been from eternity (John 17:5), together with His Human now made Divine. From both of these proceeds the **Holy Spirit**, which fills the entire heaven. Thus, from the Divine itself and the Divine Human, the Lord governs the universe through the Holy Spirit proceeding from Him.

->**On the State of Infants in the Other Life.**<-

2289. **I**T *has been granted to me to know for certain that all infants who die, throughout the entire world, are resurrected by the Lord and taken up into heaven. There, they are raised and instructed by angels who have care over them. As they advance in intelligence and wisdom, they grow up. From this, it is clear how immense the Lord’s heaven is, composed of infants alone; for they are all instructed in the truths of faith and the "goods" of mutual love, and they become angels.*

# GENESIS.

2290. **Those who know nothing of the state of life after death** might suppose that infants, as soon as they enter the next life, are immediately in angelic intelligence and wisdom. However, I have been taught through much experience that this is not the case. Those who die shortly after birth have an infantile mind, almost like they had on earth, and know nothing more. They simply possess the *faculty* <note>original: *facultatem* - the capacity or potential ability</note> for knowing, and from that, for understanding and becoming wise. This faculty is more perfect because they are spirits and are no longer in a physical body. 

That children are like this when they first come into heaven has not only been told to me but also shown. On several occasions, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, infants were sent to me in **choirs** <note>original: *choris* - In this context, choirs refers to groups of spirits who think, speak, or act in a harmonious, rhythmic unison</note>. I was permitted to read the **Lord’s Prayer** <note>original: *Orationem Domini*</note> to them. At that time, I was given the ability to perceive how the angels in whose company the infants were would instill the meaning of the prayer into their tender and new ideas. The angels filled those ideas as much as the infants could receive, and then gave the infants the opportunity to think these things as if from themselves.

2291. **What their tender intellect is like** was also shown to me when I prayed the Lord’s Prayer and they flowed into the ideas of my thought from their own intellectual capacity. This capacity was so tender that they barely grasped anything beyond the literal sense of the words. Yet, their ideas in that state of tenderness were "open" all the way to the Lord—that is, open to receiving from the Lord. For the Lord flows into the ideas of infants especially from their innermost being. Nothing has yet closed their ideas, as is the case with adults; they have no "principles of falsity" <note>false beliefs or prejudices</note> to block the understanding of truth, nor a "life of evil" to prevent the reception of good, and thus they are ready to become wise.

2292. **From these things it is clear** that infants do not immediately enter the angelic state after death. Instead, they are introduced gradually through the knowledge of good and truth, following the entire heavenly order. The very smallest details of their natural disposition are perceived most exquisitely in heaven. According to every single moment of their inclination, they are guided to receive the "truths of good" and the "goods of truth" <note>original: *vera boni, & bona veri* - truths that lead to a good life, and the goodness that comes from living by the truth</note>. This process occurs under the Lord's constant guidance and protection.

2293. **Above all, they are constantly initiated** into knowing and then acknowledging no other Father than the Lord alone, and into the realization that they have life from Him. For the fact that they are alive—meaning they possess truly human and angelic life—comes from the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of good, which they receive solely from the Lord. Because of this, they do not know otherwise than that they were born in heaven.

2294. **Many times when infants were with me in choirs**, while they were still in a purely infantile state, they were heard as something tender and disorganized. They did not yet act as a single unit, as they would later do when they became older. And...

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN.

*I was amazed that the spirits with me could not restrain themselves from trying to lead the infants’ thoughts and speech. Spirits have a natural desire to do this, but it was observed many times that the infants resisted, refusing to think or speak in that way. I often noticed their refusal and resistance, which was accompanied by a kind of indignation. I was taught that this is a type of "temptation"* <note>original: *tentatio* — in this context, a spiritual trial or testing of one's character</note> *for infants in the afterlife. It helps them become accustomed and initiated* <note>original: *inaugurentur*</note> *not only into resisting what is false and evil, but also into not thinking, speaking, or acting based on anyone else's influence. In this way, they learn to allow themselves to be led by the Lord alone.*

2295. *When infants are not in that state, but are in a more internal sphere—specifically the angelic sphere—they can never be harassed by spirits, even if they are right in the middle of them. Sometimes, infants in the afterlife are even sent by the Lord to visit infants on earth, although the child on earth is completely unaware of it; the infants in heaven find the greatest delight in this.*

2296. *I was also shown how all things are instilled in them through pleasant and beautiful things that suit their nature. I was permitted to see infants dressed most elegantly, with garlands of flowers around their chests that glowed with the most beautiful heavenly colors, and others around their tender arms. Once I was also permitted to see infants with their female educators in a paradisiacal garden* <note>original: *horto paradisiaco*</note>. *It was not made of ordinary trees, but of arbors fashioned like laurel, forming decorated porticos with paths leading toward the center. The infants were dressed in the same elegant way, and when they entered, the flowerbeds above the entrance shone most joyfully. From this, one can see the nature of their delights, and how they are led into the "goods" of innocence and charity through these beautiful and pleasant things, which are constantly provided by the Lord.*

2297. *Furthermore, as infants grow in perfection, they are surrounded by atmospheres* <note>original: *atmosphæræ* — in Swedenborg's writings, these are spiritual environments that radiate from and surround inhabitants of the spiritual world</note> *that match their state of development. (I have discussed from experience in Part One, number 1621, that atmospheres in the afterlife exist in countless varieties and ineffable beauty.) Especially for infants, these atmospheres appear like tiny, playing children in minimal, invisible forms that are only perceivable as an inner idea. From these, they grasp the heavenly idea that each and every thing around them is alive, and that they are within the life of the Lord, which fills their innermost being with happiness.*

2298. *It was shown to me—through the communication style common in the afterlife—what the ideas of infants are like when they see various objects. It was as if every single thing was alive; thus, in every single idea of their thought, they had a sense of life. It was perceived that infants on* <note>original catchword: *tellure* — the earth/world</note>

# GENESIS.

*...on the ground when they are in their games; for they do not yet have the same kind of reflection as adults. The following describes what happens to those who are inanimate.* <note>original: *quid inanimalum*</note>

2299. *Infants are primarily instructed through visual representations <note>original: "representativa" — symbolic scenes or spiritual dramas used for teaching in the afterlife</note> suited to their unique dispositions. No one could ever believe how beautiful these are, or how full they are of an inner wisdom. In this way, intelligence is gradually introduced to them—an intelligence that draws its soul and life from what is good. One single representation that I was permitted to see may be described here, from which one can imagine the rest. They represented the Lord rising from the tomb, and at the same time, the union of His Human nature with the Divine. This was done in a way so wise that it exceeded all human wisdom, yet it was also done in a characteristically innocent and childlike manner. They presented a visual idea of the tomb, but they did not include a visual idea of the Lord except so remotely that He was barely perceived as if from a great distance. This was because the idea of a tomb has something funereal about it, which they thus removed. Afterward, they very prudently admitted into the scene a kind of "atmospheric tomb" which appeared like a thin watery mist; by this, they signified—with a becoming distance—the spiritual life found in baptism. Later, I saw them represent the Lord’s descent to those who were bound <note>original: "vinctos" — souls held in the "lower earth" of the spiritual world awaiting redemption</note>, and His ascent with them into heaven. This was done with incomparable prudence and piety. And because it was for children, when they represented the Lord among the bound in the lower earth, they let down almost invisible, very soft, and tender cords to assist the Lord in lifting them up during His ascent. All of this was done with a holy fear, lest anything in the representation should touch upon something that did not contain the heavenly spiritual. Besides these, there are other representations in which they dwell, and through which they are led into the knowledge of truth and the affection for what is good, much like how children on earth are led through games that suit their young minds.*

2300. *Furthermore, infants vary in their character and temperament. This is due to heredity, which they inherit from their parents and, through succession, from their grandparents and great-grandparents. Indeed, the actual habits of parents, when confirmed by regular practice, take on a second nature and are implanted hereditarily into their infants; this is the source of their different inclinations.*

2301. *In general, infants are of either a "celestial" or a "spiritual" character. Those who are of a celestial character are easily distinguished from those who are of a spiritual character. The celestial infants think, speak, and act with a gentle softness <note>original: "molliuscule"</note>, so that nothing appears except a flow of love for what is good, directed toward the Lord and toward other infants. The spiritual infants, however, are not quite so soft; instead, a kind of vibrant or "winged" quality <note>original: "alatum vibratile"</note> manifests itself in every one of their actions. This is also evident from their sense of indignation, among other signs. Thus, every infant is of a different character from every other, and each is educated according to their specific disposition.*

2302. *There are several specific Societies of Angels who have the care of infants. These consist primarily of the female sex, who in the life of the body...*

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN.

*They loved infants most tenderly. Infants who are more upright than others are offered to the Lord in a specific way.*

2303. Angelic spirits, who were positioned above and in front of me, spoke to me in angelic speech—which is not divided into distinct words. They told me that their state was one of the tranquility of peace, and that there were also infants among them whose presence brought them great happiness. These spirits were of the female sex. 

They spoke further about infants on Earth: immediately after birth, angels from the "Heaven of Innocence" are present with them. As the child grows older, they are succeeded by angels from the "Heaven of the Tranquility of Peace." Later, they are joined by those from societies of charity. Then, as innocence and charity begin to decrease in the growing child, other angels take their place. Finally, when they become adults and enter into a life far removed from charity, angels still remain present, though more distantly. This guidance is based on the "ends" <note>original: *fines* — the underlying purposes or goals that drive a person's actions</note> of a person's life, which the angels primarily govern by constantly suggesting good thoughts and turning away evil ones. Depending on how much they are able to succeed in this, they influence the person either more closely or from a greater distance.

2304. Many people might imagine that infants remain infants in the afterlife, existing like small children among the angels. Those who do not understand what an angel truly is might be confirmed in this opinion by the statues and paintings seen in churches and elsewhere, where angels are depicted as small children. 

However, the reality is quite different. Intelligence and wisdom are what make an angel. As long as infants do not yet possess these, they are indeed in the company of angels, but they are not yet angels themselves. When they have become intelligent and wise, they then—for the first time—become angels. In fact, to my surprise, they then no longer appear as infants but as adults. This is because they no longer have an infant-like nature, but a mature angelic one. Intelligence and wisdom bring this appearance with them; it is clear to anyone that understanding, judgment, and the resulting life are what make a person appear as an adult, both to themselves and to others. 

I was not only informed of this by the angels, but I also spoke with a specific person who had died as an infant and later appeared as an adult. He spoke with his brother, who had died in adulthood, with such mutual brotherly love that the brother could not stop himself from weeping. He said he perceived nothing else but that it was "Love itself" speaking through his brother. There are many other examples of this, which I do not need to mention here.

2305. There are some who imagine that "innocence" is the same thing as "infancy," because the Lord said of infants that "the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these," and that "unless you become like little children, you cannot enter the Kingdom of Heaven." But those who think this way do not understand the internal sense <note>original: *internum sensum* — the deeper spiritual meaning hidden within the literal words of the Bible</note> of the Word, and thus they do not understand what is meant by "infancy." By infancy is meant the innocence of intelligence and wisdom, which is of such a nature that they acknowledge they receive everything from the Lord alone...

...to have life, and that the Lord is their only Father. This is because a human being is truly human because of the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of goodness, which they receive solely from the Lord. *Innocence* itself, which is called *Infancy* in the Word <note>original: *Verbo* — referring to the Bible or Sacred Scripture</note>, exists and dwells nowhere except in wisdom. This is true to the point that the wiser a person is, the more innocent they are. Therefore, the Lord is Innocence itself because He is Wisdom itself.

2306. Regarding the innocence of infants: because they still lack intelligence and wisdom, their innocence is merely a foundation <note>original: *planum* — literally a "plain" or "level surface," meaning a receptive base</note> for receiving genuine innocence. They receive this in stages as they become wise. It was shown to me what the innocence of infants is like through a kind of wooden figure almost devoid of life, which becomes animated as it is perfected by knowledge of truth and affections for what is good. Afterward, genuine innocence was represented by a most beautiful infant, completely alive and naked. For those who are innocent, who are in the inmost heaven and thus closest to the Lord, do not appear to the eyes of other angels as anything other than infants, and indeed naked. This is because innocence is represented by nakedness, of which they are not ashamed—just as we read about the first man and his wife in Paradise. In short, the wiser the angels are, the more innocent they are; and the more innocent they are, the more they appear to themselves like infants. This is why "infancy" signifies "innocence" in the Word. But regarding the state of innocence, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, more will be said in the following pages.

2307. I spoke with angels about whether infants are pure from evils, since they have committed no "actual evil" <term>Actual evil: sins committed through one's own choices and actions, as opposed to adults who have intentionally acted on wrong impulses</term>. But I was told that they are equally in evil—in fact, that they too are nothing but evil—but that they, like all angels, are held back from evil and kept in what is good by the Lord. This is done to such an extent that it appears to them as if they are in goodness of their own accord. Therefore, even infants, after they have become adults in heaven, are sometimes let back into their own inherited evils to prevent them from having a false opinion of themselves—thinking that the goodness they have comes from themselves and not from the Lord. They are left in these states until they know, acknowledge, and believe how things truly are. One person who had died as an infant but grew up in heaven held this same false opinion. Consequently, he was let back into the life of evils he was born with. It was then granted to me to perceive from his "sphere" <note>original: *sphæra* — the spiritual atmosphere or "vibe" emanating from a person's character</note> that he had a desire to command others and that he thought nothing of lustful things—evils he had inherited from his parents. But after he acknowledged that he was like this, he was again received among the angels with whom he had lived before.

2308. No one in the other life ever pays a penalty for "hereditary evil" <term>Hereditary evil: the innate tendency toward selfishness or worldliness passed down from parents</term>, because it is not their own fault that they were born with it. Instead, they suffer for actual evil, which is their own—and also for how much from hereditary evil...

...hereditary evil <note>original: *hæreditario*</note> which they have appropriated through their actual life, as was stated previously in section 966. The reason that infants who have become adults are returned to the state of their own hereditary evil is not so that they should suffer punishment, but so they may realize that on their own they are nothing but evil. It is also to show that they are taken out of the hell that is within them and brought into heaven by the Lord’s Mercy <note>original: *Misericordia Domini*</note>. They learn that they are in heaven not because of their own merit, but because of the Lord. Thus, they should not boast of the good within them before others, for such pride is against the good of mutual love, just as it is against the truth of faith.

2309. From these points that have been presented, one can see what the education of infants <note>original: *Educatio Infantum*</note> in heaven is like. Specifically, they are introduced into angelic life through the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of goodness. This life consists of love for the Lord and mutual love <note>original: *amor mutuus*</note>, within which is Innocence <note>original: *Innocentia*</note>. However, how contrary the education of infants on earth is among many people could be seen from this single example: I was in the street of a large city and saw small boys fighting with one another. A crowd gathered and watched this with great pleasure. I was informed that the parents themselves encourage their children to engage in such fights. The good spirits and angels who saw these things through my eyes were so repulsed that I felt a sense of horror—especially because the parents incite them to such acts. They said that by doing this in early childhood, parents extinguish all mutual love and all innocence which infants receive from the Lord, and instead initiate them into hatred and revenge. Consequently, through their own efforts, they exclude their children from heaven, where there is nothing but mutual love. Therefore, parents who wish for the well-being of their infants should beware of such things.

At the end of the previous chapter (Genesis 17), the Last Judgment <note>original: *ultimum Judicium*</note> was discussed. At the end of this chapter (Genesis 18), the state of infants in the other life is addressed. Both accounts are drawn from the experience of things seen and heard in the world of spirits and the heaven of angels.

# PART TWO

## THE BOOK OF GENESIS

### CHAPTER NINETEEN

<margin>2310.</margin> The internal sense of the Word <note>original: "Verbi," referring to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible</note> has been discussed several times before. However, I know that few people can believe that such a sense exists in every detail of the Word—not only in the Prophetic books, but also in the Historical ones. It is easier to believe that such a sense exists in the *Prophetic* books because they do not follow a continuous narrative and often use unusual expressions. Because of this, anyone might guess that they contain some hidden secret <note>original: "arcanum"</note>. But in the *Historical* books, this is not as easily apparent. This is partly because the idea has not occurred to anyone until now, and partly because the historical accounts are written in a way that keeps the mind focused on the literal story. This distracts the reader from thinking that something deeper might be hidden there. Furthermore, the historical accounts are true, exactly as they are recorded. 

Yet, everyone must still conclude that there is something deeper within them that is both heavenly and Divine, even if it does not shine through on the surface. This is true for two reasons. *First*, because the Word was sent down from the Lord through heaven to humanity, it follows that it must have a different nature at its origin. What that origin is like, and how much it differs from the literal sense—so much so that it is not even visible and is therefore not recognized by those who are purely focused on worldly things—will be demonstrated in many places in the following pages. *Second*, because the Word is Divine, it was written not only for the benefit of humans, but also for the angels who are present with humans. In this way, it serves not only the needs of the human race, but also the needs of <note>The text ends here; the catchword indicates the next page begins with "Heaven" or "the Heavenly kingdom."</note>

<summary>This page introduces Chapter 19 of Genesis, arguing that the Bible contains a deep, "internal sense" within its historical narratives, not just its prophecies. The author explains that this hidden meaning exists because the Word originated in heaven and serves both humans and angels.</summary>
<keywords>Internal Sense, The Word, Genesis, Prophecy vs History, Divine Origin, Angels, Arcanum</keywords>

<page-num>4</page-num>
<header>G E N E S I S.</header>

...Heaven; and that the Word <note>original: "Verbum," referring to the Bible as the Word of God</note> is thus the Medium uniting Heaven and Earth. This union happens through the Church—specifically through the Word within the Church. This is why the Word is unique and stands apart from every other piece of writing. Regarding the historical accounts specifically: unless they contained Divine and Heavenly things in a way that is abstract from the literal text, no one who thinks deeply could ever recognize them as an inspired Word, down to the very last detail <note>original: "jotham," referring to a "jot," the smallest stroke of a pen</note>.

Would anyone say it was worth recording in the Divine Word the shameful story of Lot’s daughters (found at the end of this chapter), or the story of Jacob peeling the bark off sticks to reveal the white wood and placing them in the watering troughs so the flocks would give birth to multicolored, speckled, and spotted offspring? <note>This refers to Genesis 30:37–39, where Jacob used these sticks to influence the breeding of his flocks.</note> There are many other such stories in the other books of Moses, and in Joshua, Judges, Samuel, and Kings. These would be of no importance—whether they were known or not—unless they involved a deeper Divine secret <note>original: "arcanum"</note>. Without this, they would be no different from other historical accounts, which are sometimes written in a way that seems more engaging. Because the learned world <note>original: "Orbis Eruditus"</note> is unaware that Divine and heavenly things lie hidden even within the Histories of the Word, they would easily conclude in their hearts that the Word is not holy. They only maintain a sense of its holiness because of the sacred respect for these books that was impressed upon them from childhood. However, its holiness does not come from the surface level, but because an internal sense—one that is heavenly and Divine—is within it. It is this sense that unites Heaven with Earth—that is, it joins angelic minds with human minds, and thus connects them with the Lord.

2311. That the Word is of such a nature, and so distinct from every other writing, can also be seen from the fact that not only do all Names signify specific things (as shown previously in sections 1224, 1264, 1876, and 1888), but even all individual words have a spiritual sense. Therefore, they mean something different in Heaven than they do on earth, and this is true consistently in both the Prophetic and the Historical books. When these Names and words are explained in their heavenly sense—following their consistent meaning throughout the entire Word—the Internal Sense emerges. This is the "Angelic Word." This dual nature of the Word is like a Body and a Soul: the literal sense is like the body, and the Internal Sense is like the soul. Just as the body lives through the soul, the literal sense lives through the internal sense. Through this internal sense, the life of the Lord flows into the text, according to the level of devotion in the person reading it. From this, it is clear how holy the Word really is, even though it does not appear that way to worldly minds.

### CHAPTER XIX.

1. And two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom. And when Lot saw them, he rose to meet them, and he bowed his face to the ground.

2. And he said, "See now, my lords, please turn aside to your servant's house and stay the night, and wash your feet; then you may rise early and go on your way." And they said, "No; for we will stay in the open square tonight."

3. And he urged them strongly, so they turned aside to him and came to his house. And he prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

4. Before they had even lain down, the men of the city—the men of Sodom—surrounded the house, from the young to the old, all the people from every quarter.

5. And they called out to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, so that we may know them." <note>original: "cognoscamus eos," a biblical idiom for sexual relations</note>

6. And Lot went out to them at the doorway and closed the door behind him.

7. And he said, "I beg you, my brothers, do not act so wickedly."

8. "Look now, I have two daughters who have not known a man; let me bring them out to you, I pray, and you may do to them as you see fit. Only do nothing to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof beam." <note>original: "umbram trabis meæ," a reference to the sacred protection offered to guests in one's home</note>

9. And they said, "Stand back!" And they said, "This man came here to live as a foreigner, and now he must act as a judge? Now we will treat you worse than them." And they pressed hard against the man—against Lot—and they approached to break down the door.

10. And the men <note>referring to the angels in human form</note> reached out their hands and pulled Lot into the house with them, and they closed the door.

11. And they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the door.

12. And the men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and whoever else you have in the city, bring them out of this place."

13. "For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has become great before Jehovah, and Jehovah has sent us to destroy it." <note>original: "Jehovah," the Hebrew name for God, often translated as "the LORD" in English bibles</note>

17. And it happened that when they had brought them outside, he <note>One of the angels</note> said, "Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not destroyed."

28. And he looked out toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and he saw—look!—the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a furnace.

29. And so it was, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of the middle of the destruction, while overthrowing the cities in which Lot had lived.

<margin>2312.</margin> In this chapter, in the Internal Sense <note>This refers to a deeper, spiritual interpretation of the biblical text beyond its literal meaning.</note>, the state of the Spiritual Church is described through Lot. This church is characterized by the good of charity but remains in external worship; the text describes how it declines over the course of time.

<margin>2313.</margin> *The First State* of that church is that they are in the good of charity and acknowledge the Lord; and that they are confirmed in what is good by Him (Verses 1, 2, 3) and are saved (Verse 12). *The Second State* is when evils begin to act against what is good among them, but they are powerfully withheld from those evils and kept in good by the Lord (Verses 14, 15, 16). Their weakness is described (Verse 17) and their salvation (Verse 19). *The Third State* is when they no longer think and act from an affection for good, but from an affection for truth (Verses 18, 19, 20); and that they are saved (Verse 23). *The Fourth State* is when the affection for truth perishes, represented by Lot’s wife being made a pillar of salt (Verse 26). *The Fifth State* is when an impure good, or the "good of falsity," follows, represented by Lot in the cave of the mountain (Verse 30). *The Sixth State* is when even this good is further adulterated and falsified (Verses 31, 32, 33). Likewise, the truth is also falsified (Verses 34, 35). This leads to what is con- <note>The text ends mid-word with "conci-", likely "conceived" or "conception," referring to the births of Moab and Ben-ammi.</note>

<header>GENESIS.</header>

...there might be conceived and born a kind of likeness of a Church, whose good is thus called Moab, and whose truth is also thus called the son of Ammon. <note>original: "concipiatur & nascatur quoddam instar Ecclesiae, cujus bonum ita vocatum est Moab, & cujus verum etiam ita vocatum est filius Ammonis."</note>

2314. Furthermore, in the **Internal Sense** <note>The "Internal Sense" refers to the deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note>, the inhabitants of Sodom describe the state of those within the same Church who are against the good of charity; it also describes how evil and falsity increase among them over time, until nothing remains with them but evil and falsity.

2315. **The First State** of such people is that they are against the good of charity and against the Lord (Verses 4, 5). **The Second State** is that, even though they are informed about the good of charity and the delights of its affections which they could enjoy, they still persist in their ways and reject that good (Verses 6, 7, 8). They even attempt to destroy the good of charity itself, but the Lord protects it (Verses 9, 10). **The Third State** is that they eventually become such that they cannot even see what is true and good, much less that truth leads to good (Verse 11). They become so occupied by evil and falsity that they cannot help but perish (Verse 13). **The Fourth State** is their destruction (Verse 24), and the fact that all goods and truths are separated from them.

2316. That the good are separated from the evil, and that the good are saved through the Lord’s Human made Divine <note>original: "Humanum Domini factum Divinum," a core concept in this theology referring to Jesus Christ’s physical nature becoming one with God.</note> (Verses 27, 28, 29).
