**2375.** That it says "against Lot **exceedingly**" signifies that they were acting against the greatest **good of charity**. This is clear from the representation of **Lot**, who symbolizes the good of charity (as discussed above in sections 2324, 2351, 2371, 2373). From these very words—that they "pressed against the man, against Lot exceedingly"—it is clear that "the man" and "Lot" signify different things here; otherwise, using both terms would have been redundant. <note>original: "vires... in virum, in Loth valde"</note>

**2376.** That "they came near to break the door" signifies that they reached the point of attempting to destroy both truth and good. This is clear from the meaning of "coming near," which signifies a focused attempt, and from the meaning of the "door," which is the entrance to good and to the Lord. The door also represents good itself and the Lord Himself (see sections 2356, 2357). For how these concepts relate to one another, see section 2373.

**2377.** Verse 10: *And the men put out their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.* "The men put out their hand" signifies the Lord’s powerful help. "They pulled Lot into the house to them" signifies that the Lord protects those who are in the good of charity. "And they shut the door" signifies that He also blocks all access to them.

**2378.** That "the men put out their hand" signifies the Lord’s powerful help is clear from the meaning of "the men" as the Lord (as stated previously) and from the meaning of "hand" as power (see section 878).

**2379.** That "they pulled Lot into the house to them" signifies that the Lord protects those who are in the good of charity. This is clear from the representation of **Lot** as those who are in the good of charity, and from the meaning of "bringing into the house" as protecting. To be "brought into the house" is to be brought into good; those who are in good are brought into heaven, and those in heaven are with the Lord. Thus, they are safe in their souls from all harassment. Although a person living in the body is usually unaware of it, if they are in a state of good, their soul is in society with angels and is already in heaven, even while they live on earth. They cannot yet perceive angelic joy because they are still in a physical state of preparation (see section 1277).

**2380.** That "they shut the door" signifies that He blocks all access to them. This is clear from the meaning of "the door" as that which provides entrance (sections 2356, 2357, 2376), and thus an access point. Therefore, to "shut the door" is to block access. 

In the afterlife, access is blocked so that the good are separated from the wicked. This prevents the "spheres" <note>In this context, a "sphere" is a spiritual atmosphere or aura radiating from a person's character.</note> of false persuasions and evil desires from harassing them, for the toxic exhalations of hell cannot reach heaven. 

In this life, access is blocked so that the principles and persuasions of falsehood cannot take hold of those who are in a state of good. When a false idea or evil thought is introduced—whether through the speech of a wicked person or the influence of an evil spirit—the angels present with that person immediately turn the thought away. They direct the person back toward the truth and good in which they have been established. This occurs regardless of how much they might be harassed physically, for they value the body as nothing compared to the soul. While a person is still in their physical body, their spiritual perception is in such a general and obscure state (section 2367) that they barely know whether they are in the good of charity or not. <header>G E N E S I S.</header>

Everyone knows what charity and the neighbor are, but it is important to know who truly fits these descriptions. All those who possess a **conscience** are in the "good of charity." These are the people who refuse to depart from what is just, fair, good, and true simply for the sake of justice, fairness, goodness, and truth themselves. This is what it means to act from conscience. From this state, they think well of their neighbor and wish them well, even if that person were an enemy, and they do this without seeking any reward. These are the people who are in the good of charity, whether they are outside the Church or within it. Those within the Church adore the Lord, and they gladly hear and practice what He taught.

Conversely, those who are in evil have no conscience. They do not care for what is just and fair, except for how much they can profit or gain a reputation for appearing to be that way. They do not know what is "good and true" regarding spiritual life; they even reject such things as being of no value. Furthermore, they think ill of their neighbor and wish them harm; they even do harm, even to a friend if that friend does not favor them, and they take pleasure in doing so. If they do anything "good," it is for the sake of a reward. Such people within the Church deny the Lord in secret—and openly, as long as their honor, profit, reputation, or life are not at risk.

Yet it should be known that some people think they are not "in good" <note>original: "in bono"; a state of being motivated by genuine goodness</note> when they actually are, and some think they are in good when they are not. The reason some think they are not in good when they are is that when they reflect on themselves, angels (with whom they are associated) immediately suggest they are not in good. This is to prevent them from claiming the good as their own merit or thinking they are superior to others; if they thought otherwise, they would fall into spiritual temptations. 

On the other hand, the reason some think they are in good when they are not is that when they reflect on it, evil spirits (with whom they are associated) immediately pour in the idea that they are in good. Evil people believe their selfish pleasures are "good." They are even told that whatever "good" they have done for others out of self-love or love of the world is a good that deserves a reward, even in the next life. This makes them feel they deserve more than others, whom they look down upon or consider worthless. Remarkably, if these people thought otherwise, they would fall into temptations that they could not survive.

**2381.** Verse 11: *And the men who were at the door of the house they struck with blindness, from the small to the great, and they labored to find the door.* 

"The men who were at the door of the house" signifies **rational things** <note>original: "rationalia"; the faculty of human reasoning</note> and the **doctrines** derived from them through which violence is done to the good of charity. "They struck with blindness" <note>original: "percusserunt cæcitatibus"</note> signifies that they were filled with falsehoods. "From the small to the great" signifies in every detail and in general. "And they labored to find the door" signifies that they reached a state where they could not see any truth that might lead to good.

**2382.** That "the men who were at the door of the house" signifies rational things and the doctrines derived from them through which violence is done to the good of charity is clear from the meaning of "men" as rational things (as noted in sections 158 and 1007); from the meaning of the "door" <note>original: "janua"</note> as an introduction or access leading either to truth or to good—thus, a doctrine (as noted above in section 2356); and from the meaning of the "house" as the good of charity (as noted frequently above). 

In this context, because the passage concerns those who tried to break down the door—that is, those who attempted to destroy both the good of charity and the Divine and Holy nature of the Lord (see section 2376)—it refers to evil rationalities and the false doctrines that come from them, through which violence is done to the good of charity.

2383. **That they struck them with blindness** signifies that they were filled with falsities. This is evident from the meaning of "Blindness." In the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; referring to the Bible</note>, blindness is attributed to those who are in a state of falsity, as well as those who are in ignorance of the truth. Both are called "blind," but who is meant in a specific passage can be determined from the series of things described, especially in the internal sense. That those in falsity are called "blind" is evident from these passages:

In Isaiah: "His watchmen are blind; they all know nothing, they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark" <term>Isaiah 56:10</term>. "Blind watchmen" refers to those who are in falsity due to their own reasoning.

In the same author: "We wait for light, but behold, darkness; for brightness, but we walk in thick darkness; we grope for the wall like the *blind*" <term>Isaiah 59:9-10</term>.

In Jeremiah: "The *blind* have wandered in the streets; they have polluted themselves with blood; what they cannot touch, they touch with their garments" <term>Lamentations 4:14</term>. This signifies that all truths have been polluted. "Streets" <note>original: "platea"</note> represent truths in which they have wandered (see number 2336).

In Zechariah: "In that day I will strike every horse with astonishment, and his rider with fury; every horse of the people I will strike with *blindness*" <term>Zechariah 12:4</term>. In the Word, "horse" signifies the intellectual faculty; therefore, it is said the horse is struck with astonishment and the "horse of the people" with blindness—that is, it is filled with falsities.

In John: "Jesus said, 'For judgment I have come into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become *blind*.' Some of the Pharisees heard these things and said, 'Are we *blind* also?' Jesus said to them, 'If you were *blind*, you would have no sin; but now you say, "We see," therefore your sin remains'" <term>John 9:39-41</term>. Here, "blind" is used in both senses: those who are in falsity and those who are in ignorance of the truth. For those within the Church who know what is true, blindness is falsity. But for those who do not know what is true (such as those outside the Church), blindness is ignorance of the truth, and they are blameless.

In the same author: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they should not see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them" <term>John 12:40</term>; see also <term>Isaiah 6:9-11</term>. This signifies that it is better for them to be in falsities than in truths, because they are in an evil life. If such people were instructed in truths, they would not only falsify them further but would also defile them with evils. For this same reason, the men of Sodom were struck with blindness—meaning their doctrinal matters were filled with falsities. Why this happens is shown in numbers 301, 302, 303, 593, 1008, 1010, 1059, 1327, 1328, and 2426.

Because the "blind" signified what is false, it was forbidden in the Jewish representative Church to sacrifice anything blind <term>Leviticus 22:22; Deuteronomy 15:21; Malachi 1:8</term>. It was also forbidden for any priest who was blind to approach to offer on the altar <term>Leviticus 21:18, 21</term>.

That "blindness" is also attributed to an ignorance of truth (such as the Gentiles are in) is evident in Isaiah: "In that day the deaf shall hear the words of the Book, and out of thick darkness and out of darkness the eyes of the blind shall see" <term>Isaiah 29:18</term>. "Blind" here refers to those in ignorance of truth, especially those outside the Church.

In the same author: "Bring forth the *blind* people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears" <term>Isaiah 43:8</term>, referring to the Church of the Gentiles.

In the same author: "I will lead the *blind* in a way they did not know; I will make darkness light before them" <term>Isaiah 42:16</term>.

And again: "I will give You for a light of the people, to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoner out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison house" <term>Isaiah 42:6-7</term>. This refers to the coming of the Lord, at which time they would be instructed...

These nations are called "blind, deaf, lame, and mute" in regard to their doctrine and life. Thus, the Lord’s miracles were Divine, just like those performed in Egypt, in the desert, and others recorded in the Word; this is a profound mystery <note>original: "arcanum"</note>.

2384. **From the small even to the great**, which signifies in particular and in general, is evident from the meaning of these terms in the internal sense when they are applied to rational and doctrinal matters (which are signified by the "men" at the door of the house). In this context, however, the "door" signifies the pieces of knowledge <note>original: "cognitiones"</note> that introduce a person to truth. As stated in number 2356, the door was at the front of the house; for it is said that "Lot went out to the door, and shut the entrance behind him" <term>Verse 6</term>. Therefore, "laboring to find the door" means not seeing any truth that might lead to good. 

People become like this, especially in the "latter times," when they exclude doctrinal matters through their own reasoning and believe nothing unless they can first grasp it intellectually. An example is found in those who claim that a life of affection (charity) does nothing, but that faith (which is a matter of thought) is the only thing that matters. Such is the nature of every false principle...

# CHAPTER NINETEEN

Anyone can know that whatever principle is adopted—regardless of what it is or whether it is actually false—once it is accepted, it can be confirmed by countless arguments and presented in an external form as if it were the absolute truth. This is the origin of heresies; once they are confirmed, they are never abandoned. However, from a false principle, nothing but falsehoods can flow. Even if truths are interspersed among them, as long as they are used to confirm that false principle, they become "falsified truths" because they are tainted by the very essence of the principle <note>original: "inquinata ab essentia principii"</note>.

It is entirely different if Truth itself is accepted as the principle and then confirmed. For example: if one accepts that love for the Lord and charity toward the neighbor are the foundations upon which the whole law hangs and of which all the prophets speak <term>Matthew 22:37–40</term>, and thus treats these as the essentials of all doctrine and worship, then the mind would be illuminated by the countless things within the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> that otherwise lie hidden in the darkness of a false principle. Indeed, in such a case, heresies would be dispelled, and from many different groups, one single Church would be formed. It would not matter how much their specific doctrines, rituals, or the paths leading to them might differ.

Such was the **Ancient Church** <note>In this context, the "Ancient Church" refers to a spiritual era following the flood, preceding the Hebrew and Christian eras.</note>, which was spread through many kingdoms: namely Assyria, Mesopotamia, Syria, Ethiopia, Arabia, Libya, Egypt, Philistia, all the way to Tyre and Sidon, and throughout the land of Canaan on both sides of the Jordan. Among these people, doctrines and rituals differed, yet the Church was still one because **Charity** was essential to them all. At that time, the Kingdom of the Lord was on earth just as it is in heaven; for such is the nature of heaven (see numbers 684, 690). If it were so today, everyone would be governed by the Lord as if they were a single person. They would be like the members and organs of one body which, although they do not have the same form or the same function, nevertheless all relate to one heart, upon which they and every part of their varied forms depend. Then everyone—regardless of what doctrine or external worship they followed—would say of another: "This is my brother; I see that he worships the Lord and that he is a good person."

# GENESIS

...of the city and the place, as follows: Those who are in the truth of faith are saved if they turn away from evil. This is because the truths of faith are the very "vessels" that receive what is good <note>original: "vera fidei sunt ipsa vasa recipientia boni"</note> (see numbers 1900, 2063, 2261, 2269). These vessels receive goodness in proportion to how much a person turns away from evil. Goodness continuously flows in from the Lord, but the "evil of life" <note>This refers to living according to selfish or worldly desires rather than spiritual principles.</note> is what prevents it from being received into the truths that a person holds in their memory or knowledge.

Therefore, as much as a person turns away from evil, goodness enters and applies itself to their truths. In that moment, the "truth of faith" becomes the "good of faith." A person can certainly know the truth—or even confess it because of some worldly motive, or be persuaded that it is true—yet this truth still has no life in it as long as the person lives an evil life. Such a person is like a tree that has leaves but no fruit. This kind of truth is like light that has no heat, such as in winter when nothing grows. But when heat is present, it becomes like the light of springtime when everything grows. 

In the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, truth is compared to light and is called "light," while heat is compared to love and is called "spiritual heat." In the other life <note>The spiritual world or afterlife.</note>, truth manifests itself through light, while good manifests through heat. Truth without good appears as a cold light; however, truth joined with good appears as a light similar to springtime. From this, it is clear what the "truth of faith" is without the "good of charity." This is why the sons-in-law and sons (who signify such truths) were not saved, but only Lot and his daughters. 

Regarding the statement that those in the truth of faith are saved if they turn away from evil, it should be understood that this refers to people who profess faith but do not think about charity. This is often because they were instructed that way and do not know what charity is—thinking it is only giving away their possessions or pitying everyone—or because they do not know who the "neighbor" is toward whom they should show charity, thinking it applies to almost everyone without distinction. Nevertheless, these people live a life of charity toward their neighbor because they live a life of goodness. It does not harm them to profess faith alongside others, for charity resides within their faith. Charity, in a general and specific sense, signifies every "good of life." What charity is, and who the neighbor is, will be discussed in the following pages by the Lord’s Divine Mercy.

Third, there are those who indeed know truths but are nevertheless in evil; these are signified here by the **sons-in-law** <note>original: "Generos"</note>. These are especially people who teach, but the truth they teach has not taken root deeper than the knowledge of the memory alone; for it is learned and touted only for the sake of honor and gain. Because the "soil" in such people—in which the truth is placed—is the love of self and the love of the world, they have no real faith in the truth. They only have a certain persuasive belief, the nature of which will be discussed elsewhere, by the Divine Mercy of the Lord. They are described here by the "sons-in-law" because they believed nothing regarding the overthrow of Sodom, but instead mocked it; such is the actual faith of their hearts.

2401. Regarding his saying, **"Arise, go out from this place,"** signifying that they should not remain in a state of evil, this is evident from the meaning of "arising," "going out," and "place." "To arise" is often read in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible in its spiritual capacity.</note>, but little thought is given to its deeper meaning because it is such a familiar word; yet in the internal sense, it involves elevation—as it does here—from evil to good. For the mind is elevated when it withdraws from evil (see number 2388). "To go out" means to withdraw or not to remain. "Place," however, signifies a state of evil (number 2393); thus it is clear that these are the things signified. 

What kind of people these are—those who possess knowledge of truth but at the same time live a life of evil—has been mentioned several times before. Specifically, as long as they live a life of evil, they believe nothing. For it is impossible to desire evil and do evil as a result while simultaneously acknowledging truth through genuine faith. From this, it is also clear that a person cannot be saved simply by thinking and speaking truth, or even good, when they desire nothing else and do nothing else from their **will** <note>The "will" refers to a person's deepest intentions and loves.</note> than evil. It is a person's very will that lives after death, not their thinking, except for that thinking which flows from their will. 

Since, therefore, a person is defined by their will, one can see what they would truly think about the truths of faith they have learned—or even taught—because those truths would condemn them. Far from thinking from those truths at that time, they feel an aversion to them; indeed, as far as they are permitted, they blaspheme them like a crowd of devils. Those who are not instructed about life after death might think they could easily receive faith later, once they see that the Lord rules the entire heaven, and once they hear that heaven consists in loving Him and the neighbor. But the evil are as far from being able to receive faith—that is, to believe it from the heart—as hell is from heaven. For they are entirely in evil, and consequently in falsity. From their very arrival or presence alone, it is perceived that they are against the Lord and against the neighbor, and thus against good and truth. It is a foul atmosphere <note>original: "sphæra nefanda"</note> that exhales from the life of their will and resulting thought (see numbers 1048, 1053, 1316, 1504). If it were possible for them to believe and become good simply through instruction in the next life, not a single person would be in hell; for the Lord wills to elevate everyone, however many there are, to Himself in heaven. His Mercy is Infinite, because it is Divine itself, and it is directed toward the whole human race—toward the evil as well as the good.

2402. **"Because Jehovah is destroying the city,"** signifies that they could not help but perish. This is evident from the explanation of almost the same words in numbers 2395 and 2397.

2403. **"And he was like one who mocked in the eyes of his sons-in-law,"** signifies mockery. This is evident from the meaning of "mocking" <note>original: "ludens," literally playing or joking</note>, which is to treat something as if it were a joke, a story, or trifles.

# GENESIS

...jokes <note>original: "nugæ"</note>, such that they would mock them. "In their eyes" signifies in the presence of their rational mind, as is evident from the meaning of "eyes" (see number 212) <note>These numbers refer to specific sections in the author’s larger work, *Arcana Coelestia*.</note>. From this, it is clear what kind of people they are: those who possess the truth of faith but are not, at the same time, in the good of life.

2404. **Verse 15. *And when the morning dawned <note>original: "sicut aurora ascendit"</note>, the angels urged Lot to hurry, saying, "Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found here, lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city."*** 

"When the morning dawned" signifies when the Kingdom of the Lord approaches. "The angels urged Lot to hurry" signifies that the Lord would withhold them from evil and keep them in good. "Saying, arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are found" signifies the truth of faith and the affections of truth and good; "found" means they are separated from evil. "Lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city" signifies lest they perish through the evils of falsity.

2405. That "when the morning dawned" signifies when the Kingdom of the Lord approaches is evident from the meaning of "Dawn" or "Morning" <note>original: "Aurora seu Mane"</note> in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible in its spiritual sense.</note>. Because this chapter deals with the successive states of the Church, it first dealt with what happened in the **Evening**, then what happened in the **Night**; now follows what happens at **Daybreak** <note>original: "diluculo"</note>, and soon what happens after the sun has risen. 

Daybreak is expressed here by "when the morning dawned," and this occurs when the good are separated from the evil. This separation is the subject from this verse up to Verse 22, describing how Lot, along with his wife and daughters, was led out and saved. That separation precedes judgment is clear from the Lord's words in Matthew: *"All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats"* (25:32). 

This time or state is called "the Dawn" in the Word because the Lord then comes—or, what is the same thing, His Kingdom then approaches. It is the same for the good, for the light then shines upon them like the morning daybreak or dawn. Therefore, in the Word, the coming of the Lord is compared to the **Morning**, and is even called the Morning. It is compared this way in Hosea: *"Jehovah will revive us after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we shall live in His presence, and we shall know, and we shall press on to know Jehovah; His going forth is as certain as the Dawn"* (6:2, 3). "Two days" stands for the time and state that precedes; the "third day" stands for judgment or the coming of the Lord, and thus for the approach of His Kingdom (see numbers 720, 901). This coming or approach is compared to the Dawn. 

In Samuel: *"The God of Israel is like the light of the Morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, from the radiance and from rain the sprout comes from the earth"* (2 Samuel 23:4). "The God of Israel" stands for the Lord, for no other God of Israel was understood in that Church, as He was represented in every single part of it. 

In Joel: *"The day of Jehovah comes, for it is near; a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness, like the Dawn spread upon the mountains"* (2:1, 2). There, too, it treats of the coming of the Lord and His Kingdom; it is called a "day of darkness and gloom" because that is when the good are separated from the evil (as Lot was here separated from the men of Sodom), and after the good are separated, the evil perish. 

That the coming of the Lord or the approach of His Kingdom is not just compared to the Morning, but is actually *called* the Morning, appears in Daniel: *"One Holy One said, 'How long shall the vision be, the daily sacrifice, and the transgression that desolates?' He said to me, 'Until the Evening and the Morning, two thousand three hundred days, and the sanctuary shall be justified.' The vision of the Evening and the Morning which was told is true"* (8:13-14, 26).

# CHAPTER NINETEEN

...13, 14, 26. Here, "Morning" clearly stands for the coming of the Lord. In the Psalms of David: "Your people will be willing in the day of your power, in the beauties of holiness; from the womb of the *Morning* <note>original: "Aurora"</note>, you have the dew of your youth" (Psalm 110:3). In this entire Psalm, the subject is the Lord and His victories in temptations—which are the "days of His power" and the "beauties of His holiness." "From the womb of the Morning" refers to the Lord Himself, specifically the Divine Love from which He fought.

In Zephaniah: "The righteous Jehovah is in her midst; He will do no injustice. Every morning, every morning He brings His judgment to light" (Zephaniah 3:5). Here, "morning" represents the time and state of judgment, which is the same as the coming of the Lord and the approach of His Kingdom. Because "Morning" signified these things, the following rituals were commanded to represent the same truth: Aaron and his sons were to tend the lamp and arrange it from Evening until *Morning* before Jehovah (Exodus 27:21). "Evening" there refers to the twilight before Morning (see number 2323). Similarly, it was commanded that the fire on the altar should be kindled *every morning* (Leviticus 6:12 <note>original: "vi: 5"</note>). Also, regarding the Passover lamb and the holy parts of the sacrifices, nothing was to be left until morning (Exodus 12:10; 23:18; 34:25; Leviticus 22:29–30; Numbers 9:12). This signified that when the Lord came, sacrifices would cease.

In a general sense, "Morning" refers both to when the dawn appears and when the sun rises. In those cases, "Morning" is understood as the Judgment upon both the good and the evil, as seen in this chapter: "The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar; then Jehovah rained sulfur and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah" (verses 23–24). Similarly, it refers to Judgment upon the evil in David: "In the mornings I will destroy all the wicked of the land, cutting off all workers of iniquity from the city of Jehovah" (Psalm 101:8). And in Jeremiah: "Let that man be like the cities which Jehovah overthrew and did not relent; let him hear a cry in the morning" (Jeremiah 20:16). 

Since "Morning" in its proper sense signifies the Lord, His coming, and thus the approach of His Kingdom, it is clear what else "Morning" signifies: namely, the rise of a new Church <note>original: "Ecclesia"</note>. This is because the Church is the Lord's Kingdom on earth. This happens in three ways: **generally**, when a new Church is raised up somewhere in the world; **particularly**, when a person is regenerated and becomes new, for then the Lord's Kingdom rises within them and they become a Church; and **singularly**, as often as the good of love and faith is active in them, for the Lord's coming is within that activity. Thus, the Lord’s Resurrection on the *third day in the morning* (Mark 16:2, 9; Luke 24:1; John 20:1) includes all these meanings—even in a particular and singular sense—because He rises daily, and even every moment, in the minds of those who are being regenerated.

That this signifies being withheld from evil is clear both from the internal sense of these words and from what follows. The internal sense is that when the Church begins to turn away from the good of charity, people are then more strongly withheld from evil by the Lord than when they are in the good of charity. The same is evident from what follows—namely, that although the angels urged Lot...

**2406.** ...to go out from the city, he delayed until they <note>the angels/the Lord</note> grasped his hand, and the hands of his wife and daughters, and led them out and set them outside the city. This signifies and describes what a human is like in that state. For here we are dealing with the **Second State** of this Church. The **First State** was described in verses 1, 2, and 3 of this chapter, which is that they are in the good of charity and acknowledge the Lord, and are confirmed in goodness by Him. 

The Second State is described here, which is when evils begin to act against goods within the people of the Church themselves. At that time, they are powerfully held back from evils and kept in good by the Lord. This state is discussed in this verse and in the following verses 15, 16, and 17. 

As far as the matter itself is concerned, few, if any, know that all people, however many there are, are held back from evils by the Lord. This happens with a force stronger than any human could ever believe. For the perpetual effort of every human is toward evil, stemming both from the *hereditary* <term>evil tendencies inherited from ancestors</term> nature they are born into and the *actual* <term>sins committed by the person's own choice</term> evil they have acquired for themselves. This is so much the case that if they were not held back by the Lord, they would rush headlong at every moment toward the lowest hell <note>original: "infimum infernum"</note>. 

But the Lord's Mercy is so great that at every single moment, even the smallest, the person is lifted up and held back so they do not fall there. This also happens with good people, but with a difference according to their life of charity and faith. Thus the Lord continually fights with the person—and for the person—against hell, even though it does not appear that way to the person. That this is the case has been granted to me to know through much experience, which, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, will be discussed elsewhere (see also numbers 929 and 1581).

**2407.** **By saying, "Arise, take your wife and two daughters who are found here,"** signifies the truth of faith and the affections for truth and good; and that those "found" are those who are separated. This is evident from the meaning of "arising," which is to be elevated from evil (see number 2401). It is also clear from the meaning of "wife" here, which is the truth of faith (discussed at verse 26, where Lot's wife is turned into a pillar of salt); and from the meaning of the "two daughters," which are the affections for truth and good (see number 2362). That those "found" are those separated from evil is also evident, because they were rescued. 

In these few words, this Second State of the Church is described: namely, that they no longer allow themselves to be led from good to truth as before, but rather through truth to good. Yet, they are still in an obscure affection for good. For as long as truth is the leader, good is obscured; but as long as good is the leader, truth stands clear in its own light.

**2408.** **"Lest perhaps you are consumed in the iniquity of the city,"** signifies lest they perish in the evils of what is false. This is clear from the meaning of "iniquity," which is evil, and from the meaning of "city," which is a doctrine <note>original: "doctrinale"</note>, even a false one (see number 402). What the "evil of falsehood" is can be seen from what was said in the First Part, numbers 1212 and 1679.

**2410.** "And he lingered." That this signifies resistance from the nature of evil is clear from what was said above (number 2406). For the evil that is in a person continually reacts against the good that comes from the Lord. Evil clings to a person—both from their *hereditary* <term>inherited tendencies toward sin</term> nature and from their *actual* <term>sinful habits acquired through one's own choices</term> life—in every single thought, even in the smallest parts of their thoughts. This pulls the person downward. The Lord, however, through the good that He instills <note>original: *insinuat*</note>, holds the person back and lifts them up. 

In this way, a person is held in suspension between evil and good. Therefore, if they were not held back from evils by the Lord for even the smallest moment, they would fall downward by their own weight. This is even more the case in this state, where the "person of the Church" (whom Lot now represents) begins to think and act from truth rather than from good. Because they are acting from truth, they are at a certain distance from good.

**2411.** "That the Men grasped his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hand of his two daughters." This signifies that the Lord powerfully held them back from evils, and thus strengthened the goods and truths signified by Lot, his wife, and his daughters. This is clear from the following:
*   **The Men** signifies the Lord (as mentioned above).
*   **Hand** signifies power <note>original: *potentia*</note> (see number 878).
*   **Lot** signifies the good of charity (see numbers 2324, 2351, 2371, 2399).
*   **Wife** signifies the truth of faith (see verse 26 below).
*   **Daughters** signify the affections for truth and good (see numbers 489, 490, 491, 2362).

Furthermore, as noted in number 2388, good and truth flow in from the Lord only as much as a person is held back from evil. Consequently, the goods and truths represented by Lot and his family are strengthened in proportion to that restraint. Anyone can know this from their own experience if they reflect on it: the more a person is removed from "bodily and worldly things," the more they are in a "spiritual idea" <note>original: *in idea spirituali*</note>. That is, they are lifted toward heaven. 

This happens when a person is in holy worship, undergoing a spiritual trial <note>original: *tentatio*</note>, or facing misfortunes and illnesses. It is well known that during such times, bodily and worldly concerns (meaning the love for them) are removed. The reason for this is that heavenly and spiritual influences from the Lord flow in continuously; however, it is the evil and its resulting falsity—which flow from bodily and worldly preoccupations—that stand in the way and prevent these influences from being received.

**2412.** "In the clemency of Jehovah over him." That this signifies "out of grace and mercy" is clear from the meaning of "the clemency of Jehovah," which can be nothing other than grace and mercy. The fact that a person is held back from evil and kept in good by the Lord happens out of pure Mercy (see number 1049). 

The reason both "grace" and "mercy" are mentioned (as discussed in numbers 598 and 981) is that those who are focused on truth (and thus on good) implore the Lord’s **Grace** <note>original: *gratiam*</note>. However, those who are focused on good (and thus on truth) implore the Lord’s **Mercy** <note>original: *misericordiam*</note>. This stems from the different states of humility and worship found in one person compared to the other.

**2414.** Verse 17. *And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth outside, that he said, "Escape for your life; do not look behind you, and do not stay in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest you be consumed."* <note>original: *Et fuit, cum educerent ii illos foras, & dixit, eripe te fuper anima tua, ne refpicias poft te, & ne confiftas in omni planitie; in montem eripe te, ne forte confumaris.*</note>

"And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth outside," signifies the state when they were being held back from falsehood and evil. "And he said, 'Escape for your life,'" signifies that he should look after his life for eternity. "Do not look behind you," signifies that he should not look back toward doctrinal matters. "And do not stay in all the plain," signifies that he should not linger in any of those doctrines. "Escape to the mountain," signifies escaping toward the good of love and charity. "Lest you be consumed," signifies that if he did otherwise, he would perish.

**2415.** That "it came to pass, when they had brought them forth outside" signifies a state when they were being held back from falsehood and evil, is clear from what was said just above in number 2413, as well as in numbers 2388 and 2411.

**2416.** That "he said, 'Escape for your life'" signifies that he should look after his life for eternity, is clear without further explanation. How he was to look after his life now follows.

**2417.** That "do not look behind you" signifies that he should not look back toward doctrinal matters <note>original: *doctrinalia*</note>, is clear from the meaning of "looking behind oneself" when the city was behind him and the mountain was before him. For a "city" signifies doctrine (see numbers 402, 2268, 2450), while a "mountain" signifies love and charity (see numbers 795, 1430). That this is the meaning will become clear in the explanation of Verse 26, where it is said that Lot’s wife looked back behind him and became a pillar of salt.

Anyone can see that there is a certain Divine secret <note>original: *arcanum quoddam Divinum*</note> in these words—"do not look behind you"—and that this secret lies deeper than can be seen on the surface. In the literal act of looking behind oneself, nothing criminal appears; yet it is of such great importance that he is told to "escape for his life"—that is, to look after his life for eternity—by not looking behind him. What it means to "look toward doctrinal matters" will be seen in what follows. 

For now, it must be explained what doctrine <note>original: *Doctrinale*</note> is. Doctrine is twofold: one is of love and charity, the other is of faith. Every Church of the Lord, in its beginning while it is still a "maiden" or "virgin," has no other doctrine and loves no other than that of charity, for this is the doctrine of life. However, the Church gradually turns away from this doctrine until it begins to devalue <note>original: *vilipendere*</note> and finally reject it. At that point, it acknowledges no other doctrine than what is called the doctrine of faith. When the Church separates faith from charity, its doctrine conspires with a life of evil. 

Such was the Primitive Church <note>The early Christian church after the time of the Apostles.</note> or the Church of the Gentiles after the coming of the Lord. In its beginning, it had no other doctrine than that of love and charity, for this is what the Lord Himself taught (see number 2371 at the end). But after His time, as love and charity gradually began to grow cold, the doctrine of faith began, and with it came disagreements and heresies, which increased as they relied on this doctrine. Similarly, the Ancient Church <note>The church existing after the Great Flood, spanning many nations.</note> (which existed after the flood and extended through so many kingdoms, see number 2385) knew no other doctrine in its beginning than the doctrine of charity, because that doctrine looked toward and filled their life, and in this way, they provided for themselves for eternity. But after some time, among certain people, the doctrine of faith also began to be cultivated, which they eventually separated from charity.

<meta>This page continues the internal or spiritual explanation of Genesis 19, specifically exploring why the "Most Ancient Church" used certain symbolic names for people in various states of need.</meta>

# CHAPTER NINETEEN

...but these they called Ham <note>original: *Cham*</note>, because they were evil in life; see numbers 1062, 1063, 1076. The Most Ancient Church, which existed before the flood and was called "Man" <note>original: *Homo*</note> above all others, lived in the very perception of love to the Lord and charity toward the neighbor. Thus, they had the doctrine <term>doctrinale</term> of love and charity written within themselves. But even then, there were those who cultivated faith. When they eventually separated faith from charity, they were called Cain; for "Cain" signifies such faith, and "Abel," whom he killed, signifies charity (see the explanation for *Genesis*, chapter 4).

From this, it can be seen that there is a double doctrine: one of charity and the other of faith, even though both are one in themselves. For the doctrine of charity involves everything belonging to faith. But when doctrine consists only of those things which are of faith, it is then called a "double doctrine" because faith is separated from charity. That they are separated today is clear from the fact that it is completely unknown what charity is and who the neighbor is. Those who focus only on the doctrine of faith think charity toward the neighbor is nothing more than giving of their own to others and pitying everyone; for they say everyone is their neighbor without distinction.

Yet Charity is every good thing whatever in a person—in their affection and in their zeal, and from there in their life. And the "Neighbor" is every good in others that affects us, especially those who are in good, and this with all distinction. For example, a person is in charity and mercy who exercises justice and judgment by punishing the evil and rewarding the good. In punishing the evil, there is charity, for in this way one is moved by a zeal to reform that person and, at the same time, to protect others so that no harm comes to them. In this way, one cares for and wishes well to the person who is in an evil state or an enemy, and thus cares for and wishes well to others and to the state itself—and this comes from charity toward the neighbor.

It is the same with the other goods of life; for the good of life can never exist unless it comes from charity toward the neighbor, for it looks to this and involves this. Because it is so obscure, as mentioned, what Charity and the Neighbor are, it is clear that the **Doctrine of Charity** has become a lost thing after the **Doctrine of Faith** took the primary place. Yet it was the only thing cultivated in the Ancient Church—to such an extent that they categorized all the goods of charity toward the neighbor (that is, all who were in good). They did this with much distinction, giving them names and calling them: the Poor, the Wretched, the Oppressed, the Sick, the Naked, the Hungry, the Thirsty, the Captives (or those in prison), the Strangers, the Fatherless, and the Widows. They even called some the lame, the blind, the deaf, the mute, and the maimed, among many others.

According to this doctrine, the Lord spoke in the Word of the Old Testament, which is why such terms appear there so often. The Lord Himself also spoke according to this same doctrine, as in *Matthew 25:35, 36, 38, 39, 40, 42, 43, 44, 45*; *Luke 14:13, 21*; and many other places. This is why those names signify something else in the internal sense. So that the Doctrine of Charity may be restored, in the following pages, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, we will explain who these people are, and specifically what Charity and the Neighbor are.

**2418.** That "do not stay in all the plain" signifies that he should not linger in any of those doctrines, is clear from the meaning of the "Plain" <note>original: *Planities*</note>, which is everything belonging to doctrine, as will be discussed shortly. How it works—that he should not linger in any of them—will be discussed at Verse 26, concerning Lot’s wife, who looked back behind him.

No. IV.

It also notes that biblical terms like "the poor" and "the blind" were originally technical categories used by the Ancient Church to describe different spiritual states.</summary>

# GENESIS.

That **"The Plain"** in the Word <note>original: *Verbo*; referring to the Bible</note> signifies everything belonging to **Doctrine** <term>doctrinalia; the body of teachings or principles of a church</term> is evident from Jeremiah: "The destroyer shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape; the valley also shall perish, and the **plain** shall be destroyed," *Jeremiah 48:8*. Here, "city" stands for a false doctrine, and "the plain" stands for everything that belongs to that doctrine. In the Book of Revelation: "When the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, and shall go out to deceive the nations, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle, the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up over the **entire plain** <note>original: *omnem Planitiem*; often translated as "the breadth of the earth"</note> of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints; but fire came down from God out of heaven and consumed them," *Revelation 20:7-8, 9*. In this passage, Gog and Magog represent those who are in external worship without internal worship, which becomes a form of idolatry (see section 1151). The "plain of the earth" signifies the church's doctrines, which these people devastate; the "camp of the saints" signifies the goods of love and charity. Being "consumed by fire from God out of heaven" describes a similar fate to that of the men of Sodom and Gomorrah in verse 24. Furthermore, the doctrines of charity are called "cities of the mountain," and the doctrines of faith are called "cities of the plain" in *Jeremiah 33:13*.

**2419.** **Escape to the mountain,** which signifies escaping to the good of love and charity, is evident from the meaning of a "mountain," which represents love and charity (as discussed in sections 795 and 1430).

**2420.** **Lest perhaps you be consumed,** which signifies that if he did otherwise, he would perish, is evident without further explanation.

**2421. Verses 18, 19.** ***And Lot said to them, "No, I pray, my Lords. Look now, your servant has found grace in your eyes, and you have shown great mercy, which you have done for me by saving my life; but I cannot escape to the mountain, lest some evil overtake me and I die."***

**Lot said to them, "No, I pray, my Lords,"** signifies a feeling of weakness, as if he were unable to do it. **"Look now, your servant has found grace in your eyes,"** signifies a state of humiliation arising from an affection for truth. **"You have shown great mercy,"** signifies a state similar to humiliation but arising from an affection for good. **"Which you have done for me by saving my life,"** signifies the fact that the Lord wished to save him. **"And I cannot escape to the mountain,"** signifies a doubt that he could possess the good of charity. **"Lest some evil overtake me and I die,"** signifies that in such a case, it could not happen otherwise than that he would be overtaken by evil and thus be damned.

**2422.** That **Lot's words to them, "No, I pray, my Lords,"** signify a weakness in that he was unable to do it, is evident from the emotion in the words themselves as well as from what follows. We are now dealing with the **Third State of the Church** represented by Lot in this chapter. In this state, people no longer think and act from an **affection for good**, but rather from an **affection for truth**. This state follows when the affection for good begins to diminish and seemingly withdraw. Good is indeed present, but it has pulled back more toward the interior; therefore, it is in obscurity, but it manifests itself in a certain affection called the "affection for truth." (For the difference between the affection for good and the affection for truth, see section 1997 and section 2425 below). What these states are does not appear to a person—much less their specific qualities—but they appear to Angels as if in clear light, for Angels are present in every good affection a person has. These states even appear to the person themselves...

### CHAPTER NINETEEN

<note>original: *mini, dum in alteram vitam venit...*</note> ...Lord, when he comes into the other life; according to those affections, and according to their quality, the good are separated into distinct societies (see section 685).

**2423.** **"Behold now, your servant has found grace in your eyes,"** signifies humiliation coming from an affection for truth; **"and you have magnified your mercy,"** signifies a state of humiliation coming from an affection for good. This can be established from what was said previously regarding **Grace** and **Mercy** (see sections 598 and 981). Those who are in the <term>affection of truth</term> <note>a state of being moved or motivated by what is true</note> cannot humble themselves to the point of acknowledging from the heart that everything is a matter of **Mercy**; therefore, they use the word **Grace** instead. In fact, the less affection for truth they have, the less true humility is present when they speak of "grace." Conversely, the more <term>affection of good</term> <note>a state of being motivated by what is kind, charitable, and productive</note> a person has, the more humility they feel when they speak of **Mercy**. From this, it is clear how much the adoration—and therefore the worship—differs between those in the affection of truth and those in the affection of good. For worship to exist, there must be adoration, and for adoration to exist, there must be humility; this must be present in every single aspect of worship. This explains why both "grace" and "mercy" are mentioned here.

**2424.** **"Which you have shown me to save my life,"** <note>original: *ad vivificandum animam meam*; literally "to make my soul alive"</note> signifies that He intended to save him, which is clear without further explanation.

**2425.** **"And I cannot escape to the mountain,"** signifies a doubt that he could possess the **good of charity**—that is, a doubt about his ability to think and act from that state of goodness. This is evident from the meaning of a **Mountain**, which represents love and charity (see sections 795 and 1430). 

Regarding this doubt, the situation is as follows: in those who are in the affection of truth, there is an underlying affection for good, but it is so obscure that they do not perceive it. Thus, they do not truly know what the affection for good is, or what genuine charity is. They think they know it from "truth"—that is, from intellectual knowledge—but not from the actual experience of "good" itself. Nevertheless, they perform the good deeds of charity, not to earn merit, but out of obedience. They do this to the extent that they understand something to be true, allowing themselves to be led by the Lord through an obscure sense of good, using the truth that appears to them as truth. 

For example, because they do not fully understand who the **Neighbor** is, they do good to everyone they think is a neighbor. They prioritize the **Poor**, because they call themselves poor since they lack worldly wealth; they help **Orphans** and **Widows**, because they are named as such; and they help **Strangers**, for the same reason. They continue this as long as they remain ignorant of what is spiritually signified by the poor, orphans, widows, and strangers. However, because an affection for good lies hidden (though obscurely) within their affection for apparent truth, the Lord leads them to act this way. At an inner level, they are in a state of "good," where angels are present with them, delighting in the appearances of truth that move these people. 

But those who are in the **good of charity**, and thus in the affection of truth, do all things with discernment. They are "in the light," for the light of truth comes from nowhere else but from "good," because the Lord flows in through good. They do not do good to the poor, orphans, widows, and strangers solely because they bear those names; they know that those who are "good"—whether they are poor or rich—are the Neighbor above others. For from good people, good is done to others; therefore, by helping them, they are helping others through them. They also know how to distinguish between different types of good, and thus between different good people. They consider the **Common Good** to be their Neighbor even more, for in it, the good of many more people is considered. Ultimately, the **Kingdom of the Lord**...

However, those who put the Lord before all these things adore Him alone and love Him above all else; they derive the concept of the Neighbor from Him. In the highest sense, the Lord alone is the **Neighbor**; <note>original: *Proximus*</note> therefore, everything "Good" is the Neighbor to the extent it comes from Him. 

Those in the opposite state derive the definition of Neighbor from themselves. They only recognize those who favor and serve them as neighbors. They call no others "brothers" or "friends," and they do so only to the extent that those people agree with them. From this, it can be established what "Neighbor" means: it is defined for each person according to the kind of love they possess. Truly, the Neighbor is one who is in love for the Lord and charity toward the neighbor, with all the variations that exist. Thus, it is the quality of "Good" in each person that determines the relationship.

**2426.** **"Lest evil stick to me and I die,"** <note>Genesis 19:19</note> signifies that it could not happen otherwise than that he would be in evil at the same time, and thus be damned. This is clear without further explanation. What this implies can be known from what was previously said and shown (see sections 301, 302, 303, 571, 582, 1001, 1327, 1328): namely, that the Lord constantly provides that evil is not mixed with good. To the degree that a person is in evil, they are removed from good. For it is better to be entirely in evil than to be in evil and good at the same time. If someone is in evil and simultaneously in good, they cannot help but be damned eternally. Deceitful people and hypocrites within the Church are in this danger more than others. In the internal sense, "lest evil stick to me and I die" refers to this danger of mixing the two.

**2427.** **Verse 20. "Behold now, this city is near to flee to, and it is small; let me escape there, please—is it not small?—and my soul shall live."** 

**"Behold now, this city is near to flee to,"** signifies that it would be permitted based on the <term>truth of faith</term> <note>the intellectual understanding of spiritual principles</note>. **"And it is small,"** signifies that it would be from the little truth he possessed. **"Let me escape there, please,"** signifies that from that truth it would be possible to look toward "Good." **"Is it not small?"** signifies whether he might have at least a little something. **"And my soul shall live,"** signifies that in this way, he might perhaps be saved.

**2428.** **"Behold now, this city is near to flee to,"** signifies that it was permitted based on the truth of faith. This is evident from the meaning of a **City**, which represents <term>doctrine</term> <note>original: *doctrinale*; a set of teachings or a system of religious truth</note>, and thus the truth of faith (see sections 402 and 2268). It is called "near" because truth is closely related to "Good." Therefore, "fleeing there" signifies that it was permitted from that truth, because he could not act from "Good" itself (see section 2422).

**2429.** **"That it is small,"** signifies that it is from the little truth he had. This can be established from the meaning of a city as "truth," as mentioned above. A "small city" signifies a small amount of truth—specifically, the small amount he possessed, as shown by what precedes and follows. Regarding the matter itself: those who are in an <term>affection for truth</term> have little truth compared to those in an <term>affection for good</term>. This is because they look at truth from the tiny and obscure "Good" present within them. The "Truth" in a person exists exactly according to the "Good" in them; where there is little good, there is little truth. They exist in the same proportion and degree, or "walk at the same pace," as the saying goes. This might seem like a paradox, but it is nonetheless true. Good is the very [essence]... <note>original: *essentia*; catchword for the next page</note>

# CHAPTER 19

<note>original: *Caput Decimum Nonum*</note>

...the essence of truth. <note>original: *essentia veri*</note> Truth without its essence is not truly truth, even if it appears to be so. It is merely a hollow sound, like an empty vessel. In order for someone to truly possess Truth within themselves, they must not only know it but also acknowledge it and have faith in it. Only then do they truly "have" the truth, because only then does it affect them and remain with them. Otherwise, when someone only knows the truth but does not acknowledge it or have faith in it, they do not have the truth within them. 

This is the case with many who are in a state of evil; they may know truths—sometimes even better than others—but they still do not possess them. In fact, they possess them even less because they deny them in their hearts. The Lord provides that no one has more truth—that is, acknowledges and believes it—than the amount of "Good" <term>Good: in this context, "Good" refers to love and charity in action</term> they receive. This is why it is said here of the city (which symbolizes truth) that it is "small." It is mentioned again in this verse: **"Is it not a small thing?"** <note>Genesis 19:20</note> Then, in Verse 22, he calls the name of the city **Zoar**, which in the original language <note>Hebrew</note> means "small." This is because this passage concerns those who have an affection for truth but do not yet have a similar affection for good.

**2430.** **"Please let me escape there,"** signifies that from that state, one may be permitted to look toward what is good. This is evident from what comes before and what follows. Instead, he was told to go to the city (which symbolizes the truth of faith, section 2428). Thus, from truth, he could look toward good—or, what is the same thing, from faith he could look toward charity. That city was also situated at the base of the mountain; later, he ascended from there and lived on the mountain, though in a cave (Verse 30).

**2431.** **"Is it not a small thing?"** signifies asking if he might have at least a little bit. This is clear from what was said above in section 2429, and so needs no further explanation. This question is asked because the Lord alone knows how much good is within truth, and thus how much truth is truly present within a person.

**2432.** **"That my soul may live,"** signifies that in this way, perhaps he might be saved. This is also clear without explanation. That he was indeed saved because there was good within his truth is clear from what follows—specifically from the response: **"Behold, I have accepted your face also concerning this word, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken"** (Verse 21). And later: **"The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar"** (Verse 23). By this, we understand that those who have an affection for truth—that is, those who are in faith—are saved, provided that it is a "faith of good" <term>Faith of Good: a belief system that is rooted in or leads to charitable living</term>.

**2433.** **Verse 21. *And he said to him, "Behold, I have accepted your face also concerning this word, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken."*** 

"He said to him, 'Behold, I have accepted your face also concerning this word,'" signifies divine agreement, provided that the inner qualities within the truth are derived from what is good. "That I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken," signifies that in this state, the person would not perish.

**2434.** "He said to him, 'Behold, I have accepted your face <note>original: *facies*</note> also concerning this word,'" signifies agreement if the inner states within truth draw something from good. This is clear from the meaning of the "Face." Furthermore, when the "Face" is attributed to Jehovah or the Lord, it signifies Mercy, Peace, and Good (sections 222, 223). Therefore, in this context, it refers to the "Good" that is found internally within truth. To "accept the face," then, is to agree or grant a request...

# GENESIS.

When a person accepts and acknowledges something as good, they call everything that supports this good "true." However, whatever does not support it, they reject and call "false." They might even claim that something is not true because it does not favor their version of "good," though in that case, they are pretending and thinking otherwise. **2435.** **"I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken"** signifies that the person will not perish—specifically, the person who possesses truth containing internal good. Similarly, later with **Reuben**, the firstborn son of Jacob, who also represents Faith; he defiled his father's bed (Genesis 35:22; 49:4), and for this reason, he was made unworthy, and the birthright was given to **Joseph** (Genesis 49:5; 1 Chronicles 5:1). This is the source of all the disputes and the laws regarding the **"Birthright"** <note>original: *Primogenitura*</note> in the Word <term>the Word: the Bible or Divine revelation</term>. The reason for such controversy was that people did not know—just as it is not known today—that a person has only as much faith as they have charity. While a person is being regenerated, Charity meets Faith—or what is the same, Good meets Truth—and joins itself to every single part of it, making faith into real faith. Thus, Charity is actually the "Firstborn" of the Church, even though it appears otherwise to a person. See also n. 352, 367. But because these subjects are discussed extensively in the following pages, more will be said there, by the Divine Mercy of the Lord.

### CHAPTER NINETEEN

...that you should arrive there signifies that those who are in the affection for truth (represented here by Lot) must first be saved. This is also what is meant by the fact that Lot came to Zoar (Verse 23). That the good and just are saved before the evil and unjust perish is also established elsewhere in the Word. For instance, regarding the Last Judgment in Matthew: "The sheep were separated from the goats, and the sheep were told to enter the Kingdom of the Lord before the goats were told to depart into eternal fire" (25:32, 34, 41).

A similar situation was represented by the children of Israel when they left Egypt: they were saved first, before the Egyptians were drowned in the Red Sea <note>original: *mari Suph*</note>. The same thing is signified by the passages found throughout the Prophets, stating that after the faithful were led back from captivity, their enemies would then pay the penalty and perish. This also happens continually in the afterlife: specifically, the faithful are saved first and then the unfaithful are punished; or, what is the same, the faithful are raised into heaven by the Lord, while the unfaithful cast themselves into hell. 

The reason this does not happen simultaneously is that if the good were not first snatched away from the evil, they would easily perish. This is because the evil continually spread "poisons"—the desires of evil and the persuasions of the false. In general, before this happens, the evil must be separated from the good within people, so that the good may be lifted into heaven by the Lord and the evil may cast themselves down into hell. This subject will be discussed further, by the Lord's Divine Mercy, in sections 2449 and 2451.

**2439.** **"Therefore he called the name of the city Zoar"** signifies the affection for truth. This is established from the meaning of "Zoar," which is the affection for the "good of science" <term>Good of science: the spiritual benefit gained from learning and knowledge</term>—that is, the affection for truth (see n. 1589). It is also established from the phrase "calling a name," which means to know the quality of a thing (see n. 144, 145, 1754, 2009). Here, it specifically signifies a "little truth," for in the original language <note>Hebrew</note>, **Zoar** signifies "little" or "small." 

Those who are in the "affection for truth" have only a little truth (because they have relatively little "good") compared to those who are in the "affection for good" (see section 2429). It is a fact that truths—which are true in themselves—are "more true" for one person, "less true" for another, and for some, not true at all or even false. This can be seen in almost everything that is true in itself, because a truth is transformed within a person according to their motivations <note>original: *affectiones*</note>. 

For example: **performing a good work** or an act of charity is a truth in itself—it is something that should be done. 
*   To one person, it is a **good of charity** because it proceeds from love. 
*   To another, it is a **work of obedience** because it proceeds from a sense of duty. 
*   To some, it is **meritorious** because they want to earn salvation through it. 
*   To others, it is **hypocritical**, done only to be seen by others. 

The same applies to everything else called the "truths of faith." From this, it is clear that there is much truth among those in the affection for good, and less truth among those in the affection for truth; for the latter look at "Good" as something distant from themselves, while the former see "Good" as present within themselves.

**2440. Verse 23.** ***The sun was risen upon the earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.*** "The sun was risen upon the earth" signifies the final time, which is called the Last Judgment. "And Lot entered into Zoar" signifies those who are saved because they possess an affection for truth.

# GENESIS

## Page 56

2441. **The sun was risen upon the earth.** <note>original: *Sol egressus super terram*</note> This signifies the "final time," which is called the Last Judgment. This is established from the symbolic meaning of the "rising of the sun" when the subject is the times and states of the Church. As previously shown in number 2323, the times of the day (just like the seasons of the year) represent the successive states of the Church in the internal sense. "Dawn" or "Morning" <note>original: *Aurora seu Mane*</note> signifies the coming of the Lord or the approach of His Kingdom (see number 2405). Therefore, the "Rising of the sun," or its "going forth upon the earth," signifies His actual presence.

This is because both the Sun and the East <note>original: *Oriens*</note> signify the Lord (for the Sun, see numbers 31, 32, 1053, 1521, 1529, 1530, 1531, 2120; for the East, see number 101). The presence of the Lord is the same as the final time called the "judgment" because His presence separates the good from the evil. It brings about the result that the good are raised into heaven and the evil cast themselves into hell. 

In the other life, the situation is this: the Lord is the Sun to the entire heaven (see numbers 1053, 1521, 1529, 1530, 1531). His Divine Celestial Love appears this way before the eyes of those there, and it effectively creates the very Light of Heaven. Therefore, to the extent that people are in celestial love, they are raised into that heavenly light which comes from the Lord. However, to the extent they are removed from celestial love, they cast themselves out of that light and into the darkness of hell. 

This is why the "rising of the sun," which signifies the presence of the Lord, involves both the salvation of the good and the condemnation of the evil. It is first stated that Lot came to Zoar (meaning those represented by Lot are saved), and immediately afterward, that "Jehovah caused sulfur and fire to rain upon Sodom and Gomorrah" (meaning the evil are condemned). 

To those who are in the evils of self-love and love of the world—that is, those who harbor hatred against everything belonging to love for the Lord and charity toward the neighbor—the Light of Heaven effectively appears as gloom. For this reason, it is said in the Word that the sun is "blackened" <note>original: *atratus*</note> for them. This signifies that they have rejected everything of love and charity and have accepted everything that is contrary to them. We see this in Ezekiel: 

> "When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and blacken their stars; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give its light. All the lights of light in the heavens I will blacken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land" (32:7–8).

Anyone can see that "covering the heavens," "blackening the stars," "covering the sun," and "blackening the lights of light" signify deeper spiritual realities. Similarly, in Isaiah: 

> "The sun is darkened in its going forth, and the moon shall not cause its light to shine" (13:9–10). 

And in Joel: 

> "The sun and moon are blackened, and the stars withdraw their brightness" (2:2, 10). 

From this, it is clear what is signified by the Lord's words in Matthew regarding the final time of the Church (which is called the judgment): 

> "Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven" (24:29). 

This does not literally mean the sun, the moon, or the stars. Instead:
*   **The Sun** signifies love and charity.
*   **The Moon** signifies the faith derived from that love.
*   **The Stars** signify the knowledges <term>original: *cognitiones* — spiritual insights or perceptions</term> of good and truth.

These are said to be "darkened," to "lose their light," and to "fall from heaven" when there is no longer any acknowledgment of the Lord, no love for Him, and no charity toward the neighbor. When these things happen...

## Page 57

When no good deeds are performed, self-love takes over a person, along with the falsehoods that stem from it; for one is the natural consequence of the other. This is also described in the Book of Revelation: "The fourth Angel poured out his bowl *upon the Sun*, and it was given to him to scorch people with fire; so the people were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the Name of God" <note>original: Apocalypse 16:8–9</note>. This passage also deals with the final times of the Church, when all love and charity are extinguished—or, according to the common way of speaking, when there is no longer any faith. The "extinction of love and charity" is what is meant by the bowl being poured out upon the sun. The "self-love and its lusts" are signified by the people being scorched by fire and great heat. The "blaspheming of the Name of God" is the result of this state.

The Ancient Church <term>Ancient Church: A spiritual era or state of humanity following the "Most Ancient Church" (represented by Adam), characterized by symbolic worship and a focus on charity.</term> understood nothing else by the "Sun" than the Lord and the Divine Celestial aspect of His love. This is why their ritual was to pray toward the rising sun, though at that time they were not thinking about the physical sun at all. However, after their descendants lost this spiritual meaning (along with other representative and symbolic rites), they began to worship the physical sun and moon. This idol worship spread to many nations, to the point that they dedicated temples and erected statues to them. Because the sun and moon then took on an opposite meaning, they came to signify the love of self and the love of the world, which are entirely contrary to heavenly and spiritual love. 

Therefore, in the Word <note>original: *Verbo*; referring to the Bible</note>, the worship of the sun and moon signifies the worship of self and the world. As it says in the books of Moses: "Lest you lift up your eyes to heaven and see the Sun and the Moon and the Stars, the whole host of heaven, and be driven to bow down to them and serve them" <note>original: Deuteronomy 4:19</note>. And again: "If anyone has gone and served other gods and the *Sun* or the *Moon*, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded... then you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die" <note>original: Deuteronomy 17:3, 5</note>. The ancient worship turned into such idolatry when people no longer believed that anything internal was signified in the rituals of the Church, but only what was external. Similarly, in Jeremiah: "At that time the bones of the Kings of Judah, of the leading Priests, of the Prophets, and of the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be spread out before the *Sun* and the *Moon* and all the host of heaven, whom they loved and whom they served" <note>original: Jeremiah 8:1–2</note>. Here, the sun represents self-love and its lusts; "spreading out the bones" signifies the hellish things associated with such people. In the same Prophet: "He shall break the statues of the house of the sun that are in the land of Egypt, and the houses of the gods of Egypt he shall burn with fire" <note>original: Jeremiah 43:13</note>; the "statues of the house" signify the worship of self.

2442. **And Lot came to Zoar.** This signifies those who are in an affection for truth and are therefore saved. From this, it is also clear that even those who are "in faith" are saved, provided that there is "good" within their faith—that is, if they are moved by the truths of faith for the sake of goodness, which comes from the Lord. Every life of faith comes from no other source. To see how charity is the essential of faith—and is indeed faith itself, because it is the very heart of faith—see numbers 379, 389, 654, 724, 809, 916, 1162, 1176, 1789, 1799, 1834, 1844, 2049, 2116, 2189, 2190, 2228, 2261, 2340, 2349, and 2419.

2444. **Jehovah caused it to rain sulfur and fire upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah.** This signifies the hell belonging to those who are in the evils of self-love and the falsehoods stemming from it. This is clear from the meaning of "to rain," which is to be condemned; from "sulfur," which is the hell of the evils of self-love; and from "fire," which is the hell of the falsehoods resulting from it (as follows below). It is also clear from the meaning of Sodom as the evil of self-love, and Gomorrah <note>original Latin: "Amora"</note> as the falsehood resulting from it (see sections 2220, 2246, 2322). Gomorrah is mentioned here, even though it was not mentioned earlier in this chapter, because Gomorrah signifies the falsehood that comes from the evil of self-love. Within the Church—the final time or "judgment" of which is dealt with here—it is this evil that primarily acts against good, and consequently, its falsehood acts against truth. These two are so joined together that whoever is in one is also in the other, and indeed in the same proportion and degree. It may appear otherwise, yet it reveals itself to be so—if not in this world, then certainly in the next life. Concerning the nature of self-love, how many evils come from it, and that hell originates from it, see sections 693, 694, 760, 1307, 1308, 1321, 1594, 1691, 2041, 2045, 2051, 2057, 2219.

That it signifies blessing and salvation is clear from many passages; but that it signifies a curse and condemnation in the opposite sense is evident from these: In Isaiah, "The tabernacle shall be for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a hiding place from the *Inundation*, and from the *Rain*" (Isaiah 4:6). This refers to Egypt, about which it is written in Moses: "Jehovah gave thunder and hail, and fire vibrated over the earth, and Jehovah caused it to rain hail upon the land of Egypt" (Exodus 9:23–24).
