### CHAPTER TWENTY

*...they could not admit those things which confirm the truth, as those who are ignorant do. This person had been a Gentile.* <note>original: "non admittere possent illa quæ confirmant, sicut ii qui ignorant. Hic fuerat Gentilis."</note>

**2593.** It was also granted to me to speak with others who lived in ancient times, and who were then among the wiser individuals. At first, they appeared in front of me at a distance, and from there they were able to perceive the interior depths of my thoughts. From a single idea of thought, they could fully understand an entire series of ideas and fill that series with the delightful wisdom of pleasant representations. From this, it was perceived that they were among the wiser ones, and I was told they were from the Ancients. <note>The "Ancients" refers to people from the "Ancient Church," a period of spiritual history Swedenborg describes as existing after the Flood, characterized by a deep understanding of symbols and spiritual correspondences.</note> As they drew closer, I read to them something from the Word <note>original: "Verbo"; the Bible or Divine scripture</note>, and they were exceedingly delighted. Their very delight and joy were palpable; it arose primarily because every single thing they heard from the Word was representative and significative of heavenly and spiritual things. They said that in their time, when they lived in the world, their manner of thinking, speaking, and even writing was of this nature, and this was the focus of their study of wisdom.

**2594.** As for the Gentiles who are on earth today, they are not as wise, but most are simple of heart. Nevertheless, those among them who lived in mutual charity <note>The practice of kindness and goodwill toward one's neighbor.</note> receive wisdom in the afterlife; concerning them, the following accounts may be related.

**2595.** I heard a certain "gyre" <note>A circular or rhythmic movement of spirits.</note> of sounds, but it was deeper than usual. From the sound, I recognized immediately that they were from the Gentile nations. It was told to me by angels that they were Gentiles who had been resurrected three or four days prior. The "gyre" or chorus was heard for several hours, and it was perceived that even during that short time they were becoming more and more perfected. When I expressed wonder at this, I was told that they can be initiated into choruses—and thus into a state of harmony—in a single night, whereas many Christians can hardly achieve this in thirty years. These gyres or choruses occur when many speak together at once, all as if they were one, and each individual as if they were all. But by the Divine Mercy of the Lord, these gyres or choruses will be discussed elsewhere.

**2596.** One morning, a certain chorus was at a distance from me. From the representations shown by the chorus, it was granted to me to know that they were Chinese. They presented the appearance of a woolly goat, then a cake made of millet, and an ebony spoon, as well as the idea of a floating city. They desired to come closer to me, and when they applied themselves, they said they wished to be alone with me so they might open their thoughts. But it was told to them that they were not alone, and that others were present who were indignant that they wanted to be alone, especially since they were guests. Perceiving this indignation, they began to wonder if they had trespassed—

...whether they had transgressed against their neighbor, and whether they had claimed anything for themselves that belonged to others. <note>original: "varicati sint contra proximum, & num quicquam sibi vindicaverint quod aliorum esset"</note> (**In the afterlife, all thoughts are shared with one another.**) <note>original: "Cogitationes in altera vita omnes communicantur"</note> I was permitted to perceive their agitation, which served as an acknowledgment that they might have perhaps harmed others, and I felt the shame they experienced because of it. This, along with their other honest emotions, showed they were endowed with charity <note>In this context, "charity" refers to a spiritual love for one's neighbor and a desire to do good.</note>. 

Soon after, I spoke with them, and eventually about the Lord. When I called Him by the name "Christ," a certain resistance was felt among them. However, the cause of this was revealed: they had brought this attitude from the world because they knew that Christians lived worse lives than they did and lacked all charity. But when I simply called Him "the Lord," they were moved deep within. They were then instructed by angels that Christian doctrine, above all others in the entire world, prescribes love and charity, but that there are very few people who actually live according to it.

**2597.** There are Gentiles who, while they lived in the world, learned through conversation and reputation that Christians live very bad lives—engaging in adultery, hatred, quarreling, drunkenness, and similar vices. These Gentiles were horrified by such actions because they were contrary to their own laws, customs, and religious beliefs. In the afterlife, these individuals are more hesitant than others to receive the truths of faith. However, they are eventually instructed by angels that Christian doctrine and faith itself teach something entirely different, and that these "Christians" live according to their teachings far less than the Gentiles do. When they perceive this reality, they receive the truths of faith and worship the Lord, though it happens somewhat later for them.

**2598.** When I was reading chapters 17 and 18 of the Book of Judges concerning Micah—specifically how the sons of Dan took away his carved image, his *teraphim* <term>teraphim: ancient Hebrew household gods or idols, often used for divination</term>, and his Levite priest—there was a spirit from the Gentiles present who had worshiped a carved image during his life on earth. As he listened attentively to what happened to Micah, and the intense grief Micah felt because the Danites had stolen his image, he too was overcome with sorrow. He was so affected that he hardly knew what to think because of his deep internal pain. This grief was perceptible to me, and along with it, I felt the innocence present in every one of his emotions. 

Christian spirits were also present; they observed this and were amazed that a worshiper of an idol could be moved by such a profound feeling of mercy and innocence. Afterward, good spirits spoke with him, explaining that a carved image should not be worshiped. They told him that as a rational human being, he could understand this, but that he should think of God the Creator and Governor of the entire heaven and earth as being beyond the image, and that this God was the Lord. As they said this, I was permitted to perceive the inner affection of his worship, which was shared with me; it was far more holy than the worship found among Christians. From this, it was evident that Gentiles enter heaven more easily than Christians who are not living according to their faith...

...Gentiles <note>original: "tiles"</note> may more easily enter heaven than the Christians of today who are not moved by the truth. This is according to the Lord's words in Luke 13:29–30. In the state he was in, he was able to be filled with all the principles of faith and to receive them with deep, internal affection. He possessed mercy, which comes from love, and in his ignorance there was innocence. When these two qualities are present, all the truths of faith are received almost spontaneously and with joy. **2599.** There was also another man among the Gentiles who had lived in the **good of charity** <note>original: "bono charitatis" — a term referring to a life defined by active neighborly love and kindness</note>. When he heard Christian spirits reasoning about matters of belief (and spirits reason much more fully and sharply among themselves than humans do, especially about what is good and true, as these are the concerns of the next life), he was amazed that they argued so much. He said he did not want to hear those arguments, for they were reasoning based on false appearances. He instructed them by saying: *"If I am good, I can know what is true from goodness itself; and what I do not know, I am able to receive."*

**2600.** Upright Gentiles in the other life are, for the most part, instructed according to the state of their lives and according to their own religion, so far as this is possible. This happens in various ways, but here only three may be mentioned.

**2601.** Some of them are brought into a state of tranquility, almost like a kind of sleep. In this state, they seem to themselves to build small cities and to hide some <term>arcanum</term> <note>original: "arcanum" — a sacred secret or hidden spiritual mystery</note> in the center of them, which they wish for no one to violate. They give these cities to others, ساتھ with prayers that they do not violate the secret in their midst. In this way, innocence is introduced to them, and then charity, along with the idea that the secret is about the Lord. They are kept in this state for a considerable time. It is a state of ignorance that contains innocence. They are protected by infant spirits so that no one can do them harm. I have spoken with them and was deeply moved by their state of innocence and charity, as well as by their concern for how they hide their secret and their holy fear that it might be violated.

**2602.** There is one nation, said to be from the **Indies** <note>In the 18th century, "the Indies" could refer generally to India, East Asia, or even the Americas.</note>, who have this religious custom: they worship the Supreme God in a specific ritual where, when they adore Him, they first make themselves feel great, but immediately afterward prostrate themselves like little worms. They also believe that above the universe (which they believe rotates) sits the Supreme God, looking down from there to see what they do. Because these were their religious beliefs, they are brought back into those same ideas in the next life. I spoke with them while they were visualizing these things. For the most part, they are modest, obedient, and simple-hearted. They are gradually freed from these fantasies by angels. They are instructed according to their own religious framework: that the Supreme God is the Lord, and that they can truly become "great" through the fact that they are able to adore Him, and that...

...they are even like little worms, and that the Lord from on high looks upon all things and every single detail: thus, through their own religious framework <note>original: "religiosum suum" — referring to the specific religious upbringing or belief system of a person</note>, they are suitably led into the knowledge of what is good and true.

**2603.** There are some Gentiles from those regions where people are black, who carry with them from their life in the world a desire to be treated harshly. They believe that no one can come into heaven except through punishments and afflictions, after which they will receive more joyful things, which they call "paradisiacal." Because they have such beliefs from their religion, in the other life they are also first treated harshly by certain spirits whom they call devils. Afterward, they are carried into paradisiacal states (discussed in section 1622), but they are instructed by angels that their punishments and afflictions have been turned into good for them by the Lord—just as it is with those undergoing spiritual trials <note>original: "tentationibus" — here referring to spiritual temptations or internal struggles that refine the soul</note>. 

They are also taught that these paradisiacal states are not heaven itself, but rather the affection for heavenly and spiritual things that is within them; they are told that they had been on a path toward truth, though in the shadow of ignorance. These people spoke with me for a long time; when they were in a state of affliction, their speech was like a kind of clashing sound, quite distinct from the speech of others. But once those trials were over and they were raised into the paradisiacal states, their speech was no longer like that, but was almost angelic. From their religion, they also believe that they should have "inner" qualities; they said that when they are treated harshly, they are black, but afterwards they cast off their blackness and put on whiteness, knowing that their souls are white, even though their bodies were black.

**2604.** It is common for Gentiles who have worshipped some god in the form of an image, statue, or some carved object, to be introduced to certain spirits who take the place of those gods or idols when they enter the other life. This is done so that they may shed their fantasies <note>original: "phantasias suas exuant" — to be freed from their previous delusions or false mental images</note>. After they have been with these spirits for a few days, they are taken away. 

Those who worshipped men are also sometimes introduced to them, or to others who take their place. For example, many of the Jews are introduced to Abraham, Jacob, Moses, and David; but when they perceive that these men are human just like everyone else and can offer no help, they are ashamed and are carried to their own places according to how they lived. Among the Gentiles in the other life, the Africans are loved most of all, for they receive the goods and truths of heaven more easily than others. They especially want to be called "obedient" rather than "faithful." They say that Christians, because they possess the doctrine of faith, can be called "faithful," but they themselves cannot be called so unless they receive it—or, as they say, are able to receive it.

# CHAPTER TWENTY

2605. I spoke with certain individuals who belonged to the Ancient Church <note>original: "Ecclesia Antiqua" — in the author's theology, this refers to the spiritual era that followed the fall of the first "Most Ancient" humanity</note>, and who at that time knew that the Lord was to come. Although they had been filled with the "goods of faith" <note>the practical, lived aspects of religious belief</note>, they eventually fell away and became idolaters. They were positioned in front toward the left, in a dark place and in a miserable state. Their speech was like that of a pipe <note>original: "tibialis" — a thin, monotone sound like a simple flute or reed</note>, consisting of a single tone and almost entirely lacking rational thought. They said they had been there for many centuries, and that they are occasionally brought out from there to perform certain menial tasks <note>original: "viles" — lowly or humble uses</note> for others. From their example, I was led to reflect on those many Christians who are idolaters not outwardly, but inwardly—those who in their hearts deny the Lord and the truths of faith—and what kind of fate might await them in the next life.

# PART TWO

## THE BOOK OF GENESIS

### CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

2606. The Word of the Old Testament was formerly called the *Law* and the *Prophets*. By the "Law" were understood all the historical books, which include the five books of Moses, Joshua, Judges, Samuel, and Kings. By the "Prophetic" books were understood all the prophecies, including Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Jonah, Micah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, as well as the Psalms of David. The historical parts of the Word are also referred to as "Moses"; hence, "Moses and the Prophets" is commonly used to mean the Law and the Prophets. The prophetic parts are referred to as "Elijah" <note>original: Elias</note>; see the Preface to Chapter 18 of Genesis.

2607. Regarding the historical accounts, everything written there is historically true, except for what is found in the first chapters of Genesis. Those chapters are "composed histories" <note>original: *historica facta* — stories constructed in a historical form to contain spiritual meaning rather than describing literal physical events</note>, which were discussed in Part One. Even though the other historical books are literally true, they still possess an internal sense. In that sense—just like the prophetic books—they deal exclusively with the Lord. They also deal with Heaven and the Church, and the things that belong to Heaven and the Church; but since those things belong to the Lord, they look toward the Lord through them, and for this reason, they are considered the Word. All the historical accounts in the Word are representative <note>original: *repraesentativa* — physical people or events that represent spiritual realities</note>, and the individual words used to describe them are significative <term>significative</term> <note>original: *significativa* — meaning that every specific word corresponds to a spiritual concept</note>. That these historical accounts are

It is clear that every single word used to describe these events is significant. This is evident from what has already been shown: that **Names** signify actual things. For example, **Egypt** signifies factual knowledge <note>original: *scientia* — in this context, external or sensory knowledge</note>, **Assyria** <note>original: *Aschur*</note> signifies the rational mind, **Ephraim** the intellectual, **Tyre** signifies different types of knowledge <note>original: *cognitiones*</note>, **Zion** the celestial Church, **Jerusalem** the spiritual Church, and so forth.

The same applies to other terms: a **King** signifies truth, and a **Priest** signifies good. In their internal meaning, other words are similarly symbolic, such as Kingdom, City, House, Nation, People, Garden, Vineyard, Olive-grove, Gold, Silver, Bronze <note>original: *Aes*</note>, Iron, Birds, Beasts, Bread, Wine, Oil, Morning, Day, and Light. This symbolism is consistent throughout both the historical and prophetic books, even though they were written by various authors at different times. Such consistency would never exist unless the Word had descended from Heaven.

From this, one can recognize that there is an internal sense within the Word. Furthermore, the Divine Word could never deal merely with human beings—such as Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their descendants (who were among the worst of nations)—or with their kings, wives, sons, daughters, prostitutes, robberies, and similar matters. If viewed only on the surface, these things are not even worthy of being mentioned in the Word. They only become worthy of the Word because they represent and signify things that exist in the Lord’s Kingdom.

> "...and upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon, and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah," Jeremiah 48: 3, 4, 5, 21, 22, 23, 24. <note>original Latin: & super Kirjathaim, & super Bethgamul... these are cities in Moab mentioned in a prophecy of judgment.</note>

Prophetic passages like these are found in many places throughout the Word of God. Unless they possessed an internal sense, they would be of no use to the reader. However, because the Word is Divine, it must necessarily contain within itself the laws of the heavenly Kingdom, which a person is destined to enter.

2609. Regarding the ***Precepts of life*** <note>original: *Præcepta vitæ* — moral and ethical commands</note>—such as all the commandments of the Decalogue <term>Decalogue</term><note>The Ten Commandments</note> and many others in the Law and the Prophets—these serve the very life of a person. Therefore, they are useful in both senses: the literal and the internal. 

The literal sense was intended for the people of that historical time who could not grasp internal, spiritual concepts. The internal sense is for the Angels, who do not concern themselves with external matters. If the commandments of the Decalogue did not also contain internal truths, they would never have been proclaimed with such a great miracle on Mount Sinai. After all, the commands given there—such as honoring one's parents, not stealing, not murdering, not committing adultery, and not coveting what belongs to another—are rules that even the Gentiles <note>Non-Jewish nations</note> know and have written in their own laws. The children of Israel, simply as human beings, should have already known these things without such a miraculous proclamation. 

However, because those Precepts served life in both senses, and were like external forms produced from internal truths (to which they correspond), they descended from heaven onto Mount Sinai with that great miracle. In the internal sense, they were spoken and heard in Heaven, while in the external sense, they were spoken and heard on earth. 

For example, take the commandment that those who honor their parents will have their days prolonged upon the land. 
*   **The Angels** in heaven perceived "parents" as the Lord, and "the land" as His Kingdom, which those who worship Him out of love and faith will possess forever as children and heirs. 
*   **People on earth**, however, understood "parents" as their literal parents, "the land" as the land of Canaan, and the "prolongation of days" as the years of their physical life. 

Consider the command "do not steal." 
*   **The Angels** in heaven perceived this to mean they should take nothing away from the Lord, nor claim any righteousness or merit for themselves. 
*   **People on earth**, however, understood it simply as not stealing property. That these truths exist in both senses is clear. 

Finally, regarding "do not murder": 
*   **The Angels** in heaven perceived this as a command not to hold hatred toward anyone and not to extinguish anything of "good" or "truth" in another person. 
*   **People on earth**, meanwhile, understood it as not killing their friends and neighbors. The same applies to all the other commandments.

2610. In the internal sense, this passage deals first with the Lord’s Divine Rational, which is represented by Isaac <note>original: Jiſchakum</note>, verses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.

2611. Next, it deals with the merely human Rational, which was then separated; this is the son of Hagar the Egyptian, verses 9, 10, 11, 12.

2612. After this was separated, the spiritual Church is represented by the same—namely, by Hagar's son, as well as by the mother; this passage concerns the Church and its state, verses 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.

2613. Concerning human rational things joined to the doctrine of faith, which is Divine in itself, verse 22 to the end.

### I N T E R N A L   S E N S E

2615. VERSE 1. *And Jehovah visited Sarah, just as he said, and Jehovah did for Sarah just as he had spoken.* "Jehovah visited Sarah" signifies the presence of the Celestial Divine in the Spiritual Divine. "Just as he said" signifies as he had perceived. "And Jehovah did for Sarah" signifies a state of union. "Just as he had spoken" signifies as he had thought.

2616. "Jehovah visited Sarah" signifies the presence of the Celestial Divine in the Spiritual Divine. This is evident from the meaning of **Jehovah**, which is the Celestial Divine—that is, the Divine Good, or the Essential Being <note>original: Esse</note>. Because this belongs to love and mercy, it is Good itself. It is also evident from the meaning of **to visit**, which is to be present, and from the meaning of **Sarah**, which is the Spiritual Divine—that is, Divine Truth (regarding this, see numbers 1468, 1901, 2063, 2065, 2507).

2617. "Just as he said" signifies as he had perceived. This is evident from the meaning of **to say** in the historical parts of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Bible</note>, which is "to perceive" (regarding this, see numbers 2238, 2260, 2552).

2618. **And Jehovah did for Sarah**, which signifies a state of union—namely, of the Lord's Divine Spiritual in His Divine Celestial—is clear from the meaning of "to do," when it is predicated of the Lord’s Divine, as being the total effect, and therefore a state. This is also clear from the meanings of **Jehovah** and **Sarah** mentioned just above in section 2616. Regarding the state of union of the Lord’s Divine Spiritual in His Divine Celestial: this is the actual Marriage of Good and Truth, from which comes the "Heavenly Marriage." This Marriage is the Lord’s Kingdom in the heavens and on earth; for this reason, the Lord’s Kingdom is so often called a "marriage" in the Word and is compared to a marriage. The reason for this—which is a secret <note>original: arcanum</note>—is that from the Divine Marriage of Good and Truth, and of Divine Truth and Good in the Lord, comes all marriage love, and through this, all heavenly and spiritual love. Furthermore, the secrets involved in these words—"that Jehovah visited Sarah as he said, and Jehovah did for Sarah as he had spoken"—cannot be fully declared because they are inexpressible. They encompass the actual state of the union of the Lord’s Divine with His Human. The appearances of this state are presented before the Angels by the Lord through heavenly lights and are illustrated by inexpressible representations; however, they cannot be presented before humans, because they would have to be described using things belonging to the light of the world, which these concepts do not fit into. In fact, a description using such worldly terms would only obscure them further.

2619. **Just as he had spoken**, which signifies "just as he thought," is clear from the meaning of "to speak," which is to think (as discussed in sections 2271 and 2287). The perception signified by "Jehovah said" was from the Divine Celestial; however, the thought signified by "Jehovah spoke" was from the Divine Celestial through the Divine Spiritual. Therefore, there is what seems like a repetition in the literal sense: namely, "just as he said" and "just as he had spoken." But what it means to perceive from the Divine Celestial, and to think from the Divine Celestial through the Divine Spiritual, does not fall within the grasp of even the most enlightened understanding using the light of this world. From this, it is clear how infinitely more there is to understand. That thought comes from perception can be seen in sections 1919 and 2515. In a human being, it works like this: "good" is that from which one perceives, while "truth" is that through which one thinks. Good belongs to love and its affections, and therefore perception comes from it; truth, however, belongs to faith, and therefore truth belongs to thought. In the historical parts of the Word, the former is signified by *saying*, while the latter is signified by *speaking*. But when "saying" is read alone, it sometimes signifies perceiving and sometimes thinking, because "saying" involves both.

2620. Verse 2. *And Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.* **Conceived and bore** signifies that it should be and exist. **Sarah to Abraham** signifies from the union of the Lord’s Divine Spiritual with His Divine Celestial. **A son** signifies the Divine Rational. **In his old age** signifies when the days were completed so that the human might be cast off. **At the set time** signifies when the Rational was in such a state that it could receive. **As God had spoken to him** signifies just as He willed.

2621. That **conceived and bore** signifies "to be and to exist"—namely, as follows, the Divine Rational from the union of the Lord’s Divine Spiritual with His Divine Celestial—is clear from the meaning of "conceiving and giving birth." In the internal sense of the Word, no other conceptions or births are understood than spiritual and...

...heavenly <note>original: cœlestes</note> ones, see section 2584. Here, however, the term "Divine" is used because the subject is the Lord's Rational part being made Divine. Of the Lord, "Being" and "Existence" <note>original: Esse & Existere</note> are primarily stated, for He alone Is and Exists. 

Furthermore, regarding Being and Existence: they appear as if they were almost the same thing, but they are not. Everyone and everything has its Being <note>original: Esse</note> from its conception, but its Existence <note>original: Existere</note> from its birth. Just as conception comes before birth, Being comes before Existence. The Soul is the very Being of a human, but the sensory or bodily part is its Existence, for the soul exists within the body. Heavenly and spiritual love is the very Being of a person who is being "born again" (regenerated), while the rational and sensory part—once it is filled with that love—is their Existence. This is true of every single thing in the universe, for nothing can ever exist that does not have its "conception" so that it may *Be*, and its "birth" so that it may *Exist*. This can be further illustrated for scholars: every effect has its cause, and every cause has its end (or purpose). The end is the Being <note>original: Esse</note> of the cause, and the cause is the Existence <note>original: Existere</note> of the end. Likewise, the cause is the Being of the effect, but the effect is the Existence of the cause.

2622. **To Abraham for Sarah**, which signifies that this results from the union of the Divine Spiritual with the Divine Celestial. This is clear from the representation of **Sarah** as the "Divine Spiritual" or "Divine Truth" (see sections 1468, 1901, 2063, 2065, 2172, 2193, 2198, 2507); and from the representation of **Abraham** as the "Divine Celestial" or "Divine Good" (see sections 1989, 2011, 2172, 2198, 2501). Regarding the union of the Divine Spiritual with the Divine Celestial, see what was said above in section 2618.

2623. **A son**, which signifies the Divine Rational part, is evident from the meaning of "son." In the internal (spiritual) sense of the Word, a son signifies truth (sections 489, 491, 533). Because truth is the most important element in the rational mind (sections 2072, 2189), a "son" also signifies the rational. Here, however, it signifies the Divine Rational, which is primarily composed of "Good." This is also what Isaac (who is the son here) represents, as will be shown in the following sections.

2624. **In his old age**, which signifies when the time was right for the human nature to be cast off, is evident from the meaning of "old age." It represents a state where the human nature is set aside and the Divine nature is put on <note>original: indueretur Divinum</note> (see section 2198). At that time, Abraham was a hundred years old; that this number signifies a full state of union will be shown in the explanation of verse 5.

2625. **At the set time**, which signifies when the Rational part was in a state to receive [the Divine], is evident from the meaning of "time." While a person lives in this world, two things appear essential because they belong to the nature of the physical world: namely, Space and Time. Consequently, to live in space and time is to live in the world or in nature. But these two things cease to exist in the next life. In the world of spirits, they still appear to be something because spirits who have recently left the body still carry natural ideas with them. However, they soon realize that space and time do not exist there; instead, there are "States." In the afterlife, "States" correspond to the spaces and times of nature: space corresponds to states regarding Being <note>original: esse</note>, and time corresponds to states regarding Existence <note>original: existere</note>. (On space or place, see sections 1274, 1379, 1380, 1382). From this, it can be clear to anyone what kind of idea a human can have...

...while a person is in the world or in nature, they often feel this way about things of the afterlife and the many secrets of faith. They are unwilling to believe these things until they can grasp them through worldly things—even through the physical senses. Such a person cannot imagine that if they were to set aside the ideas of space and time—and even space and time themselves—they would not simply become nothing. They fear that nothing would remain for them to feel or think, except for something confused and incomprehensible. Yet the truth is exactly the opposite: the angelic life is the most wise and the most happy.

This is why, in the internal sense of the Word <note>original: Verbo; referring to the Bible</note>, ages do not represent literal ages, but rather "states" or conditions. In this sense, "old age" does not mean being old; similarly, numbers do not mean literal quantities, but specific states—such as the number of a hundred years, which we will discuss later. From this it is clear that "at the set time" signifies a state when the Rational <term>Rational</term> <note>The Rational refers to the faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly data.</note> part of the mind was ready to receive.

Concerning the actual event—that the Divine Rational came into being and existed from the union of the Lord’s Divine Spiritual and Divine Celestial—it happened when "the days were completed" so that the merely human part could be cast off. When the Rational was ready to receive, this was represented by the phrase: "Sarah conceived and bore to Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time." We should know that the human part begins in the innermost of the Rational (see sections 2106, 2194). The Lord progressed step-by-step toward the union of the Human Essence with the Divine, and the Divine with the Human (sections 1864, 2033, 2523). He did this by His own power (sections 1921, 2020, 2026, 2083), through constant temptations and victories (sections 1737, 1813, 1690), and through constant revelations from His own Divinity (sections 1616, 2500). Ultimately, He expelled everything of the maternal human <note>original: humanum maternum; the traits and limitations inherited from his mother, Mary</note> (sections 1414, 1444, 2574) and thus made His Human part Divine as to the Rational, according to the events in this verse. 

We can get some idea of this process from what happens to people who are being "born again" or regenerated. The heavenly things of love and the spiritual things of faith are not implanted all at once, but gradually by the Lord. Once a person's rational mind has become capable of receiving them, they are then regenerated—usually through temptations in which they are victorious. While these things are happening, the "days are completed" for them to cast off the "old man" and put on the "new man." Regarding human regeneration, see sections 677, 679, 711, 848, 986, 1555, 2475.

2626. **As God had spoken with him**, which signifies "just as He willed." This is evident from the meaning of "to speak," which signifies "to think" (see sections 2271, 2286, 2619). Here, however, it means "to will" because it says "God spoke"; for Divine thinking is the same as willing.

2627. **Verse 3. And Abraham called the name of his son born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.**
"Abraham called the name of his son born to him" signifies the quality of that which is Divine. "Whom Sarah bore to him" signifies being and existing from the Divine Spiritual united to the Divine Celestial. "Isaac" <note>original: Jischak</note> signifies the Divine Rational.

# GENESIS

...Lord <note>original: nus; continuing from the previous page's "Dominus"</note> as to the Divine Celestial, or Divine Good, which has been discussed many times before. This is clear from the meaning of "calling a name," which signifies its quality (see notes 144, 145, 1754, 1896, 2009); from the meaning of "son," which represents the rational <term>Rational</term> <note>The faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge.</note> (note 2623); and from the phrase "born to him," which signifies "to exist from the Divine." From this, it is evident that the phrase "Abraham called the name of his son born to him" signifies the quality of that which is Divine. 

From these few words, three secrets <note>original: arcana</note> shine forth for those who understand the internal sense: 
*First*, that the Lord’s Divine Human existed from the Divine Itself (which is discussed further in this verse). 
*Second*, that the Lord’s Divine Human was not only conceived but also born from Jehovah; for this reason, the Lord, as to the Divine Human, is called the "Son of God" and the "Only Begotten" (see John 1:14, 18, 50; Chapter 3:16, 18, 35, 36; Chapter 5:19–27; Chapter 6:69; Chapter 9:35; Chapter 10:36; Chapter 11:27; Chapter 14:13, 14; Chapter 17:1; Chapter 20:31; and similarly in the other Gospels). 
*Third*, that the Lord’s Divine Human is the "Name of Jehovah," which is to say His quality (see John 12:28).

2629. **Whom Sarah bore to him**, signifies to "be" and "exist" from the Divine Spiritual united to the Divine Celestial. This is established from the meaning of "giving birth," which is to "exist" (note 2621). Because birth involves conception, and "existing" (birth) comes from the Divine Spiritual, while "being" (conception) comes from the Divine Celestial—which are united here—the word "bearing" or "giving birth" signifies both "to be" and "to exist." This is also clear from the representation of Sarah, who signifies the Divine Spiritual united to the Divine Celestial (notes 1468, 1901, 2063, 2065, 2172, 2193, 2198, 2507). These matters are too hidden to be described, or even illustrated by anything in this world; they are intended for angelic minds, to whom these things are presented through inexpressible things in the light of heaven.

2630. **Isaac** <note>original: Jifchak</note>, signifies the Divine Rational. This is clear from what was said previously regarding Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (notes 1893, 2066, 2083)—namely, that Abraham represents the Supreme Divine, Isaac the Divine Rational, and Jacob His Divine Natural. This will also become clear from what follows concerning Isaac.

2631. **Verse 4.** *And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son, being eight days old, just as God commanded him.* "Abraham circumcised Isaac his son" signifies the purification of the Rational. "A son of eight days" signifies a beginning and a continuous state. "Just as God commanded" signifies according to Divine order.

2632. **Abraham circumcised Isaac his son**, signifies the purification of the Rational. This is established from the meaning of "being circumcised," which is to be purified (note 2039), and from the representation of Isaac as the Divine Rational (note 2630). It was stated previously (in the discussion of Ishmael, who represents that first Rational) that the Lord's first Rational was born just like that of other people—namely, through scientifics <term>scientifics</term> <note>From the Latin "scientifica," referring to factual or academic knowledge stored in the memory.</note> and knowledges. Because that Rational was born through factual knowledge and thus through the external way of the senses (just as with others), it could not help but contain many things from the world; for the ideas of the Rational are acquired from there. This was even more true because he had an inheritance from his mother <meta>catchword: mother;</meta>

# CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

...[while what came from the] mother was worldly and hereditary. These the Lord successively expelled from His Rational <term>Rational</term> <note>The faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge.</note> until it was in such a state that it could receive the Divine (see notes 2624, 2625). Then the Lord’s Divine Rational was born, which is represented by Isaac (note 2630). This did not happen through an external way—which is the way of the senses, as with the previous Rational—but through an internal way from the Divine Itself (notes 2628, 2629). Because this was not done all at once but successively (notes 1690, 2033), it was continually purified. This is signified by the statement that Abraham circumcised his son, "a son of eight days." 

That the Lord successively made His Rational Divine and continually purified it is also evident in the Gospel of John: "Jesus said, Father, glorify Your name. Then a voice came from heaven: 'I have glorified it, and will glorify it again'" <note>original: "glorificavi, & rursus glorificabo"</note> (John 12:28). To "glorify" means to make Divine (see notes 1603, 1999). 

In the Ancient Church, Circumcision represented and signified nothing other than the purification of a person from the loves of self and the world. This also happens successively and continually (see notes 2039, 2046 to 2049, 2056), especially when a person is born anew or regenerated. At that time, the Lord flows in through an internal way—that is, through the "good of conscience"—and successively and continually separates those things that cling to the person from hereditary and actual evil.

2633. **A son of eight days**, which signifies a beginning and a continuation, is established from the meaning of the "eighth day" on which they were circumcised. This represents any beginning, and thus what is continuous (see note 2044).

2634. **As God commanded him**, which signifies "according to Divine order," is established from the meaning of God "commanding," or of His commandments. The commandments of God, or the things He has commanded, are the individual components of Divine order—so much so that Divine order is nothing other than the perpetual commandment of God. Therefore, to live according to the commandments of God, and within them, is to live according to and within Divine order. 

From this, "God commanded" here signifies "according to Divine order." It was according to Divine order that every male should be circumcised on the eighth day from birth. This was not because the act of circumcision itself did anything, or because the circumcised entered the Kingdom of God more easily than the uncircumcised; rather, it was because such a rite in the Representative Church <note>A church where outward rituals represent internal spiritual realities.</note> corresponded to the purification of the heart. (By the Lord’s Divine Mercy, this correspondence will be discussed elsewhere.) 

The fact that the heart—the inner parts of a person—must be successively and continually purified from the evils of lusts and the falsities of fantasies is according to Divine order. Every commandment regarding the purification of the heart is a part of Divine order. To the extent that a person lives by those commandments, they live in Divine order. And to the extent they are in this order, all things within them are arranged by the Lord according to the order that exists in the heavens—specifically, both their rational thoughts and their factual knowledge <note>original: "scientifica"; refers to the external, learned knowledge of the mind.</note>. In this way, a person becomes a "little heaven" corresponding to the Greatest Heaven <term>Grand Man</term> <note>original: "Maximo"; Swedenborg's concept of the entire heaven in a single human form.</note>.

2635. Verse 5. **And Abraham was a son of a hundred years when Isaac his son was born to him.** 
"Abraham, a son of a hundred years," signifies a full state of union. "When Isaac his son was born to him" signifies when the Lord’s Rational became Divine.

# GENESIS

2636. **Abraham was a son of a hundred years** <note>original: "Abraham filius centum annorum"</note>. This signifies a full state of union. This is established by the meaning of "a hundred," which refers to what is "full" (as discussed in the following sections), and from the meaning of "years," which refers to a "state" (see notes 482, 487, 488, 493, 893). In this context, it refers to the state of union. 

What a "full state of union" between the Lord’s Divine and His Human (or His **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge.</note>, for the Human begins in the inmost part of the Rational, as seen in notes 2106 and 2194) actually means cannot be easily explained to the common understanding. However, it can be illustrated by what are called "full states" in a person being reformed and regenerated. 

It is well known that a person cannot be regenerated except in adult age, because that is when they first possess reason and judgment, and thus can receive good and truth from the Lord. Before a person reaches that state, they are prepared by the Lord through the planting of things that can serve as "soil" for receiving the seeds of truth and good. These include many states of innocence and charity, as well as knowledge of good and truth and the thoughts arising from them. This process occurs over many years before a person is regenerated. 

When a person is imbued with these things and thus prepared, their state is said to be "full," for then their internal faculties are disposed to receive. All those things given by the Lord before regeneration, and through which a person is regenerated, are called **Remnants** <note>original: "Reliquiae"</note>. In the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures.</note>, these are signified by the number ten (notes 576, 1738, 2284), and also by the number a hundred when the state of regeneration is full (note 1988). 

These examples illustrate what is signified by the "full state of union" of the Human with the Divine in the Lord. Specifically, it refers to when He—by His own power, through the battles and victories of temptations, and through the power of Divine wisdom and intelligence—acquired so much of the Divine in His Human (that is, in His Rational), that He could unite the Divine Itself to the Divine acquired in the Rational. To represent this state, it was arranged that Isaac would not be born to Abraham until he was a hundred years old, even though Abraham had stayed in the land of Canaan for many years. These are the secrets contained in the number of the "hundred years" belonging to Abraham.

That the number "one hundred" signifies what is full can also be established from other places in the Word, such as in Isaiah:
> "There shall no longer be an infant of days there, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child a hundred years old shall die, and the sinner a hundred years old shall be accursed" <term>Isaiah 65:20</term>.

In this passage, "a hundred" clearly stands for "full," for it mentions an infant and an old man who has "filled his days," and a child and a sinner of "a hundred years"—that is, when their state is full. 

Similarly in Matthew:
> "Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for my Name’s sake, shall receive a hundredfold <note>original: "Centuplum"</note>, and shall inherit eternal life" <term>Matthew 19:29; see also Mark 10:29-30</term>.

Here, "a hundredfold" stands for "full," or a "good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over" (Luke 6:38). 

In Luke:
> "Other seed fell upon good ground, and when it grew up, it produced fruit a hundredfold" <term>Luke 8:8; see also Matthew 13:8, 23; Mark 4:20</term>.

Here also, "a hundred" stands for what is full; this number would not have been used unless it carried that significance. It is similar when the Lord speaks in a parable about debtors, where one owed a hundred measures <note>original: "batos"</note> of oil, and another a hundred measures <note>original: "coros"</note> of wheat...

<header>GENESIS.</header>

...the Human <note>original: "Humanum"</note>, regarding which it is said that it "nurses children for Abraham," signifies that He implanted the Human into the Divine, and that the Human is from His own power. But these things can hardly be explained more clearly to the understanding; if more were said, the meaning would become even more obscure. For these are Divine matters which can only be presented before the angels through celestial and spiritual concepts. If they were presented to a human being in a more elevated style, they would fall into the material and bodily ideas that a person holds. Furthermore, it should be known that the quality of the Lord's Divine **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge.</note> when it was first born is described by these words: *“God has made me laugh; everyone who hears will laugh with me”*—and she said, *“Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children?”* For it was the ancient custom that when a child was born, a name was given that was significant of their state, and that the state would also be described at that time. Examples include when Cain was born to Eve and Adam (Genesis 4:1); when Seth was born to them (Genesis 4:25); when Noah was born to Lamech (Genesis 5:29); when Esau and Jacob were born to Isaac (Genesis 25:25, 26); when the twelve sons were born to Jacob (Genesis 29:32, 33, 34, 35; Chapter 30:6, 8, 11, 13, 18, 20, 24; Chapter 35:18); when Perez and Zerah were born to Tamar (Genesis 38:29, 30); when Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph (Genesis 41:51, 52); and when Gershom and Eliezer were born to Moses (Exodus 2:22; Chapter 18:4). What all these individuals represent, and what they signify in the **internal sense** <term>internal sense</term> <note>The deeper, spiritual meaning of the Bible hidden beneath the literal words.</note>, is involved in the description attached to the name that was given. So it is here with Isaac <note>original: "Jischak"</note>. What is involved is apparent to some extent from a summary explanation, but deeper secrets are still hidden, for these are Divine things that cannot be expressed by any forms or formulas of words.

2644. **Because I have borne a son in his old age**, which signifies that this would happen when the days were completed, is established from the explanation of almost the same words in Verse 2, concerning which see notes 2621, 2622, 2623, and 2624.

2645. **Verse 8. And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day that he weaned Isaac.**
"The child grew" signifies the further perfection of the Lord’s Rational. "And was weaned" signifies the separation of the merely human Rational. "Abraham made a great feast" signifies cohabitation <note>original: "cohabitatio," meaning a dwelling together or conjunction.</note> and union. "On the day that he weaned Isaac" signifies a state of separation.

2646. **The child grew**, which signifies the further perfection of the Lord’s Rational, is established from the meaning of "growing," which is "to be perfected," and from the meaning of "the born" or "the son," which is the Lord’s Divine Rational (concerning which, see note 2623).

2647. **And was weaned**, which signifies the separation of the merely human Rational, is established from the meaning of "being weaned," which is "to be separated," just as infants are from their mother's breasts. The fact that the merely human Rational was separated is further described in this chapter and is represented by the son of Hagar, who was cast out of the house.

2648. **Abraham made a great feast**, which signifies cohabitation and union, is established from the meaning of a "feast," which is "cohabitation" (as discussed in note 2341). Here it also signifies union, because the subject is the Lord, whose Human was united to the Divine and whose Divine was united to the Human. Because this union is the subject, it is called a "**great** feast."

# CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

2649. **On the day when he weaned Isaac**, <note>original: "In die cum ablactaret Jischakum"</note> signifies a state of separation. This is evident from the meaning of **day** as a "state" (as discussed in numbers 23, 487, 488, 493, 893) and from the meaning of **being weaned** as "being separated" (as discussed in number 2647). From the first verse of this chapter, the subject has been the **Uniting of the Divine Essence with the Human** <term>Human</term> <note>The "Human" refers to the Lord's manifestation or nature while on earth.</note> of the Lord, in this order:
* Concerning the presence of the Divine in the Human for the sake of union (Verse 1).
* Concerning the presence of the Human in the Divine, and thus concerning the reciprocal union (as discussed in number 2004, Verse 2).
* That from this union, the Human was made Divine (Verse 3).
* And that this happened successively and continuously while the Lord lived in the world (Verse 4).
* And that this began when the **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The faculty of the mind that mediates between spiritual truth and worldly knowledge.</note> state was such that it could receive it (Verse 5).
* A description of the state of union regarding its quality, including its secrets <note>original: "arcanis"</note> (Verses 6, 7).

Now follows the separation of the maternal human, which continues through Verse 12. This separation is signified in this verse by the weaning of Isaac, and in the following verses, it is represented by the son of Hagar being sent out from the house. Because the union of the Lord’s Divine with His Human, and of the Human with the Divine, is the very **Marriage of Good and Truth**, and from this comes the Heavenly Marriage (which is the same as the Kingdom of the Lord), a **great feast** is mentioned which Abraham made when he weaned Isaac. This feast signifies the first of the marriage, or the first union. If this feast had not signified a secret, just like the weaning did, it would never have been mentioned.

Since the text now proceeds to the separation of the earlier human nature which the Lord had from His mother, and finally to its complete removal <note>original: "exuitione"</note>, it should be known that the Lord successively and continuously—until the very end of His life when He was glorified—separated from Himself and cast off that which was merely human (namely, what He inherited from the mother). He did this until at last He was no longer her son, but the Son of God, both in respect to His conception and His birth, and thus was one with the Father and was Jehovah Himself. That He separated from Himself and cast off everything human from the mother, so that He was no longer her son, is clearly evident from the Lord's own words in John:
> "When the wine failed, the mother of Jesus said to Him, 'They have no wine.' Jesus said to her, ***'Woman, what does this have to do with Me and you?'***" (John 2:3, 4).

In Matthew:
> "Someone said, 'Look, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak with You.' But Jesus answering said to the one who had spoken, 'Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?' And stretching out His hand over His disciples, He said, 'Behold My mother and My brothers; for whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother, and sister, and mother'" (Matthew 12:47–49; Mark 3:32–35; Luke 8:20, 21).

In Luke:
> "A certain woman from the crowd, raising her voice, said to Him, 'Blessed is the womb that bore You, and the breasts which You sucked.' But Jesus said, 'Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it'" (Luke 11:27, 28).

When that woman spoke of His mother, the Lord spoke of those mentioned above—namely, "whoever does the will of My Father, he is My brother, sister, and mother"—which is the same as saying, "blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it." 

In John:
> "Jesus, seeing His mother and the disciple standing by whom He loved, said to His mother, ***'Woman, behold your son!'*** Then He said to the disciple, ***'Behold your mother!'*** Therefore from that hour the disciple took her into his own home" (John 19:26, 27).

From these words, it is clear that the Lord said this to her because she thought...

...when He saw her on the cross, He still did not call her "mother" but "woman," and He transferred the name of mother to those who are signified by the disciple, which is why He said to the disciple, "Behold your mother." This is even more evident from the Lord’s own words in Matthew: "Jesus asked the Pharisees, saying, 'What do you think of Christ? Whose son is He?' They said to Him, 'David's.' He said to them, 'How then does David in the spirit call Him Lord, saying, The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool? If then David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?' and no one could answer Him a word" (Matthew 22:39 to the end; Mark 12:35, 36, 37; Luke 20:42, 43, 44). Thus, He was no longer the son of David according to the flesh.

Furthermore, regarding the separation and the casting off <note>original: "exuitionem"</note> of the maternal human: those who have merely bodily ideas about the Lord’s **Human** <term>Human</term> <note>The "Human" refers to the Lord's physical and mental manifestation on earth, which the author argues was gradually replaced by a Divine nature.</note> do not understand this. They think of Him just as they would any other human being, and so they find these ideas scandalous. They do not know that a person's nature is defined by their life, and that the Divine Being <note>original: "Esse"</note> of life, which is **Jehovah**, was in the Lord from the moment of conception; and that a similar Divine Being of life existed in His Human through their union.

# 2650. **Verse 9. And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.**

**Sarah saw** signifies the Lord’s insight from the Divine Spiritual. **The son of Hagar the Egyptian** signifies the merely human **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The Rational is the faculty of the mind that connects spiritual truth with worldly information.</note>. **Hagar the Egyptian** is the affection for external knowledge <note>original: "scientiarum"</note>, from which that Rational was born, as if from a mother. **Whom she had borne to Abraham** signifies that it existed from the Divine Celestial as if from a father. **Mocking** signifies what is not in harmony with, or favorable toward, the Divine Rational.

# 2651. 

**And Sarah saw**, which signifies the Lord’s insight from the Divine Spiritual, is established by the meaning of **seeing**, which is to understand (see numbers 897, 2150, 2325). This is the same as perceiving with the mind's sight. This is also clear from the representation of **Sarah**, who signifies the Divine Spiritual or Divine Truth (see number 2622). "Sarah saw" means the Divine Spiritual perceived it, which is the same as saying the Lord perceived it from the Divine Spiritual.

# 2652. 

**The son of Hagar the Egyptian**, which signifies the merely human **Rational**, and that **Hagar the Egyptian** is the affection for external knowledge from which that Rational was born as if from a mother, is established by the meaning of the **son**—namely, Ishmael. He represents the first Rational that the Lord possessed (as discussed in Genesis 16, where Hagar and Ishmael are mentioned). This is also clear from the representation of Hagar the Egyptian as the mother. Regarding how the first or merely human Rational in the Lord was conceived from the Divine Celestial as a Father and born from the affection for external knowledge as a mother, see numbers 1895, 1896, 1902, 1910.

# 2653. 

**Whom she had borne to Abraham**, which signifies that it existed from the Divine Celestial as if from a father, is established by the meaning of **bearing** or giving birth, which means "to exist" (see numbers 2621, 2629). It is also shown by the representation of **Abraham**, who signifies the Divine Celestial (see numbers 1989, 2011, 2172, 2198, 2501). Regarding how that Rational existed from the Lord’s Divine Celestial as a father, see numbers 1895, 1896, 1902, 1910.

2654. **Mocking** <note>original: "Illudentem"</note> signifies that which is not in harmony with or favoring the **Divine Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The "Rational" refers to the reasoning part of the mind. The author distinguishes between the "human rational" (worldly logic) and the "Divine Rational" (perfected spiritual wisdom).</note>. This is evident from the meaning of "mocking," which involves an affection or feeling against something that does not suit or favor oneself. In the previous verse, it was stated that the son grew and was weaned, and that Abraham held a great feast when Isaac <note>original: "Jischakum"</note> was weaned. This signified that the Lord’s **Divine Rational** was being established, and the earlier **Rational** was being separated. 

Therefore, the text immediately follows with the mention of the son of Hagar the Egyptian. As shown in the explanation of Genesis Chapter 16 (where Ishmael and Hagar are discussed), this son represents that first, human way of reasoning. This shows that the internal meaning of the scripture follows a continuous sequence. 

Regarding the Lord's first **Rational** mind: because it was born just like any other person's—namely, through scientific facts and learned knowledge—it could not help but exist in "appearances of truth." These are things that seem true to us but are not true in themselves (as noted in sections 1911, 1936, 2196, 2203, 2209, and 2519). Because this mind operated in appearances, it could not agree with or favor truths that lack those appearances—that is, Divine truths. It could neither grasp them nor remain unopposed to them. 

Let some examples serve as illustration: 

*   The human **Rational**, which is formed by nature from worldly things through the senses and then from scientific data and knowledge, almost laughs at or mocks the idea that **humanity does not live from itself**. It seems to us as if we live entirely by our own power. In reality, a person lives more—that is, more wisely, intelligently, and happily—the less they believe they live from themselves. This is the life of the Angels, especially those who are "celestial" and closest to the Lord; they know that no one lives from themselves except Jehovah (the Lord) alone. 

*   That same **Rational** mind would also mock the idea that a person has no **Proprium** <term>Proprium</term> <note>A technical term meaning "one's own" or "selfhood"—the sense of being a self-contained individual independent of God.</note>, but rather that it is a fallacy or an appearance that they have any "selfhood" at all. It would mock even more if told that the more someone remains in the fallacy of selfhood, the less they actually possess, and vice versa. 

*   Similarly, it would mock the idea that whatever a person thinks or does from their "self" is actually evil (even if it appears good), and that a person does not become truly wise until they believe and perceive that all evil comes from hell and all good from the Lord. All Angels are in this faith and perception; as a result, they possess a far more abundant sense of self than anyone else, yet they know and perceive that it comes from the Lord, even though it appears entirely as their own. 

*   Furthermore, that **Rational** mind would mock if it were told that in heaven, the greatest are those who are the least; that the wisest are those who believe and perceive themselves to be the least wise; and that the happiest are those who desire others to be the most happy and themselves the least. It would mock the idea that "heaven" consists in wanting to be below everyone else, while "hell" consists in wanting to be above everyone. Consequently, in the glory of heaven, there is absolutely nothing of the glory of this world. 

*   In the same way, the **Rational** would mock if told that in the next life there is no space or time, but rather "states" <note>original: "status"</note> which create the appearance of space and time. It would mock the idea that life becomes more heavenly the further it is removed from space and time, and the closer it is to eternity—in which there is absolutely nothing of the idea of time, nor anything like it. 

The Lord saw that such things existed in the merely human **Rational**, and that this reasoning mind would therefore "mock" Divine things. He saw this from His Divine spiritual perspective, which is signified by...

...that Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian <note>original: "quod vidit Sarah filium Hagaris Ægyptiæ"</note> (refer to sections 2651, 2652). Experience shows that those who possess spiritual perception—and even those who have a conscience—are able to look from their inner self at the things within them that are "below" or more external. They can see deeply enough to even correct their own thoughts. From this ability, those who are being **regenerated** <term>regenerated</term> <note>Regeneration refers to the process of spiritual rebirth or being made new by God.</note> can see the nature of the **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The "Rational" is the reasoning part of the mind that sits between our spiritual and natural selves.</note> mind they had before they were reborn. In humans, this perception comes from the Lord; however, in the Lord’s own case, this perception came from His own Divine power.

2655. **Verse 10.** *And she said to Abraham, "Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac."* <note>original: "Et dixit Abrahamo, ejice ancillam hanc, & filium ejus, quia non hæreditabit filius ancillæ hujus cum filio meo, cum Jischako."</note> 
**She said to Abraham** signifies perception from the Divine. 
**Cast out this bondwoman and her son** signifies that things belonging to the merely human Rational mind were to be removed. 
**For the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac** signifies that the merely human Rational could not share a common life with the truly Divine Rational, whether in terms of truth or of good.

2656. **She said to Abraham** signifies perception from the Divine. This is clear from the meaning of "to say" in the historical parts of the Word, which signifies "to perceive" (as mentioned often before). It is also clear from the representation of **Abraham**, who represents the **Divine Celestial** or **Divine Good** (refer to section 2622).

2657. **Cast out this bondwoman and her son** signifies that things belonging to the merely human Rational were to be removed. This is clear from the meaning of "casting out," which is to remove or exterminate. It is also clear from the meaning of the **bondwoman** <note>original: "ancillæ"</note>, which represents the affection for rational thoughts and **scientifics** <term>scientifics</term> <note>In this context, "scientifics" refers to factual knowledge or data gathered through the five senses and worldly experience.</note>—essentially their "good" (refer to section 2567). The **son** represents the truth of that same Rational (refer to sections 264, 489, 533, 1147). However, these are only "apparent" good and truth, which are associated with this first, or merely human, Rational mind. This is why "casting out the bondwoman and her son" signifies removing things that are merely human in our reasoning.

To understand how this works—specifically, that the first Rational is removed when the Divine takes its place—it has been explained elsewhere, but since this section deals with it specifically, it should be explained briefly again. 

Every person who is being regenerated has two Rational minds: one before regeneration and another after. 

1. **The First Rational (Before Regeneration):** This is developed through the experiences of the senses, through reflecting on civil and moral life, through the sciences, and through the reasoning drawn from them. It also comes from spiritual knowledge gained from religious doctrine or the Word. However, at this stage, these thoughts do not rise much higher than the ideas in the physical memory, which are relatively "material." Therefore, whatever a person thinks at this stage comes from these sources. Such thoughts are presented to the inner or intellectual sight as comparisons or analogies to material things. This is the nature of the first Rational.

2. **The Second Rational (After Regeneration):** This is formed by the Lord through spiritual affections for truth and good. These affections are wonderfully implanted by the Lord into the truths of the earlier Rational. Through this, the things that are compatible and supportive are brought to life. Other things, being of no use, are separated from it. Eventually, spiritual goods and truths are gathered together as if in bundles. The incompatible things, which cannot be brought to spiritual life, are pushed away to the edges <note>original: "peripheriam"</note>. This happens gradually, as spiritual goods and truths...

It details the two stages of the rational mind: the first based on worldly experience and the second formed by the Lord during spiritual rebirth.</summary>

# CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

...the life of those affections grows; from this, it is clear what the second **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The reasoning part of the mind that connects the spiritual and natural selves.</note> is like. How these two relate can be illustrated by comparing them to the fruit of trees. The first Rational is, in the beginning, like immature fruit that gradually ripens until it forms seeds within itself. When it reaches the age where it begins to separate from the tree, its state is "full" (as mentioned above in section 2636).

However, the second Rational, which is given by the Lord when a person is **regenerated** <term>regenerated</term> <note>The process of being spiritually reborn or made new by God.</note>, is like that same fruit planted in good soil. In the soil, the parts surrounding the seeds decay, and the seeds push themselves out from their innermost core. They send out a root and then a shoot above the earth, which grows into a new tree. This tree unfolds until it eventually produces new fruits, and eventually gardens and paradises, according to the affections for good and truth it receives (see Matthew 13:31–32; John 12:24 <note>original: "Matth: XIII: 31. 32. Joh: XII: 24." — references to the parables of the mustard seed and the grain of wheat.</note>).

But because examples are more convincing, let us look at the **Proprium** <term>Proprium</term> <note>A technical term for one's "ownness" or the sense of self—what a person feels belongs to them as an individual.</note>—specifically, the Proprium a person has before regeneration and the Proprium they have after. From the first Rational, which a person has acquired by the means discussed above, the person believes that they think truth and do good from themselves (that is, from their own Proprium). This first Rational cannot grasp it any other way, even if the person is taught that all the good of love and all the truth of faith come from the Lord. 

Yet when they are regenerated—which happens in their adult age—they begin to think from the second Rational (given by the Lord) that good and truth are not from themselves or their Proprium, but from the Lord. Even so, they still do good and think truth *as if* it were from themselves (see sections 1937, 1947). The more they are confirmed in this, the more they are led into the light of truth about these things, until finally they believe that all good and all truth are from the Lord. At that point, the Proprium of the earlier Rational is gradually separated, and the person is gifted by the Lord with a "heavenly Proprium," which belongs to the new Rational.

To give another example: at first, the first Rational knows no other love than love of self and the world. Even if the person hears that heavenly love is entirely different, they still do not grasp it. Later, when they do something good, they feel no other delight in it than that they seem to deserve someone's favor, or that they are known as a Christian, or that they might obtain the joy of eternal life from it. 

The second Rational, however, which the Lord gives through regeneration, begins to feel a delight in the good and truth itself. The person is moved by this delight, not for any selfish reason, but for the sake of good and truth. When they are moved by this delight, they reject the idea of "earning merit," eventually recoiling from it as something monstrous <note>original: "enorme"</note>. In such a person, this delight gradually grows and becomes blessedness; in the next life, it becomes happiness and their very heaven. 

From this, it is now clear how it stands with both Rationals in a person who is being regenerated. But it should be known that in a human being, even when they are regenerated, every single part of the first Rational remains; they are simply separated from the second Rational by a miracle from the Lord. The Lord, however, completely cast out <note>original: "exterminavit"</note> His first Rational so that nothing of it remained. This is because the merely human and the Divine cannot exist together. Therefore, He was no longer the "son of Mary," but Jehovah in respect to both Essences <term>Essences</term> <note>The Divine and the Human natures of Jesus, which Swedenborg argues became one unified Divine Essence.</note>.

2658. **"Because the son of this handmaid shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac"** <note>original: "Quia non hæreditabit filius ancillæ hujus cum filio meo, cum Jifchako"</note> signifies that the purely human **Rational** <term>Rational</term> <note>The reasoning part of the mind that connects the spiritual and natural selves.</note> cannot share a common life with the **Divine Rational** itself, neither in regard to truth nor in regard to good. This is evident from:
1.  The meaning of **inheriting** <note>original: "hæreditare"</note>, which is to possess the life of another (to be discussed soon).
2.  The meaning of the **son of the handmaid**, which is the purely human Rational in regard to truth and good (see section 2657).
3.  The meaning of **my son, Isaac**, which is the Divine Rational in regard to truth (represented by "my son") and in regard to good (represented by "Isaac") (see sections 2623, 2630). 

That **Isaac** <note>original: "Jifchako"</note> represents the Divine Rational in regard to good is known from the meaning of "laughter," which is what he was named after. Laughter signifies the affection for truth, or the "good of truth" (see verses 6 and 7, sections 2640, 2641, 2643).

Therefore, the phrase means that the purely human Rational cannot share a common life with the Divine Rational. That they cannot share a common life is clear from this fact alone: the Divine is life itself and thus has life within itself; however, the purely human is merely an **organ** of life and thus does not have life in itself. 

When the Lord’s **Human** <term>Human</term> <note>The "Human" refers to the part of the Lord that lived on earth; Swedenborg teaches that the Lord made this part of Himself Divine.</note> was made Divine, it was no longer an organ or recipient of life, but became life itself, of the same nature as Jehovah Himself. From His very conception by Jehovah, He possessed this potential. This is clearly shown by the Lord’s own words in the Gospel of John: 
> "*For as the Father has life in Himself, so He has given to the Son to have life in Himself*" (John 5:26). 

The **Divine Human** is what is called the "Son" (see sections 1729, 2159, 2628). Other passages in John also confirm this: 
*   "*In Him was life, and the life was the light of men*" (John 1:4).
*   "*Jesus said, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life'* " (John 14:6).
*   "*Jesus said, 'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live'* " (John 11:25).
*   "*For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world*" (John 6:33).

On the other hand, a human being is not life, but only an organ or recipient of life (see section 2021). From this, it is evident that when the Lord became **Jehovah** even in His Human, that which was not life in itself—that is, the purely human part—had to be set aside. This is signified by the statement that the son of the handmaid could not inherit with the son Isaac.

In the internal sense, when **Inheriting** is said of the Lord, it means having the life of the Father, and thus having life in Himself. When it is said of humans, it means having the Lord's life, or receiving life from the Lord. Having life in oneself is the very **Being of life** <note>original: "Esse vitæ"</note>, which is Jehovah. However, to have the Lord's life or receive life from the Lord is to receive the Lord through love and faith. Because such people are "in the Lord" and "belong to the Lord," they are called His heirs and His sons.

In the Word of the Old Testament, **Inheritance** <note>original: "Hæreditas"</note> is used to describe both celestial things (good) and spiritual things (truth). Yet, one is expressed by a different word than the other. One word may be translated as **possessing by inheritance**, while the other is simply **inheriting**. The former word in the original language implies possession, while the latter implies a derivation from it, similar to how the celestial relates to the spiritual, or good to...
