And they returned... to Moses and Aaron and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of **Paran** at Kadesh, and brought back word to them and showed them the fruit of the land." <term>Numbers XIII: 1–3, 26</term> 

The fact that they set out from the wilderness of Paran to scout the land of Canaan signifies that through the Lord’s **Divine Human**, the "children of Israel" (meaning spiritual people) are granted access to the heavenly Kingdom (signified by the "land of Canaan"). However, the fact that they failed in their mission at that time signifies their own inherent weakness. It shows that the Lord alone would fulfill everything required by the Law, endure all temptations, and emerge victorious. In this way, salvation is made possible for those who live in the faith of charity, as well as for those undergoing temptations in which the Lord conquers...

<header>GENESIS.</header>

Salvation comes from His **Divine Human** <note>original: *Divino Humano*</note>; for this reason, when the Lord was tempted, He was in the wilderness (Matthew 4:1; Mark 1:12–13; Luke 4:1; see above, no. 2708).

2715. There are two secrets <note>original: *arcana*</note> here: first, that the "good" <term>the inner motivation for doing what is right</term> of a spiritual person is relatively obscure; and second, that this obscurity is enlightened by the Lord’s Divine Human. 

Regarding the first point—that the good in a spiritual person is relatively obscure—this is evident from what was said above (no. 2708) concerning the state of the spiritual person compared to the state of the celestial person. This becomes clearly visible when comparing the two states. Among **celestial** people, "good" itself is implanted in their **will** <term>the voluntary part of the mind</term>, and from there, light enters their **intellect** <term>the intellectual part</term>. However, among **spiritual** people, the entire will is lost or destroyed, so that they have no inherent good from it. Therefore, the Lord implants "good" into their intellectual part (see nos. 863, 875, 895, 927, 928, 1023, 1043, 1044, 2124, 2256). 

The will is what primarily lives within a person, and the intellect derives its life from it. Since the will in a spiritual person is so corrupted that it consists of nothing but evil—and yet evil constantly and continually flows from it into the intellectual part or the person's thoughts—it is clear that the "good" there is relatively obscured. 

Because of this, spiritual people do not have love for the Lord in the same way celestial people do; consequently, they lack that true humility which is essential in all worship and through which good can flow from the Lord. A proud heart never receives, but a humble heart does. Spiritual people also do not have love toward their neighbor in the same way as celestial people, because love of self and love of the world continually flow from their will and obscure the good of that neighborly love. 

Anyone can see this by reflecting on their own actions: when someone does a good deed, it is often for some purpose in the world. Even if it is not obvious, they still think about a reward—either from the people they help or from the Lord in the afterlife. Thus, their "good" is still defiled by a desire for **merit** <note>original: *meritorio*; the belief that one deserves a reward for good works</note>. Furthermore, when they have done something good, if they can remember it and thereby prefer themselves over others, they find delight in it. In contrast, celestial people love their neighbor more than themselves; they never think of a reward, nor do they prefer themselves to others in any way. 

Furthermore, "good" among spiritual people is obscured by various **persuasive beliefs** <term>strongly held personal convictions</term> originating from self-love and love of the world, such as the persuasiveness of "faith alone" (see no. 2682, 2689). This also results from the influence of evil from their will. 

Additionally, it is evident that good in a spiritual person is relatively obscure because they do not know what is true through any direct **perception** <term>an intuitive inner sense of truth</term> like the celestials do. Instead, they learn from the instructions of parents and teachers, and from the doctrine into which they were born. When they add something of their own through their own reasoning, then most often the **sensory level** and its **fallacies** <note>original: *fallaciæ*</note>, as well as the **rational level** and its **appearances**, prevail. This makes it so they can hardly acknowledge any pure truth, such as the celestials acknowledge. Nevertheless, the Lord implants "good" into these "quasi-truths," even if they are fallacious or merely appearances of truth. However, the resulting good is obscure, characterized by the quality of the truths with which it is joined. This situation is like...

<header># CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE <note>original: CAPUT VIGESIMUM PRIMUM</note></header>

Just as the light of the sun flowing into objects is modified by the quality of the objects that receive it—appearing as a beautiful color if the object’s form is proper and corresponding, but as an ugly color if the form is improper and non-corresponding—so "good" <term>the inner motivation toward kindness</term> is qualified according to "truth" <term>the conceptual understanding of what is right</term>.

This is also evident from the fact that a **Spiritual person** does not truly know what is evil. He hardly believes anything to be evil except what goes against the commandments of the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>. He is unaware of the countless evils of affection and thought; he does not reflect upon them, nor does he call them evil. He views the various pleasures of his desires and appetites as nothing other than "good." Indeed, he pursues, approves of, and excuses the delights of self-love, being ignorant that such things affect his spirit and that he will become exactly like them in the next life.

Similarly, it is clear that even though almost the entire Word <note>The Bible</note> deals with the "good" of love toward the Lord and love toward one's neighbor, the Spiritual person still does not know that "good" is the essence of faith. He does not even know what love and charity are in their true essence. What he does know about faith—which he considers the essential thing—he continues to argue about, questioning whether it is actually true, unless he has been confirmed in it by a long life of practice.

**Celestial people**, however, never do this; they know and perceive that a thing is true. This is why the Lord said in Matthew: *"Let your word be 'yes, yes' and 'no, no'; whatever is more than these comes from evil"* (5:37). For celestial people are in the truth itself, while spiritual people argue about whether a thing is so. Because celestial people are in the truth itself, they can see infinite things belonging to that truth as if by the light of the whole of heaven. But because spiritual people argue about whether it is so, they cannot even reach the first threshold of the light seen by celestial people, much less view anything from that light.

2716. Regarding the second point—namely, that the obscurity among the Spiritual is enlightened by the **Lord's Divine Human** <note>original: *Divino Humano Domini*</note>—this is a secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> that cannot be fully explained to the human understanding, for it describes the "Divine influx" <term>the way God’s influence flows into the soul</term>. One can only form an idea of it by considering this: if the Supreme Divine itself flowed into a "good" such as that described—defiled by so many evils and falsities—it could not be received. If anything were received, the person would feel infernal torment and would perish. However, the Lord’s Divine Human can flow into these people and illuminate such "good," just as the sun illuminates thick clouds that are transformed at daybreak into the face of the dawn. Even so, the Lord cannot appear to them as the light of the sun, but rather as the light of the moon. From this, it is clear that the reason for the Lord's coming into the world was for the sake of the Spiritual, so that they might be saved (see no. 2661).

2717. **And his mother took for him**, which signifies the "affection for truth." This is evident from the signification of "mother" as the Church (see no. 289). Since the spiritual Church (represented here) exists within the affection for truth, and derives its status as a Church from that affection, "mother" here signifies that affection.

2718. **A wife from the land of Egypt**, which signifies the affection for scientific knowledge <note>original: *affectionem fcientiarum*; in this context, "scientifics" refers to factual knowledge and external learning</note> which belongs to the man of the Spiritual Church. <meta>This page continues the comparison between the "spiritual person" and the "celestial person." It explains how the spiritual person’s understanding of "good" is rooted in the intellect and factual knowledge, whereas the celestial person perceives "good" directly through their will and affection.</meta>

<language>Latin</language>
<page-type>text</page-type>
<page-num>54</page-num>
<header>GENESIS.</header>

...concerning what knowledge is, regarding entries 1164, 1165, 1186, and 1462. In this verse, the person of the **Spiritual Church** is described—specifically what they are like regarding "good," which is the very essence of their life. For such a person, "good" is obscure, yet it is illuminated by the **Lord's Divine Human**. From this illumination, an **affection for truth** <term>a deep desire to learn and follow what is right</term> arises in their rational mind, and an **affection for scientific knowledge** <term>original: "affectio scientiarum"; a desire for facts and information</term> arises in their natural mind. 

In a **Spiritual person**, a direct affection for "good" (like that found in a **Celestial person**) cannot exist. Instead, they have an affection for truth. The reason for this is that "good" is implanted in their intellectual part <term>the logical mind</term> and is relatively obscure, as shown in entry 2715. Therefore, the only affection that can be produced and derived in their rational mind is the affection for truth, which then leads to an affection for factual knowledge in the natural mind. 

By "truth," we do not mean absolute truth, but rather whatever that person *believes* to be true, even if it is not actually true in itself. By "scientific knowledge," we do not mean the academic sciences of the learned, but every bit of factual information <term>original: "scientificum"</term> that can be gathered through experience and hearing—whether from civic life, religious doctrine, or the Word <note>The Bible</note>. The person of the Spiritual Church lives within the affection for these things.

To understand the difference between being in an **affection for truth** and an **affection for good**, a few points should be made. Those in the affection for truth think, inquire, and argue: "Is this true? Is it really so?" Even when they are convinced it is true, they continue to ask: "What is it?" Thus, they remain stuck at the first threshold; they cannot be admitted into wisdom until they are beyond all doubt. 

However, those who are in the **affection for good** know and perceive that a thing is so directly from the "good" within them. They do not wait at the threshold but are already in the inner room, having been admitted to wisdom. 

Take this for an example: *it is a celestial thing to think and act from an affection for good, or from "good" itself.* 
* Those in the **affection for truth** argue whether this is so, whether it is even possible, and what it actually means. As long as they harbor these doubts, they cannot enter into that state. 
* Those in the **affection for good**, however, do not argue or doubt; they say, "It is so." Therefore, they are allowed to enter. 

Those in the affection for good (the **Celestial**) begin exactly where those in the affection for truth (the **Spiritual**) stop. The final boundary of the spiritual person is the starting point for the celestial. Because of this, the celestial are granted to know, recognize, and perceive that the varieties of "good" are countless—as many as there are societies in heaven. They see that the Lord has joined all these together into a **heavenly form** <note>original: "formam cœlestem"</note> so that they constitute, as it were, a single person. They are even able to distinguish the specific category and type of every affection through their perception.

Or take this example: *all delight, blessedness, and happiness come solely from love.* However, the quality of the joy depends entirely on the quality of the love. 
* The **spiritual person** keeps his mind focused on "Is this true?" or "Does joy come from somewhere else—like conversation, study, or learning?" Or perhaps "Does it come from possessions, honor, reputation, or glory?" He fails to confirm for himself that these things are nothing on their own, and that only the affection of love matters. 
* The **celestial person**, however, does not get stuck in these preliminary questions. He says, "It is so." Therefore, he lives in the very goal and use of love—that is, in the affections themselves. These affections are countless, containing within them things beyond words, and they provide an eternal variation of delight, blessedness, and happiness.

Take another example: *that the neighbor is to be loved* <note>original: "proximus amandus"</note>...

<header>CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE</header>

...one is to be loved for the "good" that is within them. Those who are in an affection for truth think, inquire, and argue whether something is true, or whether it is so; they ask what the neighbor is and what "good" is, but go no further. Because of this, they close the door to wisdom for themselves. However, those who are in an affection for good say that "it is so." Therefore, they do not close the door, but enter in; they know, recognize, and perceive from "good" who is the neighbor above another, and even in what degree they stand. They know that everyone is unique. These things are inexpressible <note>original: "ineffabilia"</note> to those who are only in an affection for truth. 

Furthermore, consider this example: one who loves their neighbor from "good" also loves the Lord. Those in an affection for truth inquire whether this is so. If they are told that whoever loves their neighbor from "good" loves "good" itself—and because all "good" is from the Lord and the Lord is in "good," when someone loves "good," they also love Him from whom it comes and in whom He resides—they still inquire whether this is so. They also ask what "good" is, and whether the Lord is in "good" more than He is in "truth." As long as they remain stuck in such questions, they cannot see wisdom even from a distance. But those who are in an affection for good know that it is so from their own perception; they see the state of wisdom as a field leading all the way to the Lord. 

From this, it can be seen why things are obscure to those in an affection for truth (that is, the **Spiritual**) relative to those in an affection for good (that is, the **Celestial**). Yet, the Spiritual can still come out of the dark and into the light, provided they are willing to be in an "affirmative state"—acknowledging that all "good" belongs to love for the Lord and charity toward the neighbor, and that love and charity are the spiritual connection <note>original: "conjunctio spiritualis"</note> that brings all blessedness and happiness. Thus, in the "good" of love from the Lord, there is heavenly life, but not in the "truth" of faith when it is separated from that love.

2719. In this chapter, we first dealt with the Lord’s **Rational** <term>the logical, reasoning part of the mind</term>, which was made Divine and is represented by **Isaac** <note>original: "Jischakus"</note>. We also dealt with the purely human Rational, which was separated and is represented by the son of **Hagar** the Egyptian. Next, we discussed the **Spiritual Church**, which was saved through the Lord’s Divine Human; this Church is represented by Hagar and her child. 

Now, we deal with the **doctrine of faith** that will serve that Church—specifically, that human rational concepts based on scientific knowledge <term>original: "scientificis"; factual or experimental information</term> are joined to it. These are represented by **Abimelech** and **Phicol**. This joining is signified by the covenant that **Abraham** made with them. Those rational concepts are "appearances" <note>truths adapted to human understanding</note> that do not have a Divine origin, but a human one. They are joined to the doctrine because the Spiritual Church could not comprehend or receive doctrine without them. 

As shown in entry 2715, the person of the Spiritual Church is in relative obscurity. Therefore, their doctrine must be clothed in such "appearances" that belong to human thought and affection. These are not so different from the truth that Divine "good" cannot reside there as if in a container. Because Abimelech and the covenant are discussed again in Chapter 26 (this time regarding **Isaac**), where the internal sense deals with rational and scientific concepts being added to the doctrine of faith a second time, it is enough here to explain these matters in summary. They will become clearer in the explanation of Chapter 26.

**Verse 22.** *And it happened at that time, that Abimelech and Phicol, the chief captain of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying: "God is with you in everything you do."*

**Verse 23.** *Now therefore, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my grandson; but according to the kindness that I have shown to you, you shall do to me and to the land where you have lived as a stranger.*

**Verse 25.** *Then Abraham reproved Abimelech because of a well of water which Abimelech’s servants had seized.*

**Verse 28.** *And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.*

**Verse 29.** *And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?"*

**"It happened at that time"** signifies the state in which the Lord's Divine Rational <note>original: "Rationale Divinum"; in this context, it refers to the bridge between the human mind and the divine.</note> was made. **"And Abimelech and Phicol, the chief captain of his army, spoke to Abraham"** signifies that human rational concepts derived from scientific knowledge <note>original: "scientificis"; refers to outward facts and sensory information</note> are to be joined to the Doctrine of Faith, which is Divine in itself. **"Saying, 'God is with you in everything you do'"** signifies that the Divine is present in all things, both generally and specifically.

**"Now therefore, swear to me here by God"** signifies a confirmation or affirmation. **"That you will not deal falsely with me"** signifies a state beyond doubt. **"With my son, and with my grandson"** signifies those things which belong to faith. **"According to the kindness I have shown to you"** signifies the rational concepts with which the Lord was previously instructed. **"You shall do to me and to the land where you have lived as a stranger"** signifies a reciprocal relationship.

**"And Abraham said, 'I will swear'"** signifies a complete affirmation. **"And Abraham reproved Abimelech"** signifies the Lord's indignation. **"Because of a well of water which Abimelech’s servants had seized"** signifies the doctrine of faith, and that scientific knowledge <note>original: "scientifica"</note> wished to claim that doctrine for itself. **"And Abimelech said"** signifies a response. **"I do not know who has done this thing"** signifies that the rational mind dictated something else. **"You did not tell me"** signifies that it was not recognized as being from the Divine. **"Nor did I hear of it until today"** signifies that this was only now discovered.

**"And Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech"** signifies Divine goods implanted in the rational doctrines represented by Abimelech. **"And the two of them made a covenant"** signifies a resulting union or conjunction. **"And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves"** signifies the holiness of innocence. **"And Abimelech said to Abraham, 'What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?'"** signifies a desire to be instructed and to acknowledge their purpose.

**"And he said, 'You will take these seven ewe lambs from my hand'"** signifies the holiness of innocence proceeding from the Divine. **"That they may be a witness for me"** signifies certainty. **"That I dug this well"** signifies that the doctrine is from the Divine. **"Therefore he called that place Beersheba"** signifies the state and quality of the doctrine. **"Because there the two of them swore an oath"** signifies that this arises from their union. **"Thus they made a covenant at Beersheba"** signifies that human rational things were joined to the doctrine of faith; and...

### 2721. **Verse 33. And he planted a grove in Beersheba; and there he called upon the Name of the God of eternity.**
"He planted a grove in Beersheba" signifies doctrine with its scientific knowledges <term>knowledges: specifically 'cognitiones,' or the spiritual facts and data that form the basis of faith</term> and its specific quality. "And he called upon the Name of the God of eternity" signifies worship resulting from that doctrine.

### 2722.
"He planted a grove in Beersheba" signifies doctrine from that source, along with its knowledges and its quality. This is evident from the meaning of a "grove" and the meaning of "Beersheba." Regarding groves: in the Ancient Church <note>The "Ancient Church" refers to the era of spiritual history following the Flood, characterized by a focus on charity and symbolic worship.</note>, holy worship was conducted on mountains and in groves. They worshiped on mountains because mountains signified the "celestial" aspects of worship <note>In this context, 'celestial' refers to things belonging to love and the will.</note>. They worshiped in groves because groves signified the "spiritual" aspects of worship. 

As long as that Church—namely, the Ancient Church—remained in its simplicity, their worship on mountains and in groves was holy. The reason for this was that celestial things, which belong to love and charity, were represented by high and lofty places like mountains and hills. Meanwhile, the spiritual things flowing from them were represented by fruitful and leafy things, such as gardens and groves. 

However, after these representative and meaningful symbols began to be used for idolatry—because people started to worship the external objects without the internal meaning—that holy worship became profane. For this reason, it was forbidden for them to have worship on mountains and in groves.

That the ancients held holy worship on mountains can be seen from Genesis chapter 12 regarding Abraham: "He moved from there to a *mountain* on the east of Bethel, and pitched his tent... and there he built an altar and called upon the Name of Jehovah" (Verse 8; see numbers 1449 to 1455). This is also clear from the meaning of a "mountain" as something celestial, belonging to love (numbers 795, 796, 1430). 

That they also held holy worship in groves is clear from the words in this verse: "**Abraham planted a grove in Beersheba, and there he called upon the Name of the God of eternity**." It is also evident from the meaning of a "garden" as intelligence (numbers 100, 108, 1588) and of "trees" as perceptions (numbers 103, 2163). 

The fact that this was later forbidden is clear from the following passages in the writings of Moses: "You shall not plant for yourself a *grove of any kind of tree* near the Altar of Jehovah your God, which you shall make for yourself; and you shall not set up a sacred pillar, which Jehovah your God hates" (Deuteronomy 16:21–22). And again: "You shall destroy the altars of the nations, break their pillars, and cut down their *groves*" (Exodus 34:13); and "that they should burn the groves with fire" (Deuteronomy 12:3). 

Because the Jews and Israelites—among whom the representative rituals of the Ancient Church were introduced—focused only on external things and were at heart nothing but idolaters, they did not know (nor did they want to know) what was "internal," what life after death was, or that the Messiah’s Kingdom was a heavenly one. Consequently, whenever they were left to their own devices, they practiced profane worship on mountains and hills, as well as in groves and forests. They even built "high places" for themselves instead of mountains and hills, and crafted carved images of groves instead of real ones, as can be seen in many places in the Word. For example, in the Book of Judges: "The children of Israel served the Baals and the *groves*" (3:7). In the Book of Kings: "Israel made *groves* to provoke Jehovah" (1 Kings 14).

...1 Kings 14:15 <note>The text likely refers to the surrounding context of 1 Kings 14:15, which discusses Israel being uprooted for making groves</note>; and elsewhere, "Judah built for themselves **High Places** <note>original: *Excelſa*, referring to elevated sites for sacrificial worship</note>, and statues, and **Groves**, upon every high hill, and under every leafy tree" (1 Kings 14:23). That these were destroyed by King Josiah is shown in the same book: "Josiah had all the vessels made for Baal and the **Grove**, and for the sun and moon, and for all the host of heaven, brought out of the Temple of Jehovah; and he burned them outside Jerusalem... he also cut down the **Groves** which Solomon had made, and also the **Grove** in Bethel which Jeroboam had made" (2 Kings 23:4, 6, 7, 14, 15).

These points are further confirmed in the Prophets. In Isaiah: "Inflaming yourselves with gods under every **leafy tree**; slaughtering children in the rivers under the overhangs of the rocks; even to the rivers you have poured out a drink offering, you have offered a gift; on a high and lofty mountain you placed your dwelling, and there you went up to offer a sacrifice" (Isaiah 57:5-7). In the same prophet: "In that day a man shall look to his Maker, and his eyes shall see the Holy One of Israel; and he shall not look to the altars, the work of his hands, and he will not see what his fingers have made, neither the **Groves** nor the solar statues" (Isaiah 17:7-8).

In Ezekiel: "That they may be pierced through in the midst of their idols, around their altars at every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, and under every leafy tree, and under every tangled oak—the place where they gave a sweet-smelling aroma <note>original: *odorem quietis*, literally 'an odor of rest'</note> to all their idols" (Ezekiel 6:13). 

From these passages, the origin of idolatrous <note>original: *idololatricus*</note> worship is now clear: it arose because objects that were meant to be representatives and symbols <note>original: *repræſentantia & ſignificantia*</note> began to be worshiped themselves. The "Most Ancient" people who lived before the flood saw something representative of the Lord’s Kingdom in every single thing—in mountains, hills, plains, valleys, gardens, groves, and forests; in rivers and waters; in fields and seeds; in trees of every kind; in animals of every kind; and in the lights of heaven. However, they never let their eyes—much less their minds—get stuck on the objects themselves. Instead, these things were to them the means of thinking about the heavenly and spiritual things in the Lord’s Kingdom. This was true to such an extent that there was absolutely nothing in the entire world of nature that did not serve them as a means. In reality, it is still true that every single thing in nature represents something spiritual—a secret <note>original: *arcanum*</note> which is today hardly believed by anyone. But...

### CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

After the celestial state—which is love for the Lord—perished, the human race was no longer in a condition to see the celestial and spiritual things of the Lord’s Kingdom through worldly objects as mediums. However, the people of the **Ancient Church** after the Flood still knew from traditions and the collections of certain individuals that these objects signified spiritual things. Because these objects held such meaning, they considered them holy. This was the origin of the "representative" worship of the Ancient Church. 

Because this Church was "spiritual" <note>The author distinguishes between the "Celestial Church" (who had direct intuitive perception) and the "Spiritual Church" (who learned through doctrine and intellect)</note>, its people did not have an internal perception <note>original: *perceptione*; an intuitive, heart-based understanding of truth</note> that things were so, but rather a knowledge <note>original: *cognitione*; factual or learned information</note> of it. Indeed, they were in a state of relative obscurity (as mentioned in entry no. 2715). Nevertheless, they did not worship external objects themselves; rather, through these externals, they were reminded of internal truths. Thus, when they engaged in those representative and meaningful rituals, they were in a state of holy worship. They were able to do this because they possessed spiritual love—that is, **charity**—which they made the essential part of their worship. Therefore, holiness from the Lord could flow into their worship. 

But when the state of the human race was changed and became so perverse that they distanced themselves from the good of charity, they no longer believed in a heavenly Kingdom or a life after death. They began to think they were in the same state as animals, except for the fact that they could think—much like many people do today. At that point, holy representative worship turned into **idolatry**, and the external objects themselves were worshiped. Consequently, among many gentiles of that time, as well as among the Jews and Israelites, worship was not "representative," but was rather a worship *of* representations and symbols—that is, of external things without any internal meaning.

Regarding **Groves** <note>original: *Lucos*; clusters of trees used as places of worship</note> specifically: among the ancients, these had various meanings depending on the species of trees found there. 
*   **Groves of olive trees** signified the celestial aspects of worship.
*   **Groves of vines** signified the spiritual aspects.
*   **Groves of fig trees, cedars, firs, poplars, or oaks** signified various other aspects of celestial and spiritual things.

In this specific passage, a "Grove" or "arboretum" is mentioned simply, and it signifies those things belonging to the **rational mind** <note>original: *rationalium*</note> which are joined to doctrine and its various types of knowledge. In general, trees signify perceptions (see nos. 103, 2163), but when they are discussed in the context of the Spiritual Church, they signify knowledge. This is because a person of the Spiritual Church has no perceptions other than those which come through the knowledge of doctrine or the Word. These pieces of knowledge become part of their faith and thus their conscience, from which their perception arises.

2723. Regarding **Beersheba**, it signifies the state and quality of doctrine—specifically, that it is Divine doctrine to which human rational concepts have been joined. This is evident from the sequence of events discussed from verse 22 to this one (nos. 2613, 2614), and also from the meaning of the word itself in the original language [Hebrew], which is **"the well of the oath"** and **"seven."** 
*   A **well** signifies the doctrine of faith (see nos. 2702, 2720).
*   An **oath** signifies a conjunction <note>original: *conjunctio*; a spiritual joining or connection</note> (no. 2720), as does a covenant made by an oath (nos. 1996, 2003, 2021, 2037).
*   **Seven** signifies what is holy, and thus what is Divine (nos. 395, 433, 716, 881).

From these points, it is clear that Beersheba signifies Doctrine which is Divine in itself, but with rational additions or "human appearances" attached to it. That this is the meaning of Beersheba is evident from the words of Abraham: 

> "Abraham said: 'Because you will receive **seven** ewe lambs from my hand, let it be a testimony to me that I dug this **well**.' Therefore he called that place **Beersheba**, because they both **swore an oath** there; and they made a covenant in Beersheba." (Genesis 21:30, 31, 32)

**2724.** **And he called there on the Name of the Eternal God.** That this signifies worship from that state is evident from the meaning of "calling on the Name of God," which refers to worship (as discussed in entry 440). Those who belonged to the **Ancient Church** did not understand a literal "name" when they saw that word, but rather the "quality" or "nature" of the thing <note>original: *omne quale*; see entries 144, 145, 440, 768, 1754, 1896, 2009</note>. Thus, by the "Name of God," they understood everything in one complex through which God was worshiped—namely, everything of love and faith. 

However, when the internal aspect of worship perished and only the external remained, people began to perceive nothing by the "Name of God" except the name itself. This reached such an extent that they worshiped the name itself, caring nothing for the love or faith from which worship should spring. Because of this, nations began to distinguish themselves by the names of their gods. The Jews and Israelites preferred themselves over others because they worshiped "Jehovah," placing the essential part of worship in the naming and invoking of that name. Yet, the worship of a name alone is no worship at all; it can even be found among the worst of people, who only profane the name further by using it. But because the "Name of God" signifies everything of worship—that is, everything of love and faith—it is clear what is meant by the phrase **"Hallowed be Thy Name"** in the Lord's Prayer (Matthew **6**:9) and by...

### CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE.

These are the things which the Lord said: **"You will be hated by everyone because of my name"** (Matthew 10:22). **"If two agree on earth in my name about anything they ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven; for where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in the midst of them"** (Matthew 18:19–20). **"Whoever leaves houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life"** (Matthew 19:29). **"Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"** (Matthew 21:9). **"Jesus said, 'You will not see me from now on until you say, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord"'"** (Matthew 23:39). **"You will be hated by all nations because of my name; and then many will be offended, and will betray one another, and will hate one another, and all these things because of my name"** (Matthew 24:9–10). **"As many as received Him, to them He gave the power to be children of God, to those who believe in His name"** (John 1:12). **"He who does not believe is already judged, because he did not believe in the name of the only begotten Son of God"** (John 3:18). <note>original: "Qui non credit, jam judicatus est..." (He who does not believe is already judged...)</note> **"Jesus said, 'Whatever you ask in my name, I will do it'"** (John 14:13–14; see also Chapter 15:16; Chapter 16:23, 24, 26, 27). **"Jesus said, 'I have manifested your name to the people'"** (John 17:6). **"Holy Father, keep them in your name, those whom you gave me, that they may be one as we are"** (John 17:11–12). **"I have made your name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them"** (John 17:26). **"That you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in His name"** (John 20:31). 

In addition to these, there are many places in the Old Testament where the "Name of Jehovah" or the "Name of God" does not literally mean a name, but rather everything associated with love and faith from which worship originates. For those who worship the name alone, without love and faith, it is said in Matthew: **"Many will say to me in that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name perform many miracles?' But I will confess to them, 'I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of iniquity'"** (Matthew 7:22–23).

When, as previously stated, the person of the Church changed from being <term>Internal</term> <note>focused on spiritual essence and inner love</note> to being <term>External</term> <note>focused on outward ritual and literalism</note>, and began to place worship in the name alone, they no longer acknowledged one God, but many. It was a custom among the <term>Ancient Church</term> <note>original: *Antiqua Ecclesia*; a term used to describe the era of spiritual history characterized by symbolic or representative worship</note> to add something to the Name of Jehovah to help them remember a specific blessing or <term>Attribute</term> <note>original: *Attributi*; a specific quality or characteristic of God</note> of His. 

For instance, here it says: **"He called upon the name of the God of eternity."** In the following chapter (22), **"Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-Jireh, that is, 'He will see'"** (verse 14). **"Moses built an altar and called its name Jehovah-Nissi, that is, 'my banner'"** (Exodus 17:15). **"Gideon built an altar to Jehovah and called it Jehovah-Shalom, that is, 'of peace'"** (Judges 6:24), among others. 

Because of this practice, those who placed worship in the name alone began to acknowledge as many gods as there were names. This is also how the Gentiles—especially in Greece and Rome—came to acknowledge and worship so many different gods. Yet, the Ancient Church from which those titles originally came never worshiped anything other than the one God under those many names. They did this because they understood the "name" to represent His *quality* or character <note>original: "per Nomen intellexit quale"</note>.

<summary>This page explains that the "Name of God" in the Bible signifies the inner quality of faith and love rather than a literal label. It further details how the loss of this internal understanding led to the rise of polytheism in ancient cultures as people began to mistake God's various descriptive titles for separate deities.</summary>

2725. Verse 34: **"And Abraham stayed as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days."** <note>original: "Et peregrinatus est Abraham in terra Philistaeorum diebus multis."</note> This means that the Lord added many things to the Doctrine of Faith from the scientific knowledge of human facts. <term>scientific knowledge</term> <note>original: "scientia cognitionum." In this context, it refers to the basic facts and information gathered through the human senses and reason.</note>

2726. The fact that Abraham staying as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days signifies that the Lord added many things to the Doctrine of Faith from the scientific knowledge of human facts is established by several points:
* From the meaning of "staying as a foreigner," which is to be instructed (see numbers 1463, 2025).
* From the representation of Abraham, who represents the Lord (see numbers 1965, 1989, 2011, 2501).
* From the meaning of "the land of the Philistines" or "Philistia," which signifies the scientific knowledge of facts (see numbers 1197, 1198).
* And from the meaning of "days," which signifies the state of the matter being discussed (see numbers 23, 487, 488, 493, 893). In this case, because the subject is knowledge derived from scientific and rational facts, and the text says "many days," it signifies a great many things. 

From Verse 22 until now, the text has dealt with rational concepts derived from human scientific knowledge being added to the Doctrine of Faith, as is clear from the explanation; this is their conclusion. Regarding the matter itself, because it is quite profound in nature, and because the same topic is discussed at length in the following chapter (26), further explanation is postponed until then.

***

### ->On Marriages, how they are viewed in heaven, and on Adulteries.<-

2727. Few people today know what genuine **Marriage (Conjugial) Love** <note>original: "Amor conjugialis." This refers to a deep, spiritual union between partners that goes beyond physical attraction.</note> is, or where it originates. The reason for this is that few people actually live within it. Almost everyone believes it is innate and simply flows from what they call a "natural instinct." They believe this even more because a form of "marriage" exists among animals. However, there is as great a difference between marriage love in humans and the mating habits of animals as there is between the state of a human being and the state of a wild beast.

2728. Because few people today know what genuine marriage love is, it will be described here based on things that have been revealed. **Marriage Love** finds its origin in the **Divine Marriage of Good and Truth**, and thus from the Lord Himself. It is not apparent to the physical senses or the common understanding that marriage love comes from this source, but it can still be proven through "influx" and "correspondence," as well as from the Word. 
* **By Influx:** Heaven is compared to a marriage and is called a "Marriage" because of the union of good and truth which flows in from the Lord. 
* **By Correspondence:** When Good united to Truth flows down into a lower sphere, it presents itself as a union of minds; when it flows into an even lower sphere, it presents itself as marriage. Therefore, the union of minds resulting from good being united to truth by the Lord is the very essence of **Marriage Love**.

2729. That genuine **marriage love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis." This specific term refers to a spiritual, divinely-inspired love between spouses that transcends mere physical attraction.</note> exists can be established by the fact that no one can experience it unless they are grounded in the **good of truth** and the **truth of good** from the Lord. <note>In this theology, "good of truth" refers to doing good because one's faith dictates it, while "truth of good" refers to the wisdom that flows from a heart motivated by love.</note> It is also evident because heavenly joy and happiness are found within that love; all who possess it enter heaven, or what is called the **Heavenly Marriage**. Furthermore, when angels speak about the union of good and truth, a symbolic representation of marriage appears among the good spirits in the lower realms. However, among evil spirits, a representation of adultery appears. This is why in the Word <note>The Bible</note>, the union of good and truth is called a "marriage," while the corruption of good and the falsification of truth are called "adultery" and "sexual immorality" (see number 2466).

2730. The people of the **Most Ancient Church** lived in genuine marriage love more than any others on this Earth. Because they were "celestial"—living from a state of good toward truth—they resided in the Lord’s Kingdom alongside the angels, and heaven was found within that love for them. But their descendants, under whom the Church began to decline, started to love their children more than their spouses. While even evil people can love their children, a spouse can only be truly loved by those who are good.

2731. I heard from those Most Ancient people that marriage love is such that each partner wants to belong entirely to the other, and this is reciprocal; in this mutual giving and receiving, they find heavenly happiness. Their minds are so joined that this mutuality exists in every single detail of life—that is, in every single affection and every single thought. For this reason, the Lord has established that wives should represent the "affections of good" (which belong to the will) and husbands should represent the "thoughts of truth" (which belong to the intellect). Marriage is meant to be like the relationship between the **will** and the **intellect**, and between every detail of those two faculties in a person who lives in the good of truth and the truth of good.

2732. I spoke with the angels about this mutual and reciprocal state, asking what it is like. They said that the image and likeness of one is present in the mind of the other. In this way, they live together not only in the outward details but in the very depths of life, so that the Lord's love and mercy can flow into such a union with blessing and happiness. They also said that those who lived in such marriage love during their life in the body remain together and live in heaven as angels, sometimes even with their children. However, they noted that there are very few from Christianity today who do so. In contrast, everyone from the Most Ancient Church (which was "celestial") and many from the Ancient Church (which was "spiritual") are joined this way. Those who lived in marriage but were joined by lust rather than marriage love are separated in the next life, because no lust is tolerated in heaven. Those who felt mutual hatred are separated even further; and further still...

*...those who hated each other; when they first both enter the other life, they usually meet, but after they have suffered hardships, they are separated.* <note>original: "qui se odio habuerunt; cum primum in alteram vitam ambo veniunt, ut plurimum conveniunt, sed postquam dura passi sunt, separantur."</note>

2733. There were certain spirits who, from their habits in the life of the body, bothered me with a peculiar skill. This happened through a soft, almost waving influence, similar to that of good spirits. However, I perceived that within it were cunning and similar traits intended to trap and deceive. Eventually, I spoke with one of them; I was told he had been an army commander while he lived in the world. 

Because I perceived that his thoughts contained lustful ideas, I spoke with him about **marriage** <note>original: "Conjugio"</note>. Our conversation was conducted in the speech of spirits, illustrated by symbolic representations <note>Spiritual communication often uses mental images or "representations" that convey complex meanings instantly.</note> which fully express feelings and many ideas in a single moment. He said that he had considered **adultery** <note>original: "adulteria"</note> as nothing during his life in the body. But I was permitted to tell him that acts of adultery are unspeakable—even though they appear acceptable to people like him because of the pleasure they took in them, which convinced them that such acts were not wrong, or even that they were permissible. 

I told him he could also know this from the fact that marriages are the nurseries of the human race, and thus also the nurseries of the **Heavenly Kingdom** <note>original: "Regnum caeleste"</note>. For this reason, marriage must never be violated but must be held as holy. Furthermore, as he was now in the other life and in a state of spiritual perception, he should know that **marriage love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis"</note> descends from the Lord through heaven. From that love, as if from a parent, **mutual love** is derived, which is the very foundation of heaven. 

I also told him that when adulterers merely approach heavenly societies, they sense their own foul odor and throw themselves toward hell. At the very least, he should have known that violating a marriage was against Divine laws, against the civil laws of all nations, and against the genuine light of reason, because it is contrary to both Divine and human order. 

But he replied that he never knew such things in the life of the body, nor had he ever thought about them. He wanted to argue whether this was true, but I told him that **truth** <note>original: "veritas"</note> does not permit such reasoning in the other life. In the afterlife, people use arguments to defend their pleasures, and thus to defend evils and falsehoods. I said he should first think about what had been said because it is true. 

Alternatively, he could consider the principle best known in the world: that no one should do to another what he would not want the other to do to him. Thus, if someone had deceived the wife he had loved (as happens at the beginning of every marriage), and if he spoke while in a state of anger over it, would he not also have detested adultery? In that moment, because he was highly intelligent, he would have confirmed his opposition to it more than others, even to the point of condemning it to hell. Thus, he was capable of judging himself by his own standards.

2734. Those who experienced happiness in their marriages in the life of the body, based on genuine marriage love, also have happiness in the other life.

2735. When it is represented in the afterlife, it appears through the most beautiful things that can ever be seen by the eye or grasped by the mind. I was told that all beauty in the afterlife originates from conjugial love. 2736. I have been taught that genuine conjugial love is **innocence** <note>original: "innocentia"</note> itself, which dwells in wisdom. Those who have lived in conjugial love possess more wisdom than anyone else in heaven. When seen by others, they appear like infants in a blooming and spring-like age; and everything that happens to them then is a source of joy and happiness. They are in the innermost heaven, which is called the **heaven of innocence** <note>original: "cælum innocentiæ"</note>. Through this heaven, the Lord flows into conjugial love; and from that heaven, angels are present with people who live in that love. They are also present with infants in their earliest years.

2737. For those who live in conjugial love, the inner parts of the mind are open through heaven even to the Lord; for that love flows from the Lord through the innermost part of a person. Thus, they have the **Kingdom of the Lord** <note>original: "Regnum Domini"</note> within themselves. Because of this, they possess a genuine love for children for the sake of the Lord’s kingdom. They are more receptive than all others to heavenly loves and excel in **mutual love** <note>original: "amore mutuo"</note>, for mutual love flows from conjugial love like a stream from its fountain.

2738. Mutual love as it exists in heaven is not the same as conjugial love. Conjugial love desires to be one with the life of the other, whereas mutual love desires better for the other than for oneself. This is like the love of parents toward their children, or the love of those who find joy in doing good, not for their own sake, but because the act itself brings them joy. Such angelic love is derived from conjugial love and is born from it like a child from its parent; this is why it is found in parents toward their children. This love is preserved by the Lord in parents even if they are not in a state of conjugial love, so that the human race does not perish.

2739. ...himself, and love toward relatives, and so on according to degrees in their order. According to those loves, which are uniquely from good and truth—that is, from love and faith in the Lord—all heavenly societies are formed. These are joined together by the Lord so that they resemble a single human being; for this reason, heaven is also called the **Greatest Man** <note>original: "Maximus Homo"; a central concept in this text where all of heaven functions together as a single collective human form.</note>. There are inexpressible varieties of these societies, all of which take their origin and are derived from the union of good and truth from the Lord, which union is the **Heavenly Marriage**.

This is why the origin of all blood relationships and legal affinities on earth is derived from marriages, and why loves are similarly derived according to degrees between them. But because there is no **conjugial love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis"; the spiritual love between spouses.</note> today, blood relations and affinities are indeed counted from it, but they are not the blood relations and affinities of love. In the **Most Ancient Church** <note>original: "Antiquissima Ecclesia"; referring to a prehistoric, spiritually pure state of humanity.</note>, such derivations of love also existed; for this reason, they live together in the heavens as if distinct into nations, families, and households, all of which acknowledge the Lord as their only Parent.

2740. Genuine conjugial love cannot exist except between two partners—that is, in the marriage of one man and one wife—and never between many at the same time. This is because conjugial love is mutual and reciprocal, and the life of one is in the other alternately, so that they are, as it were, one. Such a union is possible between two, but not among many; many partners tear that love apart. 

The people of the Most Ancient Church, who were celestial and possessed a perception of good and truth like angels, had only one wife. They said that with one wife they perceived heavenly delights and happiness, and they were horrified if the marriage of many was even mentioned. For the marriage of one husband and one wife descends, as was said, from the marriage of good and truth, or from the heavenly marriage, which is of such a nature. This can be clearly seen from the Lord's words in Matthew: 

> "Jesus said, Have you not read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female; and said, for this reason a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cling to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh? Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined, let no man separate. Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, permitted you to divorce your wives; but from the beginning it was not so. Not everyone can receive this saying, but only those to whom it is given." — **Matthew 19:3–12** <note>original: "Matthæum XIX: 3 ad 12"</note>.

2741. Good and truth continually flow from the Lord into everyone, and therefore genuine conjugial love does as well. However, it is received in different ways, and it becomes whatever the recipient makes of it. In the lustful, it is turned into lust; in adulterers, into adultery. Heavenly happiness becomes a foul pleasure; thus, heaven is turned into hell. This is similar to the light of the sun flowing into objects: it is received according to the form of the objects and becomes blue, red, yellow, green, dark, or even black, depending on that reception.

2742. Among some people, there exists something that resembles **conjugial love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis"; the spiritual love between spouses.</note>, yet it is not truly that love unless they are grounded in the love of what is good and true. It is a love that appears to be marital, but it arises from worldly or selfish motives—namely, to be served at home, to live in security, to be at leisure, or to be cared for when they are unwell or growing old; or perhaps for the sake of the children they love. For some, this bond is forced by fear for their spouse, for their reputation, or of negative consequences. In others, it is a lustful love that leads them; in the beginning, this appears like marital love because it mimics a kind of innocence. Such couples play like children and experience a joy that feels like something from heaven. However, over time they do not become more closely and tightly united as those in genuine marital love do, but instead they drift apart. Marital love also differs between spouses: in one it may be more or less present, while in the other there is little or none. Because of this difference, marriage can be heaven for one and hell for the other; it is the quality of their inner affection and how they receive that love that determines this.

2743. A large dog appeared to me, resembling **Cerberus** <note>In Greek mythology, the three-headed dog guarding the entrance to the underworld.</note>, and I asked what it signified. I was told that such a dog signifies a guard, preventing the transition from heavenly delight to infernal delight, and vice versa. Those who are in genuine marital love live in heavenly delight; however, those who live in adultery also experience a delight that appears to them as heavenly, but it is actually infernal. This is represented by the dog: a barrier to ensure those opposite delights do not mix.

2744. I was shown how the delights of marital love progress—one way toward heaven, and the other toward hell. The progression of delights toward heaven moved into ever-increasing states of blessedness and happiness, eventually becoming innumerable and inexpressible. The more interior the level, the more numerous and inexpressible these joys became, reaching the very celestial heights of the innermost heaven, which is the heaven of innocence. This progression happens in total freedom, for all freedom comes from love, and the greatest freedom comes from marital love, which is essentially celestial.

Then I was shown how the delights of marital love progress toward hell. They gradually remove themselves from heaven, though this also happens through an apparent sense of freedom, until hardly anything human remains in them. They end in a deadly and hellish state that, once seen, cannot be described. A certain spirit who was with me at the time also saw these things; he hurried forward to the **Sirens** <note>original: "Sirenes"; here used to describe spirits who use outward charm to hide deceitful or immoral intentions.</note>—who are of this nature—shouting that he would show them the quality of their delight. He initially held onto the idea of delight, but as he moved further forward, that idea continued like a progression toward hell, and finally ended in such horror. Sirens are those who are convinced that it is respectable to engage in promiscuity and adultery, while still being esteemed by others as if they were honorable and living a proper life. Most of them come into the afterlife from the Christian world; regarding them, see numbers 831, 959, 1515, 1983, and 2484.

2745. There are some women who do not love their husbands but look down on them, eventually considering them as nothing. 2746. He delighted in variety, so much so that he never loved any woman constantly. He spent his time in **brothels** <note>original: "lupinaribus."</note> and thus committed adultery with many, rejecting each one afterward. Because of this, he defrauded many women and extinguished his own desire for marriage and the procreation of children, eventually contracting an "unnatural nature." All of these things were exposed, and he was miserably punished in the sight of the angels, and then cast into hell. (Concerning the hells of adulterers, see Part One, numbers 824 to 830).

2747. Because adulteries are completely contrary to marital love, adulterers cannot be with angels in heaven. This is because they are in states contrary to what is **good and true**; they are not in the **Heavenly Marriage** <note>original: "Conjugio caelesti"; the spiritual union of goodness in the will and truth in the understanding.</note>. Furthermore, they hold only filthy ideas about marriage. The moment marriage is mentioned, or the idea of it arises, their minds are immediately filled with lascivious, obscene, and even **nefarious** <note>original: "nefanda"; unspeakable or wicked.</note> thoughts. Similarly, when angels speak of what is good and true, such spirits think in opposition to them. For all the affections and thoughts a person had in the world remain with them after death. Adulterers are inclined to destroy societies; many of them are cruel (number 824), and in their hearts, they are against charity and mercy. They laugh at the miseries of others, want to take what belongs to others, and do so as much as they dare. They find delight in destroying friendships and creating enemies. Their "religion" consists of saying they acknowledge the Creator of the universe and a Providence—but only a "universal" one—and salvation through faith alone, believing things cannot go worse for them than for anyone else. But when their hearts are explored in the next life, it is found that they do not even believe those things; instead of a Creator, they believe in nature; instead of a universal Providence, they believe in none; and they think nothing of faith. All this is because adultery is entirely against what is good and true. Therefore, anyone can judge for themselves how such people could ever enter heaven.

2748. Certain spirits who had lived a life of adultery in the world came to me and spoke with me. I perceived that they had not been in the other life for very long, for they did not know they were there, thinking they were still in the world...

# CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

...world, their ability to reflect on where they were was taken away from them. They were told they were in the afterlife, but they soon forgot and began asking where their houses were so they could settle in. When asked if they had any respect for spiritual matters—specifically **conjugial love** <note>original: "amor conjugialis"; the spiritual union of two minds.</note>, which is torn apart by such lusts—and told that their behavior was against the order of heaven, they paid no attention and did not understand. I asked further if they feared the laws and the punishments that come with them, but they held these in contempt. However, when I mentioned that they might be treated poorly or beaten by the servants of a household, this was the only thing they feared. 

Then I was allowed to perceive their thoughts (since thoughts are shared openly in the afterlife); they were so filthy and obscene that upright people could not help but shudder. Because every single one of these thoughts is made public before spirits and angels in the next life, it is clear why such people cannot be in heaven.

2749. Those who, through adultery, have developed a loathing and nausea for marriage, experience a strange reaction to heaven. When any delight, blessing, or happiness from the heaven of angels reaches them, it turns into something disgusting and nauseating to them. This feeling then turns into pain, and finally into a foul stench, until they eventually throw themselves down toward hell to escape it.

2750. I was instructed by angels that when anyone commits adultery on earth, heaven is immediately closed to them. From that point on, they live only in worldly and physical concerns. Even if they hear about matters of love and faith, these ideas do not penetrate their **interiors** <note>original: "interiora"; the inner levels of the human mind or spirit.</note>. Whatever they themselves say about such things does not come from their inner heart, but only from their memory and their mouth, driven by pride or a desire for profit. Their inner spiritual lives are closed and cannot be opened except through sincere **repentance** <note>original: "pænitentia".</note>.

2751. Up and to the front, before my left eye, there was a cluster of spirits who, during their physical lives, had plotted against others more secretly and craftily than most. These were adulterers who were still in the **world of spirits** <note>original: "mundus spirituum"; the intermediate state where souls arrive immediately after death.</note> because they had recently died. It was their habit to send members of their group out in different directions to plot not only against conjugial love, but also against everything good and true—and especially against the Lord. Those who are sent out return to the group to report what they have heard, and then they consult together. 

They even sent one to me, thinking I was a spirit because I spoke the language of spirits. When this emissary spoke, he poured out scandalous insults, mostly against the Lord; he seemed to be made of nothing but scandals. But I told him to stop, knowing exactly which group and which "dregs of society" he came from. As for the Lord, I know without any doubt that He is one with the Father, that the entire heaven is His, and that from Him comes all innocence, peace, love, charity, and mercy—as well as all conjugial love. All good and truth come from Him, and all these things are Divine. And that...

# GENESIS

Moses and the Prophets themselves—that is, every single part of the Word in its internal sense—and the fact that all the rituals of the Jewish Church represented Him <note>original: "Ipsum"; referring to the Lord</note>. When the spirit heard this, being so certain of it that he no longer had any doubt about what more he could want, he retreated in shame. These things were said so that he might report them to the adulterers who made up that wicked group <note>original: "globus"; literally a "ball" or "mass," referring to a collective of spirits</note> from which he had been sent.

2752. Those who have been enticed by adulteries desire, more than others in the afterlife, to obsess over <term>obsidere: to haunt or possess</term> humans and thus return to the world. However, they are kept in Hell by the Lord so that they do not come among those spirits who are present with humans. Most of these individuals are from the Christian world, and rarely from others.

2753. There are some in the world who are driven by a desire to lure virgins into illicit sexual acts <note>original: "scortationes"</note>, wherever they may be—in monasteries, in families, with their parents, or even among wives—insinuating themselves through clever methods and flattery. Because they became accustomed to such things and took them into their very nature, they retain in the afterlife the ability to slip into spiritual societies through charming and deceptive behavior. However, because their true thoughts are visible there, they are rejected. They move from one society to another but are rejected everywhere and even punished, for they strive to steal the joy and happiness of others. Finally, they are admitted into no societies, but after enduring heavy punishments, they are grouped with their own kind in hell.

2754. The most deceitful sometimes appear high above the head, but their hell is deep beneath the heel of the foot. These are the modern-day "antediluvians" <note>original: "antediluviani"; referring to those who live like the corrupt generations before the Great Flood</note>. They lie in wait by pretending to be innocent and merciful, and through various good emotions used for persuasion. While they lived in the world, they were adulterers above all others. Wherever there was a beautiful and young wife, they entered without conscience and used these disguises to incite her to adultery. They are invisible and do not wish to be detected because they act in secret. They are also cruel; they cared only for themselves and thought nothing of it if the whole world perished for their sake. There are a great number of such people today, even coming from "Christendom." Their hell is the most severe of all.

2755. There are several hells for adulterers. There, they love nothing more than filth and excrement, which then becomes delightful to them. This can also be seen from many of that sort during their physical life, who find it pleasant to think of and remember filthy things, though they abstain from speaking of them for the sake of social propriety <note>original: "decorum"</note>. The pleasure of adultery in the afterlife is turned into such foul things. This happens just as when the heat of the sun, even in springtime, shines upon excrement or a corpse.

2756. There are those who held as a principle the "community of wives" <note>the practice of sharing wives among a group</note>. In the afterlife, they speak like good people, but they are malicious and deceitful. Their punishment is horrifying: they are bound together as if in a bundle, and symbolically a serpent is stretched around them, encircling them all like a bundled ball, and in this way, they are cast out.

# CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

2757. As I was led through several dwellings, I came to one where heat took hold of the feet and loins. It was said that those who were there had indulged in pleasures, but yet had not extinguished the natural desire for producing offspring.

2758. That genuine marriage love <term>original: *amor conjugialis*; the spiritual and holy love between a husband and wife</term> is heaven itself is represented in the kingdoms of nature. Indeed, nothing exists in the entire universe that does not in some way represent the Kingdom of the Lord in general. For the natural world derives its entire origin from the spiritual Kingdom; whatever lacks a prior origin is nothing. Nothing exists that is disconnected from a cause, and thus from a purpose, for whatever is disconnected falls apart in a moment and becomes nothing. From this come the representations of the Lord’s Kingdom in the kingdoms of nature. That marriage love is heaven is clear from the transformation of little worms into nymphs or chrysalises, and then into flying creatures. For when the time of their "wedding" arrives—which is when they cast off their earthly form (their worm-like state) and are gifted with wings and become flying insects—they are then raised into the atmosphere, which is their heaven. There they play together, enter into marriages, lay eggs, and are nourished by the juices of flowers. They are also then in their greatest beauty, for they have wings decorated with gold, silver, and other gracefully distinct colors. The Marriage principle <note>original: *Conjugiale*; refers here to the spiritual essence of the marriage bond</note> produces such wonderful things even in such lowly little animals.

2759. Toward the right side, rising from the lower earth, there appeared something like a wave <note>original: *volumen*; literally a roll or volume, suggesting a mass of people rising together</note>. It was said that these were many spirits from the uneducated common people, though they were not wicked; they were peasants and other simple folk. When I spoke with them, they said they knew the Lord, to whose Name they commend themselves. Beyond this, they knew little about faith and its mysteries. Others rose up later who knew a little bit more. It was perceived that their inner lives could be opened (for this can be clearly perceived in the next life). They possessed a conscience, which was shared with me so that I might experience it. It was said that they had lived simply in marriage love. They said they had loved their spouse and abstained from adultery; that they did this from conscience was evident because they said they could not have done otherwise, as it would have been against their will. Such people are instructed in the next life and perfected in the "good of love" and the "truth of faith," and finally, they are received among the angels.

->THE END<-
